**Shikhar Vaish** · 2018-06-18 10:36 UTC

@Swetanjal Murati Dutta   You might want to do 'git reflog' to get the  id of the point where you'd like to be reverted. After getting the alpha-numeric id just do a 'git reset --hard <commit id>'  and the force push.

**Roman Godov** · 2018-06-30 11:47 UTC

For the V1 of the "Report Spam" feature I've done the following:

1. Added item to the "message actions" drop down menu:
[Selection_002.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/92/PNimT7elNplV2fJP8dr65REr/Selection_002.png)

2. Clicking that pops up a confirmation modal
[Selection_003.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/f8/TVHkM6WcIu9WRqyiPnm8jTrr/Selection_003.png)
 
3. "Report spam" generates a notification to the organization's administrators with a copy of the content that was reported sent by Notification bot:
[Selection_004.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/f7/ciU4S6wMD64wRQXng0F2KeQ2/Selection_004.png) 

4. All messages reported as spam get tagged in the "reactions" part of the UI:
[Selection_005.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/94/yc3va6_BeUzT_sMpgFg75zuz/Selection_005.png)
 
5. To handle cases where no admin is online, an effect of "report spam" is that if a user has had their messages reported as spam by at least 2 distinct users (added setting for amount of users) that have had accounts for at least a month (added setting for that too), then the user's account is marked as a potential spammer and their account gets immediately deactivated. They also get an email letting them know that they've been deactivated and that they can contact an organization administrator if they'd like to appeal:
[Selection_006.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/60/jZLI7c3AujD3sfYisRPpAz8_/Selection_006.png)
 
The only one thing left to implement is an organization setting.
If someone is willing to review this PR that would be greatly appreciated, thanks!

**Rishi Gupta** · 2019-04-13 19:30 UTC

took a look. I guess some thoughts:
* I feel like the right thing to do with spam is to delete it immediately. I think spam that sits for 8 hours potentially gets like a 10x exposure on average to spam that's deleted immediately (especially because spam that's deleted within a few seconds doesn't even get pushed out via notifications). 
So I'm a little worried about solutions that promote spam sitting for hours, rather than solutions that promote immediate deletion. 
* I think we don't want a "report spam" button for corporate users (not hard -- just have to add an org setting, but I think I wouldn't want to add it without the org setting, given how few reports we have currently of spam being a problem).

* add endpoint and UI for spam reports
* add management script to automatically deal with spam
* add cron support

well, I think the step before is figuring out what feature we want, which is why I want to wait till we have at least a few more reports. **Yago González** · 2018-06-25 14:58 UTC

As requested per @mir_lv, here's a more detailed explanation of what I meant:

The endpoints you reach through `/api/v1` require Basic authentication, which is basically a header in the HTTP request with user credentials that allow you to query the endpoint.

**mir_kaka** · 2018-06-25 15:00 UTC

**Yago González** · 2018-06-25 15:02 UTC

I don't know which language/library are you using to contact the API, but what you have to do is:

1. See how can you use Basic authentication with the specific tool you're using. A quick Google search should help you with that, e.g. `basic auth python requests`.
2. Get the API key for your user, following [this](https://chat.zulip.org/api/api-keys) guide.
3. Contact the endpoint using your user's email address and the API key as password, with the Basic authentication method you read about in step 1.

## Initial messages fetch

**Steve Howell** · 2018-07-06 16:12 UTC

@Roman Godov We have some message-related data in `fetch_initial_state_data`, but no actual messages.  You are correct that the client gets them via `get_messages_backend`. **saqura** · 2018-07-12 11:24 UTC

From the description I would expect to receive all messages posted in any stream. Am I missing something?

**saqura** · 2018-07-12 11:27 UTC

**saqura** · 2018-07-12 11:32 UTC

Ah, I think I found out why: I can add the bot as a subscriber to the stream, and then it works on that stream as expected. Is it possible to have a bot that receives all messages from the entire organization, without adding it to each stream? (I somehow thought this was the default behaviour for such bots.)

**Tim Abbott** · 2018-07-12 12:30 UTC

@saqura the default for bots using our Interactive Bots API is that they receive all messages in the organization that mention them.

**Tim Abbott** · 2018-07-12 12:30 UTC

But if you're using the raw real-time events API, you just get what the bot user is subscribed to by default.

**Tim Abbott** · 2018-07-12 12:31 UTC

However, if you pass the `all_public_streams` option to the `register` API endpoint, you'll get all messages sent to public streams (plus any sent to private streams the bot is subscribed to)

**Tim Abbott** · 2018-07-12 12:32 UTC

So, that should do what you want.  @Yago González we should make sure to document this feature in the "real-time events API" page; https://zulipchat.com/api/register-queue does have the flag in its arguments list, but this is a common enough desire we should highlight it in the prose sections as well.

**Steve Howell** · 2018-07-12 14:10 UTC

@saqura Thanks for the feedback!

**Rohitt Vashishtha** · 2018-07-12 17:26 UTC

What Tim suggested here and I find reasonable is just adding some parameters to `topic_data.js` as follows:

```
--- static/js/topic_data.js
+++ static/js/topic_data.js
@@ -26,8 +26,12 @@ exports.topic_history = function (stream_id) {
     self.add_or_update = function (opts) {
         var name = opts.name;
         var message_id = opts.message_id || 0;  
         message_id = parseInt(message_id, 10);

+        // If I send a message to a topic, I've 'engaged' with the topic.
+        var engaged = people.is_my_user_id(opts.sender_id);
 
         var existing = topics.get(name);
 
@@ -37,10 +41,13 @@ exports.topic_history = function (stream_id) {
                 pretty_name: name,
                 historical: false,
                 count: 1,
+                engaged: engaged,
             });
             return;
         }
 
+        existing.engaged = existing.engaged || engaged;
+
         if (!existing.historical) {
             existing.count += 1;
         }
+        sender_id: sender_id,
     });
 };
```

And then use recent_topics to just combine this data with unread data and give meaningful results.

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-01-30 18:26 UTC

It seems to me like the "recent topics" we track in `topic_data.js` is exactly the set of topics we're interested in tracking for this purpose as well; we're just adding an additional value that we keep track of (the last time the current user engaged with it by sending a message, reacting, etc.)

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-01-30 18:27 UTC

So I would think we just want to support a new attribute in the existing data structure and a new function to pull out the recent topics data sorted by that new key?

**Steve Howell** · 2019-01-30 18:33 UTC

I think as soon as you have to start sorting the data structure by a new key, you kinda lose the advantage of keeping them in one structure.  An interesting case study may be `people.js`, where we have several parallel data structures to track stuff, all efficient for specific use cases (do I know the id? do I only know the name?  do I want all uses in the realm?).  And the only place where we really couple stuff is the add/remove methods, and they're just a series of one-liners.

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-01-30 18:33 UTC

But the object is a dictionary already, so it's already a "read through everything to sort" structure.

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-01-30 18:34 UTC

**Steve Howell** · 2019-01-30 18:36 UTC

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-01-30 18:37 UTC

Yeah, so the algorithm for that would iterate through all the stream/topic pairs, sorting by `last_engagement_message_id`, and output that list.

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-01-30 18:37 UTC

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-01-30 18:37 UTC

(Which is mostly just whether the sender is me for v1, and later would also include whether the message has any reactions from me.)

**Steve Howell** · 2019-01-30 18:40 UTC

I feel like that's more complexity than just having a list of `stream_id, topic_name, message_id` tuples in its own data structure.  And keeping things separate allows us to optimize down the road (i.e. sort on write, instead of sort on read, or whatever).

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-01-30 18:48 UTC

I'm not worried about optimization of that form here; not enough data to matter for something you only interact with when you click on it.  I do worry with separate data structures that we'll end up having to write code to splice together the two data sets (because e.g. we'll want the unread count from `topic_data.js` to render it whenever we want the recent topics list).  

I guess in any case we can try to keep the interface clean by having `topic_data.add_message` call into the other module.

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-01-30 18:48 UTC

**Steve Howell** · 2019-01-30 18:51 UTC

It's easier to merge stuff (once we know what the real use cases are) than split stuff apart.  I think `recently_engaged_topics` would be fine.  What are we calling this feature from a user's perspective?

Probably "My topics"

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-01-30 19:04 UTC

bots-dir

- requirements.txt

requirements.txt

zulip

run.sh

pip3 install -r requirements.txt # if already installed, its a no-op so doesn't take much time

## Zulip's chosen frameworks, libraries, etc.

*2018-07-27 to 2018-07-27 · 34 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/Zulip.27s.20chosen.20frameworks.2C.20libraries.2C.20etc.2E/with/619507)*

**Alex UT** · 2018-07-27 18:25 UTC

I saw a commit message mention jQuery.  Anyone want to speak generally about the stack used for Zulip, and the decision making that went into the choices?

**Alex UT** · 2018-07-27 18:26 UTC

Seeing jQuery struck me, because it seems to me that most shops are moving on from jQuery and adopting other, newer things, like Angular, React, Vue, what-have-you.

**Tim Abbott** · 2018-07-27 18:28 UTC

There's a lot of tradeoffs between different options in this space :)

**Alex UT** · 2018-07-27 18:28 UTC

Sure, so I was interested in learning the thinking of the core devs.  :)

**Tim Abbott** · 2018-07-27 18:29 UTC

For example, a big downside with React is that there's this huge amount of knowledge one needs to learn in order to effectively work on a React codebase, because it has a large library ecosystem, and is hard to use without pulling in a lot of those libraries.

**Tim Abbott** · 2018-07-27 18:30 UTC

So using React comes with it a huge penalty in terms of how easy it is for people to get involved in an open source project.

**Tim Abbott** · 2018-07-27 18:32 UTC

I'm a fan of the properties provided by react/vue in that they save a bit of work in live update, but it's actually not a large portion of the total work going into a high-quality real-time sync experience (which we're certainly on the extreme end of -- everything updates in real-time even for things like users changing their name).  

You can look at `static/js/server_events_dispatch.js` and the functions it calls to get a feel for how this works.

**Tim Abbott** · 2018-07-27 18:34 UTC

When working on a project involving a lot of people (open source or not), I think the readability of the codebase is underrated in importance.  And certainly I'm extremely glad we didn't adopt any of the frameworks that were around when the first code was written on Zulip (Meteor, Ember, Angular, Backbone, etc.), because migrating off one of those is a nightmare, and I think they're basically all dying projects, because there's not a good reason to prefer them to React/Vue.

**Alex UT** · 2018-07-27 18:34 UTC

Interesting.  Thanks for sharing.

**Alex UT** · 2018-07-27 18:34 UTC

So the current plan is to continue that way?  Stick with jQuery?

**Tim Abbott** · 2018-07-27 18:34 UTC

(E.g. the poor folks at Rocket.Chat are basically rewriting their whole frontend to remove Meteor)

**Tim Abbott** · 2018-07-27 18:36 UTC

Well, our near-term plans for the frontend ecosystem are more around things that improve developer productivity directly, like static types, which can save a lot of time in data layer work.

**Steve Howell** · 2018-07-27 18:38 UTC

A lot of our front-end is actually pretty data-driven, so many of our most core modules are jQuery-free (and framework-free).

**Tim Abbott** · 2018-07-27 18:38 UTC

There's an ongoing conversation about using React or Vue, and there's some appeal to each (e.g. with React we could share code with our React Native mobile apps, while Vue is simpler), but the (migration effort / benefit) ratio for those seems a lot less than what I'd expect to gain from static types.

**Vishnu KS** · 2018-07-27 18:39 UTC

/me thinks this can be a fascinating blog post which should gain us traction in hacker news

**Alex UT** · 2018-07-27 18:40 UTC

You'll definitely get some click-throughs if you say "we eschewed all modern JS frameworks; here's why".

**Steve Howell** · 2018-07-27 18:41 UTC

GH just announced they ditched jQuery

**Steve Howell** · 2018-07-27 18:42 UTC

I'm probably in the 95th percentile of jQuery haters but I'm kinda skeptical of the 100%-framework-free philosophy...and jQuery isn't **super** heavy, we mostly use it as a battle-tested polyfill

**Tim Abbott** · 2018-07-27 18:43 UTC

I certainly imagine a world where we mostly replace jQuery with ES6, which it sounds is what GitHub did?  (I haven't seen the announcement)

**Steve Howell** · 2018-07-27 18:44 UTC

For ES6 goodness, we kinda already have that via underscore.js.  In other words we don't use jQuery for everything it offers.  We mostly use it for DOM manipulation.

**Alex UT** · 2018-07-27 18:48 UTC

Going from "jQuery for DOM manipulation" to one of the major frameworks is, um... not a small bit of work.  :)

**Steve Howell** · 2018-07-27 18:48 UTC

exactly :smile:

**Steve Howell** · 2018-07-27 18:49 UTC

The main things in our app that people see 99% of the time are the two sidebars and the message view.

**Steve Howell** · 2018-07-27 18:49 UTC

And of those three the most complex component is the message view.

**Steve Howell** · 2018-07-27 18:50 UTC

In order for the message view to work, we have some relatively complex code to deal with "windows" of only ~400 messages at a time, and there's some minor trickery that happens when new messages come into interleaved views.

**Steve Howell** · 2018-07-27 18:51 UTC

But that's by far our most battle-tested code, and the core module for that is only 1040 lines of code.

**Alex UT** · 2018-07-27 18:52 UTC

Wow, that's impressive(ly small).

**Steve Howell** · 2018-07-27 18:52 UTC

Yeah, there are other modules that come into play, but that's where all the rendering actually happens.

**Steve Howell** · 2018-07-27 18:53 UTC

https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/master/static/js/message_list_view.js

**Tim Abbott** · 2018-07-27 18:53 UTC

But as a project, we generally favor thinking through things, doing them right, and not duplicating code; one could easily have a product with the same functionality as Zulip and 10x the code.

**Alex UT** · 2018-07-27 18:54 UTC

The goal is admirable, though, in fairness, reducing LoC can also sometimes reduce the quality of a codebase.  Increased complexity, cleverness, things like that.  But I get your point.

**Steve Howell** · 2018-07-27 18:58 UTC

I think we're pretty good about not being overly clever. hopefully in a good way :smile:

**Tim Abbott** · 2018-07-27 18:59 UTC

Yeah, LOC isn't the thing we're optimizing; we have a lot of nice long block comments, and ban use of too clever 1-line hackery.

**Steve Howell** · 2018-07-27 19:00 UTC

Obviously no codebase is perfect, but we've definitely worked to improve subsystems that are kinda messy.  Our main-page code quality has always been pretty decent, but our settings system used to be fairly ad hoc, and we've had multiple people do good work to clean that up.


## broken git test

**Ajay Neethi Kannan** · 2018-07-30 14:00 UTC

Hey everyone!
My development environment is failing git tests of older commit messages . What should i do?

**Tim Abbott** · 2018-07-30 16:44 UTC

@Ajay Neethi Kannan I would recommend using `gitk` to inspect your Git repository; I bet you've gotten into a weird state in your Git repository (where you've rebased some commits that are in `upstream/master` into your branch).

**Ajay Neethi Kannan** · 2018-07-30 18:46 UTC

I tried it , but the test is failing where the commit messages do not follow the rules such as message length, and these are the commits of others

**Tim Abbott** · 2018-07-30 18:59 UTC

The way that test works is that it only checks commits that are in your branch but not `upstream/master`.  So if you have your git repository setup properly and haven't done anything weird when rebasing to create copies of other people's commits, it shouldn't check commits from others.

**Ajay Neethi Kannan** · 2018-07-30 19:16 UTC

Oh! Got it. Thank You for explaining this to me. If i am not disturbing, please do suggest some ways of correcting it

In the mobile app we always use Babel, but it is done 'invisibly' by React Native.
Our code may run on old browsers, iOS 8 and Android 4.4 being the oldest supported devices, so compared to the desktop app that can bundle a new engine that is guaranteed to run the JS supplied, that is a must for us.

On the web a very typical usage is to bundle the code with Webpack and include Babel in the build process.

**Boris Yankov** · 2018-08-03 07:28 UTC

**Boris Yankov** · 2018-08-03 07:30 UTC

Does that mean that once we assign `SELF_HOSTED = 1` we should never use `1` for anything else again? Or alternatively should I imagine that if we significantly change the plan types we would do a migration on `RealmAuditLog`?

**Tim Abbott** · 2018-08-13 16:52 UTC

Well, we could redefine what `1` means in a backwards-compatible way.  But yes, that's how this would work.  That would be true if we used strings, though, too; we couldn't reuse "self_hosted" while changing its meaning either.

**Tim Abbott** · 2018-08-13 16:53 UTC

The main difference between these options is that doing an integer is type-safe (i.e. a typo in the name crashes, rather than just doing a string comparison against a value that would never happen)

**Tim Abbott** · 2018-08-13 16:53 UTC

(So I think in either case, we need to do migrations if we re-structure the names/values)

**Rishi Gupta** · 2018-08-13 17:23 UTC

in both cases I think we'd access via Realm.SELF_HOSTED, rather than `1` or `self_hosted`. But agree that having a string makes it tempting to do the other way.

Do you feel the same way about BillingProcessorState? The reason I thought `str` would be better is that it would be nicer to read and modify by hand, and in practice there is an assertion that would catch a typoed state immediately.

**Tim Abbott** · 2018-08-13 17:29 UTC

If you're using a coding style that's type-safe, then think either string or int is fine.  I agree string is a bit more hand-readable, though note that if you're modifying by hand, you create the typo problem for those manual modifications again :)

**Rishi Gupta** · 2018-08-13 17:39 UTC

right, I meant there is an assertion on every read that checks against the list of allowed values. But I'll change it from an assertion error to an error with a test.

**Tim Abbott** · 2018-08-14 18:38 UTC

@Yago González so, the way that this works is 90% of our code is accessed via an entrypoint that does Django setup (e.g. `manage.py`).  Most of our scripts/tools code does not import anything from Django, and thus doesn't need to call the Django setup methods.

**Tim Abbott** · 2018-08-14 18:38 UTC

So, my first question for something like `api_test_helpers.py` is whether it really needs to import `models.py`; there's a moderate performance cost to doing so, and it is sorta a violation of the boundaries we have.

**Yago González** · 2018-08-14 18:53 UTC

**Yago González** · 2018-08-14 18:54 UTC

**Tim Abbott** · 2018-08-14 18:56 UTC

@Yago González well, can't you just use the API to create the objects to interact with?

**Steve Howell** · 2018-08-14 18:56 UTC

I'll push back a little and say there are big advantages to having the API tests work completely at the API level.

**Tim Abbott** · 2018-08-14 18:56 UTC

Like, we have plenty of other tests that are unitary; I think the API end-to-end integration tests should be that, and don't have the same need to be unitary.

**Steve Howell** · 2018-08-14 18:58 UTC

It's actually nice at times to see how APIs work in conjunction with each other.

**Yago González** · 2018-08-14 18:58 UTC

I wasn't sure if mixing other endpoints with the one you're trying to test was a good practice. After all, if that endpoint you depend on is broken, it will mess with the tests of something else that may be working fine.

**Steve Howell** · 2018-08-14 18:59 UTC

Yeah, but our APIs should be pretty stable.

**Yago González** · 2018-08-14 18:59 UTC

We definitely want the tests to break (and they will) if something isn't right, but it makes difficult to debug.

**Steve Howell** · 2018-08-14 19:00 UTC

There are less invasive ways to solve the tests-are-hard-to-debug problem.

**Steve Howell** · 2018-08-14 19:00 UTC

Maybe a concrete example would be helpful here.

**Steve Howell** · 2018-08-14 19:01 UTC

Have you had a recent test that was tricky?

**Yago González** · 2018-08-14 19:11 UTC

Well the specific case I had in mind was while testing the endpoints for updating & deleting user groups. Since we don't have a way right now to list them, I couldn't get a group's ID.

**Yago González** · 2018-08-14 19:13 UTC

The only way to do it using only the API would be creating a new group and using the ID 1, which implies making some assumptions about the existence of previous groups.

**Yago González** · 2018-08-14 19:14 UTC

Probably in this case the best thing to do probably is to just implement the endpoint for listing user groups, but in other endpoints for modifying objects I wondered the same.

**Steve Howell** · 2018-08-14 19:34 UTC

> Probably in this case the best thing to do probably is to just implement the endpoint for listing user groups, but in other endpoints for modifying objects I wondered the same.
Yeah, I agree here.  This is some ways the essence of "test driven development".  Your tests are literally telling you which APIs are missing.  And fortunately list-stuff APIs are usually pretty straightforward, since there's not quite as many things to validate and insert/update APIs.

*2018-08-16 to 2018-08-18 · 4 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/user.20pills/with/632725)*

**Yashashvi Dave** · 2018-08-16 16:57 UTC

I am working on issue #10303. I am trying to add user pills in user profile popover, instead of user names for custom user field. [image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/25907420/44205803-45420400-a175-11e8-834b-ba5a05e28252.png)

Last two commits in #10319 implement this, but somehow it is not appending user pills in pill container and not throwing any error. I am trying to debug this issue for so long, but I am not able to find whats wrong. [This is the commit](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/10319/commits/92d722e53edebe72724126d95e39cdd9d1dfe278) which adds user pills.

**Tim Abbott** · 2018-08-17 18:49 UTC

@Cynthia Lin and @Shubham Padia may be able to help with this.

**Cynthia Lin** · 2018-08-17 20:54 UTC

@Yashashvi Dave It seems that you need to insert an input pill even though you don't want users to edit there:
```diff
diff --git a/static/templates/user_profile_modal.handlebars b/static/templates/user_profile_modal.handlebars
index 58b90dc38..18dad0afd 100644
--- a/static/templates/user_profile_modal.handlebars
+++ b/static/templates/user_profile_modal.handlebars
@@ -26,7 +26,9 @@
                 <div class="user-profile-key-value-section">
                     <div class="user-profile-modal-field-name">{{this.name}}:</div>
                     {{#if this.is_user_field}}
-                    <div class="pill-container" data-field-id="{{this.id}}"></div>
+                    <div class="pill-container" data-field-id="{{this.id}}">
+                        <div class="input" contenteditable="false"></div>
+                    </div>
                     {{else}}
                     <div class="user-profile-modal-field-value">{{this.value}}</div>
                     {{/if}}
```

You can use CSS to make the input to not display by adding a `display: none` property if you want to hide it :)

**Yashashvi Dave** · 2018-08-18 05:03 UTC

Thanks, it worked. Our code seems to append pills before this-input element, so template must include input element.

@Marc you need to use `manage.py knight` to create an `api_super_user` bot if that's what you want; those have permissions even administrator users don't have (including the ability to do things one doesn't usually want, like forge messages as being sent by other users)

## Check if message is first in topic

*2018-10-15 to 2018-10-16 · 17 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/Check.20if.20message.20is.20first.20in.20topic/with/652452)*

**August Eriksson** · 2018-10-15 12:32 UTC

Hi there, I'm working on https://github.com/zulip/zulip/issues/10539 . If using the email mirror, the first message in a topic should have it's email subject added to the message, if the subject is longer than 60 characters (the max length of a topic).

What I don't understand is how you would check if the message is the first in a topic while in the `send_zulip` function. Is there some way we can see this using the `stream` object that gets sent as a parameter to `send_zulip`?

**August Eriksson** · 2018-10-16 11:56 UTC

I've solved this for now by doing a query directly, `Message.objects.get(subject=topic[:MAX_SUBJECT_LENGTH])`. Not sure if this is the "proper" way of doing it.

**Tim Abbott** · 2018-10-16 18:28 UTC

@August Eriksson I don't think you need to do this filtering on the subject like.

**Tim Abbott** · 2018-10-16 18:29 UTC

The email mirror is primarily used for third-party tools to send data into Zulip, so there's no reason to expect that the subject lines of several emails with the same topic prefix will have the same subject.  So I think we should just be checking the length of the email's subject line (after stripping re/fwd/etc.), not the Zulip message history

**Tim Abbott** · 2018-10-16 18:29 UTC

@Rishi Gupta we should discuss, I suppose, since you proposed that filter.

**Tim Abbott** · 2018-10-16 18:30 UTC

A correct check  would involve a `Message.objects.filter(subject=..., recipient=...)`; otherwise you're looking at that topic name across all streams and all realms on taht server.

**Rishi Gupta** · 2018-10-16 18:42 UTC

The main motivation for this is "use zulip from your email", not the automated stuff.

**Tim Abbott** · 2018-10-16 18:43 UTC

@Rishi Gupta in that case, the subject should never be longer than 60 characters in the first place assuming we strip the `re` stuff properly (and if we don't, it'll be hopelessly split anyway).

**Tim Abbott** · 2018-10-16 18:43 UTC

Certainly the user request we had for "include the rest of the subject line in the email" was definitely for an automated stuff use case.

**Rishi Gupta** · 2018-10-16 18:43 UTC

New topics started by email won't be, though?

**Rishi Gupta** · 2018-10-16 18:44 UTC

I think for automated stuff the answer is to use shorter subjects

**Tim Abbott** · 2018-10-16 18:48 UTC

Once the first message is sent via email, the topic will be clipped to 60 characters when emailed back out to other users.

**Tim Abbott** · 2018-10-16 18:48 UTC

So ... any replies would go to the original topic without any special activity here.

**Tim Abbott** · 2018-10-16 18:49 UTC

The whole point of the automated thing is that you're using some internal or third-party tool that only knows how to generate emails and you may not control anything about its formatting (e.g. the subject lines might always be 50-120 characters beyond your direct control).  So ...  "use shorter subjects" is not an option in that context.

**Tim Abbott** · 2018-10-16 18:49 UTC

(There's tons of old software that has great support for sending email notifications but no API for doing other types of notifications)

**Rishi Gupta** · 2018-10-16 18:50 UTC

Ah, good point

**Rishi Gupta** · 2018-10-16 18:51 UTC

Ok, I'm fine with the straightforward version of this

@Paurakh Sharma Humagain I see what you mean here:

~~~
 31                 {% if not embedded %}

**Steve Howell** · 2019-03-01 14:04 UTC

@Tim Abbott @Rishi Gupta So the way we handle "New private message" vs. "New conversation is kinda janky now.  Ideally we would just build the three buttons entirely client-side and do everything responsively based on screen size (and other context, like what narrow you're in).  But instead...

**Steve Howell** · 2019-03-01 14:08 UTC

We have the main buttons in our server-side template.  We hide the "New private message" button if the embedded flag is turned on.  And then we have `/mobile_message_buttons_popover_content.handlebars` for either "New private message" or "New conversation" that gets launched from some popover.

**Steve Howell** · 2019-03-01 14:11 UTC

In the context of the "normal" app, if we want to use different text in that button depending on whether we're in a private narrow or not, we probably want to move at least the code for that button into a handlebars template.  Or I suppose we could just directly update the button text with jQuery (or toggle a class with jQuery that CSS uses).

**Steve Howell** · 2019-03-01 14:12 UTC

@Paurakh Sharma Humagain This might not be the easiest issue to work on until we sort out our strategy here.

**Rishi Gupta** · 2018-10-17 06:13 UTC

If I have something like the following:
```python
class Cow(object):
    def __init__(self):
        pass
    def moo(self):
        print('moooo')
c = Cow()
```

then 
`c.moo()` and `Cow.moo(c)` both seem to do the same thing. Is this true for class methods in general?

Asking because there are some things in the Stripe API where the docs have one form, and it would be more convenient from a test mocking perspective to have it in the other form. 
@Vishnu Ks  fyi

**Steve Howell** · 2018-10-17 14:06 UTC

I believe it's 100% true in python3 that `c.moo() == Cow.moo(c)` for normal classes.  In python2 there were annoying subtleties about how functions got bound.  It wouldn't shock me if there's still a way to make this `c.moo()` behave differently than `Cow.moo(c)` in python3, but I think you'd have to be doing some kind of deep magic.

(Order-dependent tests of any sort are the source of flaky tests, and in any case, we rollback the database after each test finishes)

@mock_stripe('stripe.Foo.bar', 'test_first_thing')

def test_third_thing(...)
```

where all the `test_*_thing`s would use the fixtures generated by the first one.

## Internal bots & get_members

*2018-10-29 to 2018-10-30 · 9 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/Internal.20bots.20.26.20get_members/with/656536)*

**Neil Pilgrim (neiljp)** · 2018-10-29 06:05 UTC

A bug was reported in ZT regarding a crash when narrowing to messages from the welcome-bot. Upon further investigation, I remembered 'internal bots' and how they're (currently?) in a separate realm, confirmed from the server code and API AFAICT. Consequently, the `get_members` call (in the python API, presumably elsewhere) does not return details of the internal bots. I've not looked at the web app, but I assume it works around this somehow? I remember mention of some potential plan to migrate the bots into individual realms? Either way, what's the correct approach, or is this actually a bug? :)

**Tim Abbott** · 2018-10-30 00:08 UTC

@Neil Pilgrim I replied to this question in the #**zulip-terminal** stream; basically, there's this extra data structure, `cross_realm_bots`, that you need for the "cross-realm bot" users like welcome-bot.

**Neil Pilgrim (neiljp)** · 2018-10-30 00:13 UTC

Could you clarify a little - is this a change necessary to the server code, an extra parameter to pass to the API, or...?

**Tim Abbott** · 2018-10-30 00:14 UTC

The data is in the `register` response, just in another key you're probably not using, the `cross_realm_bots` key.

**Neil Pilgrim (neiljp)** · 2018-10-30 00:15 UTC

Should it also be available via https://zulip.com/api/get-all-users ?

**Tim Abbott** · 2018-10-30 00:16 UTC

For a full client like zulip-terminal, I'd recommend getting all user data via the `/register` request when the client starts up.

**Tim Abbott** · 2018-10-30 00:17 UTC

That avoids unnecessary RTTs and also protects the client from having to deal with certain races that might otherwise be present (because the `/register` call does some careful atomicity work to ensure the event queue is in a consistent state with the data it returns)

**Tim Abbott** · 2018-10-30 00:17 UTC

https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/subsystems/events-system.html has some useful reading on how this works :)

**Neil Pilgrim (neiljp)** · 2018-10-30 00:18 UTC

I'll take a look in a bit, but if it just adds in the extra users I imagine it'll hopefully be reasonable to look at tonight :)

## reactions: id & user_id keys

*2018-11-18 to 2019-04-11 · 19 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/reactions.3A.20id.20.26.20user_id.20keys/with/662711)*

**Neil Pilgrim (neiljp)** · 2018-11-18 19:07 UTC

While debugging a ZT issue I've noticed that (in a ZT context at least) I'm having unexpected behavior when I look at message reaction data received from the server (notably in updates), namely sometimes the message nested `reactions` `user` dict has an `id` field, and sometimes `user_id`. The latter seems like the expected result from `actions.py`; is it likely/possible the server might be generating `id` instead under some conditions?
(I'd be happy to be proven wrong, but I don't obviously see something which would generate that in ZT)

**Tim Abbott** · 2018-11-19 02:26 UTC

@Neil Pilgrim hmm, interesting.  I'm not sure, but from skimming the `sew_messages_and_reactions `function and `get_raw_db_rows` on the `Reaction` object in the `zulip/zulip` project, I suspect that messages you get from the `get_messages` API query might come with just an `id` field.  May be worth testing?

**Neil Pilgrim (neiljp)** · 2019-04-03 05:52 UTC

@Tim Abbott Having not had a chance to follow this up earlier, this issue has resurfaced as #T334, and has an active PR to resolve on the client end.

 That said, I do believe the issue is that getting messages gives reactions with a `'user'={'id': n, ...}` entry, whereas `notify_reaction_update` in `actions.py` gives a reaction entry a `'user': {'user_id': n, ...}` element.

I imagine the latter is the 'incorrect' one?

**Steve Howell** · 2019-04-03 16:41 UTC

I generally prefer explicit names (`user_id`) to implicit names (`id`), although in this case, we just have three fields inside a `user` struct, so I could see it either way.  The `notify_reaction_update` code comes from 001847ac, which goes back to Nov 2016.

**Steve Howell** · 2019-04-03 16:43 UTC

The webapp code only looks at `user.user_id` currently, so the other fields (`email` and `full_name`) are just a waste of bandwidth, actually.

**Steve Howell** · 2019-04-03 16:44 UTC

@Neil Pilgrim Do you know which code is sending just `id`?  If you find it, it's worth doing `git blame` to see when it was written.

**Neil Pilgrim (neiljp)** · 2019-04-03 17:25 UTC

@Steve Howell In alignment with what Tim said, I believe this is initiated in ReactionDict, and has existed in broadly that form since 2016.

**Steve Howell** · 2019-04-03 18:03 UTC

Interesting, yeah the commit there is 61d2297c17865fd4559fc4e6594b3ed607c49649, which was in Dec 2016 (a month after the commit I mentioned earlier).  It's a shame we weren't consistent there.

**Neil Pilgrim (neiljp)** · 2019-04-03 18:06 UTC

I imagine we want to update the `notify_reaction_update` to add `id` to improve things, and remove `user_id` in a future version?

**Steve Howell** · 2019-04-03 18:12 UTC

The long term goal for both of these is probably to just have `user_id` and do away with the `user` struct (since apps should have email/name for users).  Theoretically, we need to worry about backward compatibility for API users, although I seriously doubt there are any mission-critical API applications in the world that pull reactions from messages.

**Steve Howell** · 2019-04-03 18:13 UTC

I'm mostly inclined to do nothing here.  It mainly affects the three major apps, and we can all work around it with something like:

~~~
user_id = foo['user'].get('id') or foo['user'].get('user_id')

**Steve Howell** · 2019-04-03 18:15 UTC

I just looked the webapp code, and there we have two separate codepaths--one for pulling them out of messages, and one for handling events.  And then internally we have a different data structure then what comes over the wire, so after the initial code in both places that handles the payloads, everything is consistent after that.

**Neil Pilgrim (neiljp)** · 2019-04-03 18:15 UTC

I imagine it could be useful for non-app uses of the API, perhaps. There's a fix in ZT coming in, and we'll have to maintain that, but I wanted to clarify the issue and find out what might change, so let's see what happens :)

**Steve Howell** · 2019-04-03 18:22 UTC

Feel free to open an issue on the server for this.  Just make it's clear that we haven't fully decided anything, and you'll want to link back to the conversation.

**Steve Howell** · 2019-04-03 18:24 UTC

Long term, we should really just send `user_id` in both places.  We want to reduce bandwidth when possible, and we also eventually want to support orgs that don't want emails to be visible to users (even in payloads and events).  Of course, that's still a long project, but that's the endgame.

**Neil Pilgrim (neiljp)** · 2019-04-03 18:49 UTC

Reported as #12049. Please clarify if I've misrepresented anything.

**Steve Howell** · 2019-04-03 18:58 UTC

@Neil Pilgrim Looks great.  Thanks for opening the issue!

**Neil Pilgrim (neiljp)** · 2019-04-03 18:59 UTC

Glad to have it finalized (at least as an issue) after noticing it from last year! :)

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-04-11 00:56 UTC

@Greg Price @Boris Yankov I'd be interested in the mobile team's perspective on #12049, which has a clear description of this API irregularity.    I'm happy to resolve this whatever way.

**Tim Abbott** · 2018-11-26 20:20 UTC

@Akash Nimare there are a few different types of proxies.  We're mostly interested in different types of "forward proxies" discussed in https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Proxy_servers_and_tunneling.  If you google around, there's a ton of free open proxy services that you can proxy your traffic through; the tricky part for testing this sort of thing is that generally nothing will fail by default if the code is skipping the proxy and accidentally using your computer's existing Internet connection (which probably works fine).

**Tim Abbott** · 2018-11-26 20:21 UTC

Tools like https://www.telerik.com/fiddler can help, in that they'll log all the network requests, and you can compare that against the app's browser console.

With this `nginx` config:
```
server {

}

```

/home/zulipdev/zulip/scripts/setup/setup-certbot \                                                                                          
  --hostname=hostname.example.com --no-zulip-conf \                                                                                         
  --email=username@example.com --method=standalone                                                                                          
```

but of course any valid cert correctly setup for `nginx` at the provided paths is fine.

**Tim Abbott** · 2018-12-10 06:15 UTC

@Neil Pilgrim so, I think the problem here is your manual upgrading/downgrading; the Zulip provisioning process creates requirements.txt-hash named virtualenvs and installs the things in the requirements files there, but if you manually upgrade/downgrade packages while inside that virtualenv, you effectively end up corrupting that cache.

**Tim Abbott** · 2018-12-10 06:16 UTC

https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/subsystems/dependencies.html explains how this works, but maybe we should add a paragraph there warning that if you do manual edits, you should `rm -rf /srv/zulip-venv-cache/` before re-provisioning to be sure you have a clean state?

**Neil Pilgrim (neiljp)** · 2018-12-10 06:26 UTC

@Tim Abbott Wouldn't it be cleaner to have a `tools/provision --from-clean` option or similar?

**Tim Abbott** · 2018-12-10 06:39 UTC

Potentially, yeah.  Feel free to open an issue; it probably needs to do at least:
* Removing cache stamp files from under `var/`
* Removing the cache directories from `/srv/`

## Weird import

*2018-12-15 to 2018-12-23 · 14 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/Weird.20import/with/672268)*

**Shubham Padia** · 2018-12-15 21:11 UTC

At https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/master/scripts/lib/zulip_tools.py#L19 L19, the classes for mypy type annotations are imported as follows, which is unusual. Also a thing to note that these imported classes can only be used when the annotation is done in comments. The imports do not work on inline annotation like `def get_config_file() -> your_type_here`.
```python
if False:
    from typing import Sequence, Set, Any, Dict, List
```

I'd be grateful for any pointers on this or a link to the mypy-documentation page dealing with this.

**Tim Abbott** · 2018-12-15 22:20 UTC

@Shubham Padia yeah, the story here is that we need that for any scripts that might be run with Python 2, where those values aren't defined.

**Tim Abbott** · 2018-12-15 22:20 UTC

For a long time after we moved the main app to Python 3, we still supported Python 2 for some scripts, and that's why we have that pattern.

**Tim Abbott** · 2018-12-15 22:20 UTC

I suspect we could do some auditing for how we call individual scripts and migrate the places we're doing that to not do so, and just be a 100% Python 3 codebase.

**Shubham Padia** · 2018-12-15 22:31 UTC

Ah, cool. Thanks for the info :)

**Tim Abbott** · 2018-12-16 21:35 UTC

Oh, I remembered more precisely why we need these.

**Tim Abbott** · 2018-12-16 21:35 UTC

In Python 3.5, the `typing` module needs to be installed, and so `provision` and anything it runs before the virtualenv is setup needs this pattern.

**Tim Abbott** · 2018-12-16 21:35 UTC

We should probably put a comment with a link to a doc explaining this in all the places we're doing that.

**Tim Abbott** · 2018-12-17 19:49 UTC

@Shubham Padia following up on this, I added the series of mypy commits ending with a0da4f6d30750a4f778620d3be582b1e011938f7, which should both make clear what's going on here, and make it harder for folks to accidentally break it.  Thanks for bringing this up!

**Shubham Padia** · 2018-12-18 04:13 UTC

Cool, thanks @Tim Abbott

**Rein Zustand** · 2018-12-20 05:48 UTC

> In Python 3.5, the `typing` module needs to be installed, and so `provision` and anything it runs before the virtualenv is setup needs this pattern.
The  `typing` module needs to be installed only on 2.7 and 3.4. From 3.5 and later, the stdlib `typing` is usually preferred.

**Tim Abbott** · 2018-12-21 03:33 UTC

@Rein Zustand do you have a reference for 3.5 being the cutoff?

**Rein Zustand** · 2018-12-21 20:50 UTC

@Tim Abbott right, should have cited (I thought this is "common knowledge" and that I just have to remind): 

> NOTE: in Python 3.5 and later, the typing module lives in the stdlib, and installing this package has NO EFFECT. To get a newer version of the typing module in Python 3.5 or later, you have to upgrade to a newer Python (bugfix) version. For example, typing in Python 3.6.0 is missing the definition of ‘Type’ – upgrading to 3.6.2 will fix this.

> Also note that most improvements to the typing module in Python 3.7 will not be included in this package, since Python 3.7 has some built-in support that is not present in older versions (See PEP 560.)

ref: https://pypi.org/project/typing/

**Tim Abbott** · 2018-12-23 12:40 UTC

Great, OK, given that, @Rein Zustand we can change things to install the typing module only on 3.4.

**Steve Howell** · 2018-12-24 16:36 UTC

The Stripe library is most likely responsible for this:

~~~ python
/srv/zulip-py3-venv/lib/python3.5/site-packages/stripe$ find . -name '*.py' | xargs grep 'error_code='
./api_requestor.py:            error_code=error_data.get('code'),

~~~

**Steve Howell** · 2018-12-24 16:37 UTC

And they call their logger "stripe":

~~~
$ find . -name '*.py' | xargs grep 'logging'
./util.py:import logging
./util.py:logger = logging.getLogger('stripe')
./__init__.py:# Set to either 'debug' or 'info', controls console logging

**Steve Howell** · 2018-12-24 16:39 UTC

Here's more context on the code that looks relevant here (or it might be a similar call elsewhere):

~~~
122     def specific_api_error(self, rbody, rcode, resp, rheaders, error_data):
123         util.log_info(
124             'Stripe API error received',
125             error_code=error_data.get('code'),

127             error_message=error_data.get('message'),
128             error_param=error_data.get('param'),
129         )

## issue #10612: Improve email gateway

*2018-12-31 to 2019-01-02 · 5 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/issue.20.2310612.3A.20Improve.20email.20gateway/with/677482)*

**Mateusz Mandera** · 2018-12-31 15:17 UTC

Link to issue:  https://github.com/zulip/zulip/issues/10612
It says  "We use talon to remove automatic signatures and stuff.", but in the code, in zerver/lib/email_mirror.py I only see usage of "extract" from talon.quotations, which only attempts to remove quotations of older emails in the conversation. In that case, should use of talon.signatures be added to strip the additional stuff?

**Rishi Gupta** · 2019-01-01 13:40 UTC

@Mateusz Mandera yeah, that seems promising! Does talon have documentation on this we could read?

**Mateusz Mandera** · 2019-01-01 18:06 UTC

@Rishi Gupta not much, the README at https://github.com/mailgun/talon seems to be the "documentation". But basically, we have talon.quotations which removes quotations of older emails, and talon.signatures which tries to remove signatures - there is talon.signatures.bruteforce which uses very simple heuristics to attempt to identify the signature part of the email, and then the main module which does that using machine learning. it comes pre-trained using the data set from https://github.com/mailgun/forge . It isn't very effective though. I suppose one way of trying to fix the issue would be by making a different data set and training talon on it, such that it would be able to pick out the google groups unsubscribe footers and such? 

But machine learning is really not my area so I'm not sure how feasible it is or how much effort it would take.

**Mateusz Mandera** · 2019-01-01 19:25 UTC

Alternatively, we could  just add some custom regexes to search for in talon.signatures.bruteforce that would remove the footers produced by google groups emails. I don't know which is more appropriate.

Also, we already have a function filter_footer which tries to do this, but all it does is that in case there's just a single occurrence of the standard '--' line,  the rest of the message is assumed to be a footer and gets deleted. The issue with google groups email format is that there are multiple segments of the footer, separated by '--' so since there are multiple occurrences, the function just decides to do nothing. The simplest solution would to assume that emails will follow the standard that after the '--' tag there is no more useful content and just remove everything after it, at the risk of deleting some content if we have a message that doesn't abide by this rule.

So there are different possible approaches, all of them kind of hacky and each with their own tradeoffs, I'm not sure what the best choice is though.

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-01-02 03:26 UTC

@Mateusz Mandera we don't use any of talon's ML logic -- just the basic featureset to strip signatures that's rule-based.  I'm not super happy with the library overall, but I also don't have a great plan for how we can develop something similar without a lot of annoying iteration.

## checking which stream a message comes from

*2019-01-08 to 2019-01-08 · 8 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/checking.20which.20stream.20a.20message.20comes.20from/with/679934)*

**Mateusz Mandera** · 2019-01-08 15:21 UTC

I'm sorry if this is a silly question and I missed something obvious, but - given a Message type object, how can I get the stream from which it comes from (assuming that it is a stream message of course)? I'm writing a test in which I want to check whether a message was posted to the correct stream.

**Steve Howell** · 2019-01-08 15:27 UTC

You can get the stream id from `message.recipient.type_id`.

**Steve Howell** · 2019-01-08 15:28 UTC

And if you're starting with a stream name, you get stream id as follows:

~~~ python
stream_id = get_stream(stream_name, self.user_profile.realm).id
~~~

**Steve Howell** · 2019-01-08 15:34 UTC

It might make sense for us to create a helper in `zerver/lib/test_classes.py` that looks something like this:

~~~ python
    def assert_message_stream(self, message, stream_name):
        stream_id = get_stream(stream_name, message.sender.realm).id
        self.assertEqual(message.recipient.type, Recipient.STREAM)
        self.assertEqual(message.recipient.type_id, stream_id)

~~~

**Mateusz Mandera** · 2019-01-08 15:54 UTC

ohhh, that's very useful, thank you. that's not necessary right now, but how could we get the Stream object from stream_id?

**Steve Howell** · 2019-01-08 16:01 UTC

That's what `get_stream` does.  (We have a helper function for that due to the fact that we cache stream objects.  In tests you can also look directly at the DB with `Stream.objects.get(id=stream_id)`.)

**Mateusz Mandera** · 2019-01-08 16:02 UTC

ohh, i see now, thank you

**Steve Howell** · 2019-01-08 16:08 UTC

:thumbs_up:

## understanding regex for alert_words

*2019-01-14 to 2019-01-14 · 26 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/understanding.20regex.20for.20alert_words/with/681634)*

**Bennet Sunder** · 2019-01-14 07:26 UTC

I was going through the logic for looking for alert_words in the content of the message. 
If the alert word is (hello) 
the match returns true for >(hello)
the match returns false for > >(hello)
the match returns true for (hello)]
the match returns true for (hello)]]
So is the regex logic like the character preceding the start of the alert_word in the content should be either **exactly** a space, start of sentence or one of the before_punctuations? while the text after the alert_word can be pretty much anything ?
I was trying out in https://www.debuggex.com/r/CussiQBINqQCMm5H

**Steve Howell** · 2019-01-14 15:39 UTC

@Bennet Sunder Here is the relevant code:

~~~ python
1572             allowed_before_punctuation = "|".join([r'\s', '^', r'[\(\".,\';\[\*`>]'])
1573             allowed_after_punctuation = "|".join([r'\s', '$', r'[\)\"\?:.,\';\]!\*`]'])
1574
1575             for word in realm_words:
1576                 escaped = re.escape(word.lower())
1577                 match_re = re.compile('(?:%s)%s(?:%s)' %
1578                                       (allowed_before_punctuation,
1579                                        escaped,
1580                                        allowed_after_punctuation))
1581                 if re.search(match_re, content):
1582                     self.markdown.zulip_message.alert_words.add(word)

~~~

**Bennet Sunder** · 2019-01-14 15:41 UTC

@Steve Howell  Thanks, that is the code i was looking at. I think i got misled by the online regex  compiler I'll run it directly on the python interpreter and try to see how it works.

**Steve Howell** · 2019-01-14 15:55 UTC

@Bennet Sunder Sounds good.  If you find any interesting quirks, it should be relatively simple to at least update our test suite with more examples.  (It may be harder to actually fix stuff--things like forcing balanced parens can get tricky, but it may not really be a big deal in practice.)

**Bennet Sunder** · 2019-01-14 16:32 UTC

@Steve Howell I'll look into adding more test cases. However, Is having matching tags around a particular word expected for this?

**Steve Howell** · 2019-01-14 16:37 UTC

I think there's an argument that our current liberal behavior (i.e. don't enforce matching parens) is appropriate here.

**Steve Howell** · 2019-01-14 16:38 UTC

If your alert word is red, I think it should show up for you for strange punctuation like `"red'`, where it might just be a typo.  As long as we prevent obvious false positives like "shared" or "redact".

**Bennet Sunder** · 2019-01-14 16:42 UTC

although It will show up for "ha'red" too

**Bennet Sunder** · 2019-01-14 16:45 UTC

that is it will show up if the alert_word is surrounded by allowed punctuation even when it is a substring of a larger string

**Steve Howell** · 2019-01-14 16:50 UTC

Yeah, those edge cases are a bit tricky.  I'd want "light-red" to alert me, but not "ha'red".

**Bennet Sunder** · 2019-01-14 16:54 UTC

"light-red" is an interesting example. although "ha'red" is more likely a typo

**Steve Howell** · 2019-01-14 16:56 UTC

Yeah.  It's hard to get too fussy about alert words--for these edge cases, it's often the case that making it better for Alice makes it worse for Bob, as they may have different tolerances for false alarms.

**Steve Howell** · 2019-01-14 16:58 UTC

Having said that, I don't think we've done much fine tuning here, so if there are compelling use cases that we can make better, it's worth doing, as long as there's not a huge performance hit (unlikely unless you just have a crazy regex).

**Steve Howell** · 2019-01-14 16:59 UTC

It's worth mentioning that a lot of core developers use English, which has no accents, so we're probably not as aware of issues in other spoken languages.

**Bennet Sunder** · 2019-01-14 17:06 UTC

Yes you're right. getting similar alert_word detection across multiple language where the usage of - or other might change is pretty tough

**Steve Howell** · 2019-01-14 17:07 UTC

Indeed.

**Steve Howell** · 2019-01-14 17:09 UTC

Over the years we haven't gotten a ton of feedback on alert words.  I have several theories to explain this, none of them necessarily valid but all somewhat plausible, I think:
* lots of people don't know about the feature
* some people are just happy with how it is
* some people gave up on it and never reported bugs to us
* most users work with languages somewhat similar to English in terms of punctuation/spacing
* people set up conventions carefully for using alert words

**Bennet Sunder** · 2019-01-14 17:10 UTC

So even if we were to implement the matching parenthesis the only benefit we'd get is the alert words with typos would not be detected `get_rgb("red') ` will not be while`get_rgb("red") ` will be

**Steve Howell** · 2019-01-14 17:10 UTC

One use case for alert words is going slowly away, which is notifying a group of people.  People who wanted to notify `support` used to have a workaround of setting alert words, but now you can manage that with user groups.

**Steve Howell** · 2019-01-14 17:11 UTC

> So even if we were to implement the matching parenthesis the only benefit we'd get is the alert words with typos would not be detected `get_rgb("red') ` will not be while`get_rgb("red") ` will be
 
Yep.  Which might not only be a misfeature (at least for some users), but also would probably make the code a bit more complex and slow.

**Bennet Sunder** · 2019-01-14 17:22 UTC

Yes, but isn't user groups, mentions and alert words different from a feature perspective. user groups is when a sender of a message wishes to notify a group of people. While alert words is more like when you as a reader wants notification on a word or a phrase when ever senders send message independently

**Bennet Sunder** · 2019-01-14 17:23 UTC

like if i had set up @Steve Howell  as a alert_word i'd get a notification every time someone mentioned you in a message

**Bennet Sunder** · 2019-01-14 17:25 UTC

`@Steve Howell ` as an alert_word I mean

**Rishi Gupta** · 2019-01-14 17:30 UTC

it is, but before we had user groups peolpe would use alert words as a convention. E.g. everyone on the support team would add `@support` as an alert word, everyone on the marketing team would add `@marketing` as an alert word, etc.

**Steve Howell** · 2019-01-14 17:34 UTC

Just to echo what @Rishi Gupta said, I'm aware that alert words and user groups are different features--it's just that before we had user groups, people would do alert-word related hacks.  There are still plenty of use cases for alert words; I just meant one fairly common use case is becoming less relevant over time.

**Bennet Sunder** · 2019-01-14 17:35 UTC

ah got it. Thanks for the info @Steve Howell  and @Rishi Gupta  I didn't really know the history behind it. It makes sense now

This is the relevant code:
```python3
def build_email(template_prefix: str, to_user_ids: Optional[List[int]]=None,
                to_emails: Optional[List[str]]=None, from_name: Optional[str]=None,
                from_address: Optional[str]=None, reply_to_email: Optional[str]=None,
                language: Optional[str]=None, context: Optional[Dict[str, Any]]=None
                ) -> List[EmailMultiAlternatives]:
    # Callers should pass exactly one of to_user_id and to_email.
    assert (to_user_ids is None) ^ (to_emails is None)
    if to_user_ids is not None:
        to_users = [get_user_profile_by_id(to_user_id) for to_user_id in to_user_ids]
        # Change to formataddr((to_user.full_name, to_user.email)) once
        # https://github.com/zulip/zulip/issues/4676 is resolved
        to_emails = [to_user.delivery_email for to_user in to_users]

    public_keys = {}  # type: Dict[str, str]
    want_signature = {}  # type: Dict[str, bool]
    for to_email in to_emails: # MYPY ERROR HERE
        public_keys[to_email] = ''
        want_signature[to_email] = False
```

Mypy is throwing "error: Item "None" of "Optional[List[str]]" has no attribute "__iter__" (not iterable)". I understand its concern, to_emails is Optional, so it thinks it could be none, so we cannot iterate. But the code above the "problematic" for loop guarantees that to_emails is no longer None, so we certainly can iterate. What's a good way of placifying mypy here?

**Mateusz Mandera** · 2019-01-18 16:25 UTC

Okay never mind, I solved it using defaultdict from collections modules and replacing the ugly stuff at the bottom with
```python3
    public_keys = defaultdict(str)  # type: DefaultDict[str, str]
    want_signature = defaultdict(bool)  # type: DefaultDict[str, bool]
```

Still, seems interesting how to deal with this kind of mypy error in other situations, where we really would need to iterate over the "Optional"-type item that's guaranteed to not be None any more at the point of doing the iteration.

    if to_user_ids is not None:
        for to_user in to_users:
            if settings.ENABLE_EMAIL_ENCRYPTION and to_user.want_encrypted_emails:
                try:
                    user_pgp = UserPgp.objects.get(user_profile_id=to_user.id)
                    public_keys[to_user.delivery_email] = user_pgp.public_key
                except UserProfile.DoesNotExist:  # Should never happen
                    logger.error('User (id %s) has want_encrypted_emails=True, '
                                 'but no public key in the database' % (to_user.id))
            if settings.ENABLE_EMAIL_SIGNATURES and to_user.want_signed_emails:
                want_signature[to_user.delivery_email] = True

    # ... render templates and prepare a EmailMultiAlternatives object (mail)

    return pgp_sign_and_encrypt(mail, public_keys, want_signature)
```

I know 'heartbeat' is an exception (exploring this in #T276 in ZT), but I wasn't sure if otherwise 'x in event_types => expect might receive x event type'... and no other types of events. I'm not missing an obvious 'potential_event_types' or equivalent key in the `register` response dict, am I?

**Steve Howell** · 2019-01-23 21:43 UTC

@Neil Pilgrim If I understand your question correctly, no, you should not have the app complain about unexpected events.  The server may add more events at any time, and if ZT silently ignores them, it's usually fine (just means you're not live updating stuff for features that might not even pertain to ZT yet).

**Neil Pilgrim (neiljp)** · 2019-01-23 23:27 UTC

Oh sure, but if `register` is called with `event_types` then it should only be *expected* to handle those types? I get the point of ignoring unknown ones, that's... expected ;)

**Neil Pilgrim (neiljp)** · 2019-01-23 23:30 UTC

I was hoping it would be reasonable if the register response included an entry listing events that could be expected. That might be the requested types, but also extras like heartbeat.

**Steve Howell** · 2019-01-23 23:35 UTC

That might not be too hard to do.  Although I am not sure how much value it would really have.

**Neil Pilgrim (neiljp)** · 2019-01-24 02:58 UTC

Well, registration with no types would provide a full list of events, rather than needing to just wait for if a given event shows up. Plus if an event type was unsupported it wouldn't show up in the 'will_receive_events` list back from the server.
Could it actually be used for incremental feature checking, a bit like has been discussed recently (stream ids in 1.9+?)

**Steve Howell** · 2019-01-24 03:03 UTC

I think things are slightly asymmetrical.

**Steve Howell** · 2019-01-24 03:05 UTC

There’s only one server, so we can do a lot by just having the server advertise its version number to test capabilities.

**Steve Howell** · 2019-01-24 03:06 UTC

The bigger problem is that we have a myriad of clients, which are all limited in different ways.

**Steve Howell** · 2019-01-24 03:06 UTC

So the biggest problem is the server needs to know how modern the clients are.

**Steve Howell** · 2019-01-24 03:07 UTC

But yeah I see your point.

**Steve Howell** · 2019-01-24 03:09 UTC

We need lots more metadata from the clients than the server, but in both directions it’s a tricky balance how to advertise capabilities.

+                    {{recipients}}
+                </a>
+                <div class="private_message_count {{#if is_zero}}zero_count{{/if}}">
+                    <div class="value">{{unread}}</div>
+                </div>
+            </span>
+            <span class="arrow topic-sidebar-arrow">
+                <i class="fa fa-chevron-down" aria-hidden="true"></i>
+            </span>
+        </li>
+        {{/each}}
+        {{#if want_show_more_messages_links}}
+        <li class="show-more-private-messages" data-name='more-private-messages'>
+            <a href="#">({{t "more conversations" }})</a>
+        </li>
+        {{/if}}
+    </ul>
+</div>

**Steve Howell** · 2019-01-30 16:04 UTC

The only real subtlety there is that when you call `remove()`, it's now going to be `$(".private_messages_container").remove();`.

Hello @Tim Abbott,  I was playing around with issue #11220 and may have a tentative solution.  If I have an issue assigned and  a PR has been opened for it, is the best practice to stay with only that issue until a final status has been determined?  Or, is it acceptable to comment on GitHub that the issue has migrated to the PR and remove the assignment? Or, just stick to the ```help wanted``` / ```good first issue``` tags?  Thanks

**Steve Howell** · 2019-01-28 21:23 UTC

@Wyatt Hoodes You can keep yourself assigned to it, but I would update the issue with comments to the effect of what you just said.

**Steve Howell** · 2019-01-28 21:24 UTC

How confident are you in your tentative solution?  If you're 80% confident that your approach is correct, I would try to take it to the finish line.

**Steve Howell** · 2019-01-28 21:26 UTC

We use the convention "[wip] Fix something" in PRs, where wip == work in progress.

**Steve Howell** · 2019-01-28 21:27 UTC

This prevents Tim from wasting time reviewing something that is only partially complete, while making it easy for other folks to do preliminary reviews, help with testing, or help you troubleshoot problems.

**Wyatt Hoodes** · 2019-01-28 21:32 UTC

> This prevents Tim from wasting time reviewing something that is only partially complete, while making it easy for other folks to do preliminary reviews, help with testing, or help you troubleshoot problems.

**Wyatt Hoodes** · 2019-01-28 21:38 UTC

**Steve Howell** · 2019-01-28 21:40 UTC

> If I can't claim more than one issue as a new contributor, how should I go about working on another while a previous working issue is a [WIP]? This would be my more general question.
 
Oh, you can unassign yourself from the other issue as long as it's clear that you have the PR pending.

Also, if you see me, Tim, or Rishi online, we can often override the restriction and assign you to a second issue.

**Wyatt Hoodes** · 2019-01-28 21:41 UTC

Awesome, thank you!

**Steve Howell** · 2019-01-28 21:41 UTC

Another thing that's worthwhile is to spend some time reading docs while your first issue is being reviewed.  And it's often not the end of the world if you start on an issue, and somebody else grabs it--it can allow you to compare notes with the other person.

If I have an issue assigned and a PR has been opened for it, is the best practice to stay with only that issue until a final status has been determined? @Wyatt Hoodes our restrictions against claiming multiple issues (etc.) are primarily for folks who don't have any commits merged yet, basically to help prevent folks who don't have the skills to contribute from accidentally DoSing the project by claiming several issues that they're not able to work on (this used to happen a lot).

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-02-02 02:25 UTC

@Wyatt Hoodes yeah, so the realms created by `populate_db` in the development environment are a bit funny.

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-02-02 02:25 UTC

(This actually would be a totally reasonable follow-up project to fix)

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-02-02 02:25 UTC

Basically, they're not created through the actual Zulip signup flow, but instead via the `populate_db` tool

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-02-02 02:25 UTC

And that tool does some clever optimizations to make the setup process a lot faster

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-02-02 02:26 UTC

But with the side effect of violating some invariants that are true for any real Zulip organization

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-02-02 02:26 UTC

So in particular, it sounds like that stream is miscreated in `populate_db` (or probably `populate_analytics_db` with 0 subscribers)

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-02-02 02:26 UTC

The right fix is likely to modify `populate_analytics_db` to subscribe a user to that stream.

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-02-02 02:27 UTC

Probably worth just fixing that (and any similar issues, though it'll probably just be this one) for your testing; it'll be about as much work as working around this.

Hey @Wyatt Hoodes  @Tim Abbott  sorry for the delayed reply
So I don't think I ended up coding anything from the recent discussions Tim and I had.

Basically to explain what was the idea at the time of PR #8961:
I was basically introducing a new category of bots called the SYSTEM BOTS which would be assigned to zulip's internal bots. These bots would have a copy inside every realm. Now this is totally different from what happens in production where all the bots live inside a different realm from actual org realms. This realm is called Zulip. From the given PR what I was trying to achieve was targeted towards the use case of a users ability to message a bot which could be useful for the reminders feature.
Untended effects of system bots appearing in bot lists and typeaheads in some places where it didn't make sense for them to be present would have been handled using selective exclusions.

Now the idea which we are pursuing over here (in this topic) is to bridge the gap between development and production environment is a bit different. Here we just want the following:
* our system bots to live in a different realm for the development environment as they do for the production. In production system bots are part of the realm called zulip.
* This realm where our system bots live should be called zulipinternal since the name makes more sense. This means the new realm which we use to create the bots in populate_db could straight away be called zulipinternal. For production systems we will need to rename the realm somehow (zulip -> zulipinternal) .

Now what I see is that there are two overlapping tasks or ideas which we must try to achieve and it feels like having more discussion about this topic and the tasks could clear up things a bit more and probably save us from work.

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-02-08 17:48 UTC

My view is the right path forward is to do the following commit series:
* Migrate the codebase to use the variable `SYSTEM_BOT_REALM` in places where we we mean that rather than hardcoding `'zulip'`.  This should involve changing like 1% of the lines where we interact with `zulip` in our tests (etc.).  We'll probably discover these places through trying the next steps, though.
* Change `SYSTEM_BOT_REALM` in the development environment to be `zulipinternal` via `zproject/dev_settings.py`, and have the system bots for that realm be created by `populate_db` calling the same code as `zerver/management/commands/initialize_voyager_db` (i.e. what we use in production).  This will make a bunch of tests that interact with the number of bots in the organization fail; we will eventually need to change those tests.  But to simplify this big cutover change, I think it'd be wise for this commit to have a transitional state where we add the right number of generic bots to `populate_db` to replace the moved system bots, so that the default realm has the same number of bots + users as before this commit.
* We can figure out the following steps from there.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2019-02-08 01:32 UTC

Testing this fix:
```diff
--- a/tools/lib/provision.py
+++ b/tools/lib/provision.py
@@ -398,6 +398,9 @@ def main(options):
     setup_shell_profile('~/.bash_profile')
     setup_shell_profile('~/.zprofile')
 
+    # This needs to happen before anything that imports zproject.settings.
+    run(["scripts/setup/generate_secrets.py", "--development"])
+
     run(["sudo", "cp", REPO_STOPWORDS_PATH, TSEARCH_STOPWORDS_PATH])
 
     # create log directory `zulip/var/log`
@@ -437,8 +440,6 @@ def main(options):
     else:
         print("No need to run `tools/setup/build_pygments_data`.")
 
-    run(["scripts/setup/generate_secrets.py", "--development"])
-
     update_authors_json_paths = ["tools/update-authors-json", "zerver/tests/fixtures/authors.json"]
     if file_or_package_hash_updated(update_authors_json_paths, "update_authors_json_hash", options.is_force):
         run(["tools/update-authors-json", "--use-fixture"])
```

**Rishi Gupta** · 2019-02-08 00:18 UTC

**Steve Howell** · 2019-02-08 00:22 UTC

borders go outside the element...which is SUPER annoying

**Steve Howell** · 2019-02-08 00:23 UTC

Some one more pro in CSS may have a better way to do it.

**Steve Howell** · 2019-02-08 00:23 UTC

On a related note, I plan to write a good rant about padding and margin tomorrow.

**Steve Howell** · 2019-02-08 00:25 UTC

I kinda want to write it now, but I'm too fired up, haha.

**Steve Howell** · 2019-02-08 00:30 UTC

> borders go outside the element...which is SUPER annoying
 
(which increases the overall size of the element and throws off positioning of nearby elements)

**Steve Howell** · 2019-02-08 00:32 UTC

@Rishi Gupta What probably is happening here is that it's actually the element below that has the border, and you're using the top element's bottom border to overwrite the bottom element's top border, and because borders go outside the element, you need the `-1` hack.  Does that make sense?

**Rishi Gupta** · 2019-02-08 00:33 UTC

ah, I guess the -1 drops the element down, so that it's border can cover the thing below it

**Steve Howell** · 2019-02-08 00:33 UTC

it pushes it up, actually, I think

**Steve Howell** · 2019-02-08 00:33 UTC

but yeah, that's the idea

**Steve Howell** · 2019-02-08 00:35 UTC

If the top element's bottom was at y-coord 13, the border would be at y-coord 14, but then -1 changes the bottom to y-coord 12 and puts the border at y-coord 13.  (where y-coords are relative to the top of the screen, despite what you learned in high school)

This is a pretty challenging issue.  Not only do you need to backfill data in the migration, but you also need to handle the case of the first message being sent to a stream.  Basically, every time we get a new message, we have to see if it's the first message on a stream, and then we need to update the database accordingly.  And this will probably add an additional query to the send-message codepath, which will require fixing a couple tests.

* Maybe other things -- would google around a bit as we're mostly using the stock Django test runner.

* Moving to bottom

If we're talking about missed message emails, don't we already do something like this? We have:
```python
def create_missed_message_address(user_profile: UserProfile, message: Message) -> str:
    if settings.EMAIL_GATEWAY_PATTERN == '':
        logger.warning("EMAIL_GATEWAY_PATTERN is an empty string, using "
                       "NOREPLY_EMAIL_ADDRESS in the 'from' field.")
        return FromAddress.NOREPLY

    if message.recipient.type == Recipient.PERSONAL:
        # We need to reply to the sender so look up their personal recipient_id
        recipient_id = get_personal_recipient(message.sender_id).id
    else:
        recipient_id = message.recipient_id

    data = {
        'user_profile_id': user_profile.id,
        'recipient_id': recipient_id,
        'subject': message.topic_name().encode('utf-8'),
    }

    while True:
        token = generate_random_token(32)
        key = missed_message_redis_key(token)
        if redis_client.hsetnx(key, 'uses_left', 1):
            break

    with redis_client.pipeline() as pipeline:
        pipeline.hmset(key, data)
        pipeline.expire(key, 60 * 60 * 24 * 5)
        pipeline.execute()

    address = 'mm' + token
    return settings.EMAIL_GATEWAY_PATTERN % (address,)
```

which seems to create a one-time use address? In process_missed_message we do `` mark_missed_message_address_as_used(to) ``, which does:

def mark_missed_message_address_as_used(address: str) -> None:
    token = get_missed_message_token_from_address(address)
    key = missed_message_redis_key(token)
    with redis_client.pipeline() as pipeline:
        pipeline.hincrby(key, 'uses_left', -1)
        pipeline.expire(key, 60 * 60 * 24 * 5)
        new_value = pipeline.execute()[0]
    if new_value < 0:
        redis_client.delete(key)
        raise ZulipEmailForwardError('Missed message address has already been used')
```

        // so it is seen as the next token.
        space = item.length;// takes the length of the string
        item = item.replace(/^ *([*+-]|\d+\.) +/, '');// replaces the bullet(i.e. * with '')
        // Outdent whatever the
        // list item contains. Hacky.
        if (~item.indexOf('\n ')) {//check whether \n_ is present in the item or not
          space -= item.length;//space is length of original string - replaced string
          item = !this.options.pedantic
            ? item.replace(new RegExp('^ {2,' + space + '}', 'gm'), '')
            : item.replace(/^ {1,4}/gm, '');
        }
```

**Wyatt Hoodes** · 2019-03-08 08:02 UTC

I played around with typeaheads a little  today.  From what I've read, simply adding:
```
minLength: 0,
hint: true,
```
To the following block should produce the desired results:

```javascript
    $("#stream_message_recipient_stream").typeahead({
        source: function () {
            return stream_data.subscribed_streams();
        },
        items: 3,
        fixed: true,
        highlighter: function (item) {
            return typeahead_helper.render_typeahead_item({ primary: item });
        },
        matcher: function (item) {
            // The matcher for "stream" is strictly prefix-based,
            // because we want to avoid mixing up streams.
            var q = this.query.trim().toLowerCase();
            return item.toLowerCase().indexOf(q) === 0;
        },
    });
```
I've tried some variations here, along with trying to manually trigger the typeahead to no avail.  I'd appreciate any insight here :slight_smile:

**Wyatt Hoodes** · 2019-03-08 17:19 UTC

I'm sorry, I should have stated the desired result as opening the typeahead with 0 characters.

**Steve Howell** · 2019-03-08 18:25 UTC

@Rishi Gupta Is the trigger here supposed to be that the element gains focus?

**Steve Howell** · 2019-03-08 18:28 UTC

I'm not a fan of this proposal, to be honest.  We limit the stream typeahead to 3 items.  You can type space to trigger the first 3 already.  I think we just need to be more aggressive about matching characters in situations where you don't find prefix matches.

**Rishi Gupta** · 2019-03-08 18:31 UTC

yup, when the element gains focus. The issue is that:
* you're a new user
* you don't know what a stream is
* If you don't happen to type a letter that matches one of the 2 existing streams for new realms (general and core team), you're stuck

**Rishi Gupta** · 2019-03-08 18:33 UTC

but more philosophically, for situations where you're picking from a list, it makes sense to open the typeahead/dropdown/etc right away, so the user immediately knows that's what's going on

**Rishi Gupta** · 2019-03-08 18:33 UTC

the reason we don't do it in the compose box is only because we aren't sure if they really do mean to type a stream when they type `#`

**Steve Howell** · 2019-03-08 18:45 UTC

Do we want to show more than three streams?

**Steve Howell** · 2019-03-08 18:49 UTC

Can you say what's happening before they get to stream in your use case?  Are they coming from "new topic" button generally?

**Rishi Gupta** · 2019-03-08 18:50 UTC

coming from "New stream message" button, from PMs (which is the place we dump you when you first register)

**Rishi Gupta** · 2019-03-08 18:51 UTC

**Steve Howell** · 2019-03-08 18:51 UTC

Instead of typeahead hack, why don't we just have that pop a modal?  So that you can actually search for streams?  And then once you select one, we can advance the cursor to topic.

**Rishi Gupta** · 2019-03-08 18:51 UTC

why modal instead of typeahead with more options?

**Steve Howell** · 2019-03-08 18:51 UTC

because it's not gross

**Rishi Gupta** · 2019-03-08 18:52 UTC
