**Rishi Gupta** · 2019-03-08 18:52 UTC

but really this issue was meant to be a quick fix

A modal is still better.

**Steve Howell** · 2019-03-08 18:53 UTC

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-03-14 20:07 UTC

@Paras Lakhani as discussed in our guidelines, we generally don't pick out issues for GSoC projects until about a week before the GSoC application deadline, and only do so for established contributors.

**Steve Howell** · 2019-03-15 16:00 UTC

> @Vinit Singh we can say rust people use Zulip!

**Steve Howell** · 2019-03-15 16:02 UTC

**Steve Howell** · 2019-03-15 16:24 UTC

My advice to contributors is that if you see two issues that are equally interesting to you, but one of them is also from the Rust community, then it's a good tie-breaker.  And no matter which issue you choose (Rust or otherwise), you want to make sure it's something that has good tradeoffs in terms of how easy it is to implement, how valuable it will be to the entire Zulip community, etc.

## memcached rabbitmq

*2019-03-18 to 2019-03-18 · 7 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/memcached.20rabbitmq/with/720593)*

**Vishnu KS** · 2019-03-18 17:56 UTC

I was wondering whether its possible to replace Memcached and Rabbimq in Zulip with Redis? Also would it reduce our memory requirements?

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-03-18 18:32 UTC

People ask about this often; we should potentially have an FAQ entry about it.  First, it would not reduce our memory requirements materially, because only memcached of those 3 uses significant memory (and if we changed the backing technology, whatever we replaced it with would use that cache size).

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-03-18 18:33 UTC

Second, we use redis for some purposes that require medium-term persistence, and run it in a configuration consistent with that purpose.  Whereas we use memcached in a mode where it's totally fine if all its data is lost, and run it in a configuration consistent with that purpose.  We could replace memcached with another redis process, but last I checked, redis doesn't support handling different keys with different persistence strategies.

**Vishnu KS** · 2019-03-18 18:41 UTC

hmm. I guess its the same case with RabbiMq as well. (ie we might not get any performance improvement that justifies the time and energy spend on changing). I can create a PR for adding what you wrote in docs.

**Vaibhav Rabber** · 2019-03-22 19:59 UTC

@Vinit Singh and I have been discussing this and there's a problem that we're facing.

The thing is -- after the introduction of the popover, there will be more than one ways we have to handle the copying event. These are:
* `Ctrl + C`
* Clicking on `copy selected text`
* Clicking on `copy complete message`

Right now we simply do this in `copy_and_paste.js`:
```javascript
$(document).on('copy', copy_handler);
```
I am not able to figure out a way in which I can know what "triggered" the copy event, whether it was the click or the normal copy.

What I thought was when clicking on a button to copy complete message, we could pass custom parameters like this:

```javascript
$(document).trigger({
  type: 'copy',
  triggered_by: 'copy_complete_message',
});
```

and then add an `if` statement where the "on copy" handler exists. The problem is just triggering the "copy" event does not actually seem to execute the "copying".
We cannot add `execCommand` there because then it will fire the default copy event and the thing we've been avoiding all this time will take place.

So at last what I thought was using `event.clipboardData.setData` rather than manipulating the selection for the browser to copy the content. I'm not sure though how good this is to use.

---

On another hand, this is the alternative I thought of. There are four cases we have right now on clicking either button in the popover:
1. single message && copy selected text -- :check: using simply `execCommand('copy')`
1. multiple messages && copy complete messages -- :check: again
1. single message && copy complete message -- simply by changing selection to complete message it becomes the same case as the first one
1. multiple messages && copy selected text -- this is the only part that's bugging now

**Steve Howell** · 2019-03-26 14:33 UTC

The main context here is that we a get a list of unread counts from the server with message ids, but we don't get the full messages.  So then the client ends up knowing about some topics for which there aren't any actual messages.  I don't remember much beyond that, but there are probably situations where we need to treat those topics a bit differently.

**Steve Howell** · 2019-03-26 14:37 UTC

We probably just need to filter out topics inside of this code in `unread.js`:

~~~ js
328         topic_names = _.reject(topic_names, function (topic_name) {
329             return topic_dict.has(topic_name);
330         });
331
332         var result = _.map(topic_names, function (topic_name) {
333             var msgs = per_stream_bucketer.get_bucket(topic_name);
334
335             return {
336                 pretty_name: topic_name,
337                 message_id: msgs.max(),
338             };
339         });

~~~

**Steve Howell** · 2019-04-02 17:06 UTC

@Lino Lemmer That sounds like an issue with access rights, although in most cases generic bots have access to any streams that the owner is subscribed to.  Just to be clear, were the messages from a stream?  (If they were in PMs, that would maybe explain the bot not seeing them.)

Can you give more details on how you make the call here?

{
    "msg": "",
    "found_newest": true,
    "anchor": 1334130,
    "history_limited": false,
    "result": "success",
    "found_anchor": false,
    "found_oldest": true,
    "messages": []
}

**Lino Lemmer** · 2019-04-03 07:36 UTC

OK, now I'm feeling stupid. It actually is the access right thing. Adding the bot to the stream solves the problem. It is strange behavour, though. Without access to the stream the bot can post, but not read. Why "result" is "success" is also kind of misleading.
Anyway: Thanks for your time and help!

**Steve Howell** · 2019-04-03 16:31 UTC

Interesting.  So in `validate_sender_can_write_to_stream`, there's clearly logic where the bot can send to any stream that its owner is subscribed to:

~~~ python
2166     if sender.is_bot and (sender.bot_owner is not None and
2167                           subscribed_to_stream(sender.bot_owner, stream.id)):
2168         # Bots can send to any stream their owner can.
2169         return

~~~

**Steve Howell** · 2019-04-03 16:35 UTC

But in `access_stream_common` we do **not** have any similar code for bots getting permissions their bot owner.  @Tim Abbott Do we intentionally require bots to subscribe to streams in order to read data?  (For typical chat bots, this is often a non-issue, since users typically at-mention the bots, and the server then directs messages to the bot.  But for something more like an archiving/mirroring bot, I'd expect them to just read stuff via their owner.)

**Steve Howell** · 2019-04-03 16:36 UTC

@Lino Lemmer For your particular application, it's not clear why you'd actually use a bot to get data out of Zulip, vs. just using your own API key.  Perhaps this is something where we can give better advice in our API docs.

**Lino Lemmer** · 2019-04-04 06:00 UTC

@Steve Howell It's just that I can show: Look there is a bot reading and writing stuff.

**Steve Howell** · 2019-04-07 19:46 UTC

I think "success" is appropriate even when there aren't messages, as long as the query is valid.  It can be a bit challenging to give precise errors in some situations, because we don't want people to use bots to fish around for things like private stream names.

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-04-09 05:31 UTC

@Steve Howell I think that difference is intentional -- we have bot types (like incoming webhook bots) that are allowed to send to streams that they don't have read access to.

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-04-09 05:31 UTC

I don't think there's a change to the security model that makes sense to do for this issue.

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-04-09 05:32 UTC

(Result is success because the bot successfully read the history it can from that stream, which is 0 messages; but because it's possible that an unsubscribed bot was a previous subscriber and has access to some history on the stream for that reason, I'm not sure that it makes sense to throw an error here)

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-04-09 05:34 UTC

The one thing I will mention is that our own code for provisioning is pretty carefully designed and tested to recover fine if you end up doing a `ctrl+C` and restarting, so you don't need to worry about ending up with a messed-up environment.

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-04-09 05:34 UTC

I don't think our development environment re-provisioning should ever hang for more than like 5 minutes without continued output.

## Fedora Development Environment

*2019-04-11 to 2019-05-14 · 26 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/Fedora.20Development.20Environment/with/731385)*

**Hemanth V. Alluri** · 2019-04-11 17:09 UTC

For anyone who successfully set up the Zulip development environment via lxc/vagrant on Fedora, how did you deal with the absence of cgroups-lite?

**Hemanth V. Alluri** · 2019-04-11 17:43 UTC

Rather, did you face any issues with the virtual network bridge settings for lxc?

**Hemanth V. Alluri** · 2019-04-11 18:00 UTC

Ah, after several hours, I finally figured out what's going wrong.

**Hemanth V. Alluri** · 2019-04-11 18:01 UTC

Posting here for future reference....

**Hemanth V. Alluri** · 2019-04-11 18:11 UTC

On Fedora systems, all installed services will be disabled by default. 
You will have to manually enable these services (Fedora users already know this, but I'm bringing it up to re-enforce this). 
In particular, lxc seems to depends on lxc-net which is part of the lxc package which can be obtained from dnf.
lxc-start requires a virtual network bridge (seems to default to "lxcbr0") which will bind with a veth interface.

***Make sure that lxc-net.service has been enabled*** this can be done by `sudo systemctl enable lxc-net` followed by `sudo systemctl  start lxc-net` This will help setup this network bridge.

**Hemanth V. Alluri** · 2019-04-11 18:19 UTC

yaeh, adding documentation for that would be great!

Because of this,  I wasn't able to do `vagrant up`.

## Show invites dependencies (#11685)

*2019-04-13 to 2019-04-21 · 16 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/Show.20invites.20dependencies.20.28.2311685.29/with/732751)*

**Ayush Shah** · 2019-04-13 21:12 UTC

Hi all, the issue we're trying to address is listed here (https://github.com/zulip/zulip/issues/11685)

The current point to address is to no longer show invites for a user who is in a LDAP-only realm, and invitations are not required to join.

From our understanding of the codebase, there are functions that provide the realm authentication types in zprojects.backend, in different functions such as ldap_auth_enabled() and email_auth_enabled(). We were wondering  if it would make sense to create another function such as only_auth_enabled() that takes in a auth method as an argument and returns True if that method is the only auth method for a realm. The alternative would be to loop through all the auth_enabled() functions and ensure that ldap is the only one that returns True.

Any thoughts/suggestions would be greatly appreciated.

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-04-14 02:01 UTC

@Ayush Shah I think such a function would be reasonable.

**Ayush Shah** · 2019-04-14 02:43 UTC

Excellent! I've created a PR (#12118) with a single commit to show the thought process behind the idea. I've modeled the only_auth_enabled function on the existing auth_enabled_helper function.

**Ayush Shah** · 2019-04-16 19:46 UTC

Currently, the PR has some failed builds because the tests no longer have 100% coverage. I believe to get 100% coverage, I need to create a realm that falls under the second category above (LDAP-auth only and invites not required), but I'm not quite sure how to do this. I've looked into how to instantiate a realm with only LDAP-auth, but the get_realm function is used, which appears to only get pre-defined realms. Could someone please point me in the right direction?

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-04-17 23:46 UTC

@Ayush Shah if you look at our `test_signup.py` and `test_auth_backends.py` tests, you'll see the standard approach for this sort of thing is to edit the existing `zulip` realm's setting in the first lines of the test to match the configuration you want to verify.

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-04-17 23:47 UTC

You can use `with self.settings()` and/or `@override_settings` to change values in `settings.py` for just the duration of a test.

**Ruchit Vithani** · 2019-04-16 19:00 UTC

Drafts like view for scheduled messages is finished now. Next part is,
* if you remove a message from that table, actual schedule for it should also get cancelled
* if you edit a schedule of that message (edit date/time in slash command), then in the backend side, old schedule should be deleted and a new updated should be created (or alternatively, old one should be edited)
* if you edit that message, and remove /schedule command, old schedule should be cancelled. 
So, for cancelling those schedule, the simplest approach I could figure out was to remove that ScheduledMessage object from the backend to prevent that message from sending.

The other option is some kind of deleted flag.

@Ruchit Vithani yes, I agree with what other folks said:
* Using the frontend markdown processor is fine, though we could just as easily use the other one if we wanted to.
* Local storage doesn't make any sense -- these must be stored in the database in order for things to work if your browser isn't online when the scheduled message is supposed to be sent.

* table for messages should not be filled from data of local storage (in fact the method of storing messages to local storage should be removed completely)
* Instead of that, table should be filled from the list or dict returned somehow from the backend, like we fill tables in settings section.

@Ruchit Vithani that's correct.

## # Commits Behind Master

*2019-04-20 to 2019-04-21 · 2 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/.23.20Commits.20Behind.20Master/with/735150)*

**Preethi Prabhu** · 2019-04-20 19:31 UTC

I'm working on my first issue (#4685) and it was suggested that we could run 
git log --pretty=oneline 2.0.2..HEAD | wc
to find out how many commits behind master the current Zulip server is.

But when I run that after cd-ing into my local zulip branch, I'm getting
     408    3222   38969
and none of the numbers correspond with the 532 commits to master since this release as reported at https://github.com/zulip/zulip/releases.

How would I get the correct number of commits?

**Puneeth Chaganti** · 2019-04-21 03:33 UTC

`wc` prints newline, word, and byte counts. So, you want to be looking at the first number, or calling `wc` as `wc -l` to print just the number of lines. 

Are you on the latest `master`? If so, you should see `532` printed by `wc -l` when you run the command.

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-04-23 18:12 UTC

@Yash RE it's not totally clear to me, but that issue looks kinda like a missing `preventDefault` or `.stopPropagation` in a click handler resulting in the click double toggling something.

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-04-23 18:13 UTC

We try to be consistent about most click handlers using those two functions because not doing so often neglecting to do so results in problems like what you describe.

**Ryan Rehman** · 2020-06-05 16:33 UTC

So I don't have the bug in the gif shown above.
But I notice that the [click event handler](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/master/static/js/tab_bar.js#L162) gets called twice.

```js
exports.initialize = function () {
    const filter = narrow_state.filter();
    build_tab_bar(filter);

    // register navbar click handlers
    $('#search_exit').on("click", function (e) {
        tab_bar.exit_search();
        e.preventDefault();
        e.stopPropagation();
    });
};
```
So `tab_bar.initialize` is called every time the narrow activates, and I guess a new handler is attached?
So the `exit_search` function gets called multiple times after the cross button is clicked.


Is there a reason we don't use `e.stopImmediatePropagation()`, so that it only executes once ?
I don't understand this well enough but my question is that is there any benefit in adding this instead ?

[searchbox_cross.mp4](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/6a/ISHzHhUvNvIjRhGQIznLpLMF/searchbox_cross.mp4)

**Steve Howell** · 2020-06-05 16:37 UTC

We should really only call `tab_bar.initialize` once, and from `ui_init.js` (which we do now).

**Steve Howell** · 2020-06-05 16:37 UTC

And then we could extract these two lines into something more like `tab_bar.rebuild_for_new_narrow`:

~~~ js
158     const filter = narrow_state.filter();
159     build_tab_bar(filter);

**Steve Howell** · 2020-06-05 16:39 UTC

There is no reason to create this click handler multiple times, since I'm pretty sure `$('#search_exit')` never gets totally replaced (although we'd want to double check it):

~~~ js
161     // register navbar click handlers
162     $('#search_exit').on("click", function (e) {
163         tab_bar.exit_search();
164         e.preventDefault();
165         e.stopPropagation();
166     });

~~~

**Ryan Rehman** · 2020-06-05 16:40 UTC

I see, I'll add this extraction as a prep commit. :+1:

**Steve Howell** · 2020-06-05 16:41 UTC

@Ryan Rehman Thanks!

wait

**Yash RE** · 2020-06-05 16:48 UTC

@Ryan Rehman see #14999

## Replacing --parallel default

*2019-05-02 to 2019-05-02 · 4 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/Replacing.20--parallel.20default/with/738509)*

**Wyatt Hoodes** · 2019-05-02 02:31 UTC

@Tim Abbott after researching a little more, for full disclosure I wanted to post these here (just grabbed them from the python docs) if in case we decide against a config file: 

* using `os.cpu_count()`. returns the number of CPUs in the system or `None` if undetermined. This isn't equivalent to the number of available CPUs for a process to use.

* `len(os.sched_getaffinity(0))` will return the number of usable CPUs.

Looking forward to hearing your thoughts.

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-05-02 05:13 UTC

@Wyatt Hoodes it seems like one of those is probably what we want.  I did some testing and it appears `--parallel=12` is faster than `--parallel=6` on my laptop (34s vs. 43s) so probably we want 12; I think `os.cpu_count` seems pretty reasonable.

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-05-02 05:13 UTC

So let's try that out and see how it goes.

**Wyatt Hoodes** · 2019-05-02 08:37 UTC

Cool, updated. 

Side-note: After a little more reading, it seems like on somewhat quiescent systems utilizing dynamic CPU activation,  idle cores losing power can cause this type of idiom to break down.  Not sure if this will be a problem here though, just putting it in the discussion.

## page params in admin_tab

*2019-05-15 to 2019-05-16 · 4 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/page.20params.20in.20admin_tab/with/742328)*

**Rishi Gupta** · 2019-05-15 22:32 UTC

It seems like our settings pages have access to page_params, but our org setting pages don't. In particular:
`exports.build_page` in `admin_tab.js` seems to copy a bunch of fields over
`git grep page_params` in `static/templates` only seems to give non-admin pages.

Is this correct / intentional?

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-05-16 01:02 UTC

It's a bit complicated.  In general, `page_params` is not available when rendering templates unless you pass it into the `templates.render` function.

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-05-16 01:02 UTC

So the main rendering function in `settings.js` passes `page_params` in, and that's why it's available there:

```
exports.build_page = function () {                                                                   
    ui.set_up_scrollbar($("#settings_page .sidebar.left"));                                          
    ui.set_up_scrollbar($("#settings_content"));                                                     
                                                                                                     
    setup_settings_label();                                                                          
                                                                                                     
    var rendered_settings_tab = templates.render('settings_tab', {                                   
        full_name: people.my_full_name(),                                                            
        page_params: page_params,                                                                    
        enable_sound_select: page_params.enable_sounds || page_params.enable_stream_sounds,          
        zuliprc: 'zuliprc',                                                                          
        botserverrc: 'botserverrc',                                                                  
        timezones: moment.tz.names(),                                                                
        can_create_new_bots: settings_bots.can_create_new_bots(),                                    
        settings_label: settings.settings_label,                                                     
    });                                                                                              
                                                                                                     
    $(".settings-box").html(rendered_settings_tab);                                                  
};                                                                                                   
```

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-05-16 01:03 UTC

I would not describe that as great style; for one thing, there's kinda a performance issue that `page_params` is a quite large data structure.

**matfer** · 2019-10-16 10:44 UTC

@Tim Abbott As I said in my original request, I am interested in uses with a large realm with tens of thousands of users. Could you please provide some information about server specs and bottlenecks? Are there best practices about features to turn off to gain performance?

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-10-16 22:22 UTC

@matfer the main bottleneck is sharding of the Tornado server which does server->client push.  In master we only support sharding by realm, and so if you have 10K+ concurrently active users you will see that system be overloaded.  If you're talking 10Ks of users where only a fraction will be concurrently active, you don't need a particularly big server.

BTW, I just wanted to highlight that `vagrant reload` on the Docker system will end up rebuiding the image from scratch: it's no longer a 1-command alias for `vagrant halt; vagrant up` as it was with LXC.

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-06-07 18:33 UTC

(The difference is that `vagrant` reload wants to resync any configuration changes to `Vagrantfile` to the image, and the only way it can guarantee achieving that is to destroy + recreate the vm.  I am not sure that was the right decision on the part of the folks who made `vagrant-docker`, but that's what it is)

## git practices

*2019-05-24 to 2019-05-25 · 3 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/git.20practices/with/745504)*

**David Wood** · 2019-05-24 20:31 UTC

I’ve noticed in my last few PRs that often reviewers will prefer to modify a PR locally and then push changes or request that I cherry-pick from their copy of the branch. 

I don’t have any problems with this, I was just wondering what the rationale was as it isn’t a practice that I’ve seen used in other projects.

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-05-25 00:26 UTC

@David Wood cool, yeah, I think to some extent it's a practice that one wouldn't try without a lot of Git experience and tooling (e.g. `tools/reset-to-pull-request` and `tools/push-to-pull-request`).  There's are things we use it for:

* Probably 50% of PRs have some text that I want to edit before merging (often user-facing strings or adding/clarifying comments to make the code easier to understand for someone with less context).  A lot of these changes don't need to be tested in CI and there's significant delay, merge conflict and re-review work savings in avoiding an additional round-trip with the other developer by just merging the commits that are ready to be merged.  
* We do a lot of incrementally merging the first few commits in a PR and then requesting changes on the rest, which is a huge part of how I'm able to review such a large fraction of work happening in this community (because I don't spend much time re-reading code that I was already happy with last time).  My priority in reviewing (and giving advice about construction of) PRs is generally to minimize outstanding changes by getting all the pieces we know are correct merged as quickly as possible.
* Also, as part of code review, one usually checks out the code locally to do manual QA/testing, so one already has a copy locally.  For some types of edits, especially to UI things or code organization, it's sometimes easier and faster to make the changes locally, verify that indeed they actually make sense, and push those changes back to the PR, than to figure out and then communicate.  My practice is usually to post diffs showing what I changed or comment on each individual change so that the original contributor can see the changes, verify them, and potentially learn from them.

We probably should put a cleaned up version of this writeup in our docs, because it definitely belongs there; I've been generally unsatisfied with our "version control" docs as having the wrong focus.

**David Wood** · 2019-05-25 07:28 UTC

Thanks, that all makes sense.

## typeahead: How does "/" force open?

*2019-05-29 to 2019-05-30 · 4 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/typeahead.3A.20How.20does.20.22.2F.22.20force.20open.3F/with/747085)*

**Yash RE** · 2019-05-29 16:20 UTC

I'm trying to make a change for the new navbar, making an icon select the search and *explicitly* open the typeahead when clicked. Using `/` or `cntrl + k` hotkeys makes this happen, but it's not clear to me how it's being explicitly forced open.

in `hotkey.js` the `/` key corresponds to a case which only calls `search.initiate_search();` which doesn't do anything to force the typeahead open... currently I'm looking at old commits like 0e2c509 to try and find leads, but any help would be appreciated, is there a function that I could just call?

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-05-29 22:21 UTC

@Yash RE I believe the typeahead being opened is triggered by focus being added to that text box?  @Shubham Padia might know the details better than I do.

**Shubham Padia** · 2019-05-30 03:57 UTC

@Yash RE  After `search.initiate_search()` focuses on the search query bar, the typeahead code at https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/master/static/third/bootstrap-typeahead/typeahead.js#L292 processes a keyup event of the `/` key and calls `Typeahead.lookup()`

**Shubham Padia** · 2019-05-30 04:17 UTC

You can call `$('#search_query').typeahead('lookup').focus();` (from https://stackoverflow.com/a/23638206) to trigger the typeahead.

I would also advise to replace the existing `initiate_search focus` with `$('#search_query').typeahead('lookup').focus();` so that we don't rely on the event reaching to `third/bootstrap-typeahead/typeahead.js` just after `search.initiate_search()` focuses on the search query bar.

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-06-03 20:08 UTC

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-06-03 20:08 UTC

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-06-04 05:52 UTC

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-06-04 05:53 UTC

**Hemanth V. Alluri** · 2019-06-07 18:36 UTC

> It seems like there's also a bug here where we're not getting the right error message raised when creating a test database fails due to insufficient disk. Bug might be in the core Django code we're using to create databases, though.

Just want to reinforce that this occurs due to insufficient disk space.

**Wyatt Hoodes** · 2019-06-07 19:33 UTC

@Hemanth V. Alluri yeah there's an on going effort to deal with leaking of the test databases from adding the multiple `test-backend` instances functionality. Which is why this error was occurring.

**Wyatt Hoodes** · 2019-06-07 19:42 UTC

I'm not sure if we can catch this `OperationalError` and output the correct message in the event where disk is full. It would be really nice if we could though.

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-06-07 20:28 UTC

In case anyone's having trouble with disk space leaks:
* `rm -rf var/` and then reprovisioning can save a lot of space caused by our data export tests leaking files (this is a separate issue).
* I don't have a super convenient block of code to do `DROP DATABASE` queries on all the cloned test database; @Wyatt Hoodes you might want to start your work on the cleanup stuff with just writing a function in `zerver/lib/test_fixtures.py` that loops over `zulip_test_template_*` databases and deletes them; I think that might require some research to figure out how to do cleanly and is what we need to have a manual workaround.

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-06-07 18:31 UTC

OK, yeah, so it's very possible that the guest configuration gets copied from the host, so if you're not happy with host DNS configuration, you might want to do that there.  (It's probably more likely guest configuration is just reset from something standard every time you `vagrant reload`)

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2019-06-25 21:57 UTC

Investigating the issue where the container doesn’t follow changes of the host DNS settings, I found this in the Docker [documentation](https://docs.docker.com/v17.09/engine/userguide/networking/default_network/configure-dns/):

> When the host file changes, all stopped containers which have a matching `resolv.conf` to the host will be updated immediately to this newest host configuration. Containers which are running when the host configuration changes will need to stop and start to pick up the host changes due to lack of a facility to ensure atomic writes of the `resolv.conf` file while the container is running.

**Yash RE** · 2019-06-06 16:49 UTC

Why is it that, after `checkout` really far back (1000+ commits), provisioning seems much more likely to fail?
Is this something that's happening just with me or do we sometimes make changes which make it impossible to go back and provision old code?

I made the mistake of trying to checkout really far back to try and find the commit that caused a regression, I thought I could just provision and wait and things would be fine. Things were not fine. Could there be some way of keeping track how far back is stable for provision or is that too set up specific?

**Yash RE** · 2019-06-06 16:52 UTC

(@Puneeth Chaganti )

**Puneeth Chaganti** · 2019-06-06 17:03 UTC

In an ideal world, it shouldn't matter and you should be able to provision any version of Zulip. But, you are only able to lock down so much of "the state of the world" in the various requirements and dependency files. The farther back you go, the more the state of the world (that isn't captured in our requirements files) is different from what it is now. And that could lead to provisioning failing.

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-06-06 18:51 UTC

I'd be curious to see the exceptions you get with that.  Sometimes third-parties take down dependencies we would have installed, etc., but that's pretty rare and I generally don't have problems provisioning versions from a release or two ago.

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-06-06 18:53 UTC

So it's possible what @Yash RE is seeing here is just that provisioning from ~1000 commits ago is much more similar to provisioning fresh (in that we need to reinstall all dependencies)

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-06-07 17:08 UTC

Each distinct version of the Zulip dependencies you provision with results in your having stuff under the various cache directories in `/srv/`

So, we have a tool, `scripts/purge-old-deployments`, that provision runs, which will clean up unused ones.

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-06-07 17:09 UTC

By default, it keeps everything you've used in the last 2 weeks, so switching around between branches is fast.  It has a `--threshold` option you can use to have it purge more recent stuff, which you probably want to use.

## handler for clicking outside search

*2019-06-12 to 2019-06-15 · 5 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/handler.20for.20clicking.20outside.20search/with/753116)*

**Yash RE** · 2019-06-12 19:42 UTC

I'm having some trouble finding the code which handles the behavior of the search bar when you've typed in a search query and then click outside the search box [search-clicking.gif](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/7/7Ly38AqILoVS9W_HPYurOmLf/search-clicking.gif).

I tried searching over all the IDs and classes on the search box to try and find any listeners attached to it, but I couldn't find anything special.
I've also tried to search for places where we reset the search query through `.val(`, but again, couldn't find anything special.
I've also tried to use chrome break points on `click` events but I wasn't able to understand where the effect was coming from.

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-06-14 22:34 UTC

@Yash RE hmm, I'm not sure off the top of my head.

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-06-14 22:35 UTC

But a quick investigation suggests it's this:
```
    search_query_box.on('blur', function () {                                                        
        // The search query box is a visual cue as to                                                
        // whether search or narrowing is active.  If                                                
        // the user blurs the search box, then we should                                             
        // update the search string to reflect the current                                           
        // narrow (or lack of narrow).                                                               
        //                                                                                           
        // But we can't do this right away, because                                                  
        // selecting something in the typeahead menu causes                                          
        // the box to lose focus a moment before.                                                    
        //                                                                                           
        // The workaround is to check 100ms later -- long                                            
        // enough for the search to have gone through, but                                           
        // short enough that the user won't notice (though                                           
        // really it would be OK if they did).                                                       
                                                                                                     
        setTimeout(function () {                                                                     
            var search_string = narrow_state.search_string();                                        
            search_query_box.val(search_string);                                                     
            exports.update_button_visibility();                                                      
        }, 100);                                                                                     
    });                                                                                              
```

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-06-14 22:35 UTC

(i.e. the trigger is unfocusing the search box, not the click)

**Yash RE** · 2019-06-15 15:50 UTC

I'd gone over that segment a few times, I should have realized that was the trigger.

*2019-06-14 to 2019-06-17 · 6 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/event.20names.2Ftypes/with/753673)*

**Neil Pilgrim (neiljp)** · 2019-06-14 06:04 UTC

If the API is called with `register`, with `event_types=['foo', 'bar', ...]`, then is it true that the server only sends events with `type='foo'` and so on, in that list? There seems to be a one to one mapping, except maybe the extra `'heartbeat'` event type? The 'register-queue' docs aren't completely clear on that. We seem to have a 1-1 correlation in Z-T, which led me to want to simplify that, but I wanted to confirm that assumption first.

**Neil Pilgrim (neiljp)** · 2019-06-14 06:05 UTC

(this would allow this change, for example: https://github.com/neiljp/zulip-terminal/commit/bfcb681b3935652abc45986533debc32b13bebbc)

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-06-14 22:32 UTC

@Neil Pilgrim yes, that's correct.

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-06-14 22:33 UTC

It's a little more complicated, in that we have a separate `fetch_event_types`  that can be used to fetch additional values, and there's some event types we only send if you've requested two things, but that's the high-level story.

**Neil Pilgrim (neiljp)** · 2019-06-15 03:17 UTC

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-06-17 01:11 UTC

`fetch_event_types` is just an override if you want to fetch a different set of initial data than the event types you want to receive new events for.

```python
import pdb; pdb.set_trace()
```
https://docs.python.org/3/library/pdb.html
https://pypi.org/project/ipdb/

**Puneeth Chaganti** · 2019-06-25 16:44 UTC

> I tried it but I couldn't get which lines run and which doesn't and in what order.
You can step through the execution of a code path using this. Just drop this line in a place that you know you will surely hit. Then you can step through the execution by using the [commands](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pdb.html#debugger-commands).  Usually, you'll want to use `n` to go to the next line, or `s` to step into a function.

*2019-06-28 to 2019-07-12 · 22 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/populate_db.20not.20distributing.20message.20dates.20correctly.3F/with/761351)*

**Mateusz Mandera** · 2019-06-28 17:56 UTC

The code says
```python
        # Spoofing time not supported with threading
        if options['threads'] != 1:
            message.pub_date = timezone_now()
        else:
            # Distrubutes 80% of messages starting from 5 days ago, over a period
            # of 3 days. Then, distributes remaining messages over past 24 hours.
            spoofed_date = timezone_now() - timezone_timedelta(days = 5)
            if (num_messages < tot_messages * 0.8):
                # Maximum of 3 days ahead, convert to minutes
                time_ahead = 3 * 24 * 60
                time_ahead //= int(tot_messages * 0.8)
            else:
                time_ahead = 24 * 60
                time_ahead //= int(tot_messages * 0.2)

            spoofed_minute = random.randint(time_ahead * num_messages, time_ahead * (num_messages + 1))
            spoofed_date += timezone_timedelta(minutes = spoofed_minute)
            message.pub_date = spoofed_date
```

But when  I run it (with one thread), it seems that every message pub_date gets set  to today - 5 days? I generate 100,000 messages and here are their pub_dates:
[date.txt](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/92/3__h2qTT0251VYB_Yv1tSNEL/date.txt)

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-06-28 19:23 UTC

@Mateusz Mandera thanks for the report!  Were you using the threads option?

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-06-28 19:24 UTC

Oh, I see the bug.

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-06-28 19:24 UTC

We're doing the `int()` in the wrong place, so if `tot_messages` is large enough, 3 * 24 * 60 // (tot_messages * 0.8) = 0

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-06-28 19:25 UTC

I think the right fix is probably to (A) use seconds rather than minutes and (B) do the float-to-integer conversion after the multiplication.

**Mateusz Mandera** · 2019-07-10 19:35 UTC

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-07-10 20:02 UTC

the `zilencer/zerver` thing isn't a problem for the tests.  The main motivation for it is to have `populate_db` not be runnable in most productions systems since it will wreck your database.

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-07-10 20:05 UTC

We don't have any unit tests for populate_db; I would probably just fix the bug here rather than starting an investment into that, but I'd be fine with adding a test in a new `zerver/tests/test_populate_db.py`.

**Mateusz Mandera** · 2019-07-10 20:23 UTC

Fair enough!

This is very slow for high numbers of messages/users. Is there a reason for this message-by-message, as opposed to sending all the Message objects in one `` do_send_message `` call (or at least in chunks), to avoid making massive numbers of db queries?

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-07-10 20:48 UTC

I don't there's strategy behind that.  For context, back in the day we used to have a mode for `populate_db` to very quickly restore messages from a database log, but it was also very fragile (e.g. it wouldn't set flags on messages correctly when we started adding things like links and mentions and so to the data set).

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-07-10 20:49 UTC

It's worth testing whether we can significantly improve performance using the bulk support in `do_send_messages` that we've been maintaining despite not a lot of users because it might come in handy.

Hahaha, yes it is intended, that's how we make sure you don't run tests with an old version of the `populate_db` data set.

I am currently working on issue #4676, and I have noticed while looking through the tests that are failing that there are many cases of hard coded emails being used in tests to confirm that emails were sent to the right users. 

After I complete the commit that will allow using formataddr in send_email, using formataddr there will cause many tests to break, as they are looking for only the email, not the prettyfied `name <email@zulip.com>` format

I am wondering if It would be a better option to manually change these as so that it correctly tests for the full prettyfied form, or if instead the test should be changed to use parseaddr to extract only the email to test against.

**Conner Bondurant** · 2019-06-29 02:03 UTC

Im not sure if this conversation would fit better in the actual issue or not, so Im willing to take this conversation there instead

**Rishi Gupta** · 2019-06-29 02:41 UTC

This is a good place for the conversation (though I don't have an opinion on the actual question)

**Conner Bondurant** · 2019-06-29 02:47 UTC

I don't know which one is better, but my main thoughts are:
1) If the focus of these tests is to see that the emails are sent to the right address, then parseaddr is probably preferred, as we don't want tests that fail due to formatting errors when they are focusing on target, preferably separate tests would fail.

2) If the focus of these tests is to see if the user end of these emails is properly displayed to the user in all cases, then we want to confirm proper formatting in each instance that we are testing for proper display, and it would be better to more properly rewrite the examples.

I would like to have someone who's been here a bit longer pitch in on which of these two sounds closer to ground truth before I do any more work on the matter.

One thing I should mention here that probably more people should know about is `tools/provision --force`; that causes most of our caches (that let a noop provision run in ~1s) to be skipped, and fixes a pretty broad category of issues like this one.

(It's still worth reporting that you had to use it, because in this case there was a thing we should fix for everyone, but I think it's worth knowing about since it's much cheaper than rebuilding the vagrant guest)

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-07-10 17:20 UTC

My guess is #6040 can be resolved by changing a few things:
```
exports.process_loaded_messages = function (messages) {                                              
    _.each(messages, function (message) {                                                            
        if (!message.unread) {                                                                       
            return;                                                                                  
        }                                                                                            
                                                                                                     
        unread_messages.add(message.id);                                                             
                                                                                                     
        if (message.type === 'private') {                                                            
            exports.unread_pm_counter.add(message);                                                  
        }                                                                                            
                                                                                                     
        if (message.type === 'stream') {                                                             
            exports.unread_topic_counter.add(                                                        
                message.stream_id,                                                                   
                util.get_message_topic(message),                                                     
                message.id                                                                           
            );                                                                                       
        }                                                                                            
                                                                                                     
        if (message.mentioned) {                                                                     
            exports.unread_mentions_counter.add(message.id);                                         
        }                                                                                            
    });                                                                                              
};                                                                                                   
```

As well as the `unread_msgs` data structure in `page_params` that generates `unread_msgs.mentions`.

## initialized

*2019-07-05 to 2019-07-08 · 8 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/initialized/with/764023)*

**Yash RE** · 2019-07-05 08:23 UTC

This is a small stylistic thing I've noticed that kind of bugs me, not very important, but

when we have areas with a ".initialize()" function, we tend to do something like:
```javascript
exports.initialize = function () {
    .
    .
    // initialize or create variable foo here
    .
    .
}
```
and then later on if we're working on something that either needs to run on every event except initialization, or just needs to make sure that initialization has been done, we do something like:
```javascript
function () {
    if (! foo === undefined) {
    // we've initialized
   } else {
   // we haven't initialized
   }
}
```

**Yash RE** · 2019-07-05 08:31 UTC

An example would be how `activity.js` has `user_cursor` and `user_filter` or how `tab_bar.js` checks for `narrow_state.filter()`, etc.

@Yash RE I'm not sure `user_cursor` is what you had in mind, since that one doesn't seem to have a similar check.

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-07-08 05:23 UTC

But it depends a bit on the context for whether we expect the thing not being initialized to be a case that happens, or we're just writing error-reporting code to better debug a theoretically impossible situation where it won't be.

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-07-08 05:24 UTC

We generally expect that during the runtime of most code, everything should be initialized, and so I think for many of our modules a `module.is_initialized` check would be just clutter and confusing in its own way (making one think that's a thing that might actually happen).

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-07-08 05:25 UTC

Can you point to a few specific examples you think we might want to change?  In general `activity.js` is very old code, so there are likely some patterns there that reflect a lot of cross-codebase refactoring without much in the way of direct edits to that file.

## Rationale behind full name restrictions

*2019-07-06 to 2019-07-08 · 3 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/Rationale.20behind.20full.20name.20restrictions/with/764394)*

**Conner Bondurant** · 2019-07-06 14:13 UTC

While working on issue #4676, I have found that `parseaddr`and `formataddr`properly handle all valid ASCII characters, and can be used without any risk. The only exceptions being the double quote, and backslash. This is actually more lenient than the current restrictions that are placed on email fields, excluding that we do not currently restrict the backslash. Are there any other reasons for restricting these otherwise legal full name characters? Specifically: *, `, @, >

**Rishi Gupta** · 2019-07-07 05:04 UTC

I think most of those are restricted because they are special characters in Zulip's markdown.

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-07-08 05:18 UTC

@Conner Bondurant Rishi is correct, it's because they are low-value for use in people's names and things we want to be able to use in our markdown/typeahead syntax.


## Structured test result data #12727

*2019-07-07 to 2019-07-08 · 8 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/Structured.20test.20result.20data.20.2312727/with/764665)*

**Wyatt Hoodes** · 2019-07-07 22:48 UTC

Some notes regarding adding structured test result exports for the backend tests:
* https://github.com/xmlrunner/unittest-xml-reporting patches the test runner to allow for the reports, which conflics with the current patching we've done in `test_runner.py`.  
  * We'd have to refactor a lot of `test_runner.py` to be able to run via the  `XMLTestRunner` class: With [this](https://github.com/xmlrunner/unittest-xml-reporting/blob/4ab171c49ad7d1de300558b652dff37bf106c713/xmlrunner/extra/djangotestrunner.py#L20) suggested usage for a custom Django test runner, we implement the [XMLTestRunner](https://github.com/xmlrunner/unittest-xml-reporting/blob/master/xmlrunner/runner.py) class that seems to break everything anyway (Test stdout looks terrible, majority of tests don't run, `parallel=1` breaks).
  * This seems to not really be worth the return, when as mentioned [here](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/issues/8593#issuecomment-371978230), we could focus on switching to [django-nose](https://github.com/jazzband/django-nose).  Which is more active (4 days compared to 4 months), and is recommend  by [CircleCI](https://circleci.com/docs/2.0/collect-test-data/#enabling-formatters).

Not sure how big of a project that would actually be, but I'm interested in hearing feedback relating to what it would actually take to switch over to django-nose, and whether that would be worth it/doable at this time.

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-07-08 05:13 UTC

My guess is that there's little to gain from migrating to django-nose.  These are the advertised benefits:
> * Testing just your apps by default, not all the standard ones that happen to be in INSTALLED_APPS
> * Running the tests in one or more specific modules (or apps, or classes, or folders, or just running a specific test)
> * Obviating the need to import all your tests into tests/__init__.py. This not only saves busy-work but also eliminates the possibility of accidentally shadowing test classes.

We already do these in `test-backend` in a way that feels nice, and have since like 2012.

> * Taking advantage of all the useful nose plugins

I'm not sure what we might gain here.  https://nose-plugins.jottit.com/ has an expired SSL cert and isn't visitable right now.

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-07-08 05:15 UTC

> * Fixture bundling, an optional feature which speeds up your fixture-based tests by a factor of 4

I don't think fixture-based tests are a material time cost for us, but I could be wrong on this.

> * Reuse of previously created test DBs, cutting 10 seconds off startup time

My guess is our template management stuff already handles this.

> * Hygienic TransactionTestCases, which can save you a DB flush per test

No idea whether this is useful.

> * Support for various databases. Tested with MySQL, PostgreSQL, and SQLite. Others should work as well.

Not relevant to us.

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-07-08 05:16 UTC

I think it's unlikely that moving to `django-nose` would provide real benefits to us, given the already high level of development of our test-backend ecosystem and the number of useful custom plugins we have built into `test-backend` (e.g. checking which files don't have coverage).

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-07-08 05:16 UTC

If it was the case they had something fancy they did that would actually make our tests run faster, I would be tempted by that.

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-07-08 05:17 UTC

What we could do is only support the XML generation in `test-backend --parallel=1` and use our new `--replicate` option with that to get a nice report in a rerun of the failing part of the test suite.

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-07-08 05:17 UTC

Not sure if it's worth doing that, but probably worth thinking about once `--replicate` is merged.

**Wyatt Hoodes** · 2019-07-08 07:10 UTC

Great, thanks for running through all of those points, @Tim Abbott !  You're actually addressing the thought I had after thinking about this a little more.  Which is, we already have an awesome testing infrastructure, we are just looking to graft in XML generation for failures, not go around replacing stuff.

> What we could do is only support the XML generation in test-backend --parallel=1 and use our new --replicate option with that to get a nice report in a rerun of the failing part of the test suite.

Ohh, this actually sounds like a super cool idea!  Which could certainly prove to be an interesting followup.

```python

# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
from django.conf import settings
from django.db import migrations
from django.db.backends.postgresql_psycopg2.schema import DatabaseSchemaEditor
from django.db.migrations.state import StateApps

def rename_zulip_realm_to_zulipinternal(apps: StateApps, schema_editor: DatabaseSchemaEditor) -> None:
    if not settings.PRODUCTION:
        return

    Realm = apps.get_model('zerver', 'Realm')
    UserProfile = apps.get_model('zerver', 'UserProfile')

    if Realm.objects.filter(string_id="zulipinternal").exists():
        return

    internal_realm = Realm.objects.get(string_id="zulip")

    # For safety, as a sanity check, verify that "internal_realm" is indeed the realm for system bots:
    welcome_bot = UserProfile.objects.get(email="welcome-bot@zulip.com")
    assert welcome_bot.realm.id == internal_realm.id

    internal_realm.string_id = "zulipinternal"
    internal_realm.save()

class Migration(migrations.Migration):

    dependencies = [
        ('zerver', '0235_userprofile_desktop_icon_count_display'),
    ]

    operations = [
        migrations.RunPython(rename_zulip_realm_to_zulipinternal)
    ]

```

## Newbie git question/sanity check

*2019-07-10 to 2019-07-10 · 4 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/Newbie.20git.20question.2Fsanity.20check/with/766425)*

**Laurel Michaels** · 2019-07-10 23:08 UTC

I am a newbie API doc contributor. Thanks to @Rishi Gupta    for suggesting and helping me get set up with the remote dev env (zulipdev@laurel-personal.zulipdev.org) - it's very helpful.

I have now worked through the how-Zulip-uses git/GitHub doc (very good!) and that has helped me brush off the dust on how to use these tools from when I used them before.

Moving forward, the first thing is -- I'd like to request a small "sanity check." I have come up with a mini-cheat-sheet for how I plan to do a git/GitHub workflow in the Zulip env -- it is copied in below. Would you please take a quick look and let me know if it makes sense? I don't want to mess up my remote dev instance before I even get started doing doc!

I am looking for the most basic workflow - other stuff can come in later.

```

***** Daily (or so) workflow with feature branch *****

# First, make sure my remote dev instance's master branch (aka my local branch) is up-to-date with Zulip upstream. I want to do this before I make a new feature branch, so that my new feature branch will be based on the most recent upstream files

$ git fetch upstream

$ git checkout master

$ git rebase upstream/master


# This is skipping ahead a bit, but note that as time goes on, if I want to keep both a local feature branch and the GitHub version of that same feature branch up to date with upstream, I basically use the same method as above:

$ git fetch upstream

$ git checkout feature-branch

$ git rebase upstream/master

$ git push origin feature-branch 


# Returning to the basic daily workflow -- now I need to make my feature branch

$ git checkout master

$ git checkout -b issue-123


# edit and test whatever files i need for issue-123



# run git add on both newly-created files and newly-edited existing files

$ git status

$ git add file_1.md

# or if i want to add all changes i made:

$ git add -A



# commit with a multi line message

$ git commit

# in theory an editor will open and i can type in a multi line message

First line: Imperative sentence ending with a period, for example:

docs: Update doc for Feature X.

Next line: must be a blank line

Subsequent lines: Less than 76 characters per line

Last line: Fixes: #123


# look at any messages that the pre-commit hook sent me. background -- i installed ./tools/setup-git-repo, which should run the linter suite on just the files i changed in this commit. if anything is wrong, fix it and commit again, using git commit --amend:

# if i need to make more than  one commit, use:

$ git commit --amend

# the editor will pop up and i can completely redo my commit msg -- my new message completely overwrites the old one and i have just one commit - no changed history



# push commits to GitHub -- the feature branch "issue-123" doesn't already have to exist on GitHub - git will automatically create it there

$ git checkout issue-123

$ git push origin issue-123

# if i want to do a dry run to see what git will do before actually pushing:

$ git push -n origin issue-123



# Now that GitHub has my issue-123 changes, submit a [WIP] pull request, using the GitHub "Create draft pull request" option.

# Additional steps will likely take place with feedback on the PR, but to be continued at a later date. Just wanted to start with "first things first."


********* end git cheat sheet ************

```

Will that work?

Thx,
L

**Mateusz Mandera** · 2019-07-10 23:14 UTC

@Laurel Michaels One comment I have is that if you
```
1. Do some work
2. commit
3. push to your github
4. Oh, new commits in upstream/master,  let's git fetch and rebase.
```
After this rebase, your next push needs to be with `` --force ``.  So `` git push -f origin issue-123 ``. That's because you're "changing history", so it requires the `` -f `` to confirm you're aware of things.

**Mateusz Mandera** · 2019-07-10 23:16 UTC

Same if you make a commit, push it, realize you need to fix something, so you amend it, when you push again you need it with `` -f ``.

**Laurel Michaels** · 2019-07-10 23:26 UTC

Thanks for the tips @Mateusz Mandera

```python
def notify_new_user(user_profile: UserProfile, internal: bool=False) -> None:

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-07-18 19:41 UTC

@Rishi Gupta for context, statsd is a thing for doing realtime graphs of rates of things happening.  It is not in general the sort of thing deprecated by analytics.  It's also not a tool anyone has run with Zulip since 2016.  

It's debateable as to whether we should keep the code for it because we're likely to want to do some sort of similar graphing thing down the line with a similar API, but it's also likely we won't do that for a long time.

**Aditya Bansal** · 2019-07-19 21:29 UTC

Hey @Wyatt Hoodes 
yeah that commit was aimed at fixing this kinda things only. Basically the idea was that, whenever a bot was added or removed from the setting, we should rebuild the DB.
Thing is this basically added an optional parameter to the `template_database_status` function called `check_settings` which is basically a list of settings that should be checked in order to decide whether to rebuild DB or not.
Right now nobody supplies that setting to that function and therefore the default list that I used is the only list of settings checked. That default list only included `REALM_INTERNAL_BOTS` settings.

I never included the `INTERNAL_BOTS` setting there because from understanding once a Zulip server is installed and the `zulip/zerver/management/commands/initialize_voyager_db.py` has been ran (which actually creates the internal bots mentioned in the INTERNAL_BOTS setting) even if we modify the setting INTERNAL_BOT there is no code path which translates that update in the INTERNAL_BOTS setting to the actual DB.
I believe since I was in process of migrating things to REALM_INTERNAL_BOTS it made sense to just include that setting because that was the setting which actually affected DB whenever updated.

PS: One can easily start passing in the `check_settings` parameter and get those specific settings checked up before deciding if DB should be rebuilt.

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-07-19 23:14 UTC

Note that `populate_db` never runs `initialize_voyager_db`

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-07-19 23:15 UTC

But I think we should include `INTERNAL_BOTS` on the list as well.

`EXTERNAL_HOST` is the example here, and it's defined in `prod_settings_template` as a `string` and is imported via

from .prod_settings_template import *
```

**Wyatt Hoodes** · 2019-07-23 23:15 UTC

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-07-23 23:44 UTC

That, or this change, which is likely cleaner in that it correctly preserves the fact that `EXTERNAL_HOST` is a str, not an `Optional[str]`:
```
diff --git a/zproject/dev_settings.py b/zproject/dev_settings.py
index 5bf8cb0f9c..a6a4d00264 100644
--- a/zproject/dev_settings.py
+++ b/zproject/dev_settings.py
@@ -14,8 +14,8 @@ LOCAL_UPLOADS_DIR = os.path.join(DEPLOY_ROOT, 'var/uploads')
 
 FORWARD_ADDRESS_CONFIG_FILE = "var/forward_address.ini"
 # Check if test_settings.py set EXTERNAL_HOST.
-EXTERNAL_HOST = os.getenv('EXTERNAL_HOST')
-if EXTERNAL_HOST is None:
+EXTERNAL_HOST_ENV = os.getenv('EXTERNAL_HOST')
+if EXTERNAL_HOST_ENV is None:
     user_id = os.getuid()
     user_name = pwd.getpwuid(user_id).pw_name
     if user_name == "zulipdev":
@@ -31,6 +31,7 @@ if EXTERNAL_HOST is None:
             'zulip': 'localhost:9991'
         }
 else:
+    EXTERNAL_HOST = EXTERNAL_HOST_ENV
     REALM_HOSTS = {
         'zulip': EXTERNAL_HOST,
     }
```

**Wyatt Hoodes** · 2019-07-24 00:15 UTC

**Tommy Ip** · 2019-07-24 06:38 UTC

How does one serve a single file from django? I want to have a dev url `^static/source-map.wasm$` point to `node_modules/source-map/lib/mapping.wasm`. Do I use the `url` function like the other paths in `zproject/dev_urls.py`?

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2019-07-24 07:27 UTC

I’m pretty sure you want that to be taken care of by webpack, not Django.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2019-07-24 07:43 UTC

Hmm…I think you’ve found quite a rabbit hole here.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2019-07-24 07:57 UTC

https://github.com/webpack/webpack/issues/8412

**Tommy Ip** · 2019-07-24 08:05 UTC

Cool I will have a look at those

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2019-07-24 08:10 UTC

This should do the trick.
```diff
--- a/tools/webpack.config.ts
+++ b/tools/webpack.config.ts
@@ -106,7 +106,11 @@ export default (env?: string): webpack.Configuration[] => {
                 },
                 // load fonts and files
                 {
-                    test: /\.(woff(2)?|ttf|eot|svg|otf|png)$/,
+                    test: [
+                        /\.(woff(2)?|ttf|eot|svg|otf|png)$/,
+                        require.resolve("source-map/lib/mappings.wasm"),
+                    ],
+                    type: "javascript/auto",
                     use: [{
                         loader: 'file-loader',
                         options: {
```
and then in the code
```js
const mappingsWasmUrl = require("source-map/lib/mappings.wasm");
```

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2019-07-24 08:12 UTC

(On the theory that we don’t necessarily want to disable webpack’s special treatment of all `.wasm` files, just this one.)

## generic_bulk_cached_fetch argument types

*2019-08-07 to 2019-08-08 · 13 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/generic_bulk_cached_fetch.20argument.20types/with/776978)*

**Mateusz Mandera** · 2019-08-07 16:00 UTC

After struggling against this for a bit, I think some of the types are not general enough? For reference:
```
def generic_bulk_cached_fetch(
        cache_key_function: Callable[[ObjKT], str],
        query_function: Callable[[List[ObjKT]], Iterable[Any]],
        object_ids: Iterable[ObjKT],
        extractor: Callable[[CompressedItemT], ItemT] = default_extractor,
        setter: Callable[[ItemT], CompressedItemT] = default_setter,
        id_fetcher: Callable[[ItemT], ObjKT] = default_id_fetcher,
        cache_transformer: Callable[[ItemT], ItemT] = default_cache_transformer
) -> Dict[ObjKT, ItemT]:
```

`` query_function `` returns `` Iterable[Any]``, which seems right - it returns some database objects, which could be anything.
But now:
`` id_fetcher `` is supposed to take one of those database objects and return the id - but according to its type, it takes ``ItemT`` - that doesn't seem correct, as we just said database objects should be ``Any``.
Same for `` cache_transformer `` - it's supposed to take a db_object and convert it to a cache object. But according to the type it takes ``ItemT``. Again I think the argument type should be ``Any `` - the database object can be anything.

So to sum up, I think we should have:
```
 id_fetcher: Callable[[Any], ObjKT] = default_id_fetcher,
cache_transformer: Callable[[Any], ItemT] = default_cache_transformer
```

on these arguments?

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-08-07 19:13 UTC

@Mateusz Mandera I think `ItemT` is supposed to be a typevar for the database object, though?

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-08-07 19:14 UTC

So that should be anything; the requirement is just that the `extractor` and `cache_transformer` and `id_fetcher` use a consistent database class here.

**Mateusz Mandera** · 2019-08-07 19:18 UTC

It looks to me that ``ItemT`` is supposed to be the object in "cache-form":
For example:
```
cached_objects = {}  # type: Dict[str, ItemT]
    for (key, val) in cached_objects_compressed.items():
        cached_objects[key] = extractor(cached_objects_compressed[key][0])
```

Perhaps instead of ``Any`` like I suggested, we could have a new TypeVar, but separate from ItemT :thinking:  To enforce the consistency between ``id_fetcher`` and ``cache_transformer``. I don't think we want consistency with `` extractor ``, because extractor takes a compressed cache object to a cache object. `` cache_transformer `` should be taking a database object to a cache object I think.

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-08-07 19:20 UTC

**Mateusz Mandera** · 2019-08-07 19:27 UTC

In the uses we have so far I think the difference I'm describing doesn't manifest, but here's an example of what I'm trying to do where it demonstrates:

The display_recipient cache: For PERSONAL recipient, the "database object" is the corresponding ``UserProfile``.  The "cache object" is the `` display_recipient`` object for it - so a dictionary storing the email, full name etc. 

So ``query_function`` maps ids to UserProfiles. ``id_fetcher`` maps UserProfiles to `` recipient_ids `` they came from. `` cache_transformer `` maps UserProfiles to the ``display_recipient`` dictionaries - and the dictionaries are what we'd cache.

**Hemanth V. Alluri** · 2019-08-08 10:06 UTC

@Arslan, it's just basic Python. There's nothing special is going on here (all you have to so is use the `bot_handler` that `handle_message` gets). So assuming that `process` is a function that you're defining, then you could do something like:
```python3
class NormHandler(object):
    def usage(self) -> str:
        return "This is a special bot made by Dr.Doof"
   
    def process(self, message: Dict[str, Any], bot_handler: Any) -> str:
        if "perry" in message["content"].lower():
            try:
                pc = bot_handler.storage.get("perry_count")
            except:
                pc = 0
            pc += 1
            bot_handler.storage.put("perry_count", pc)
            return "It's PERRY! Perry the PLATYPUS! He broke in {} times!".format(pc)
        return "Hi there! I'm Norm."

    def handle_message(self, message: Dict[str, Any], bot_handler: Any) -> None:
        content = self.process(message, bot_handler)
        bot_handler.send_reply(message, content)

handler_class = NormHandler
```

## macOS Vagrant changes

*2019-08-09 to 2019-08-16 · 15 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/macOS.20Vagrant.20changes/with/778122)*

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-08-09 23:50 UTC

So, we're looking at merging https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/12963, which will remove use of NFS as the host/guest file synchronization system on macOS, returning to the default Vagrant system for that.  For background, a few years ago, we switched to NFS because the guests started crashing every ~30 minutes after some update to non-Zulip software (and the NFS thing had less bad problems).  In theory, this transition will likely improve development environment performance on macOS.

I'd really appreciate it if folks who use macOS tested this PR to make sure that Vagrant development works with it, and commented here on how it went (succeed or fail), so we can be confident in merging this.

        result = self.client_get('/json/users?client_gravatar=true')
        self.assert_json_success(result)
        members = result.json()['members']
        hamlet = find_dict(members, 'user_id', user.id)
        self.assertEqual(hamlet['email'], "user%s@zulip.testserver" % (user.id,))

This last line fails:
```
======================================================================
FAIL: test_admin_api_hide_emails (zerver.tests.test_users.PermissionTest)
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/srv/zulip/zerver/tests/test_users.py", line 220, in test_admin_api_hide_emails
    self.assertEqual(hamlet['avatar_url'], "https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/5106fb7f928d89e2f2ddb3c4c42d6949?d=identicon&version=1")
AssertionError: 'http[23 chars]/avatar/638dfff153d3934dc10f8dc2cab47f7e?d=identicon&version=1' != 'http[23 chars]/avatar/5106fb7f928d89e2f2ddb3c4c42d6949?d=identicon&version=1'
```

I don't understand what exactly is going on - in what way do the assigned gravatar urls change, if the user id changes? :thinking: 
And how should this be handled to get the intended url more "dynamically" - I don't think we should have a completely hard-coded one here?

**Mateusz Mandera** · 2019-08-13 21:58 UTC

As a small explanatory note: my populate_db changes cause the order in which users are created to be changed - so the ids get renumbered compared to what they used to be.

**Rohitt Vashishtha** · 2019-08-13 22:03 UTC

Gravatars are similar to hashing a string, here, email. Since our email format for this test appears to be `user{user.id}@zulip.testserver`, the email changes when the user id is changed.

On a simple search, I found this link on the first page of Google that should be able to help you generate the new urls needed (to cross check with the output of the tests)

https://codepen.io/TimPietrusky/pen/xfdKD

**Rohitt Vashishtha** · 2019-08-13 22:06 UTC

The exact algorithm is basically `hash = email.strip().toLower().md5()`. You can read about it here: https://en.gravatar.com/site/implement/hash/

**Mateusz Mandera** · 2019-08-19 02:16 UTC

Okay, I'm back on this finally :sweat_smile:

``get_gravatar_url(hamlet['email'], 1)`` - this produces the same url as the link, so that's additional confirmation things are okay.

I think it's more reasonable to replace the hardcoded urls with these ``get_gravatar_url`` calls, than to change the old hardcoded urls to new, correct ones but still hard-coded?

**Rohitt Vashishtha** · 2019-08-19 09:46 UTC

Yes, that sounds like a better solution @Mateusz Mandera.

*2019-08-19 to 2019-08-19 · 2 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/operator.20sorting.20and.20levels.20.3F/with/781018)*

**Mohit Gupta** · 2019-08-19 21:28 UTC

I am adding a new filter operator for search bar. I encountered some `levels` variable in some kind of sort routine. Code in doubt from filter.js is as follow:
```
Filter.sorted_term_types = function (term_types) {
    var levels = [
        'stream', 'topic',
        'pm-with', 'group-pm-with', 'sender',
        'near', 'id',
        'is-alerted', 'is-mentioned', 'is-private',
        'is-starred', 'is-unread',
        'has-link', 'has-image', 'has-attachment',
        'search',
    ];

    function level(term_type) {
        var i = levels.indexOf(term_type);
        if (i === -1) {
            i = 999;
        }
        return i;
    }

    function compare(a, b) {
        var diff = level(a) - level(b);
        if (diff !== 0) {
            return diff;
        }
        return util.strcmp(a, b);
    }

    return _.clone(term_types).sort(compare);
};

**Mateusz Mandera** · 2019-08-29 00:29 UTC

In ``initialize_voyager_db.py`` there are these two mysterious lines:
```
        get_client("website")
        get_client("API")
```

I found [this](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/commit/97e9615921e8c680021a943c08fbce7b02671052#diff-74d9a978c5004b807abd93037eed4062)old commit with a comment giving some context to them, but it's been deleted since and I'm not sure if that even applies anymore in any sense?
```
        # Create the "website" and "API" clients; if we don't, the
        # default values in zerver/decorators.py will not work
        # with the Django test suite.
        get_client("website")
        get_client("API")
```

What is the role of these calls nowadays?

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-08-29 00:29 UTC

@Mateusz Mandera ahh, I can explain that.

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-08-29 00:32 UTC

I think the purpose in `populate_db` (there's a copy there) is to ensure that the default `Client` value of `website` exists in the initialized database; we probably want it there.

If I had to guess, it was copy-pasted from `populate_db` into `initialize_voyager_db` when we created that during the Hack Week to get Zulip open sourced.

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-08-29 00:36 UTC

So my belief is that (1) `get_client("API")` is useless and should be deleted everywhere; we haven't used that as a `client` string in a long time.  (2) It's potentially useful to call `get_client("website")` for convenience to make sure that (default for browsers) value has ID 1, but my guess is things would work in production if we deleted that too (we likely want it in development to avoid creating a new row for it on every test that makes an HTTP request).

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-08-29 00:38 UTC

(I'm pretty sure that code is a relic from before we had our test suite setup to change the memcached key prefix before each test, and thus the issue was that we needed `get_client`, which uses a cache, to always return an object with the same ID in the unit tests)

**Mateusz Mandera** · 2019-08-29 00:44 UTC

okay, interesting, thanks!

**Eric Gumba** · 2019-08-29 06:15 UTC

https://github.com/zulip/zulip/issues/12784

As the topic says, I am not sure how to go about solving it, all I've done so far is try using `git grep /activity` , `git grep model_name='confirmation'` , and `git grep /support.` and have a vague idea that this is probably a front-end task maybe either in static/js directory or zerver/view directory. Also maybe when someone enters an email `email` in the search bar it redirects to something like `zulip/org/activity/support/email`. 

However, I'm not sure which file is responsible for searching for activity and preregistration table.

Does anyone have any advice on how I can make progress on this? Thanks.

**Hemanth V. Alluri** · 2019-08-29 07:09 UTC

@Eric Gumba  have you worked with Django before? If not I recommend that you complete the [official tutorial](https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/2.2/intro/tutorial01/) first as that would help you make much more sense of what's going on the backend (as well as give you a fair idea of the full stack implementation).

Having said that, I can give you a gist of how you can approach doing recon for this issue. Since a URL was mentioned we can easily analyse which frontend and backend components use it or are mapped to by it.

A good place to look at first is `zprojects/urls.py`, here you can find out which backend view(s) is/are involved and all of the related helper functions. With this you'll get a good idea of what is involved on the backend side (e.g. is this a callable endpoint for POSTing to or is this more of a GET-type endpoint?). Now for the frontend side, you're on the right track. Grepping `/static` to see which JS functions potentially contact the endpoint would give you an idea of which frontend files are involved. If that doesn't yield enough info, then try to visit the page in the development environment and see if you can find unique strings on that page (like headers) and then grep `templates/` and `static/` for them and you should find some more relevant files.

Once you've found the files, the rest is just figuring out how you want to implement a solution (I recommend discussing the solution in the appropriate stream first before actually going ahead with it, if you're unsure about your approach).

Oh, seems that finally I dug out the function that does specifically the search part of the work:
```
    def _search_for_user_dn(self):
        """
        Searches the directory for a user matching AUTH_LDAP_USER_SEARCH.
        Populates self._user_dn and self._user_attrs.
        """
        search = self.settings.USER_SEARCH
        if search is None:
            raise ImproperlyConfigured(
                "AUTH_LDAP_USER_SEARCH must be an LDAPSearch instance."
            )

        results = search.execute(self.connection, {"user": self._username})
        if results is not None and len(results) == 1:
            (user_dn, self._user_attrs) = next(iter(results))
        else:
            user_dn = None

        return user_dn
```

It returns ``None`` if more than one match was found? I don't think it's that great for us, so I think it could be best to just do this in a custom way and have code like

user = _LDAPUser(backend, email)

  # yes, email belongs to ldap
```

This is icky, but I don't know what better we can do, since the module doesn't provide a proper API for doing custom searches like this.
