## Adding a new daemon to run in production

*2019-09-07 to 2019-09-11 · 3 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/Adding.20a.20new.20daemon.20to.20run.20in.20production/with/785373)*

**Mateusz Mandera** · 2019-09-07 18:02 UTC

So I'm figuring out how to do [Improve placement of rate-limiting for email mirror](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/issues/12501). To describe briefly, I think the design would be to configure postfix to use a [policy delegation server](http://www.postfix.org/SMTPD_POLICY_README.html) so that it would connect on a unix socket to a python daemon (seems best to use Twisted for this) that will process its requests about emails incoming to the email gateway. The current email gateway rate-limiting code would be just moved into the Twisted daemon.

Now, this brings a question - what would be the best way to go about adding an additional daemon that should be run in production? Just adding appropriate configuration in ``puppet/zulip/templates/supervisor/zulip.conf.template.erb``?

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-09-07 21:21 UTC

@Mateusz Mandera I think it makes sense to use a separate configuration file installed to e.g. `/etc/supervisor/conf.d/zulip-postfix.conf`, since that's easier to do with making this daemon conditional on whether `postfix_localmail` is configured.

**Mateusz Mandera** · 2019-09-11 22:32 UTC

The daemon seems to be working nicely with postfix now, I'm just having some issues with configuring things:

The way our master.cf is setup, smtpd gets run inside chroot (in /var/spool/postfix). My daemon opens a unix socket, that postfix is supposed to be configured to connect to to make its requests. But because of the chroot, of course if the socket is outside /var/spool/postfix then smtpd can't access it.

I'm struggling to figure out how to make things work  - the socket should be created somewhere in the chroot directory, but since the daemon is run via ``manage.py``, it runs as the ``zulip`` user and doesn't have the permission to mess with that directory.

For testing I just changed the master.cf config to make smtpd run without chroot and things seems to be going well. But that's lazy for a "solution". Can this be configured in a nice way, or should the chroot really be disabled? I'm not sure how to proceed here.


## test-backend output

*2019-09-10 to 2019-09-12 · 9 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/test-backend.20output/with/785691)*

**Wyatt Hoodes** · 2019-09-10 00:17 UTC

Hey @Tim Abbott just a couple of quick clarifications:
* Regarding the usage of `subTest`in `test_management_commands`, are we looking to remove all `Test management command for: ...`output by using `subTest` to only show said output upon failure?
* Similarly, we also have the use of `subTest` implemented regarding `test_bugdown_fixtures`, do we want to simply remove the `print` statement that outputs each fixture being tested?

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-09-10 22:17 UTC

@Wyatt Hoodes re: `test_management_commands` yes, that's correct; the purpose of that print output was just to make failures reasonably debuggable

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-09-10 22:17 UTC

(And same for `test_bugdown_fixtures`; if it's easy to understand failures, we probably don't need the extra print)

**Wyatt Hoodes** · 2019-09-10 23:47 UTC

cool, thanks

**Wyatt Hoodes** · 2019-09-12 20:05 UTC

Looking at this more, now I'm curious why using the `stdout_suppressed` context manager isn't suppressing this print statement (also why make the extra effort to print something to `/dev/null` at all)?
```python
        with stdout_suppressed() as stdout:
            for command in self.commands:
                print('Testing management command: {}'.format(command),
                      file=stdout)
```

`stdout_suppressed` also appears to only be used in `test_management_commands_show_help`.  Do we need to keep this function around?

**Wyatt Hoodes** · 2019-09-12 20:08 UTC

Okay, so it seems setting the `file` parameter to `stdout` is why this wasn't being suppressed.

**Wyatt Hoodes** · 2019-09-12 20:11 UTC

Though I'm a little unclear as to why that should be the case.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2019-09-12 20:21 UTC

`stdout_suppressed()` yields the original `stdout`, not `/dev/null`.

**Wyatt Hoodes** · 2019-09-12 21:02 UTC

Ahh okay, I see, this should have been obvious.  It's suppressing the help messages and printing "Testing management command..." by setting the file back to the original `stdout`.

**Leni** · 2019-09-15 18:06 UTC

Hi. New to the Zulip project. I notice that usage of Docker to set up Zulip is still considered experimental according to the `README` here: https://github.com/zulip/docker-zulip. From the `README`:
> The core Zulip community recently adopted this project, and hasn't yet cleaned it up to our satisfaction. We recommend using the normal Zulip installer for production usage.

**Leni** · 2019-09-15 18:08 UTC

Because I would love to use a Docker container instead. I find it much easier to setup dependencies that way since finding one's way around software packaging in Linux  is something I have found tricky when it comes to installing dependencies of an open source project.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2019-09-16 20:13 UTC

@Leni Kadali Mutungi The normal Zulip installer fetches all dependencies for itself—you need only give it an Ubuntu system (which we recommend should be a fresh machine/VM/container dedicated to Zulip). If you are comfortable enough with Docker to dive in and troubleshoot things yourself, Docker may still be a good option for you. But if you want a polished experience where you don’t have to deal with tricky issues, we recommend the normal installer.

**Mateusz Mandera** · 2019-09-15 22:05 UTC

From ``settings.py``:
```
DATABASES = {"default": {
    'ENGINE': 'django.db.backends.postgresql',
    'NAME': 'zulip',
    'USER': 'zulip',
    'PASSWORD': '',  # Authentication done via certificates
    'HOST': '',  # Host = '' => connect through a local socket
    'SCHEMA': 'zulip',
    'CONN_MAX_AGE': 600,
    'OPTIONS': {
        'connection_factory': TimeTrackingConnection
    },
}}
```
And in the puppet ``postgresql/pg_hba.conf`` file:
```
# Zulip app frontends access the zulip user
hostssl zulip           zulip           172.31.0.0/16           cert
```

So if I understand correctly, the connection happens on an SSL authenticated TCP socket. But I'm unable to find (on my test production instance) where the certificates are stored, and can't see in the code where they're generated. What am I missing? :thinking:

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-09-16 23:11 UTC

@Mateusz Mandera see the block around `LOCAL_DATABASE_PASSWORD` further down.

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-09-16 23:11 UTC

There's actually 3 models for how this can work: 
* password auth via that setting
* `peer` auth (if database is on localhost)
* cert auth

By default, production with everything on one server uses `peer` auth, so that comment is wrong.  I'll fix this.

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-09-16 23:13 UTC

Actually, that's not accurate; default is password auth in production.

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-09-16 23:31 UTC

Actually, my original understanding was correct; sigh.  About to merge comments explaining this correctly.

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-09-16 23:33 UTC

0a426c6a445f6ee2ab92cf785bbb64cd78ec43d4

**Mateusz Mandera** · 2019-09-16 23:39 UTC

Ohh, okay, now it's clear with the added comments, thanks!

**Mateusz Mandera** · 2019-09-16 23:44 UTC

On second thought, what's the purpose of these lines in ``puppet/zulip_ops/files/postgresql/pg_hba.conf`` then?
```
# Zulip app frontends access the zulip user
hostssl zulip           zulip           172.31.0.0/16           cert
# Zulip replication accesses the replicator user
hostssl replication     replicator      172.31.0.0/16           cert
```

if I understand correctly, this config file gets installed locally,  but in local scenarios we don't do the cert-based SSL authentication?

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-09-16 23:56 UTC

That configuration enables certificate authentication from some IP address blocks for only for two users: the `zulip` user and the `replicator` user (an internal `postgres` thing for its full-text replication).  Note also that config file is from the `zulip_ops` section, not something we distribute for installations outside zulipchat.com.

**Mateusz Mandera** · 2019-09-17 20:37 UTC

So, here's the situation:
python_social_auth for using the saml backend, requires ``python3-saml``.  Sounds easy, that can just be added the usual way for python modules we need.
But - it ends up pulling in ``python-xmlsec`` https://github.com/mehcode/python-xmlsec . And as can be seen in the README, this requires some system packages to be installed before:
``apt-get install libxml2-dev libxmlsec1-dev libxmlsec1-openssl``
or ``pip`` will fail.

How should that be handled? Making those packages required when installing zulip, and then normally adding ``python3-saml`` to ``requirements/common.in`` (and prod.txt, dev.txt)? Or some kind of setup to make it optional to fetch all this stuff for installations that will want to use SAML - would puppet be used for this somehow? (our [doc](https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/subsystems/dependencies.html#system-packages) doesn't really go into how to add system packages in general).

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2019-09-17 21:02 UTC

Those packages are probably reasonable to pull in unconditionally.

## SAML social auth tests

*2019-09-23 to 2019-09-27 · 19 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/SAML.20social.20auth.20tests/with/788170)*

**Mateusz Mandera** · 2019-09-23 22:10 UTC

So I'm reading into our sociai auth tests via ``SocialAuthBase``, and I can see that we get around the inability to access necessary external URLs by essentially "mocking" them via httpretty to return specific HTTP responses when the test makes requests to them.

I don't have any good idea for how to do this for SAML though. Here is the authentication flow as far as I understand:
1. User clicks the "sign in with saml" button.
2. Running through the python-social-auth saml internals, we end up redirecting the user to the IdP (let's say Okta) with a base64-encoded ``SAMLRequest`` in GET.
3. Okta reads the ``SAMLRequests`` and authenticates the user on its own side.
And here's where the difficulty arises:
4. Okta redirects the user to us, to the ``/complete/saml/`` endpoint with a base-64 ``SAMLResponse`` (info about the authenticated user, with okta's digital signature) in ``POST``. 
5. python-social-auth processes the SAMLResponse and sends it further down the pipeline, where we form the UserProfile objects etc.

I believe it's not possible to REDIRECT with POST via pure HTTP, and the redirection in point 4 must be done through Javascript? So it doesn't seem possible to mock the behavior of the IdP via httpretty :thinking: And we can't simplify this by redirecting and sending the SAMLResponse in ``GET``, because the ``/complete/saml`` endpoint requires it  to come via ``POST`` and I don't think the module even supports configuring for GET.

Can something be done here to test SAML using our "social test" framework somehow, or will taking a different approach be needed here? :thinking:

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2019-09-23 22:19 UTC

I think you should feel free to extend our test framework as needed. There’s already a redirect-related special case in `verify_backend` for `SocialAuthMixin`.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2019-09-23 22:21 UTC

Isn’t `httpretty` being used to mock the backend server-to-server communication invisible to the browser, not the browser-visible redirects?

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2019-09-23 22:29 UTC

What our test needs to verify is that (a) sending our server the GET request of step 1 yields the redirect response of step 2, and then (b) sending our server the POST request of step 4 yields a successful authentication. This doesn’t require mocking the game of browser ping-pong that happens in between.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2019-09-23 22:33 UTC

This seems to be how `social_auth_test` works.

**Mateusz Mandera** · 2019-09-23 22:44 UTC

Yeah, I think you're right. Okay, this should be much more doable now, thanks!

**Mateusz Mandera** · 2019-09-24 01:28 UTC

Hmm, I'm running into a difficulty with `` (b) sending our server the POST request of step 4 yields a successful authentication``.
The SAMLResponse contains time-limiting attributes - things like NotOnAfter in `` <saml2:Conditions NotBefore="2019-09-24T00:07:03.707Z" NotOnOrAfter="2019-09-24T00:17:03.707Z">``. Which say that the Assertions are invalid after a certain time. So an otherwise successful SAMLResponse should result in rejected authentication if the current time is not within the specified limits.

Dynamically generating a correct SAMLResponse during the tests doesn't seem feasible - a lot of complexity. So I was going for grabbing a valid okta-generated SAMLResponse to use as a fixture. But the timestamps are an issue now - the responses have to be signed, so the tests can't just alter those time bounds in the Response - the signatures will break.

Any ideas for a better approach here than diving into the internals of the SAML libraries to find where to ``mock.patch``  ``time.time`` (or some equivalent that the internals use) to make the current time match the time bounds specified in the Response, so the modules accept it?

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-09-24 19:39 UTC

Hmm, good question.  I'd expect mocking `time.time` or datetime around the block to work pretty well, and to likely be a better experience (in terms of the resulting code readability) than doing a find-replace of those properties.  But if that isn't workable, I think it shouldn't be too hard to parse the XML with `lxml`.

**Mateusz Mandera** · 2019-09-24 20:00 UTC

I finished my library diving last night with the conclusion that it should be doable with a pretty reasonable mocking of ``Onelogin_Saml2_Auth.is_valid()`` to always return True, so I'm going to try that.
The issue with XML-parsing approach is that then we'd have to figure out how exactly to sign the SAML response (changing the NotOnOrAfter attributes will break the existing signatures), which seems potentially time consuming and also worse for readability of the test code.

Yeah, giving the signing, mocking time might not do the right thing either, so sounds good.

**Richard Gregory** · 2019-10-01 15:25 UTC

Hi! I need help concerning an issue!
I get the error below when running tools/provision
```
Cached version not found! Installing node modules.
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "./lib/provision.py", line 410, in <module>
    main(options)
  File "./lib/provision.py", line 349, in main
    setup_node_modules(prefer_offline=True)
  File "/srv/zulip/scripts/lib/node_cache.py", line 66, in setup_node_modules
    stderr=stderr)
  File "/srv/zulip/scripts/lib/node_cache.py", line 86, in do_yarn_install
    shutil.copytree("node_modules/", cached_node_modules)
  File "/srv/zulip-py3-venv/lib/python3.6/shutil.py", line 321, in copytree
    os.makedirs(dst)
  File "/srv/zulip-py3-venv/lib/python3.6/os.py", line 220, in makedirs
    mkdir(name, mode)
FileExistsError: [Errno 17] File exists: '/srv/zulip-npm-cache/20d1346db5e686834931f3e124d72adae1bed08e/node_modules'

Provisioning failed (exit code 1)!
```

**Vishnu KS** · 2019-10-01 16:01 UTC

@Richard Gregory Delete `/srv/zulip-npm-cache/20d1346db5e686834931f3e124d72adae1bed08e/node_modules` and run provision again.

**Richard Gregory** · 2019-10-01 17:22 UTC

@Vishnu Ks that worked. Thank you!

**David Rosa** · 2019-10-24 00:19 UTC

I got the same error. The problem is "the destination directory, named by dst, must not already exist" when `shutil.copytree("node_modules/", cached_node_modules, symlinks=True)` gets called. https://docs.python.org/3.6/library/shutil.html#shutil.copytree

**David Rosa** · 2019-10-24 00:21 UTC

A possible solution that seems to work would be to use
`dir_util.copy_tree("node_modules/", cached_node_modules, preserve_symlinks=False, update=True)` instead.

https://docs.python.org/3.6/distutils/apiref.html#distutils.dir_util.copy_tree:
> If dst does not exist, it is created with mkpath()
> If preserve_symlinks is true, symlinks will be copied as symlinks
> If update is true, src will only be copied if dst does not exist, or if dst does exist but is older than src.

However, I think `preserve_symlinks` should be `False` so that the destination of the symlink will be copied?

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2019-10-24 00:25 UTC

We need symlinks to be preserved as symlinks. Certain JS modules rely on them.

**David Rosa** · 2019-10-24 00:35 UTC

I replicated the error by removing the `.success-stamp` file and tried using `dir_util.copy_tree` with `preserve_symlinks=True` but it gave a similar error, this time, caused by a symlink though:
```bash
FileExistsError: [Errno 17] File exists: '../../../glslify/bin.js' -> '/srv/zulip-npm-cache/145a077ad01a840e0c40412b052ad55639ff87ad/node_modules/gl-error3d/node_modules/.bin/glslify'
```

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2019-10-24 00:40 UTC

Switching to `dir_util.copy_tree` isn't going to change the fact that this shouldn't have happened to begin with. You should delete `/srv/zulip-npm-cache/145a077ad01a840e0c40412b052ad55639ff87ad` and try again.

**David Rosa** · 2019-10-24 00:56 UTC

Right. I figured manually deleting the entire directory is the current fix, but I also wanted to figure out the root cause ^^ 

Would catching the `FileExistsError` thrown by `shutil.copytree` and handling it by removing the directory make a decent alternative here? If so, I'd like to give that a shot and make a PR.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2019-10-24 00:58 UTC

I mean we could just remove it unconditionally before the copy. But if you really want to figure out the root cause, we'd need to know why it existed in the first place.

**David Rosa** · 2019-10-24 01:01 UTC

Ah okay, got it. I'll investigate a bit more next time I see it happen.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2019-10-24 01:02 UTC

Maybe it would be better to check if `cached_node_modules` exists, and if it does, just skip the copy and let `yarn` do its thing.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2019-10-28 23:47 UTC

I may have figured out a cause for this; it just happened to me after
```
error Your lockfile needs to be updated, but yarn was run with `--frozen-lockfile`.
```
while I was editing `package.json`.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2019-10-29 00:00 UTC

#13335.

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-10-29 19:30 UTC

Ahh, nice.

## creating database for our bot

*2019-10-16 to 2019-10-16 · 8 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/creating.20database.20for.20our.20bot/with/791935)*

**Hemanth V. Alluri** · 2019-10-16 07:02 UTC

Hi @Zia Hazara.
Bots *do* get database access. In a nutshell, your bot is allowed to store key:value pair information using the `bot_handler.storage` API. You can refer to https://zulipchat.com/api/writing-bots#bot_handlerstorage for more information.

**Zia Hazara** · 2019-10-16 07:16 UTC

tnx for response @Hemanth V. Alluri  actually my bot is a little complex i need to have my own database. and its written on its own documentation also that for complex bot you can create your own database

**Hemanth V. Alluri** · 2019-10-16 07:17 UTC

Oh, then, well, you'd need to create and communicate with a database that is **not** the same one that Zulip uses.

**Hemanth V. Alluri** · 2019-10-16 07:18 UTC

At this point it becomes more of a gen development issue (not really related to Zulip anymore).

**Hemanth V. Alluri** · 2019-10-16 07:19 UTC

You would need to create your own database (ideally on the same server where your bot is being served from - though this isn't a requirement) and then communicate with it using the corresponding libraries for it.

## uppy i18n

*2019-10-31 to 2019-11-04 · 7 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/uppy.20i18n/with/795143)*

**Vishnu KS** · 2019-10-31 14:16 UTC

Uppy comes with its own locale pack. Here is an example from the Uppy website. Uppy has locale packs for 27 languages.
```js
const russianLocale = require('@uppy/locales/lib/ru_RU')
// ^-- OR: import russianLocale from '@uppy/locales/lib/ru_RU'
const uppy = Uppy({
  locale: russianLocale,
})
```

There is also an option to override the strings used by Uppy. That means we can provide our own strings and translations. 
```js
locale: {
  strings: {
    youCanOnlyUploadX: {
      0: 'You can only upload %{smart_count} file',
      1: 'You can only upload %{smart_count} files'
    },
    youHaveToAtLeastSelectX: {
      0: 'You have to select at least %{smart_count} file',
      1: 'You have to select at least %{smart_count} files'
    },
    exceedsSize: 'This file exceeds maximum allowed size of',
    youCanOnlyUploadFileTypes: 'You can only upload: %{types}',
    companionError: 'Connection with Companion failed'
  }
}
```
I am thinking of going with the first approach, ie making use of the locale packs suppllied by Uppy instead of managing this by ourselves. Let me know if this doesnt makes sense. 
https://uppy.io/docs/uppy/#locale

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-10-31 20:52 UTC

@Vishnu Ks that sounds good to me.  No reason to duplicate work on this stuff.  Though we might need to pass to the library what language to use from our i18n code.

**Vishnu KS** · 2019-11-01 13:09 UTC

Okay. I tried using the locale that came with Uppy. This turned out to be a bit more tricky than I expected. Issue was that the [Uppy locale files](https://github.com/transloadit/uppy/tree/master/packages/%40uppy/locales/src)  use a diffrent naming convention than the one used by us. Most of the locale files are named as `{language_code}_{country_code`.  eg en_US.js, ja_JP.js. And some of languages have multiple files in Uppy (eg  sr_RS_Cyrillic.js and sr_RS_Latin.js) while Zulip languages map have only one version of the language. 

I have created mapping of languages that were straightfoward and skipped the complex ones for now. [Here](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/13323/commits/da8e0ad0b6cd19c963d55fa5806c6b829fd4ea02) is the commit. Is there a better way to solve this issue?

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-11-01 17:47 UTC

Hmm, most i18n systems have a fallback system for stripping those suffixes.

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-11-01 17:48 UTC

If there's only like 5 strings I'd switch to the other approach

**Vishnu KS** · 2019-11-04 07:54 UTC

Yeah. But in this case we have to manually require the JS file and pass it to the Uppy object. So we need to take care of the stripping ourselves.

`restore-backup` and `import` fail (as documented) if I try to load output from an old version, and `scripts/upgrade-zulip-from-git` seems to be intended for production – it expects a user and group named `zulip` to exist, which isn't the case in the development VM.

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-11-19 00:52 UTC

Yeah, neither of those is intended to work.

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-11-19 00:52 UTC

Normally, you should be able to just run `provision` on the system after updating what's checked out, and it'll apply migrations to the existing data rather than replacing that data.  However, that won't work if we've changed `populate_db` itself since then.  Your best bet is to just run `manage.py migrate` directly.

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-11-19 01:04 UTC

## tus

*2019-11-28 to 2019-12-02 · 3 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/tus/with/799667)*

**Vishnu KS** · 2019-11-28 11:48 UTC

I have been working on enabling [tus upload protocol](https://tus.io/)  in Zulip server. From what I understand there are mainly two ways of making this work in Django.

*  [django-tus package](https://github.com/alican/django-tus) - This is the djago app reccomended by tus team. In heinsight this is the obvious way  to go forward but unfortunately there has not been any activity in their GitHub repo for the last 2 years. But the good thing is that the package source is not that big and easy to understand.  So we  should be able to fork it and maintain it ourselves.

* The other alternative was to use [tusd](https://github.com/tus/tusd), a stand-alone tus server written in Go actively maintained by tus team. Using tusd means we need to worry about running another service as well integrate it to the the django server using [hooks](https://github.com/tus/tusd/blob/master/docs/hooks.md).

So far I have decided to just fork the django-tus package, make approriate changes to fit it to our upload system.  I would love to hear feedback on this. https://tus.io/faq.html should also be helpful.

**Vishnu KS** · 2019-11-29 12:01 UTC

Did some initial protyping in https://github.com/hackerkid/zulip/tree/tus-backend and https://github.com/hackerkid/django-tus/tree/zulip-integration

Hmm, I'm not sure what the best approach is here.  We'll need to do some research into the options for this sort of thing; this sounds like a potentially significant dependency to add where we'd need to give a lot of thought to security/reliability considerations. ## curl and markdown

*2019-12-05 to 2019-12-06 · 9 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/curl.20and.20markdown/with/800684)*

**Volker** · 2019-12-05 09:41 UTC

When I send a message using curl, the markdown is not interpreted, the message is displayed as is. Can I somehow change that?

**Volker** · 2019-12-05 09:42 UTC

```bash
#/bin/bash

curl -X POST https://chat.example.org/api/v1/messages \
    -u bot@chat.example.org:abcdefg \
    -d "type=stream" \
    -d "to=test" \
    -d "subject=Mittagessen-Tasty" \
    -d $"content=John möchte: 
    * Central Park mini ohne Dressing ohne Brötchen
    * Chicken Wings"
```

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-12-06 01:58 UTC

@Volker markdown is definitely interpreted when posting via the API.  That said, `curl` isn't a great language for doing this sort of thing and I wouldn't be surprised if you have some sort of multi-line shell encoding issue.  Haven't tested your example but we have no mechanism for delivering a message without running the markdown processor on its content.

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-12-06 01:58 UTC

Oh, I guess one question is how you're reading the messages?

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-12-06 01:59 UTC

If you're reading them through the API (and not the UI), the API without the `apply_markdown` flag will send the raw content, not the rendered HTML.

**Volker** · 2019-12-06 08:03 UTC

> Oh, I guess one question is how you're reading the messages?
Not the API, just the regular web-interface.

> `curl` isn't a great language for doing this sort of thing and I wouldn't be surprised if you have some sort of multi-line shell encoding issue
Ok, maybe I'll invest the time to actually do this in Python after all, thanks!

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2019-12-06 08:04 UTC

The most obvious problem with your script as written is that it sends four spaces before each `*`, so Markdown interprets that as normal text continuing the paragraph, not a bulleted list.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2019-12-06 08:06 UTC

According to CommonMark, a list can be indented by at most three spaces. Four spaces would be a code block, except that a code block is not allowed to interrupt a paragraph without an intervening blank line.

**Volker** · 2019-12-06 08:07 UTC

You are 100% correct Sir! Removed the spaces, works like a charm, thank you! :hug:

## ABCs

*2019-12-08 to 2019-12-09 · 4 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/ABCs/with/801038)*

**Mateusz Mandera** · 2019-12-08 21:57 UTC

Do we avoid using python abstract classes via the ``abc`` module on purpose and if so, what are the main reasons that went into that decision? I know they don't "do" much and are never "necessary", but the ability to mark methods that need to be overriden with ``@abstractmethod`` so that classes that don't do it can't even be instantiated seems pretty nice.
```
class RateLimitedObject:
    def get_keys(self) -> List[str]:
        key_fragment = self.key_fragment()
        return ["{}ratelimit:{}:{}".format(KEY_PREFIX, key_fragment, keytype)
                for keytype in ['list', 'zset', 'block']]

    def key_fragment(self) -> str:
        raise NotImplementedError()

    def rules(self) -> List[Tuple[int, int]]:
        raise NotImplementedError()

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        raise NotImplementedError()
```

As an example, if we used ``abc``, I think this class would obviously subclass ``ABC`` and mark these 3 methods with ``@abstractmethod``.

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-12-09 00:34 UTC

@Mateusz Mandera I don't think we do that intentionally.  If I had to guess, the history was that nobody in the early team was familiar with and used to using the `abc` module back in 2013, and that code hasn't been touched much since ~2013.

**Tim Abbott** · 2019-12-09 00:34 UTC

I think if you're going to fix that, I'd recommend doing `git grep NotImplemented` and fixing all of our similar classes.

**Neil Pilgrim (neiljp)** · 2019-12-09 01:03 UTC

I couldn't find it, but for some reason I thought this had come up before and was decided against at the time.

## Promise propogation

*2020-01-15 to 2020-01-15 · 2 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/Promise.20propogation/with/809243)*

**Divyanshu Agrawal** · 2020-01-15 08:07 UTC

Do promise rejections not propogate?
A js function calls another function from within itself, which returns a promise ( that rejects ). On applying a try catch to the outermost function, the catch block never gets executed.

**Divyanshu Agrawal** · 2020-01-15 09:47 UTC

Got it. One must await for the Promise to resolve/reject for it to be catch-able in a try-catch :)

## user_profile.is_mirror_dummy in authentication flow

*2020-01-17 to 2020-01-22 · 4 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/user_profile.2Eis_mirror_dummy.20in.20authentication.20flow/with/809883)*

**Mateusz Mandera** · 2020-01-17 16:25 UTC

In ``login_or_register_remote_user`` there's the block:
```
    if user_profile is None or user_profile.is_mirror_dummy:
        # We have verified the user controls an email address, but
        # there's no associated Zulip user account.  Consider sending
        # the request to registration.
        return maybe_send_to_registration(request, email, full_name, password_required=False,
                                          is_signup=is_signup, multiuse_object_key=multiuse_object_key,
                                          full_name_validated=full_name_validated)
```
This  should lead to ``account_register`` where there's an if to catch the ``is_mirror_dummy`` scenario:
```
        if existing_user_profile is not None and existing_user_profile.is_mirror_dummy:
            user_profile = existing_user_profile
            do_activate_user(user_profile)
            do_change_password(user_profile, password)
            do_change_full_name(user_profile, full_name, user_profile)
            do_set_user_display_setting(user_profile, 'timezone', timezone)
```

can someone explain the role of ``.is_mirror_dummy`` here and why it's handled this way? What is the typical scenario where the login flow (and then registration flow) is run  for a mirror dummy?

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-01-22 23:00 UTC

@Mateusz Mandera yeah, so the `is_mirror_dummy` case is for where we're importing data from another chat system (either 1-time or live), and want to create a user account as the sender for some message history (but who shouldn't be able to login).

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-01-22 23:01 UTC

We created these users with `is_mirror_dummy=True, is_active=False`, and then have a code path for turning those UserProfile objects into a real account if the user later signs up for Zulip (this avoids there being duplicate "Tim Abbott" accounts for messages before and after the user created an account post-migration)

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-01-22 23:01 UTC

It's not a super commonly used corner case, but we do want to avoid breaking it.

**Steve Howell** · 2020-03-02 21:51 UTC

@Chris Bobbe  `./tools/do-destroy-rebuild-database`can help sometimes

**Steve Howell** · 2020-03-02 21:52 UTC

`./manage.py purge_queue` is also occasionally useful

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-03-02 21:56 UTC

Yeah, purging the queue is a workaround.  The error is what happens when we change the format of an event without writing some backwards-compatibility code to migrate existing events.  @Steve Howell I'm not aware of our having changed the format of `presence` events; we should look at whether we need to add code to convert the format.  We added such a format conversion for `delete_message` events when changing the format recently.

**Steve Howell** · 2020-03-02 22:14 UTC

@Tim Abbott I did add the `user_id` field in a672a00677860687d7ea5f506038149402a9baaa but that was almost a month ago.  Given how ephemeral `presence` is here, I think we might just want to drop the event on the floor if `user_id` is missing?

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-03-02 22:16 UTC

Yeah, I think that's a reasonable solution.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-03-02 22:16 UTC

This issue we're seeing in development will also be seen in production -- basically if you upgrade the server at the right moment, you'll end up with one of these events stuck in a queue which can be ugly for a sysadmin to debug.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-03-02 22:17 UTC

@Steve Howell can you submit a PR covering this?

**Chris Bobbe** · 2020-03-02 23:02 UTC

Ah, `git checkout a672a0067^` and `tools/provision` fixed this for me; nothing else (including `./manage.py purge_queue --all`) did.

**Chris Bobbe** · 2020-03-02 23:02 UTC

Thanks both of you!

**Mateusz Mandera** · 2020-03-03 10:21 UTC

Should we perhaps try to work out some system for "migrating" existing events to new format when upgrading the server? Kind of like Django database migrations, but much simpler of course.

**Steve Howell** · 2020-03-03 11:58 UTC

I think that would be way overkill.   I feel like the better solution here is that during an upgrade, we should purge all the transient event queues and rely on the subsequent reload to populate `page_params` with the appropriate data.  I may misunderstand something here, though.

**Steve Howell** · 2020-03-03 12:36 UTC

@Mateusz Mandera @Tim Abbott See #14092 for the fix here.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-03-03 20:04 UTC

Yeah, we don't need a migrations system for this; just the occasional if statement.  We don't change these formats often, in large part because doing so often leads to bugs.  I do think it'd be nice if we could build some sort of tooling that reminds us of the need to think about this issue when making changes to queue worker communication event formats, though.

**Steve Howell** · 2020-03-03 20:46 UTC

The most logical migration for the thing I just fixed would only be accurate and reliable if the old event had user_id instead of email.  And what field was missing? user_id. Oh the irony. 😉

## hierarchical topics

*2020-02-18 to 2020-02-18 · 6 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/hierarchical.20topics/with/817879)*

**Mikko Mäkelä** · 2020-02-18 14:14 UTC

I would like to develop hierarchical topics to Zulip, so that it becomes possible to use Zulip for many more services, like storing information efficiently and having threaded discussions etc. How can I start, which part of the code should I look and would someone be possibly interested in joining this effort?

**Steve Howell** · 2020-02-18 14:30 UTC

@Mikko Mäkelä I think hierarchical topics would be a pretty major change to Zulip, and you probably want to get buy-in on the feature before starting development.  I think there are three possible ways to achieve the underlying goal here, and all of them have tradeoffs:
- instead of hierarchical topics, we could have stream categories (similar to Discord, I believe)
- we could have topics within topics (I feel this is usually more easily accomplished with simple name conventions)
- we could have Slack-style threading on messages

**Mikko Mäkelä** · 2020-02-18 17:45 UTC

Thanks for the reply! What do you think would be tradeoffs in "topics within topics" approach? That might be closest to what I'm looking for, and also I think it might be easiest of them all to implement.

**Steve Howell** · 2020-02-18 18:10 UTC

I don’t have any specific objections, just think you might run into unexpected complexity.  I also slightly prefer the other two options, and they have had some success in other products.  I know Slack threads are somewhat polarizing, but I have found them useful when I have been forced to use Slack.  The Discord stream categories seem easy enough to implement, and I found them super intuitive, but I will concede that they don’t solve quite the problem that I think you are trying to address.

**Steve Howell** · 2020-02-18 18:25 UTC

One thing that Zulip struggles with is that some newbies resist topics at first.  Adding subtopics could potentially aggravate that.  Most users embrace topics after a day or two, but it can be hard to get users past their initial objections.

**Steve Howell** · 2020-02-18 18:27 UTC

I also think that while our topics model is what makes Zulip great, there are still some places we could improve the current topics experience before adding major new features.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-02-20 18:07 UTC

Ahh, the bug here is that `static/generated/pygments_data.js` isn't in `.gitignore`.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-02-20 18:09 UTC

Wait, no, the `.json` path for it (which is where it lives since d7d8632525048120c3be3bc849b3ef96649fdbf4) is in `.gitignore`.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-02-20 18:10 UTC

So why does the IDE think the file is untracked?

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-02-20 18:15 UTC

OK, I think the problem is this:
* We moved the pygments output file last week from a `.js` file to a `.json` file.
* The logic in `provision` knows to rerun the code to build `pygments_data` if the inputs for doing so have changed.  But it doesn't check if the output file exists (i.e. it doesn't assume the user might modify its output files).
* If you're switching and rebasing branches across d7d8632525048120c3be3bc849b3ef96649fdbf4, you'll end up with both `pygments_data.js` and `pygments_data.json` files, which is fine.  If you then discard untracked changes, you'll delete the file not being used in the commit you have checked out.  Which means that if you start on master, check out a branch 2 weeks old, discard untracked changes, and then rebase onto master, you'll end up in this buggy state.

As a sidenote, `tools/provision --force` would have rebuilt it here; it's a hand thing to know about.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-02-20 18:17 UTC

I suppose we could extend our check to see whether the output file exists to prevent this category of bug in the future; would only work for `pygments_data` (not our other similar tooling) since only `pygments_data` has a top-level file under `static/generated`.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-02-20 18:17 UTC

The other thing we could think about doing is making all of `static/generated` sit in `.gitignore`, rather than just specifically named subdirectories.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-02-20 18:26 UTC

I added aaee506fb2c2b766476d84774430ee07b6fc9a55 to address this in the short term.  We might want to revert that in a few months, since it's mostly useful during this filename transition period, and will become more clutter than value then.

**Steve Howell** · 2020-02-20 18:32 UTC

Are we possibly gonna have similar confusion with emoji stuff?  e257253e646b9db023da91dd4af3d755c94c96b6

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-02-20 19:10 UTC

No, because the whole `static/generated/emoji` directory is in `.gitignore`.

**Yash RE** · 2020-02-20 21:28 UTC

Tim, just to be clear here, that file being untracked has *nothing* to do with the ide, it shows up on [git status](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/b3/bpUc8BZjxK9cgL9FAd3bkTa9/image.png)

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-02-20 22:50 UTC

@Yash RE did you see the background?  `pygments.data.js` is not the file that's used these days; it's now in a different format as `pygments_data.json`.  So you can safely remove that file.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-02-20 22:51 UTC

The point is if you now check out a branch from 2 weeks ago, and remove untracked files not in gitignore, you'll delete `pygments_data.json` instead, and then when you switch back to master after doing so, we won't recreate it.

**Yash RE** · 2020-02-20 22:52 UTC

**Hemanth V. Alluri** · 2020-02-26 12:53 UTC

For this issue, rather than trying to reproduce it, try to logically determine the root cause from the error message and the source code. Here's how I'd start:

1. As of commit `6d211e359a`, the actual line number for the where the failure occurred is line number 193 in `rate_limiter.py`. the last commit for this line was `5ba4b1bd4f` - so you can read this commit if you think it's necessary. But let's skip it for now.

2. The error message says:
```
boundary = float(timestamp) + range_seconds
ValueError: could not convert string to float:
```
So this obviously means that the value of timestamp is not something that can be converted to a float. Since there's nothing after the `:` at the end of the message that the **timestamp was an empty string**. Ok, now to backtrack and see where this variable is being used and how it's being populated.

Interestingly enough, on line number 190 we see that we're performing a check to see if the timestamp is explicitly None and not it if it's any falsy value - make a mental note of this.

On line 172, we have:

```python3
rule_timestamps = pipe.execute()  # type: List[Optional[bytes]]
```

Which means that the value is being passed to the process running this code from some other process (Redis as we can see on line 21) via. what I assume to be a Unix pipe (based on the variable name). The redis client is being returned by:
```python3
def get_redis_client() -> redis.StrictRedis:
    return redis.StrictRedis(host=settings.REDIS_HOST, port=settings.REDIS_PORT,
                             password=settings.REDIS_PASSWORD, db=0)
```
in `redis_utils.py`

Now you should read more about the rate limiting system in Zulip (hit the dev docs first).
Then go through the source code for it while paying special attention what "timestamp" here could be (my **guess** is that it is the time of last access or something like that).
Now come back to this code and try see why timestamp is an empty string.
Finally implement the fix. This could be either changing line 190 in `rate_limiter.py` to accept any falsy value (probably **NOT** the actual fix) or it might have arisen from some deeper issue elsewhere in the code where the timestamp is not actually being populated (that's for you to figure out).

I haven't spent any time on the rate limiting system myself so I'll let you take it from here.

 282     # plan_type controls various features around resource/feature

**Vaibhav Raj Singh** · 2020-03-10 21:18 UTC

I was trying to make zulip.yaml work on [swagger online editor](https://editor.swagger.io/). A problem that came up was-
```Structural error at paths./messages.post.responses
should only have three-digit status codes, `default`, and vendor extensions (`x-*`) as properties```

This was due to the fact that there are response messages like `'400_topic_not_muted'` and `'400_topic_already_muted'`. Why and how do we have response codes like these, could I get some info regarding them?

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-03-10 21:40 UTC

@Vaibhav Raj Singh great question!  That's how we currently encode multiple examples for a given endpoint in the API documentation.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-03-10 21:40 UTC

```
(zulip-py3-venv) tabbott@coset:~/zulip$ git grep topic_not_muted
templates/zerver/api/mute-topics.md:{generate_code_example|/users/me/subscriptions/muted_topics:patch|fixture(400_topic_not_muted)}

Yes  `oneOf` will work fine and is a common hack for api endpoints with multiple responses.

**Sahil Batra** · 2020-03-18 18:09 UTC

**Sahil Batra** · 2020-03-18 18:11 UTC

**Sahil Batra** · 2020-03-19 15:47 UTC

@Steve Howell does above question gives enough explaination or do I need to give some more explaination?

**Steve Howell** · 2020-03-19 15:58 UTC

This is how the sequence should work in my opinion:
- In Users (U), deactivate user.  They should not disappear from U. 
- Go to Deactivated Users (DU), do nothing.  You should see the recently deactivated user.
- Go back to U, do nothing.  Not sure whether you should see the user here--I would argue **no**.
- Go back to DU, reactivate the user.  They probably should not disappear from DU.
* Go back to U, do nothing.  You should see the user.
* In U, deactivate and immediately reactivate the user. 
* Go back to DU.  You should not see the user.

**Steve Howell** · 2020-03-19 16:01 UTC

I would summarize this as follows:
* while in a panel, never actually remove users from the relevant list
* when entering Users from any other panel, only show active users
* when entering Deactivated Users from any other panel, only show deactivated users

We'll need @Tim Abbott to confirm all this.

**Steve Howell** · 2020-03-20 14:54 UTC

(replying to Sahil Batra)
> So, I also have to make a change in removal of user from users list after deactivating which now removes after reload but now should be removed once we come to users panel after going to some other panel. And it should be followed for reactivating from deactivated users list. Is this right?

I'm having a hard time understanding your question, but I think I can give you some guidance, anyway:
* Whenever you click a button, do **not** immediately remove a user from the list (so that you can easily re-toggle them in case of a mistake).
* Whenever you enter a screen from somewhere else, make sure you have the up-to-date and non-cluttered version of either "Users" or "Deactivated Users"

I think it's better to just do things properly when entering a screen, rather than having screen A try to notify screen B (which isn't even visible yet) to update its data.

In other words, just make each screen responsible for its own data integrity.

**Rohitt Vashishtha** · 2020-03-19 10:27 UTC

@anubhav_sharma you should pass data to `call_endpoint` in the following manner:

```python
    return self.call_endpoint(
            url='mark_stream_as_read',
            method='POST',
            request={'stream_id': stream_id},
        )
```

In your case, it should become `request={'topic_name': topic_name}`.

**anubhav_sharma** · 2020-03-19 10:35 UTC

@Rohitt Vashishtha  thanks.
worked.
but unable to understand why  request = topicname also didn't work

**Rohitt Vashishtha** · 2020-03-19 10:36 UTC

Because we need to pass JSON data to the API, and call_endpoint internally converts a Python Dict to JSON. So, to generate the final JSON:

```json
{
    "topic_name": "some text here"
}
```

we need to pass a Dict.

## Private messages via API by outgoing email: is it possible?

*2020-03-18 to 2020-03-23 · 11 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/Private.20messages.20via.20API.20by.20outgoing.20email.3A.20is.20it.20possible.3F/with/833657)*

**Mike Kozhurin** · 2020-03-18 18:19 UTC

In Send a Message API method we set "private" type and pass the list of emails. 
All works well when they are zulip's internal (like user34@zulip.domain.com).
But it's not working when we pass outgoing user emails (like donald_trump@domain.com).
Problem is we dont know internal zulip emails of users in outer systems.
Is there any way to send private message via api to zulip user using his outgoing zulip email, not internal?

**Steve Howell** · 2020-03-19 00:09 UTC

@Mike Kozhurin 

The send-message API currently only accepts internal emails or user_ids.  It would be a bit tricky security-wise to accept real emails, since if you set up your realm not to have emails visible, you don't want to leak info about emails via error messages from the API.

I haven't tested this, but I believe if you're an admin you could use this API call to map "real" emails (we call them "delivery_email") to either the internal emails or user_ids.  https://chat.zulip.org/api/get-all-users

I suppose there's an argument that we should at least let admin accounts pass in `delivery_email` for send-message, although we're really trying to move folks toward using `user_id` if they can.

We'll see what Tim says here, too.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-03-19 18:16 UTC

@Mike Kozhurin can you talk about your use case for having real email addresses be private but wanting to access the API using them?

**Mike Kozhurin** · 2020-03-19 20:45 UTC

Our company uses LDAP auth for pass-through authorization in our services. And domain email is a comfort way to integrate between them. There is no special need to hide user's domain emails. I am a newbie in zulip and it was installed by our admin (i think he used default settings to integrate it with AD). My task was to integrate Redmine task service with it. As I understand now (thanks to you with Steve), we can reconfig zulip to use real emails as internal. It's ok for us, we will try it. The solution proposed by Steve, to get internal emails via get-all-users, is good too. I understand your concerns about privacy, so we will use recommended functionality.
Thanks to both of you!

**Steve Howell** · 2020-03-20 14:32 UTC

@Mike Kozhurin Thanks for following up here!  If you have any issues with the Redmine integration, I recommend the #**integrations** stream, which is usually a bit lower traffic than this one.  But this stream is also a fine place to ask questions.

Regarding your admin's decision to set it up this way, I'm kinda curious if something in our docs or defaults could be clarified here.  But it's not that big a deal for now, just something we'll keep in mind if we get similar reports from other installations.

Thanks again!

**Mike Kozhurin** · 2020-03-23 11:57 UTC

@Steve Howell Hi, Steve! 
Our admin and I failed with configure Zulip to use real email addresses instead of internal. 
it seems to be discribed in "Incoming email integration / Polling setup", but we dont understand how it can help to send a message via API using user's real email.
You say we have set up our realm not to have emails visible. May be you can point us how to set it to have?

**Steve Howell** · 2020-03-23 12:13 UTC

@Mike Kozhurin Your admin should be able to change this from the screen below:

[image.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/8b/5kvd-4BZj7kUjTrArAZxvhAr/image.png)

**Steve Howell** · 2020-03-23 12:16 UTC

In the gear menu (see top right corner), your admin will need to select "Manage Organization" and then select "Organization Permissions" in the left panel.  Then at the very bottom of the right panel, change the dropdown that says "Who can can access user email addresses" so that it's everybody.  Now here's the **gotcha**--be sure to hit "Save".  (The Save button is up a bit on the screen--it should be obvious on a large monitor, but can scroll offscreen on a smaller laptop screen.  We intend to fix this.)

**Steve Howell** · 2020-03-23 12:23 UTC

(I created #14298 to improve the docs here.)

**Mike Kozhurin** · 2020-03-23 14:10 UTC

@Steve Howell Wow, it works like a charm, thanks! 
This way was not obvious for us, but now it seems reasonable )
Thanks, you helped us a lot!

**Steve Howell** · 2020-03-23 14:13 UTC

@Mike Kozhurin You're welcome!  I can understand how this wasn't obvious--we do need to work on making this more obvious to users.  But glad you worked it out!

# Setting Up VS Code for Debugging Zulip

Set up VS Code to debug the django zulip sever. The following can only setup VS Code to debug the *django application* and not the *JS* (frontend) part of zulip. This is still a work in progress and any suggestions to simplify or ease the workflow are encouraged. 

I hope this helps the community of VS Code users and helps them significantly ! :D

The main ingredient is [ptvsd](https://github.com/microsoft/ptvsd). You can learn more about VS Code and debugging applications and configurations [here](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/editor/debugging).

## Steps

1. Download and install VS Code.
2. Download and install the [Python](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=ms-python.python) extension for VS Code by Microsoft.  
3. Set up the vagrant dev environment from [here](https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/setup-vagrant.html)
4. Make sure you run the dev server at least once. ( So that you know everything is working before making changes to the files )
5. Expose *port* in Vagrant file

    Add the following line in `./Vagrantfile` and replace `YOUR_GUEST_PORT_NUMBER` which you want to connect your VS Code Debugger to the ptvsd server and `YOUR_HOST_PORT_NUMBER` to one on which ptvsd server is going to run on. 
    
    **Note**: You can keep both same for simplicity
```vagrant
config.vm.network "forwarded_port", guest: YOUR_GUEST_PORT_NUMBER, host: YOUR_HOST_PORT_NUMBER, host_ip: host_ip_addr
```
Example:

```vagrant
config.vm.network "forwarded_port", guest: 5678, host: 5678, host_ip: host_ip_addr
```

6. Expose port in Docker

    If you are using a *virtual box* instance, you can skip this step.
    Add the following lines at the end of the `tools/setup/dev-vagrant-docker` and replace `YOUR_PTVSD_PORT_NUMBER` with the port number on which ptvsd server will run. (This must be same as the `YOUR_HOST_PORT_NUMBER` from last step)
```docker
EXPOSE YOUR_PTVSD_PORT_NUMBER
```
Example:

```docker
EXPOSE 5678
```

7. Download and install ptvsd by `ssh-ing` into the vagrant server. 

    **Note**: You should activate the `zulip-py3-venv` if not already activated and then run the following.

```python
pip install ptvsd
```

8. Edit `tools/settings.py`

    Add the following lines in `zproject/settings.py` after `if DEBUG:`
```python 
    if DEBUG:                                   # Already present
        INTERNAL_IPS = ('127.0.0.1',)           # Already Present
        import ptvsd
        if "runserver" in sys.argv and os.environ.get("RUN_MAIN"):
            try:
                ptvsd.enable_attach(redirect_output=True)
                print("VS Code Debugging Enabled.")
            except OSError:
                print("Debugging Setup Error,  Exception: ")
                tracback.print_exc()
```
The `redirect_output` gets the output from the server redirected to the debug console of VS Code (quite a handy thing!).

Here you can have a bit of modifications like:
- If you want the django server to wait for debugger *prior to running* just add
```python 
...
ptvsd.enable_attach()
ptvsd.wait_for_debugger()
...
```
- If you want to run the ptvsd server on some other port than default ( default is *0.0.0.0* and *5678* ) then
```python
    ptvsd.enable_attach(YOUR_HOST_IP, YOUR_HOST_PORT)
```

9. Create a `launch.json` file

    Add a debugging config by checking out the instructions [here](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/editor/debugging#_launch-configurations). In the launch.json add the following lines
```js
    {
        "version": "0.2.0",
        "configurations": [
            {
            "name":"Python: Remote Attach",     // name of config
            "type":"python",        
            "request":"attach",                 // attach type request
            "port":5678,                        // the port on which ptvsd is running
            "host":"localhost",                 // host ip of the vagrant server
            "django" : true,                    // Not neccessary
            "subprocess" : true,                // multi-process architecture
            "pathMappings":[{                   // your local->server mappinps
                "localRoot":"${workspaceFolder}",       
                "remoteRoot":"."
                }]
            }  
        ]
    }
```

10. Launch `run-dev.py` via command line
11. Attach the debugger from VS Code
12. Set up breakpoints and catch those nasty bugs!

## Note
- You need to attach the debugger everytime the sever reloads. No alternative to this right now.
- You need to unstage `settings.py`, `Vagrantfile` and `Dockerfile` before committing.
- Haven't tested with manual installation of Zulip
- Need an internet connection
- Not secure for running on production servers and / or for remote dev server (i.e. not on local servers).
- You may need to increase the nginx's `connection_timeout` and `read_timeout` for stepping through the code for long times and still needing a response at client side.

**Steve Howell** · 2020-03-22 17:52 UTC

The purpose of `deepcopy` is **not** to prevent multiple calls.  The purpose of `deepcopy` is to prevent any of the calls from mutating the shared data structure.  If every call to `finalize_payload` makes its own copy of the dictionary, then we won't end up corrupting data for the subsequent callers.

I think what we should do here, honestly, is just have `finalize_payload` always return a new copy.  But I kind of want Tim to weigh in here.

**Udit Krishna Chaudhary** · 2020-03-22 19:05 UTC

I will wait for Tim's response and then get to working on it!

Do we need a deepcopy, or just a copy?

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-03-22 22:33 UTC

**Steve Howell** · 2020-03-22 22:35 UTC

We technically only need a shallow copy.  If we do the copy within `finalize_payload`, there's a lot less risk with doing a shallow copy (since we know, in context, that we're not doing any deep mutations).  If we were to keep it the responsibility of the callers, which is probably a bad idea at this point, then we'd want to be a bit more paranoid.

**Steve Howell** · 2020-03-22 22:35 UTC

So I vote let's do a shallow copy in `finalize_payload`.

**Steve Howell** · 2020-03-22 23:04 UTC

**Steve Howell** · 2020-03-22 23:06 UTC

~~~ py
class MessageDict:
    @staticmethod
    def post_process_dicts(objs):
        # hydrate objs
        for obj in objs:
            MessageDict._finalize_payload(obj, apply_markdown, client_gravatar)

    @staticmethod
    def finalize_payload(obj, apply_markdown, client_gravatar):
        return MessageDict._finalize_payload(
            shallow_copy(obj)
            apply_markdown,
            client_gravatar)

    @staticmethod
    def _finalize_payload(obj, apply_markdown, client_gravatar):
        # mutate the object

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2020-04-08 04:39 UTC

So I completed the setup once again using the following steps:
```
Install WSL2 - https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/wsl2-install
Install Ubuntu 18.04 from windows store

sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade

Clone Zulip:
git clone --config pull.rebase git@github.com:YOURUSERNAME/zulip.git
cd zulip
git remote add -f upstream https://github.com/zulip/zulip.git


Sudo apt install rabbitmq-server memcached redis-server postgresql rabbitmq-server

Sudo vim /etc/rabbitmq/Rabbitmq.conf
NODE_IP_ADDRESS=127.0.0.1
NODE_PORT=5672


sudo service rabbitmq-server start && sudo service memcached start && sudo service redis-server start && sudo service postgresql start
(Click Allow access if you get popups for windows firewall blocking some services.)


./tools/provision
```

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-03-23 19:45 UTC

(replying to Tejas Tank)
> Btw, why is it named bankruptcy?
Because you're declaring "Zulip bankruptcy" by marking everything as read and start over, in analogy to declaring bankruptcy financially.  I don't think it's a great name, but it is nice to have a unique name for this concept, and I'm not sure there's anything better.

## property decorator

*2020-03-23 to 2020-03-23 · 8 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/property.20decorator/with/836932)*

**Vishnu KS** · 2020-03-23 16:21 UTC

Is it a good design practice to make a database query inside a model method that is used as a property? 

For example, I have a function called `get_current_plan`

```
def get_current_plan(customer: Customer) -> Optional[CustomerPlan]:
    return CustomerPlan.objects.filter(
        customer=customer, status__lt=CustomerPlan.LIVE_STATUS_THRESHOLD).first()
```

The function is currently called in the codebase like this.

```
plan = get_current_plan(customer)
```

This works great.

This can be simplified a bit more by making the function a method of the CustomerPlan class.

```
    def current_plan(self) -> Optional['CustomerPlan']:
        return CustomerPlan.objects.filter(
            customer=self, status__lt=CustomerPlan.LIVE_STATUS_THRESHOLD).first()
```

So the code would now become

```
plan = customer.get_current_plan()
```

This also works great. But I find it simpler to wrap the method with the `property` decorator so that It can be treated like a property.

```
@property
    def current_plan(self) -> Optional['CustomerPlan']:
        return CustomerPlan.objects.filter(
            customer=self, status__lt=CustomerPlan.LIVE_STATUS_THRESHOLD).first()
```

So ` customer.get_current_plan()` can be replaced with

```
plan = customer.current_plan
```

I think one drawback of this approach is that developers may not realize that a query is made whenever the `current_plan` property is accessed. So they might call the `current_plan` attribute method directly many times in a function instead of storing the result in a variable. I don't necessarily think this is a big issue though since I guess Postgres should be caching the result after the first query is made. Are there any other issues that one should be worried about?

**Steve Howell** · 2020-03-23 17:06 UTC

My vote is to just use a function.

**Vishnu KS** · 2020-03-23 17:07 UTC

Alright. Does it make sense to move the function inside the Customer model?

**Vishnu KS** · 2020-03-23 17:08 UTC

So  `plan = customer.get_current_plan()` instead of `plan = get_current_plan(customer)`.

**Steve Howell** · 2020-03-23 17:10 UTC

I would be fine having it on the model, unless it fits naturally in an existing library.

**Vishnu KS** · 2020-03-23 17:14 UTC

`get_current_plan` is currently present inside corporate/models.py file. So I guess it makes sense to move it to the Customer model in the same file.

**Steve Howell** · 2020-03-23 17:20 UTC

👍

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-03-23 19:44 UTC

Yeah, I agree, properties doing database queries is unexpected and probably a confusing way to write it (since reading code using that property will give the wrong idea about to what extent that line can fail).

**Vaibhav Raj Singh** · 2020-03-23 19:53 UTC

Issue: Changes on ediiting the messsage are not reflected back to the widget. e.g. if you change a poll topic  from `/ poll <topic name>`, it isn't being reflected back to the poll itself.

Most probably I might be going/thinking in the totally wrong direction, but here's what I think is happening. The current widget data is being handled by submessage.js, which is not connected to message_edit.js. Hence, the widget data isn't getting updated on editing. Basically, widgets haven't yet been connected to the edit message functionality. 
Moreover, while all other messages go through the `/json/messages/` endpoint, widgets are handled by `/json/submessage/` endpoint, which isn't there in message_edit.js.

You can do the same thing using the unbound method call syntax: `str.center('hello', 15)`. You could also consider using a variable format string instead of a function pointer: `'{:^{}}'.format('hello', 15)`

## Presence (ZT-focus)

*2020-03-25 to 2020-03-25 · 9 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/Presence.20.28ZT-focus.29/with/839818)*

**Neil Pilgrim (neiljp)** · 2020-03-25 19:01 UTC

The minimal approach for presence followed in ZT is to do the following:
* set up others' presence from initial data
* notify the server of being active each 60s
* use the returned data from the notify to regenerate others' presence

My understand is that there is an 'improved' version whereby we can pass `ping_only=True` to notify, and rely on presence events to update the list, which is simpler for the client, though relies on good synchronization between server and client. This is our 'v2' update listed in the code.

I was prompted to write this, since I saw a post by @Tim Abbott that indicated "clients" (presumably webapp/desktop and maybe mobile?) explicitly do still request the presences each minute - pending any changes to the presences logic in future, as being discussed.

Is there a reason the 60s was chosen? Any thoughts for ZT?

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-03-25 19:07 UTC

@Neil Pilgrim I don't think your understanding is correct.  The presence events will only cause users to go from offline to online; they won't update users state who were previously online.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-03-25 19:07 UTC

We're in the process of doing some redesign here that will hopefully result in documentation, so possible the right answer for terminal is to defer action until that happens if this isn't an important priority area for the terminal app anyway.

**Neil Pilgrim (neiljp)** · 2020-03-25 19:12 UTC

Thanks for clarifying! This was based on my assumption (without digging very deeply, in the past) that the events were a way of moving from a regular 'fetch all' to an as-needed 'diff-only' approach. The recent discussion makes a little more sense now.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-03-25 19:22 UTC

In short, presence is structurally a high-throughput, quadratic API that it's actually better to poll for presence separately from everything else.

**Chris Bobbe** · 2020-03-25 19:29 UTC

@Tim Abbott [said](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/stream/49-development-help/topic/Presence.20(ZT-focus)/near/839829):
> We're in the process of doing some redesign here that will hopefully result in documentation, so possible the right answer for terminal is to defer action until that happens if this isn't an important priority area for the terminal app anyway.
This might be #13734 ("Improve presence system's scalability for large realms", Tim opened on Jan 24)?

Yep!  And @Steve Howell has a few PRs working towards that.

**Neil Pilgrim (neiljp)** · 2020-03-25 23:20 UTC

> In short, presence is structurally a high-throughput, quadratic API that it's actually better to poll for presence separately from everything else.
Does this mean quadratic due to the n-users/n-users relationship?

def common_context(user: UserProfile) -> Dict[str, Any]:

## boto3 upgrade

*2020-03-29 to 2020-04-22 · 31 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/boto3.20upgrade/with/843313)*

**Wyatt Hoodes** · 2020-03-29 19:51 UTC

So for `public_url` that is returned from `upload_export_tarball` the approach I have in #14378 just constructs the url like before but doesn't feel that robust.  I was thinking to use `generate_presigned_url()` to instead do this.  With that change the code looks like:
```python
def upload_export_tarball(self, realm: Optional[Realm], tarball_path: str) -> str:
    bucket = settings.S3_AVATAR_BUCKET
    key = os.path.join("exports", generate_random_token(32), os.path.basename(tarball_path))
    s3_object = get_s3_object(bucket, key)
    s3_object.upload_file(tarball_path)

    public_url = s3_object.meta.client.generate_presigned_url(
        'get_object',
        Params={
            'Bucket': bucket,
            'Key': key
        },
        ExpiresIn=0
    )
    return public_url
```

Which is nice, but returns urls in the form
```
https://test-avatar-bucket.s3.amazonaws.com/exports/efebd56086189878f0aad232ca0cccd8/tarball.tar.gz?AWSAccessKeyId=test-key&Signature=Vu2KtGPL1KLN7E%2Bf6avEzLaIlRY%3D&Expires=1585508910
```

So I could instead `return public_url.split('?')[0]` and this gives us back our original url without the signature.  Would this be an acceptable approach?

**Wyatt Hoodes** · 2020-03-29 20:24 UTC

Oh, wait, found something better I think.  I can configure the active session to have an unsigned `signature_version` then create a client from our session that generates the url based on that config.

**Wyatt Hoodes** · 2020-03-29 20:25 UTC

Then we don't have that hacky `.split('?')[0]`

```python
import sys, os, zulip

## Toggle full width in wide screens #14319

*2020-04-11 to 2020-04-12 · 6 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/Toggle.20full.20width.20in.20wide.20screens.20.2314319/with/851886)*

**Shubham Gupta** · 2020-04-11 19:55 UTC

@Vinit Singh  For enabling the user list toggle in a wide view, we have to use some of the CSS for `max-width:1165px`. For achieving this,  we have two options:-
* We can write the while CSS again i.e. copy the common CSS part and put it outside the media query.
* We can make a mixin and use it for current screen size as well as screens with `max-width: 1165px`.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2020-04-18 11:54 UTC

Here’s a reduced test case. This script runs in Python 3.6 but not Python 3.7.

```python
class Foo:
    def __getattr__(self, name):
        if name == "keys":
            raise RuntimeError(name)
        return getattr(super(), name)

    def __iter__(self):
        yield from []

{}.update(Foo())
```

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2020-04-18 12:07 UTC

`git bisect` on CPython implicates https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/60c3d3551a96febac7b6016fb44605643842c686.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2020-04-18 12:19 UTC

Should be fixed by #14630.

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2020-04-18 12:20 UTC

@Anders Kaseorg can you explain this in simple terms?

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2020-04-18 12:29 UTC

Well this is a complicated interaction. When `page_params` is not defined by the context, Jinja2 evaluates it to an instance of the [`jinja2.Undefined`](https://jinja.palletsprojects.com/en/2.11.x/api/#jinja2.Undefined) class. This object allows a handful of operations like iteration, but has a `__getattr__` handler that raises a [`jinja2.UndefinedError`](https://jinja.palletsprojects.com/en/2.11.x/api/#jinja2.UndefinedError) on anything else. Now, `dict.update` should work on any iterable, so this should be fine. However, it has to check whether the argument is in fact a mapping first. It does that by checking whether it has `keys` attribute. This has to go through the `__getattr__` handler. Python 3.6 interprets any exception as indicating that the attribute doesn’t exist. Python 3.7 [only interprets `AttributeError`](https://bugs.python.org/issue31572) as indicating that the attribute doesn’t exist, and passes other exceptions through. `jinja2.UndefinedError` is not `AttributeError`. Hence the bug.

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2020-04-18 12:31 UTC

Wow! Thanks for the explanation.

**Lars Petersen** · 2020-04-18 12:55 UTC

… and for the quick fix! :thank_you:

* We make a PR that just removes the dictionary and sends the `user_id`, that can be used for testing.  We likely won't merge this for some time.

* We wait like 6 months for versions without that support to disappear.
* We merge the API change.

**Greg Price** · 2020-04-22 01:18 UTC

I think the ideal plan from the mobile perspective would be a small variation on this one:

(replying to Tim Abbott)
> I think basically the path forward for this needs to be: * We make a PR that just removes the dictionary and sends the `user_id`, that can be used for testing. We likely won't merge this for some time. * The terminal and mobile app developers test against that PR, and release versions that work with …

which is that in step 1 we go ahead and merge a change that adds the `user_id`, without removing the dictionary. Then steps 2 to 4 are the same as quoted.

That way, when we make a mobile release that's designed for the new API (and compatible with the old one), the API we're writing against is one that's actually been merged into master, rather than one that's only in an unmerged PR.

**Steve Howell** · 2020-04-22 01:20 UTC

I am fine with the add-first approach that Greg suggests.

**Greg Price** · 2020-04-22 01:24 UTC

One reason I like that better is sort of a narrow tooling reason, but I think a pretty significant one practically: it means that the mobile development doesn't require maintaining a server dev environment and running against that. That's a fairly heavyweight cost (especially when running it on a laptop alongside a mobile-device emulator, or some of the other memory-hungry tools needed in mobile development) which we've largely been successful in avoiding.

**Greg Price** · 2020-04-22 01:32 UTC

The other is at more of a workflow or coordination level: I'd feel kind of nervous about shipping releases for six months that try to use an API that's still in development. It'd feel ungrounded -- going out on a bit of a limb -- because it'd feel like the API wasn't completely settled yet, and perhaps when it came time to merge it we'd decide we wanted something else instead.

If we were determined to solve that without actually merging the new API on the server, we could do so with some sufficiently explicit way of agreeing on an exact API. But I think we have already a pretty good way of writing down an exact API we've decided on, which is that we merge it into the server -- so the simplest way to solve that problem is to just continue using that solution.

I'd just leave the `user` dicts as they are -- they'll be inconsistent, but that's OK because they're on their way out.

**Greg Price** · 2020-04-22 01:56 UTC

I think you'll need to pass the is_admin variable to the template in line 53 settings_invite.js

**Jagan S** · 2020-04-25 16:23 UTC

**Pranav Joglekar** · 2020-04-25 16:25 UTC

I may be wrong, but according to me is_admin is available in all settings pages, i.e why it is available in invites_list_admin, but not in admin_invites_list.hbs. @Steve Howell Could you confirm?

**Sahil Batra** · 2020-04-25 16:38 UTC

**Sahil Batra** · 2020-04-25 18:40 UTC

## is it safe to login from self-write login page ?

*2020-04-26 to 2020-04-26 · 2 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/is.20it.20safe.20to.20login.20from.20self-write.20login.20page.20.3F/with/862948)*

**lixiran** · 2020-04-26 11:21 UTC

I write a login page.  I wanna use my own login page to login zulip instead of zulip login form. 
here is what I do in my login page:
1. the xhr call the /login url.
2. get the csrfmiddlewaretoken value from xhr response.
3.  create a hidden input "csrfmiddlewaretoken" my form put the csrfmiddlewaretoken value in it.
4. post my form to /accounts/login/?next=.  params are : username, password and csrfmiddlewaretoken
5. the login succeed. 

I wanna discuss with team that, is it safe for login action ?
beside, the csrf token and sessionid are stored in the cookie. I doubt if this can prevent the csrf attack. if the user click  an "attack" url from other website and redirect back to zulip, this attack request could still get the csrf token from cookie.

**willy** · 2020-04-26 13:49 UTC

I read this artical:   https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/3.0/ref/csrf/
this is my understanding:
when a user open the django web site to raise a POST request, the django will give TWO tokens: one is the crsf_token set in the cookie. the other one  is  csrfmiddlewaretoken in the Form body.
when the post request submitted, the django will compare the  crsf_token  and csrfmiddlewaretoken. if they has the same secret, then the post request will be proceed.  
what interesting is ,  I did a quick experiment, I set the csrfmiddlewaretoken value the same as crsf_token manually and send to django.  that can make django think the secret is the same.
but if the cookie is set httponly by zulip, so it cannot be read via js. so the website cannot be CSRF attack.

an extreme case is :
User A login zulip.  User B must find a way to get the  CSRF token from User A  MANUALLY( the js won't work because it is httponly). then set it to csrfmiddlewaretoken value in FORM.  then User B should be able to do CSRF Attack.

I am not security expert. so anyone feel free to raise commet.

## vagrant port

*2020-05-01 to 2020-05-01 · 6 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/vagrant.20port/with/866224)*

**Steve Howell** · 2020-05-01 15:08 UTC

When we run `run-dev` for tests, we print the following message:

~~~
Note: only port 9981 is exposed to the host in a Vagrant environment.

**Steve Howell** · 2020-05-01 15:09 UTC

That message is actually inaccurate, I believe, and I'm not sure it's truly necessary.  When we run `run-dev.py` for normal mode, it properly refers to port 9991, which is indeed proxied by vagrant (afaict):

~~~
103   config.vm.network "forwarded_port", guest: 9991, host: host_port, host_ip: host_ip_addr
104   config.vm.network "forwarded_port", guest: 9994, host: host_port + 3, host_ip: host_ip_addr

**Steve Howell** · 2020-05-01 15:11 UTC

And then we don't actually mention anything about the webpack port (9994), and I'm not sure we actually need to expose that for Vagrant, anyway, since I think browser users go through the proxy (9991) even for webpack things.

**Steve Howell** · 2020-05-01 15:18 UTC

I think my main request for now would be to make the message a little more vague, but still helpful.  Something like:

~~~
Vagrant users: Look at forwarded_port settings in Vagrantfile to see if 9991 is available.
~~~

And then suppress that if `--test` is passed in.

**Steve Howell** · 2020-05-01 15:19 UTC

I'd also be fine to just eliminate the warning at this point.  It was created in Oct 2016 in e09c27f1ae1d844c3b070617706e8343c8f0a877.  It's plausible that we've improved our documentation since then.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-05-01 20:49 UTC

I think suppressing under `--test` would certainly be appropriate.
