## any suggesting on realm using different settings ?

*2020-05-11 to 2020-05-12 · 21 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/any.20suggesting.20on.20realm.20using.20different.20settings.20.3F/with/873618)*

**willy** · 2020-05-11 13:23 UTC

As I know, the zulip has the realm which allow multiple organization running on one zulip instance. but in my understanding, those organizations are still sharing the same settings.py.
does zulip  or django support that each realm use its own settings.py ?  each realm can has different admin, auth backend, jitsi server and etc.
e.g. 
realm1 use emailbackend auth
realm2 use githubbackend auth.

**Rohitt Vashishtha** · 2020-05-11 13:25 UTC

We can have different admins for different realms, and yes, we can have different auth backends configured for different realms.

Zulip's settings are divided into two main areas: Server level settings and Realm level settings. We can't have a different settings.py for each realm, and anything inside settings.py is a server level setting.

**willy** · 2020-05-11 13:26 UTC

@Rohitt Vashishtha 
is there anything about the "Realm level settings" in doc ?

**Rohitt Vashishtha** · 2020-05-11 13:28 UTC

Anything that an admin can modify from the interface is a realm level setting. Take a look at https://chat.zulip.org/#organization/auth-methods or https://chat.zulip.org/#organization/organization-settings as an example.

**willy** · 2020-05-11 13:30 UTC

those settings are stored in the DB ?

**Rohitt Vashishtha** · 2020-05-11 13:34 UTC

Yes.

**willy** · 2020-05-11 13:39 UTC

I am reading this doc
https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/stable/subsystems/settings.html?highlight=Realm%20level%20settings#realm-settings
is there anyway to set the realm-settings via API  or  by server admin(who is not a member of orgnization) ?

**Rohitt Vashishtha** · 2020-05-11 13:53 UTC

@willy some realm settings can be changed via API. What do you have in mind?

**willy** · 2020-05-11 13:58 UTC

I want to make a realm management page for the super admin. the admin maybe or may not be a member of a organization. but he is allowed to change some realm settings.  like avatar, name, auth backend.

**Rohitt Vashishtha** · 2020-05-11 14:04 UTC

We don't have the concept of a super admin and each API key is restricted to one realm only. To make such a dashboard, you would need API keys of all the realms.

**willy** · 2020-05-11 14:08 UTC

ok got it.   BTW, does zulip support to let each realm  has it’s own database ?

**Rohitt Vashishtha** · 2020-05-11 14:10 UTC

No, database is a server level setting. You can have a setup where the database server is different from your Zulip server, but then all the realms will be on that database.

Why do you require this? Maybe we have some other option to get what you want done.

**willy** · 2020-05-11 14:18 UTC

@Rohitt Vashishtha 
I want to do the data isolation between realms.  What I expect to do in zulip is :   shared application server, separate databases.
shared applications: this can be done via Realms.
separate databases: not find a easy way.

**Rohitt Vashishtha** · 2020-05-11 17:07 UTC

Its still the same application that's serving different realms. If you want complete separation, you would have to host two instances of Zulip.

**Rohitt Vashishtha** · 2020-05-11 17:08 UTC

You might want to do something like having the same postgresql, memcached etc but 2 separate instances of the django server in docker containers.

**willy** · 2020-05-12 02:16 UTC

Thanks for advice. so only separate the DB  while share the same application is not possible ?

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2020-05-12 02:24 UTC

Correct, you would need to run two instances of the application if you wanted them to use two different databases.

**willy** · 2020-05-12 02:25 UTC

ok understand~ @Anders Kaseorg

"two instances of the application"  means two instance of django ? or two instance of complete zulip deployment ? @Anders Kaseorg

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2020-05-12 02:29 UTC

Two deployments. (Of course, you can point them to two databases on the same PostgreSQL server, if that’s what you want.)

**willy** · 2020-05-12 02:29 UTC

ok. I see. thanks!

## "near:" narrow

*2020-05-18 to 2020-05-18 · 5 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/.22near.3A.22.20narrow/with/880468)*

**Vinit Singh** · 2020-05-18 12:34 UTC

Which narrow do we refer to as the "near" narrow? 
(Relevant Issue - #14971)

**Chris Bobbe** · 2020-05-18 17:18 UTC

If you type `near: 880468` in the search box it'll bring you to https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/near/880468.

If I select "Copy link to conversation", I get https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/stream/49-development-help/topic/.22near.3A.22.20narrow/near/880468 copied to the clipboard. (Regardless, I think, of which narrow I saw message 880468 in when I clicked "Copy link to conversation".)

**Steve Howell** · 2020-05-18 17:35 UTC

Both "near" links that @Chris Bobbe are valid--it depends on what you want.  I generally prefer the second, longer version, which brings me into the exact conversation, rather than the interleaved view.

**Rohitt Vashishtha** · 2020-05-18 17:37 UTC

`near` is simply an operator on any existing narrow (or no narrow at all). If you say: `near: 100000000000`, you'd be scrolled to the latest message, if you say `near: 0`, you'd be scrolled to the oldest message in a stream/topic.

The message need not be in the same narrow either. For example, if I want to see messages sent in #**mobile** at the same time as the message in, say, #**development help** with id: 1234, I could write: `stream: mobile, near:1234`.

**Vinit Singh** · 2020-05-18 17:47 UTC

I tried `near` as is, but didn't know I should use the message IDs. Thanks. :)

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-05-19 18:14 UTC

I bet we do this copy without doing something to prevent `success_stamp` from being copied.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-05-19 18:16 UTC

We handle that for venvs with this code:
```
        # virtualenv-clone, unfortunately, copies the success stamp,                                                   
        # which means if the upcoming `pip install` phase were to                                                      
        # fail, we'd end up with a broken half-provisioned virtualenv                                                  
        # that's incorrectly tagged as properly provisioned.  The                                                      
        # right fix is to use                                                                                          
        # https://github.com/edwardgeorge/virtualenv-clone/pull/38,                                                    
        # but this rm is almost as good.                                                                               
        success_stamp_path = os.path.join(venv_path, 'success-stamp')                                                  
        run_as_root(["rm", "-f", success_stamp_path])                                                                  
```

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-05-19 18:16 UTC

So probably a `try/finally` block around that `copytree` to remove `success_stamp` would fix this.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-05-19 18:17 UTC

(And maybe we should look at cleaning up and integrating that `virtualenv-clone` change, since we control that project, while we're thinking about this).

my instincts say that we should, especially so they get translated in non-latin scripts.

**Steve Howell** · 2020-05-30 13:06 UTC

I wouldn't worry about it too much, unless you're interested in tracking down specific techniques for localizing number representations.  We've had the unread counts forever, and nobody has ever brought this up.

## delete/patch submessages

*2020-06-10 to 2020-06-10 · 22 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/delete.2Fpatch.20submessages/with/900342)*

**Vinit Singh** · 2020-06-10 16:08 UTC

Zulip's widgets (like poll or to-do) cannot be deleted (entirely or partly) (Issue #14229 & #14799). I assumed at first that this would only require frontend changes, since most of the data and actions for the widgets are handled that way.
I think adding a PATCH endpoint for submessages is the correct way to do it. I have read the relevant documentation [[1]](https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/tutorials/writing-views.html) [[2]](https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/subsystems/widgets.html?highlight=submessage#overview), but have been unable to get it to work as expected. 

What would be the right approach to handle this issue (especially for the submessages)?

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-06-10 16:43 UTC

@Vinit Singh I'm not sure.  I've generally been thinking in the direction that perhaps we want to change the structure of how submessages work to address this.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-06-10 16:46 UTC

Specifically, rather than a `submessage` replacing the `content` field of a message, you'd have some base content for the message, e.g.:
````
This is a message containing a poll

``` poll Question for the poll
1. First option which can contain emoji/latex/etc (any Zulip markdown)
1. Second option 
1. Third option
```

This is some other content in the message with the poll.
````

And that would generate normal message content.  And then the submessage table would aim to store the voting data for the poll.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-06-10 16:48 UTC

The main problem with that sort of design is that there isn't with the current architecture a good way to record the mapping between the submessages/options in the message that will be stable across message editing (which would rerender the HTML).  E.g. imagine swapping the order of the first 2 options while editing their text; how do we know which option is which?

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-06-10 16:48 UTC

But that design would provide a very straightforward approach to deleting the widget -- you just edit the message as normal.

**Rohitt Vashishtha** · 2020-06-10 18:38 UTC

This would be trivial if we move to frontends sending rendered HTML to the server.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-06-10 18:50 UTC

I wouldn't say trivial; the editing user experience problem would still exist (as to which submessage gets which votes).

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-06-10 18:50 UTC

It'd just move the problem to be a frontend UI problem rather than a server/client protocol detail.

**Rohitt Vashishtha** · 2020-06-10 19:05 UTC

Couldn't we have the frontend simply insert `data-poll-option-id=123` for each option when composing the message? And then if the person is operating on the HTML directly, moving an option around would move the complete tag, thus allowing to edit *and* move options in a single edit.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-06-10 19:07 UTC

Well, except that we want the "edit message" UI to resemble what they entered in markdown, not some potentially large HTML thing.

**Rohitt Vashishtha** · 2020-06-10 19:08 UTC

I thought we were considering using a WYSIWYG approach, but with markdown based shortcuts.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-06-10 19:09 UTC

I think probably the right answer for the near term would involve just using the numbering feature (1/2/3/4, not 1/1/1/1) and overriding the OrderedList processor renumbering to store the original number on a data element for access by this.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-06-10 19:09 UTC

I think a WYWIWIG that supported live-editing fields of a somewhat complex HTML poll object would be tricky to get right.

**Rohitt Vashishtha** · 2020-06-10 19:10 UTC

BTW the current version is even different, we only use the markdown to only init the poll and then message edits do not have any effect on it.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-06-10 19:14 UTC

Correct, as I said, submessages are a prototype that ignore the message content entirely.

**Rohitt Vashishtha** · 2020-06-10 19:14 UTC

So should we rethink submessages as a whole while we haven't built too much using them?

**Rohitt Vashishtha** · 2020-06-10 19:17 UTC

For the poll widget, for example, if we just stick to message editing that would make it impossible for anyone else to add an option. And obviously people expect that removing a poll option by editing a message should remove it from the poll.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-06-10 19:27 UTC

Yes, my view is that we should rethink submessages before spending more time extending their API.  Which is why I proposed a different design that I think could address their needs in a more flexible and native way.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2020-06-10 20:01 UTC

Does the poll widget even go through the Markdown processor? It doesn’t support any other kind of Markdown.

**Rohitt Vashishtha** · 2020-06-10 20:05 UTC

It doesn't. We have a separate function to extract the poll options.

**Rohitt Vashishtha** · 2020-06-10 20:07 UTC

`zerver/lib/widget.py:23:def get_extra_data_from_widget_type()`

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-06-10 20:38 UTC

As I said, the current `widgets` system was a quick prototype; if we're going to spend more resources on it beyond UI styling, we should probably rethink its protocol to be something we'll be happy with long term.

## wsl limit ram usage

*2020-06-11 to 2022-02-10 · 17 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/wsl.20limit.20ram.20usage/with/901321)*

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2020-06-11 15:32 UTC

So, I have been using wsl with this config for past few weeks:
[.wslconfig](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/84/xMeokewOhD4VOqaeDTVly6xw/.wslconfig) 
```
[wsl2]
memory=8GB
swap=16GB
localhostForwarding=true
```
This file rests in your `%userprofile%`(or `C:\Users\USERNAME`)

This limits  max RAM usage of WSL and remove all memory overflow issues (which I never encountered anyway) 
NOTE:  I am using this on SSD.

**Mohit Gupta** · 2020-06-26 17:35 UTC

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-06-26 17:36 UTC

OK, I see the issue.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-06-26 17:37 UTC

The "problem" is on your branch; the fact that we now have a `markdown.py` is making `isort` detect imports of the third-party markdown module seem to be importing part of our project.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-06-26 17:38 UTC

I think in that case we need to do this:
```
diff --git a/.isort.cfg b/.isort.cfg
index fc0db9b93d..263016922f 100644
--- a/.isort.cfg
+++ b/.isort.cfg
@@ -1,7 +1,7 @@
 [settings]
 src_paths = .
 multi_line_output = 3
-known_third_party = decorator, jinja2, stripe, tornado, zulip
+known_third_party = decorator, jinja2, markdown, stripe, tornado, zulip
 include_trailing_comma = True
 use_parentheses = True
 line_length = 100
```

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-06-26 17:38 UTC

In that first commit.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2020-07-15 17:46 UTC

There’s a fundamental issue here in that we need to import at least `zulint.command.add_default_linter_arguments` to build the `argparse` parser that we use to check whether the user passed `--force` which affects how we call `assert_provisioning_status_ok`. **Steve Howell** · 2020-07-15 17:48 UTC

Yeah, there are definitely tradeoffs here.  I want to make these tools robust against provisioning deficiencies, but I don't want to uglify the tools too much.

**Steve Howell** · 2020-07-15 17:50 UTC

I am not totally convinced we need a `--force` flag for the linters, to be honest.  That may be a relic of when provisioning was 10x more experience, and we wanted to allow "consenting adults" behavior.

**Steve Howell** · 2020-07-15 17:57 UTC

I'm in favor of force flags for things like `rm`, where you're just saying if it's already done, I'm happy.

When force flags are used to override situations where things are clearly out of whack, I feel they are more dangerous, and they're generally only justified to work around performance problems (like provisioning is slow).  Especially with open source, you can always force stuff by mucking with the code if you're truly trying to save time.  Most of the time you're better off just fixing the problem.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2020-07-15 17:58 UTC

It’s useful when I’m in the middle of adding lint-related dependencies with `yarn`.

**Steve Howell** · 2020-07-15 18:01 UTC

We could replace it with an environment variable?

**Steve Howell** · 2020-07-15 18:04 UTC

I'm pro-env-var for this kind of stuff.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-07-15 18:35 UTC

Environment variable is more typing to use, but I at least almost never actually use `--force`, so that's probably not a real problem.

    def django_to_ldap_username(self, username: str) -> str:
        """
        Translates django username (user_profile.email or whatever the user typed in the login
        field when authenticating via the ldap backend) into ldap username.
        Guarantees that the username it returns actually has an entry in the ldap directory.
        Raises ZulipLDAPExceptionNoMatchingLDAPUser if that's not possible.
        """
        result = username
        if settings.LDAP_APPEND_DOMAIN:
            if is_valid_email(username):
                if not username.endswith("@" + settings.LDAP_APPEND_DOMAIN):
                    raise ZulipLDAPExceptionOutsideDomain(f"Email {username} does not match LDAP domain {settings.LDAP_APPEND_DOMAIN}.")
                result = email_to_username(username)
        else:
            # We can use find_ldap_users_by_email
            if is_valid_email(username):
                email_search_result = find_ldap_users_by_email(username)
                if email_search_result is None:
                    result = username
                elif len(email_search_result) == 1:
                    return email_search_result[0]._username
                elif len(email_search_result) > 1:
                    # This is possible, but strange, so worth logging a warning about.
                    # We can't translate the email to a unique username,
                    # so we don't do anything else here.

            error_message = "No ldap user matching django_to_ldap_username result: {}. Input username: {}"

            )

        return result

**Dinesh Ch** · 2020-07-15 06:00 UTC

We need to use two different `assertLogs` to capture both. 
* When you set it to root logger it doesn't capture the `DEBG` output as `zulip.ldap` doesn't propagate to root logger.

>  Note: I am not specifying loggers and level to capture all logs.
Also for experiment I mentioned zulip.ldap as logger name still the DEBG log was not captured.

When level is not specified it defaults to `INFO`. So, it didn't work when you mentioned `zulip.ldap`. It wouldn't even capture the `WARN` log output if `zulip.ldap` is set as the logger as we're logging it with root logger.

So, this is the solution that is working but it requires two `assertLogs`. 
```diff
index d9357be024..e2b0ffd6ee 100644
--- a/zerver/tests/test_auth_backends.py
+++ b/zerver/tests/test_auth_backends.py
@@ -1394,7 +1394,7 @@ class SocialAuthBase(DesktopFlowTestingLib, ZulipTestCase):
                 AUTHENTICATION_BACKENDS=(backend_path,
                                          'zproject.backends.ZulipLDAPAuthBackend',
                                          'zproject.backends.ZulipDummyBackend'),
-        ):
+        ), self.assertLogs('zulip.ldap',level='DEBUG'), self.assertLogs(level='WARN'):
             account_data_dict = self.get_account_data_dict(email=email, name=name)
             result = self.social_auth_test(account_data_dict,
                                            expect_choose_email_screen=True,
```

I think it would be nice to have everything as `assertLogs` for consistency.

```py
def start_social_login(request: HttpRequest, backend: str, extra_arg: Optional[str]=None,
                       ) -> HttpResponse:
    backend_url = reverse('social:begin', args=[backend])
    extra_url_params: Dict[str, str] = {}
    if backend == "saml":
        result = SAMLAuthBackend.check_config()  # WE ARE RETURNING HERE SOMETIMES
        if result is not None:
            return result

        # This backend requires the name of the IdP (from the list of configured ones)
        # to be passed as the parameter.
        if not extra_arg or extra_arg not in settings.SOCIAL_AUTH_SAML_ENABLED_IDPS:
            logging.info("Attempted to initiate SAML authentication with wrong idp argument: %s",
                         extra_arg)
            return redirect_to_config_error("saml")  # THIS IS WHERE WE ACTUALLY WANT TO RETURN FOR THIS TEST
        extra_url_params = {'idp': extra_arg}
```

**Dinesh Ch** · 2020-07-17 14:17 UTC

but looks like filters do not propagate like handlers and level.
 https://docs.python.org/3/library/logging.html#filter-objects 
> Note that filters attached to handlers are consulted before an event is emitted by the handler, whereas filters attached to loggers are consulted whenever an event is logged (using debug(), info(), etc.), before sending an event to handlers. This means that events which have been generated by descendant loggers will not be filtered by a logger’s filter setting, unless the filter has also been applied to those descendant loggers.

There's also this comment in `zproject/computed_settings.py`
```
        # For `filters`, no ancestors count at all -- only the exact logger name
        # the record was logged at.
```

**Gittenburg** · 2020-07-18 20:57 UTC

My 3-line fix #15850 works fine but the node test fails because for some godforsaken reason it calls `composebox_typeahead.initialize()` twice in the same unit test, which fails because zjquery doesn't support having multiple event handlers for the same element & event (see 6dbff03b9bf5c94009acabe4bb0341e81223a8a6). I don't really have the nerve to work through the 600 line unit test and would appreciate some help.

**Wyatt Hoodes** · 2020-07-19 01:37 UTC

Just looking at this briefly, could it not be handled in hotkey.js when processing the escape key?

**Wyatt Hoodes** · 2020-07-19 01:41 UTC

(as opposed to the current approach)

**Steve Howell** · 2020-07-19 02:16 UTC

(replying to Gittenburg)
> My 3-line fix #15850 works fine but the node test fails because for some godforsaken reason it calls `composebox_typeahead.initialize()` twice in the same unit test, which fails because zjquery doesn't support having multiple event handlers for the same element & event (see 6dbff03b9bf5c94009acabe4b …

 Adding your code to the existing handler would probably solve this.

**Gittenburg** · 2020-07-19 05:58 UTC

>Just looking at this briefly, could it not be handled in hotkey.js when processing the escape key?

`hotkey.js` is calling `compose_actions.cancel()`, which does `$(document).trigger($.Event("compose_canceled.zulip"));` after it's done. So this was already handled by hotkey.js.

>Adding your code to the existing handler would probably solve this.

The problem was that the handler adding logic was being called twice in the same test.

Thanks guys, I figured it out: just blurring in `compose_actions.hide_box()` doesn't break the tests and that's probably also the best place since it's right next to `blur_textarea();`.

## Topic case sensitivity

*2020-07-21 to 2020-07-21 · 18 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/Topic.20case.20sensitivity/with/946993)*

**Neil Pilgrim (neiljp)** · 2020-07-21 20:36 UTC

I discussed an issue I saw recently in ZT and mobile, which after discussion with Tim in #**issues>Topic names/unreads** appears to be related to case sensitive handling of topic names.

**Neil Pilgrim (neiljp)** · 2020-07-21 20:55 UTC

Given that this is variance between clients, I trust that this is (primarily) a front-end issue, though there are presumably aspects to consider with endpoints such as that which fetch the topic list - which appears to combine topics based on `lower`. Based on the backend approach, I expect a similar approach is required in front-ends, namely to unify topic names after conversion via `lower`?

**Neil Pilgrim (neiljp)** · 2020-07-21 20:56 UTC

I understand the appeal of the case insensitivity for topic matching, though it may explain some strange behavior where I was trying to adjust the case of the topic in the webapp a while back and not getting anywhere.

**Neil Pilgrim (neiljp)** · 2020-07-21 20:58 UTC

I assume we don't unify using something like `casefold` since the display text would be even more ambiguous? I don't have enough experience to know significant examples where this would cause issues other than ambiguity, but would be interested ŧo hear reasoning for this.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2020-07-21 21:06 UTC

I suspect naïve lowercase was chosen because proper Unicode case-folding is difficult in JavaScript.

**Neil Pilgrim (neiljp)** · 2020-07-21 21:21 UTC

Sure, and the same could perhaps be said for Python, given we were previously Python2 and that has no (native) casefold.

**Neil Pilgrim (neiljp)** · 2020-07-21 21:24 UTC

Ah, this was considered in January 2019 and Tim voted against casefold (#**development help>Case insensitive topic name #11308**)

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2020-07-21 21:38 UTC

That seems like a strange argument… if an English speaker wants FLUSS and fluss to be the same topic, wouldn’t a German speaker equally want FLUSS and fluß to be the same topic?

**Neil Pilgrim (neiljp)** · 2020-07-21 21:47 UTC

My expectation was that the display ambiguity might have been a problem, ie. which gets displayed? I was also reading around this, and it's unclear from the docs if python does a 'full' or 'simple' casefold.

**Neil Pilgrim (neiljp)** · 2020-07-21 21:49 UTC

Not combining seems like the safe (albeit manual) approach, whereas if it's not handled properly then we could get unwitting unification.

**Neil Pilgrim (neiljp)** · 2020-07-21 21:50 UTC

I think the (relatively recent?) topic typeahead helps with this, by prompting for similar previous topics, but presumably still unifies automatically.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2020-07-21 22:02 UTC

What makes you think FLUSS = fluß is unwitting?

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2020-07-21 22:03 UTC

And in any case, we’d only use lowercase or case-folding for matching and never for display.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-07-21 22:11 UTC

Right, the algorithm is "display what a user typed (not necessarily the user who typed a particular message)", not "display the case-folded version".

**Neil Pilgrim (neiljp)** · 2020-07-21 22:12 UTC

@Anders Kaseorg Right, but what to display? Is FLUSS always right? Is fluß? Maybe n years ago there was a topic with the former, and someone writes the latter; should it update to show the latter? Is that always guaranteed to be correct/equivalent? Capitalization/'shouting'/etc have no meaning? Unicode presumably claims equivalence at some level ('full'), but what level does python and JS provide?

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-07-21 22:12 UTC

It is increasingly rare that folks type the same topic as a previous one using different case, thanks to typeahea.

**Neil Pilgrim (neiljp)** · 2020-07-21 22:14 UTC

I completely accept that ZT should implement case insensitivity if that's the current standard. My first point was really to understand it better, the second was whether we should (could) be casefolding for matching, and if so how.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-07-21 22:18 UTC

At present we don't do unicode casefolding, and we haven't really had end users ask for it.  I'm not sure if it's just a small/rare enough annoyance or something else (we certainly have plenty of non-English speaking users).

My idea is to display my own code for webrtc streaming, being video/audio streaming or anything else. I know Zulip offers Jitsi and Zoom integration, I am not interested in that. The spirit of my question is purely interested if I can modify the interface from source. Thanks a million for your assistance.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-07-23 17:36 UTC

@King David yeah, you can certainly fork Zulip!  https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/production/upgrade-or-modify.html#modifying-zulip is a detailed guide on how to deploy changes to production; you'll want to prototype in a Zulip development environment.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-07-27 18:52 UTC

## puppeteer flake -- local echo=False

*2020-07-30 to 2020-07-31 · 7 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/puppeteer.20flake.20--.20local.20echo.3DFalse/with/965058)*

**Dinesh Ch** · 2020-07-30 18:33 UTC

There's this rare flake that occurs when a message is sent but isn't locally echoed(for some reason that we're not aware of).
It fails in the `waitFor` of `wait_for_fully_processed_message` which checks if the message is sent by validating with few conditionals.

One of them is `last_msg.raw_content !== content` which is supposed to be false but is true when a message isn't locally echoed(found this from the server logs). Figured that `last_msg.raw_content` is returning `undefined` in that case. Do we not include `raw_content` for messages that aren't locally echoed? (I tried a bit to find the code that deals with `message.raw_content` to see if I could find something but couldn't get much info)

Here's a failed run with some console logs saying `raw_content` is `undefined` with screenshot showing that the message has been sent. https://circleci.com/gh/chdinesh1089/zulip/1340
Also notice this in the server log that is seen only for a failed test (passed tests have `echo:True`)
`/json/report/send_times [377ms/355ms/(unknown)ms/echo:False/diff:False]`

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-07-30 19:28 UTC

One possibility for why we might not be locally echoing the message is if we're still loading the content for the current view.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-07-30 19:28 UTC

You may be able to do a wait until there's no loading indicator visible to resolve that.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-07-30 19:30 UTC

I don't remember the details of `raw_content` but my recollection is it gets fetched in message edit code paths for messages the current user didn't themselves send.

**Dinesh Ch** · 2020-07-30 19:39 UTC

I'll see if that's the case and check if waiting for content to load fixes it. Thanks!

**Dinesh Ch** · 2020-07-31 09:42 UTC

Waiting till the content to load fixed it. none out of 900 runs failed! I'll add this wait to `log_in` so that we don't have to add this line for every test.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-07-31 19:33 UTC

@Dinesh Ch awesome!

## Encoded stream names

*2020-08-14 to 2020-08-25 · 12 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/Encoded.20stream.20names/with/988506)*

**Preet Mishra** · 2020-08-14 17:00 UTC

I am working on handling internal narrow links in Zulip Terminal. For which, I have worked on a function to decode `zerver` encoded stream names.

However, I am not sure how to distinguish between 'intended' `-` and encoded `-` as the library code encodes both, for instance, `zulip terminal` and `zulip-terminal` as `zulip-terminal`.

**zerver/lib/url_encoding.py**:
```python3
def encode_stream(stream_id: int, stream_name: str) -> str:
    # We encode streams for urls as something like 99-Verona.
    stream_name = stream_name.replace(' ', '-')
    return str(stream_id) + '-' + hash_util_encode(stream_name)
```

**My functions**:
```python3
def decode_stream_data(stream_data: str) -> Tuple[Optional[int], str]:
    """
    Returns a tuple with stream ID and stream name.
    """
    stream_data = hash_util_decode(stream_data)
    split_stream_data = stream_data.split('-')
    try:
        stream_id = int(split_stream_data[0])
    except ValueError:
        # Assume it to be the deprecated version (without the stream ID).
        pass

    if 'stream_id' in locals():
        return stream_id, ' '.join(split_stream_data[1:])
    else:
        return None, ' '.join(split_stream_data)
```

```python3
def hash_util_decode(string: str) -> str:
    """
    Returns a decoded string given a hash_util_encode() [present in
    zulip/zulip's zerver/lib/url_encoding.py] encoded string.
    """
    # Acknowledge custom string replacements in zulip/zulip's
    # zerver/lib/url_encoding.py before unquote.
    return unquote(string.replace('.', '%'))
```

**Preet Mishra** · 2020-08-14 17:30 UTC

I should mention that an alternative could be to rather use the `stream_id` (to lookup for the stream name). However, our deprecated links didn't have any `stream_id`.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-08-14 18:25 UTC

The right algorithm is that if it starts `[0-9]+[-]`, one should always use the modern stream ID decoding; otherwise attempt stream_name decoding.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-08-14 18:25 UTC

@Preet Mishra does that make sense?

**Preet Mishra** · 2020-08-14 18:40 UTC

It makes sense. However, if I understand correctly, it would still lead to an ambiguity in the case of deprecated links.

**Preet Mishra** · 2020-08-14 18:42 UTC

For instance, the encoded `generic-name` could either be `generic name` or `generic-name` itself.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-08-14 18:45 UTC

I suspect deprecated links always encoded ` ` as `.20`, but we should dig up the historical logic.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-08-14 18:46 UTC

(I would be very surprised if we'd used an ambiguous algorithm, and that's what we do for topics).

**Preet Mishra** · 2020-08-15 07:52 UTC

Ah, yes! Thanks for the pointer.

**Preet Mishra** · 2020-08-15 08:12 UTC

To summarize:
* Modern links are patched with the stream ID and `-` as delimiters, where the stream name is later encoded via the library's `hash_util_encode()`.
* Deprecated links were purely encoded via `hash_util_encode()` (like the topics).

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-08-25 00:35 UTC

Yes, that's right.  @Preet Mishra is the draft `python-zulip-api` PR ready for another review?

**Preet Mishra** · 2020-08-25 03:19 UTC

Yes, it is ready.

@Dipen Sompura Zulip itself is built on Django, so I don't entirely understand your question.  It's plausible that folks who have a non-Zulip Django app would try to combine it with Zulip somehow, but I have never heard of anybody doing it, and it's not something that I'd recommend to most people.

@Vishnu KS Hi, I am currently using a script to dump the mongodb. I cannot currently push to gitlab, but will release the code in a pull request to the zulip project.
```python

import argparse
import logging
import os
import json
import pymongo
import yaml


STATS = {}


def connect(hostname: str, port: int) -> pymongo.MongoClient:
    client = pymongo.MongoClient(hostname, port)
    return client


def get_data(database: pymongo.database.Database) -> dict:
    STATS['tables'] = len(config['tables'])
    _ret = {}
    for table in config['tables']:
        logger.info("Processing table: %s", table)
        cache_file = config['tables'][table]['cache']
        if not os.path.isfile(cache_file) or args.no_message_cache:
            ret = database[table].find()
            with open(cache_file, 'w') as cfile:
                ret = list(ret)
                _ret[table] = ret
                STATS[table] = len(ret)
                cfile.write(json.dumps(ret, default=str))
        else:
            with open(cache_file, 'r') as cfile:
                ret = list(json.loads(cfile.read()))
                _ret[table] = ret
                STATS[table] = len(ret)
    return _ret


if __name__ == '__main__':
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    paa = parser.add_argument
    paa('-l', '--log-level', default='error',
        choices=['info', 'error', 'debug'])
    paa('-n', '--no-message-cache', action='store_true')
    paa('-o', '--outfile', default='./rocketchat_out.json',
        help='Set output filename and path. (default: ./rocketchat_out.json)')
    # get configuration
    with open('config.yml', 'r') as cfgfile:
        config = yaml.load(cfgfile.read(), Loader=yaml.FullLoader)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    logger = logging.getLogger()
    logger.addHandler(logging.StreamHandler())
    logger.setLevel(getattr(logging, args.log_level.upper()))
    mongoclient = connect(config['db']['host'], config['db']['port'])
    parties_db = mongoclient.parties
    # messages = get_messages(parties_db)
    # rooms_list = get_rooms(parties_db)
    data = get_data(parties_db)
    with open(args.outfile, 'w') as efile:
        efile.write(json.dumps(data, default=str))
    logging.info(json.dumps(STATS, indent=4, sort_keys=True, default=str))
    logging.debug(json.dumps(data, indent=4, sort_keys=True, default=str))
```
This is the content of the config file

```yaml
---  # Configuration file for rocketchat json exporter

db:
  host: 127.0.0.1
  port: 27017

tables:
  rocketchat_room:
    cache: room.cache
  rocketchat_message:
    cache: message.cache
  custom_emoji.files:
    cache: custom_emoji.cache
  rocketchat_avatars.chunks:
    cache: avatars_chunks.cache
  rocketchat_avatars.files:
    cache: avatars_files.cache
  rocketchat_avatars:
    cache: avatars.cache
  rocketchat_subscription:
    cache: subscription.cache
  users:
    cache: users.cache
```

@Kaustubh Nair Look at `topic_list_data.js` and `stream_topic_history.js`.

**Steve Howell** · 2020-09-01 16:34 UTC

We are usually pretty aggressive on re-drawing the entire topic list for any kind of change.

**Steve Howell** · 2020-09-01 16:36 UTC

(To be precise, we don't redraw the whole list, but we re-compute the whole list, and then `vdom.js` will redraw stuff as needed.)

@Steve Howell So as per my understanding, the topic data is updated every time `GET /messsages` is called?

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2020-09-03 08:43 UTC

Topic data is updated when messages are fetched and via events continuously.
I think calling `/topics` on every topic edit is not necessary. You already receive `update_message` events which include topic edits and you need to track info about topics locally. There are some minor details around this which need to be done right, `stream_topic_history.js` handles this for webapp. What data about topics are you having trouble tracking?

**Neil Pilgrim (neiljp)** · 2020-09-03 13:20 UTC

See Kaustubh's original question. My understanding is that topic data can of course be maintained via message updates, but the issue is that topic data in terms of the messages is not guaranteed complete.

The purpose of `--force` is to run `run-dev.py`even if you haven't provisioned recently.  Like the code says, "If you really know what you are doing, use --force to run anyway."  But generally you don't want to run `--force`.

**Priyansh Garg (garg3133)** · 2021-06-23 12:45 UTC

Opened #18966 as the first version of Rocket Chat import tool.

This version will allow you to import the following data from Rocket Chat:
* All users
* All public/private channels
* All teams and its public/private channels
* All discussion rooms as topics in their parent channel
* All the messages in all the channels
* All private conversations
* Reactions on messages (except for custom emojis)
* Mentions in messages (except `@all`, `@here` mentions)

Features remaining to be added:
* User avatars
* Attachments
* Default streams
* Custom emojis
* `@all`, `@here` mentions
* Starred messages
* Threads as separate topics.

(replying to Priyansh Garg (garg3133))
> While this works correctly for the custom emojis used as message reactions, custom emojis used inside the messages are not rendered properly. This is probably because we do not pass the imported messages through our markdown processor? [Screenshot-from-2021-08-02-22-42-18.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/61/gra …
I did some investigation regarding this and found that the actual problem here is the presence of `self.md.zulip_message` in [this line](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/cde86fbaca9951d3cdb633aa7b0a629dd05e848c/zerver/lib/markdown/__init__.py#L1485).

For processing the realm emojis in the imported messages, `self.md.zulip_message` shouldn't be `None`, but as no `message` argument is provided [here](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/master/zerver/lib/import_realm.py#L346-L352), it takes `message` as `None` [here](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/cde86fbaca9951d3cdb633aa7b0a629dd05e848c/zerver/lib/markdown/__init__.py#L2426) and hence, the realm emojis are not processed during the import.

**Priyansh Garg (garg3133)** · 2021-08-05 20:19 UTC

Why does it check for `self.md.zulip_message` in [this line](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/cde86fbaca9951d3cdb633aa7b0a629dd05e848c/zerver/lib/markdown/__init__.py#L1485) anyway?

**Priyansh Garg (garg3133)** · 2021-08-06 17:55 UTC

The same problem is with the linking of streams to stream mentions in messages. **Anders Kaseorg** · 2020-09-21 21:08 UTC

This does fix it:
```diff
--- a/tools/lint
+++ b/tools/lint
@@ -1,6 +1,7 @@
 #! /usr/bin/env python3

 import argparse
+import sys

 from zulint.command import add_default_linter_arguments, LinterConfig

@@ -21,7 +22,7 @@ def run() -> None:
     by_lang = linter_config.list_files(file_types=['py', 'sh', 'json', 'md', 'txt'],
                                        exclude=EXCLUDED_FILES)

-    linter_config.external_linter('mypy', ['tools/run-mypy'], ['py'], pass_targets=False,
+    linter_config.external_linter('mypy', [sys.executable, 'tools/run-mypy'], ['py'], pass_targets=False,
                                   description="Static type checker for Python (config: mypy.ini)")
     linter_config.external_linter('flake8', ['flake8'], ['py'],
                                   description="Standard Python linter (config: .flake8)")
```

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2020-09-21 21:09 UTC

(There are still other problems, but it fixes that problem.)

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2020-09-21 21:11 UTC

It is true that zulint treats the `FileNotFoundError` as fatal and doesn't run the other linters. We should add an exception handler to fix that, for parity with the parallel implementation.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2020-09-21 21:12 UTC

But the fundamental problem is that `tools/run-mypy` by itself is only a valid command on Unix which supports shebang lines (`#! /usr/bin/env python3`), and adding `shell=True` doesn't magically turn Windows into Unix.

Probably because then Unix users would have to type the `.py`.

## Developing on Arch Linux

*2020-09-20 to 2020-10-06 · 8 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/Developing.20on.20Arch.20Linux/with/1021024)*

**Vandan Rogheliya** · 2020-09-20 12:34 UTC

Hey! I am running Arch Linux and facing some issues. I was wondering whether Arch Linux is supported or not?

**ReCore** · 2020-09-21 00:05 UTC

You can develop on any OS (https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/setup-vagrant.html) but you can only run a production server on Debian or Ubuntu (https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/production/requirements.html#operating-system). You can get around this by running either a VM with Ubuntu or Debian which is what most people do or messing around with OS files but I don't recommend this. I barely managed it on a Debian branch and that uses the same package manager. You'd need to do some serious reworking for it to run on Arch. We don't recommend running directly off you OS anyway. We recommend running inside a VM or container because there is no uninstallation process.

**ReCore** · 2020-09-21 00:06 UTC

@Vandan Rogheliya

**ReCore** · 2020-09-21 00:09 UTC

There is an experimental docker image that can run on any OS though, so maybe look into that.
https://github.com/zulip/docker-zulip

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-09-21 19:08 UTC

@Vandan Rogheliya if you're interested in adding support for `tools/provision` directly on Arch Linux, that's certainly possible, but you'll need to do some work.  `git grep os_families tools/` will find some of the code involved.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-09-21 19:08 UTC

Otherwise, I'd recommend going with Vagrant.

**Steve Howell** · 2020-09-21 21:03 UTC

@Aryan Shridhar Are you sure that code was too long to paste here?  Anyway, that's not important.  It seems like `parseISO` is a module object.  Just to be clear, were these console statements in the browser?

**Aryan Shridhar** · 2020-09-22 06:20 UTC

@Steve Howell  , Yup you are right , these were console statements in the browser

**Steve Howell** · 2020-09-22 10:24 UTC

@Aryan Shridhar The next step might be for you to post a PR, so somebody else can try to debug this.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2020-09-23 00:00 UTC

@Aryan Shridhar You need to use `const {parseISO} = require("date-fns")`. The problem is that the `date-fns/parseISO` package has an incompatible `pkg.main` and `pkg.module`, so `require("date-fns/parseISO")` resolves to a function in Node and a module in Webpack.

**Aryan Shridhar** · 2020-09-23 07:47 UTC

@Anders Kaseorg  , Yes , its finally working  , Thanks a lot :+1:

**Mateusz Mandera** · 2020-09-24 16:06 UTC

**Mateusz Mandera** · 2020-09-24 16:15 UTC

@Ritik Did you run `tools/provision`? That fixed it for me

**Ritik** · 2020-09-24 18:29 UTC

That work , but why " ./tools/run-dev.py  --force" not work.

**Alex Vandiver** · 2020-09-24 19:34 UTC

Because `--force` skips the safety checks that verify that the environment is up to date for the code you're running.  When you make a branch from the latest commit and run-dev, you're running the latest code.  If that code has new dependencies (as it did here), you need to re-provision to get those installed.  The `--force` explicitly skips the checks that you have the right dependencies.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-09-30 20:30 UTC

**Abhijeet Bodas** · 2020-10-22 16:34 UTC

I think you are mixing up interactive rebase with the standard `git rebase`.
You would have probably used `git rebase upstream/master` before to keep your branch up-to-date with zulip/master. This is the standard rebase.
The interactive git rebase (the one with the `-i`) is generally used for fixing the commit history on your local branch, before pushing it.
You may find this helpful: https://www.atlassian.com/git/tutorials/rewriting-history/git-rebase

The error states that `US/Pacific` (as `user_pref.timezone`) isn't a valid parameter when passed to `utcToZonedTime(new Date() , user_pref.timezone);`  , But on checking it out locally , `utcToZonedTime` does seem to work fine with `US/Pacific` or `Us/Pacific` .

**Steve Howell** · 2020-10-26 14:10 UTC

It looks like in node you need to tell node where to find the time zones:

https://nodejs.org/docs/latest-v12.x/api/intl.html#intl_providing_icu_data_at_runtime

**Aryan Shridhar** · 2020-10-26 15:53 UTC

Hey Sorry , but could you elaborate a bit and passing any other timezone let's say  , `Asia/Kolkata` works fine as well .

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2020-10-26 21:20 UTC

The `US/Pacific` name was [deprecated](https://github.com/eggert/tz/blob/2020d/backward#L127) in favor of `America/Los_Angeles` in 1993. `America/Los_Angeles` works in Node.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2020-10-26 21:45 UTC

This may be a real problem on recent-ish Chrome versions: https://crbug.com/364374.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2020-10-26 21:50 UTC

(Which makes this a great example of the kind of problem that can only be caught when your tests aren’t mocking away all the cross-interface calls!)

**Neil Pilgrim (neiljp)** · 2020-11-08 08:07 UTC

This repo generates three separate python packages - the python api wrappers, external bots, and a botserver - which need a server to interact with. If you plan to do complex work then a development server is useful to make it easier to isolate what is happening or possible, and ensure this server (or another you have access to) is not unduly affected by the changes you make. However, note that this repo (or the packages) do not have to be installed on the same system as the zulip server - eg. you can run a bot on your own machine against a zulip server anywhere else.

## Working on other PRs

*2020-11-10 to 2020-11-17 · 8 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/Working.20on.20other.20PRs/with/1060598)*

**Abhijeet Bodas** · 2020-11-10 06:01 UTC

I want to know what the code of conduct is for working on PRs opened by other contributors. There are many PRs open where the person who opened it has done a substantial amount of work but is currently inactive or got busy with something else. It does make sense to not start from scratch to avoid duplication of effort, but how does one work on such PRs and get them merged? Should the original contributor be asked for consent? What if they are busy and can't respond? How to avoid taking credit for their work?

**Vishnu KS** · 2020-11-10 06:16 UTC

You can feel free to take over the PR if one of the following is true
* The PR creator has not responded back to the feedback left on the PR for a long time (3 weeks or older seem to be good criteria)
* The PR creator has explicitly stated that they won't be working on the PR anymore.

Just mention in the PR that you are taking over it and close it. And create a new PR by checking out the branch of the initial PR and pushing to your own fork. And work on top of the existing commits.  In that way the original PR creator will also get the credits.

**Steve Howell** · 2020-11-10 11:38 UTC

I agree with what Vishnu said, and I'll add that if it's difficult to preserve the commits from the original PR, you can still mention the person in your commit messages.  Example: "Some of this work was helped by my reading Alice's initial work on this at #NNNNN."

This was actually an intentional thing. This is more reproducible by renaming a topic in private stream.

We also have this in stream _topic_history.js
```js
        if (existing.historical) {
            // We can't trust that a topic rename applied to
            // the entire history of historical topic, so we
            // will always leave it in the sidebar.
            return;
        }
```

@Steve Howell maybe we can improve upon this code in same way?

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2020-12-09 02:43 UTC

historical has different meaning here actually - 

```
* historical: Whether the user actually received any messages in
          the topic (has UserMessage rows) or is just viewing the stream.
```

**Steve Howell** · 2020-12-09 02:46 UTC

We can probably improve on this.  A first step might be to leave it in the sidebar and just improve messaging somehow.

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2020-12-09 02:53 UTC

So, when renaming a topic, we should inform user that the old topic may persist in the sidebar because we don't know if we actually moved the whole topic. If there are no messages left in the topic, it will be automatically removed on a refresh.

I imagine the best way would be to show an alert type popup when executing this code:
```js
        if (existing.historical) {
            // We can't trust that a topic rename applied to
            // the entire history of historical topic, so we
            // will always leave it in the sidebar.
           alert()
            return;
        }
```

```
git fetch upstream

instead of force pushing since I had made a change.

**Aryan Shridhar** · 2020-11-17 08:12 UTC

I would suggest to undo the commits (by logging into [interactive rebase](https://git-scm.com/book/en/v2/Git-Tools-Rewriting-History)) and bring the branch to original commit . Checkout to master and pull (fetch with merge) the new changes , rebase your branch to master (fix merge conflicts , if any ) to place your commits upon the original master branch and finally force push it .

**Max Zawisa** · 2020-11-17 15:17 UTC

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2020-11-17 20:56 UTC

This seems to be a common mistake when creating a pull request from a branch named `master` rather than a feature branch. We do document that you should [work on a feature branch](https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/git/using.html#work-on-a-feature-branch), but maybe our advice is not clear enough and/or in the right place.

#16761

Follow the docs as written and rebase your branch onto upstream/master, not the other way around.

```python3
    @contextmanager
    def assertNoLogs(self, logger: Union[str, logging.Logger] = 'root', level: Union[str, int] = 'INFO') -> Any:
        if isinstance(logger, logging.Logger):
            logger = logger
        else:
            logger = logging.getLogger(logger)
        if isinstance(level, str):
            log_string = f'no logs of level {level} or higher triggered on {logger.name}'
        else:
            log_string = f'no logs of level Level {level} or higher triggered on {logger.name}'

        with self.assertLogs(logger, level) as m:
            try:
                yield m
            except AssertionError as assertion_error:
                if log_string in assertion_error:
                    pass
                else:
                    raise AssertionError('Unexpected logging occured.')
```

**Alex Vandiver** · 2021-07-18 18:28 UTC

@Pulkit Bhargava: The error looks very unrelated to your changes - it's an error installing groomga packages.

In cases like this, there are three possibilities:
 - it's a random failure.  We try hard to weed these out, but some tests occasionally have "flakes" when they fail randomly, such as due to a race condition.
- it's a real failure.  Some weird action at a distance is causing something to fail due to the change, but the reason why is complicated and not obvious at first
 - it's a failure caused by something outside the repo changing.  Since we don't version the should world, the diff of your change is not the only difference from the last test run - packaging systems on the internet may have updated, etc.

I'm these cases, rerunning the test will likely fix the first case, and /may/ fix the last.  I suspect the last case, here, so I reran your test - which passed.

**Alex Vandiver** · 2021-07-18 18:31 UTC

I'd groonga packages had a problem, they've since fixed it.  I'd it hadn't resolved after a rerun, I'd have retested a commit which *currently passes* - if it too starts to fail, that's a strong indication that something outside the repo has broken tests, and they're *all* going to fail until we accommodate that change.

**Alex Vandiver** · 2021-07-18 18:32 UTC

It's also always worth choosing your own topic for a failure, and not hijacking one that isn't related, and that is already marked resolved. :)

I merged your two topics into one.

def bulk_get_streams(realm: Realm, stream_names: STREAM_NAMES, stream_ids: STREAM_IDS) -> Dict[str, Any]:

**Ganesh Pawar (ganpa3)** · 2021-02-08 17:05 UTC

Tornado provides no way to monitor an event loop. I asked the devs, and they said the only way to do that is through asyncio's [debug mode](https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-dev.html#debug-mode).
So, there is no simpler way to do what we want here using tornado.

Asyncio has an attribute [`slow_callback_duration`](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/10ac0cded26d91c3468e5e5a87cecad7fc0bcebd/Lib/asyncio/base_events.py#L1878-L1884) in the main event loop which may be helpful here. It reports when a task takes longer than `slow_callback_duration` seconds.
This blog provides another to monitor the loop: https://blog.meadsteve.dev/programming/2020/02/23/monitoring-async-python/

Requests have been made to the asyncio community to add monitoring hooks to the library https://discuss.python.org/t/adding-monitoring-hooks-to-the-event-loop/3448

**Ganesh Pawar (ganpa3)** · 2021-02-08 17:06 UTC

Alternatives:
[Trio](https://github.com/python-trio/trio) has a [small (unmaintained) library](https://github.com/python-trio/trio-monitor) which helps in monitoring the loop. It plays well with asyncio and tornado.

[Curio](https://github.com/dabeaz/curio) also [provides a way](https://curio.readthedocs.io/en/latest/reference.html#debugging-and-diagnostics) to do the same thing we want here. Although it's quite a different library(as in does things differently) than others, so maybe difficult to go along.

Some external tools that monitor an event loop:
1. [Aiodebug](https://github.com/qntln/aiodebug)
2. [Python agent](https://docs.newrelic.com/docs/agents/python-agent/supported-features/python-event-loop-diagnostics)
3. [aiomonitor](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiomonitor)

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2021-02-09 04:43 UTC

I had some fun learning enough about Python’s `async` internals to write this, though I don’t think there’s a particular reason to prefer something like this over debug mode:

```python
def my_create_task(loop, coro):
    def check_time():
        nonlocal old_time
        new_time = time.monotonic()
        if new_time - old_time > 0.5:
            logging.warning(
                f"task name={task.get_name()} coro={coro} blocked for {new_time - old_time:.3f} s"
            )
        old_time = new_time

    async def wrapped_coro():
        nonlocal old_time
        input = None
        while True:
            try:
                value = coro.send(input)
            except StopIteration as stop:
                return stop.value
            finally:
                check_time()
            while True:
                try:
                    try:
                        input = await AsyncYield(value)
                    finally:
                        old_time = time.monotonic()
                    break
                except BaseException:
                    try:
                        value = coro.throw(*sys.exc_info())
                    except StopIteration as stop:
                        return stop.value
                    finally:
                        check_time()

    old_time = time.monotonic()
    task = asyncio.Task(wrapped_coro(), loop=loop)
    return task

class MyEventLoopPolicy(asyncio.DefaultEventLoopPolicy):
    def new_event_loop(self):
        loop = asyncio.SelectorEventLoop()
        loop.set_task_factory(my_create_task)
        return loop

asyncio.set_event_loop_policy(MyEventLoopPolicy())
```

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-02-17 22:41 UTC

I think there's two things we're looking for with this monitoring:
* First, a good way to judge the utilization of the Tornado process for the purpose of knowing whether we're close to overloading any of them -- currently we output that information via print-logging, but I imagine in the future we'll hook this up to a graph.
* I think `slow_callback_duration` seems good enough for logging any situations where a single callback is unusually expensive -- I'd want to start with that for `0.1s` or so.  We haven't had a bug of that form in a long time, and I'm not super worried about a "forever block" situation -- those will be pretty noticeable in their own way.

**Ganesh Pawar (ganpa3)** · 2021-06-13 16:48 UTC

So, I'm thinking of trying this again. I went through the internals of asyncio and have patched an asyncio version of our current busyness logging hack.

```spoiler Selector-based poll
```py
import time
import logging
import math
import select
from selectors import EpollSelector

from tornado.ioloop import IOLoop


# generic events, that must be mapped to implementation-specific ones
EVENT_READ = 1 << 0
EVENT_WRITE = 1 << 1


class CustomPollSelector(EpollSelector):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self._times = []
        self._last_print = 0.0

    def select(self, timeout=None):
        print("HI")
        if timeout is None:
            timeout = -1
        elif timeout <= 0:
            timeout = 0
        else:
            # epoll_wait() has a resolution of 1 millisecond, round away
            # from zero to wait *at least* timeout seconds.
            timeout = math.ceil(timeout * 1e3) * 1e-3

        # epoll_wait() expects `maxevents` to be greater than zero;
        # we want to make sure that `select()` can be called when no
        # FD is registered.
        max_ev = max(len(self._fd_to_key), 1)

        ready = []
        try:
            t0 = time.time()
            fd_event_list = self._selector.poll(timeout, max_ev)
            t1 = time.time()

            self._times.append((t0, t1))
            while self._times and self._times[0][0] < t1 - 60:
                self._times.pop(0)

            if self._times and t1 - self._last_print >= 5:
                total = t1 - self._times[0][0]
                in_poll = sum(b - a for a, b in self._times)
                if total > 0:
                    percent_busy = 100 * (1 - in_poll / total)
                    print(
                        f"Tornado 9993 {percent_busy:.2f} busy over the past {total:.2f} seconds",
                    )
                    self._last_print = t1

        except InterruptedError:
            return ready
        for fd, event in fd_event_list:
            events = 0
            if event & ~select.EPOLLIN:
                events |= EVENT_WRITE
            if event & ~select.EPOLLOUT:
                events |= EVENT_READ

            key = self._key_from_fd(fd)
            if key:
                ready.append((key, events & key.events))
        return ready


def test():
    time.sleep(1.1)
    IOLoop().current().stop()


loop = IOLoop().current()

# Equivalent of tornado's `set_blocking_log_threshold`, but spammy
loop.asyncio_loop.slow_callback_duration = 1

# Replace asyncio's poll with ours
loop.asyncio_loop._selector = CustomPollSelector()

loop.asyncio_loop.set_debug(True)

loop.add_callback(test)

try:
    loop.start()
finally:
    loop.close()
```

## #16946

*2020-12-22 to 2020-12-24 · 4 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/.2316946/with/1085431)*

**Riken Shah** · 2020-12-22 04:56 UTC

@Anders Kaseorg  I am thinking the fix for this issue is to avoid `admin` to set private stream as notification stream and to fix the `init_dropdown_widgets` function.

**Tim Abbott** · 2020-12-23 16:44 UTC

@Riken Shah can you explain in more detail what you mean?

**Riken Shah** · 2020-12-24 04:31 UTC

I think, what happens is `stream_data` does not have access to private streams so when `signup_notifications_stream_widget` is called it raises an `item is undefined` error as a (private) stream does not exist in `stream data`.

This only happens if we set `New stream notifications` or `New user notifications` to a private stream.

One more thing I have noticed is if you logged in as a guest user and `New stream notifications` is set to public stream(in my case `Scotland`) it raises the same error. 
But if I set it to `all` it works.

I think the fix for this will be
- Add condition in `render` function of `DropdownListWidget` to only render item if it exists 
```javascript
if(!item)
return;
```

**Riken Shah** · 2020-12-24 05:42 UTC

Another Possible fix:
- We can add a fallback stream name instead
```javascript
const text = opts.render_text(item ? item.name: 'Unknown Stream');
```

I was working on the issue https://github.com/zulip/zulip/issues/16538 . So, I was going through https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/master/static/js/server_events_dispatch.js file to see how an unsubscribe event is handled . 
I have a doubt here there are two events remove and peer_remove what is the difference between the two . Can anyone help?

**Steve Howell** · 2020-12-24 14:59 UTC

@Tushar Upadhyay So `peer_remove` informs you that one of the other folks in the realm has subscribed to a stream.  We live-update in that case so that when you do things like managing streams, you can accurately see all the subscribers.

**Steve Howell** · 2020-12-24 15:00 UTC

I believe the `remove` event is for the specific case that **you yourself** have unsubscribed, which has different implications.  (For example, if you follow the code for `stream_events.mark_unsubscribed`, you will see things like ` stream_list.remove_sidebar_row`, where we remove the stream from your left sidebar.)

**Steve Howell** · 2020-12-24 15:02 UTC

A great way to build your understanding on code like this is to put some `console.log` statements there, and then try both scenarios:

* unsubscribe yourself
* open an incognito window and unsubscribe some other user

**Tushar Upadhyay (tushar912)** · 2020-12-24 15:04 UTC

Thanks! that was very helpful .I will surely try to console.log that event

**Steve Howell** · 2020-12-24 15:04 UTC

Sounds good. :smile:

## send_event to inactive users

*2021-01-08 to 2021-01-11 · 23 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/send_event.20to.20inactive.20users/with/1095195)*

**Dinesh Ch** · 2021-01-08 19:15 UTC

What happens to the events sent to inactive users using `send_event`? Do they stay in the event queue till the user connects through some client or are deleted after a certain time? (by inactive I mean not connected through any client. in other words, no green or orange dot in the users list)

I checked https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/subsystems/events-system.html to see if I could find an answer but wasn't able to figure out anything from docs. perhaps I should've tried to understand code in `tornado/event_queue.py`?

**Steve Howell** · 2021-01-08 19:57 UTC

@Dinesh Ch The short answer to your questions is, yes, you should read `tornado/event_queue.py`.   Longer answer coming...

**Steve Howell** · 2021-01-08 20:00 UTC

First, some background.  These two subsystems are actually separate:
* events system -- clients can register for events that eventually go through `send_event`
* presence system -- clients can hit the presence endpoint, which eventually leads to the green/orange dots

**Steve Howell** · 2021-01-08 20:00 UTC

Of course, most of the time, and particularly for the main webapp, it's likely that the client is both registered for **events** and periodically updating **presence**.

**Steve Howell** · 2021-01-08 20:02 UTC

Likewise, when the webapp disconnects or goes idle, the client no longer sends **presence** info and eventually either the client or the server shuts down the **event** queue.

**Steve Howell** · 2021-01-08 20:05 UTC

For examples of when they're different, it's quite plausible for an API client to register for events, which will lead to it getting events via `send_event`, while not ever sending presence updates, and hence no green dots (even if the API key is for the human user).  For example, maybe I, the human, am not online, but I have some automated job that is snooping on messages that will kick out a message to a non-Zulip system when something happens.

**Steve Howell** · 2021-01-08 20:06 UTC

The opposite scenario is slightly more contrived, but I could have a little API thing that calls the presence endpoint to show me present when I'm not actually online or even registering for events.

**Steve Howell** · 2021-01-08 20:07 UTC

Having said all that, I don't think the distinction between presence and events really gets to the heart of your question.

**Steve Howell** · 2021-01-08 20:08 UTC

I think what you may have noticed is that `send_event` calls may involve thousands of users, of which maybe only tens or hundreds are actually "active" in the sense of having registered for events.

**Steve Howell** · 2021-01-08 20:09 UTC

Most of the calls to `send_event` are in `actions.py`, and the functions in `actions.py` aren't really responsible for knowing who's online.  The action functions are very smart about updating the database and knowing who's **eligible** to receive an event, but they're oblivious about who's actually online.  They simply call `send_event` and let the Tornado system sort out who actually needs events now.

**Steve Howell** · 2021-01-08 20:12 UTC

It's worth mentioning that `send_event` itself is not really doing anything but pushing stuff to a queue.  It, too, is oblivious to who's actually online now:

~~~ py
130 def send_event(realm: Realm, event: Mapping[str, Any],
131                users: Union[Iterable[int], Iterable[Mapping[str, Any]]]) -> None:
132     """`users` is a list of user IDs, or in the case of `message` type
133     events, a list of dicts describing the users and metadata about
134     the user/message pair."""
135     port = get_tornado_port(realm)
136     queue_json_publish(notify_tornado_queue_name(port),
137                        dict(event=event, users=list(users)),
138                        lambda *args, **kwargs: send_notification_http(realm, *args, **kwargs))
~~~

**Steve Howell** · 2021-01-08 20:18 UTC

Then our `runtornado` job slurps up the events from the queue and eventually calls `process_notification` in `event_queue.py`:

~~~ py
1055 def process_notification(notice: Mapping[str, Any]) -> None:
1056     event: Mapping[str, Any] = notice['event']
1057     users: Union[List[int], List[Mapping[str, Any]]] = notice['users']
1058     start_time = time.time()
1059
1060     if event['type'] == "message":
1061         process_message_event(event, cast(Iterable[Mapping[str, Any]], users))
1062     elif event['type'] == "update_message":
1063         process_message_update_event(event, cast(Iterable[Mapping[str, Any]], users))
1064     elif event['type'] == "delete_message":
1065         if len(users) > 0 and isinstance(users[0], dict):
1066             # do_delete_messages used to send events with users in
1067             # dict format {"id": <int>} This block is here for
1068             # compatibility with events in that format still in the
1069             # queue at the time of upgrade.
1070             #
1071             # TODO: Remove this block in release >= 4.0.
1072             user_ids: List[int] = [user['id'] for user in
1073                                    cast(List[Mapping[str, int]], users)]
1074         else:
1075             user_ids = cast(List[int], users)
1076         process_deletion_event(event, user_ids)
1077     elif event['type'] == "presence":
1078         process_presence_event(event, cast(Iterable[int], users))
1079     else:
1080         process_event(event, cast(Iterable[int], users))
1081     logging.debug(
1082         "Tornado: Event %s for %s users took %sms",
1083         event['type'], len(users), int(1000 * (time.time() - start_time)),
1084     )
~~~

**Steve Howell** · 2021-01-08 20:20 UTC

For now you can ignore the special-case handling that we do for these events:
* message
* update_message
* delete_message
* presence

Most events simply go directly through `process_event`...

**Steve Howell** · 2021-01-08 20:20 UTC

And at last we basically get to the answer to your question.  Note the simple code for `process_event`:

~~~ py
 915 def process_event(event: Mapping[str, Any], users: Iterable[int]) -> None:
 916     for user_profile_id in users:
 917         for client in get_client_descriptors_for_user(user_profile_id):
 918             if client.accepts_event(event):
 919                 client.add_event(event)
~~~

**Steve Howell** · 2021-01-08 20:24 UTC

Basically, we loop though however many gazillion user_ids that were in the original `send_event` call, but we only call `add_event` for users who have clients, and then for those clients, we only add events if the clients actually "accept" the event, which is basically about whether the client registered for that event type.

**Steve Howell** · 2021-01-08 20:25 UTC

So on a realm like czo, where you have lots of users, but a relatively small number of clients actually registering for events at any given time, that double nested loop actually does a fairly low amount of work.

**Steve Howell** · 2021-01-08 20:26 UTC

And even `add_event` itself is fairly cheap, as it's just updating a data structure.

**Steve Howell** · 2021-01-08 20:29 UTC

So then you might ask..."If event_queue is dropping events for me whenever I have no clients, what happens the next time I register for events?"  Which would be a reasonable question.  And the answer to that is when you register for events, the first thing we do is just grab all the latest, greatest data from the database.

**Steve Howell** · 2021-01-08 20:30 UTC

The events are just incremental updates for clients that are already registered. **New** clients get kind of a current snapshot, then register for the increment events.

**Steve Howell** · 2021-01-08 20:30 UTC

The `event_queue.py` code is worth skimming, as it's only ~1100 lines, albeit somewhat technical in nature.

**Steve Howell** · 2021-01-08 20:34 UTC

https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/subsystems/events-system.html#the-initial-data-fetch may be worth re-reading if any of the above makes sense to you.  Also, feel free to ask follow up questions.

**Dinesh Ch** · 2021-01-11 17:59 UTC

Thanks for making it clear @Steve Howell ! Rereading the events-system doc having read the details you've provided gave me a much better understanding.

Asked this for "typing indicators for streams" that I've been working on. It sends the typing event to all users subscribed to the stream. Wanted to make sure it does no harm. From reading the details you provided I see there won't be any issue as the event is added to queue for only a few user clients which accept the event.

I have opened a WIP PR for that. #17040. Could you take a look?
(Might take some time for me to respond as we came to our grandparents' place for [Sankranti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Makar_Sankranti))

**Steve Howell** · 2021-01-11 20:31 UTC

I added one comment to the PR: https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/17040#pullrequestreview-565712775

@Ganesh Pawar (ganpa3) in case it's helpful, if you're working on a branch with a new migration 0310, and you're about to switch to another branch, if you just run `manage.py migrate 0309` before moving off the branch, it'll work OK.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-02-17 22:44 UTC

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-07-07 16:55 UTC

@Abhijeet Bodas I think so, probably something like `env DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE=zproject.test_settings ./manage.py migrate zerver 0329`.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-07-07 16:55 UTC

That said, that likely doesn't adjust the accounting logic, so the Zulip server might still think it needs to rerun migrations / rebuild things.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-07-07 16:56 UTC

This is one reason why we generally aim to merge relatively early commits adding new database models once we've settled on their design, even if the rest of the feature isn't ready.


## #17009

*2021-01-10 to 2021-01-16 · 8 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/.2317009/with/1095964)*

**Ganesh Pawar (ganpa3)** · 2021-01-10 16:58 UTC

def bot_owner_user_ids(user_profile: UserProfile) -> Set[int]:
    is_private_bot = (
        user_profile.default_sending_stream and
        user_profile.default_sending_stream.invite_only or
        user_profile.default_events_register_stream and
        user_profile.default_events_register_stream.invite_only)
    if is_private_bot:
        return {user_profile.bot_owner_id}
    else:
        users = {user.id for user in user_profile.realm.get_human_admin_users()}
        users.add(user_profile.bot_owner_id)
        return users
```

**Purushottam Tiwari** · 2021-01-19 16:16 UTC

@Steve Howell I found out that mistake was occuring in the `apply_events`. It is occuring because when a bot(which is of administrator type) is demoted then in `check_change_bot_type` function it calls `do_change_user_role` to update the role of user. And then it changes the bot type and sends the event. So in this case(when bot is of type `administrator`) two events are sent:
- `realm_user`: due to the update of bot's role.
- `realm_bot`: due to the update of bot's type.
So realm_bot applies its changes in apply_event and updates bot type(therefore it works as expected).
But `realm_user` event updates only role of the user and not bot type as it does not has that.

This feels cleaner to me:

~~~ py
def do_change_user_role(user_profile: UserProfile, value: int, acting_user: Optional[UserProfile]=None) -> None:
    # This function works for both humans and bots, and the only difference
    # is how we send events.
    old_value = user_profile.role

    if old_value == value:
        # log something
        return

    user_profile.role = value
    user_profile.save(update_fields=["role"])
    RealmAuditLog.objects.create(
        realm=user_profile.realm, modified_user=user_profile, acting_user=acting_user,
        event_type=RealmAuditLog.USER_ROLE_CHANGED, event_time=timezone_now(),
        extra_data=orjson.dumps({
            RealmAuditLog.OLD_VALUE: old_value,
            RealmAuditLog.NEW_VALUE: value,
            RealmAuditLog.ROLE_COUNT: realm_user_count_by_role(user_profile.realm),
        }).decode())

    user_info = dict(user_id=user_profile.id, role=user_profile.role)
    if user_profile.is_bot:
        event = dict(
            type="realm_bot",
            op="update",
            bot=user_info,
        )
        users = # whatever
    else:
        event = dict(
            type="realm_user",
            op="update",
            person=user_info,
        )
        users = active_user_ids(user_profile.realm_id)
    send_event(user_profile.realm, event, users)
~~~

~~~ py
def do_change_user_role(user_profile: UserProfile, value: int, acting_user: Optional[UserProfile]=None) -> None:
    # This function works for both humans and bots, and the only difference
    # is how we send events.
    old_value = user_profile.role
    user_profile.role = value
    user_profile.save(update_fields=["role"])
    RealmAuditLog.objects.create(
        realm=user_profile.realm, modified_user=user_profile, acting_user=acting_user,
        event_type=RealmAuditLog.USER_ROLE_CHANGED, event_time=timezone_now(),
        extra_data=orjson.dumps({
            RealmAuditLog.OLD_VALUE: old_value,
            RealmAuditLog.NEW_VALUE: value,
            RealmAuditLog.ROLE_COUNT: realm_user_count_by_role(user_profile.realm),
        }).decode())

    user_info = dict(user_id=user_profile.id, role=user_profile.role),
    send_event(user_profile.realm, event, active_user_ids(user_profile.realm))

    if user_profile.is_bot:
        # For reasons that are mostly historical, whenever we have a bot and
        # we update fields that apply to both human users and bot users, such as
        # name/avatar/role, then we actually send two events.  Theoretically
        # API writers may be only subscribing to "realm_bot" events, so we send
        # that as a somewhat redundant event to the smaller audience of folks.
        # Our main clients, such as the webapp, can probably just ignore the
        # realm_bot events, depending on how their code is structured.
        event = dict(
            type="realm_bot",
            op="update",
            bot=user_info,
        )
        users = # whatever
        send_event(user_profile.realm, event, users)
~~~
