**Matt Hall** · 2021-01-11 00:02 UTC

Hi folks, finally got a working version of my bot, Snoozebot. I'd love to get some feedback from real programmers before I submit a pull request, etc. The general idea is to allow users to set a time to be pinged on a topic as a way of reminding themselves. Snoozebot sets an At job to @mention the user on the topic via zulip-send. This works well for me, as I often read a Zulip that I can't really address until later. 

Still need to prune away some comments/todos and non-used code/modules (I didn't know what I didn't know), but, Snoozebot does do what I intended. I also still plan to implement passing a specific date to it.

Here is the code:

```python3
from typing import Any, Dict
import  re
from datetime import datetime
from crontab import CronTab
import os
import subprocess


# Current plan is to have the user send snoozebot a message
# containing the desired interval for a reminder (like 4 days).
# Then snoozebot sets a cron job. Cron then calls a python script,
# ping.py with parameters for the send_message function in the Rest
# API. This is a POST https: request to POST https://yourZulipDomain.zulipchat.com/api/v1/messages
# I am thinking the datetime module might be useful for calculating the required
# inputs for the chron job.  




#Todos: 
# 1) Figure out what the incoming web hook needs to be to have
#    snoozebot send the reminder.
# 2) figure out how to have snoozebot start the cron job
# 3) I'm thinking I am going to need a function in snoozebot
# to handle the incoming web hook from crontab





class SnoozeBotHandler:


    def usage(self) -> str:
        return '''
        Snoozebot is a reminder tool that will message you at your requested time in the future. Currently, Snoozebot
        accepts the format '# time', as in '2 minutes.' With this format, Snoozebot is using the 'now +# time' syntax
        for the At command. If that means nothing to you, no worries, here is an example of what you would type in a 
        zulip reply: @snoozebot 4 days
        What that means is, snoozebot, message/mention me in this thread 4 days from this moment.
        In the future, specific date + time formatting will be implemented, such as: @snoozebot 4:13PM on 12/01/2027.
        If you have any questions or feedback, please PM me on Zulip Community Chat. -- MLH 
        '''

    def handle_message(self, message: Dict[str, Any], bot_handler: Any) -> None:
        pattern1 = re.compile(r'(\b\d+\s(minute|hour|day|week|month|year))', re.IGNORECASE)
        # hopefully this pattern object will work for any iteration of "snooze for x days/weeks/months...will have to test.
        #pattern1 = re.compile('\b\d+\s(minute|hour|day|week|month|year)[s]?', re.IGNORECASE)
        pattern2 = re.compile(r'(\b\d{1,2}:\d{2}\s?(AM|PM|am|pm)\s?(Monday|Tuesday|Wednesday|Thursday|Friday|Saturday|Sunday|tomorrow))', re.IGNORECASE)
        #pattern3 will be specific date + time
        # Changing the match variables to use the group method instead of the findall method to get around the tuple issue
        #match = pattern1.findall(message['content'])
        #match2 = pattern2.findall(message['content'])
        match = re.search(pattern1, message['content'])
        match2 = re.search(pattern2, message['content'])
        stream_id = message['stream_id']
        topic = message['subject']
        user = message['sender_full_name']
        heredoc = f"""END 
                   zulip-send --stream '{stream_id}' --subject '{topic}' --message 'Ping! @{user}' --config-file ~/python-zulip-api/zulip_bots/zulip_bots/bots/snoozebot/zuliprc 
                   END"""
        
        # Setting up At command (pipe method)
        # zulip_send_command = zulip-send %(stream name) %(message name) %(message)
        # at_command = " %(zulip_send) | at %(time_input)"
			
        
        #setting up the crontab variables here, but realized that At is the right tool, not crontab
        #cron = CronTab(user='root')
        
        
        # message handling
        if message['content'] == '':
            bot_response = "Please specify the **snooze interval**, such as '4 days'. For help, message me with 'help.'"
            bot_handler.send_reply(message, bot_response)
        elif message['content'] == 'help':
            bot_handler.send_reply(message, self.usage())
        else:
            if pattern1.search(message['content']) != None:
            
                x = match.group(1)
                #y = str(x[0])
                z = "Ok, I'll remind you in " + x
                #print(message['content'])
                #print(pattern1)
                # print(message['stream_id'])
                #print(x[0])
                #print(y)
                #print(match)
                #print(match[0])
                #print(pattern1.search(message[content])
                #y.join(x)
                print(x)
                print(heredoc)
                bot_handler.send_reply(message, z)
                # This is where the At job will be called.
                os.system("at now +%s << %s" %(x, heredoc))                
                # Decided to use At instead of cron. keeping just in case
                # job = cron.new(command='echo hello_word')
                # job.minute.every(5)
                # cron.write() 
                emoji_name = 'alarm clock'
                bot_handler.react(message, emoji_name)
            elif pattern2.search(message['content']) != None:
                # print(pattern2.search(message['content'])
                #print(message['content'])
                l = match2.group(1)
                #m = str(l[0])
                n = "Ok, I'll remind you at " + l
                bot_handler.send_reply(message, n)
                os.system("at %s << %s" %(l, heredoc))  

            else: 
                bot_handler.send_reply(message, "Oops, that won't work. Message me with 'help' for help on how to use me.")
        return 

handler_class = SnoozeBotHandler

```

Any feedback is welcome and greatly appreciated -- thanks!

**Matt Hall** · 2021-01-22 16:08 UTC

I figured out the solution. I was making the beginner error of accessing the dictionary values directly instead of using the get() method for dictionaries, which was causing my code to fail when the value for the 'stream_id' key was empty. I think I've got snoozebot in pretty good shape now. I will upload the latest to my PR on github, 

Basically, it now functions such that, if you set a reminder within a topic, it pings you in the Snoozebot PM stream with a link to the stream/topic. You can also set the reminder for yourself in the Snoozebot PM thread itself, in which case, when it pings you, it is set to display the full content of your message. That way, you can c/p the thread link that you want to remember, or any other details like "Remind me to talk to Karen about...". I think having the pings occur in the PM thread results in a less spammy experience for the other users. I think it is nice to be able to set the ping within a topic to telegraph to other users about when you will remind yourself/when you think you be able to address an issue.

## access_user_by_id naming

*2021-01-24 to 2021-01-27 · 23 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/access_user_by_id.20naming/with/1105969)*

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-01-24 17:37 UTC

Following up on the discussion here: https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/stream/49-development-help/topic/Admin.20Bot.20.20.2312424/near/1104966 @Steve Howell @Purushottam Tiwari:

I think we should have a broader conversation before renaming `access_user_by_id` to `validate_and_access_user`.  For one thing, that name is part of a broader pattern (E.g. `access_stream_by_id`, `access_message`).  And I also would have thought that folks would read an `access_` function as doing some sort of validation that the user doing the access has the permission to do so, but not any further validation.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-01-24 17:37 UTC

(E.g. we're not checking the type of anything).

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-01-24 17:37 UTC

Also, `validate_and_access_user` doesn't make clear how we're looking up the user, though maybe at this point in the codebase, folks will assume by ID since that's the natural mechanism (much more so than by email or some other key).

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-01-24 17:39 UTC

Ahh, hmm, but `access_user_by_id` is somewhat different than the others because it requires administrative access, not read-only access.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-01-24 17:40 UTC

So yeah, maybe something like `access_user_for_administration()` would be more appropriate, and in line with `access_stream_for_unmute_topic_by_id`?

**Purushottam Tiwari** · 2021-01-24 17:48 UTC

> So yeah, maybe something like access_user_for_administration() would be more appropriate, and in line with access_stream_for_unmute_topic_by_id?
I have a doubt on it as it is also used as at places which call this function by using `read_only=True`. So at  those places this name may be somewhat misleading.

**Purushottam Tiwari** · 2021-01-24 17:54 UTC

But on `git grep -n "access_user_by_id"`
I could find only one such instance where we use it with `read_only=True`. It is in `get_subscription_backend`.

**Purushottam Tiwari** · 2021-01-26 06:25 UTC

I think we can rename it to something like `access_user_by_id_if_allowed` or `access_user_by_id_if_permitted` this we are also making clear that user is accessed by id as before, and we can have similar functions in *future* for accessing using other fields like `access_user_by_email_if_permitted`.

**Steve Howell** · 2021-01-26 14:55 UTC

I like the `if_allowed` suffix.

**Purushottam Tiwari** · 2021-01-26 18:38 UTC

Okay so should I move ahead with `if_allowed` suffix and update the pr or any other workaround here(though I can not think of any as of now).
@Tim Abbott  ?

**Purushottam Tiwari** · 2021-01-26 18:40 UTC

Also we have a similar function for bots to which does same job in similar way so renaming `access_bot_by_id` can also be thought of here?

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-01-26 21:20 UTC

Here's another proposal:
* `access_user_by_id` => Works like the current `read_only=True`
* `access_user_by_id(for_admin=True)` => Works like the current `read_only=False`.

I think that'd be more consistent with the rest of our libraries.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-01-26 21:21 UTC

I don't like `if_permitted` because it's not clear what sort of permission we're checking -- permission to see that user (e.g. because you're in the same realm) or permission to modify it (where you need to be an administrator).

**Purushottam Tiwari** · 2021-01-27 12:49 UTC

(replying to Tim Abbott)
> Here's another proposal: * `access_user_by_id` => Works like the current `read_only=True` * `access_user_by_id(for_admin=True)` => Works like the current `read_only=False`. I think that'd be more consistent with the rest of our libraries.
I think this is mostly same as what we have at present. Because we have `read_only` parameter at present and the problem is that at all of the places where it is used, it's simply passed as `access_user_by_id(..., True)` (without passing it as a keyword parameter, thus feels like any normal parameter)reading this doesn't really gives any hint that we also check for accessing permissions here apart from fetching the user.

**Steve Howell** · 2021-01-27 13:26 UTC

We should make the boolean parameters require keywords in the callers, because I agree it's a readability issue if you don't know what `True` actually signifies without going to the function definition.  This is easy to do with the python3 `*` syntax, as I showed in the earlier topic.

**Purushottam Tiwari** · 2021-01-27 18:20 UTC

Okay I think we have some what settled upon keeping the name `access_user_by_id` only and just changing the way parameters are passed. So I will update the current [pr #17112](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/17112) to use `for_admin` parameter as a keyword argument instead of `read_only`.

**Steve Howell** · 2021-01-27 18:32 UTC

@Purushottam Tiwari I hope you can still introduce this change, which adds `*` to make keywords required, plus a more diff-friendly format:

~~~ py
def access_user_by_id(
    user_profile: UserProfile,
    *,
    target_user_id: int,
    allow_deactivated: bool=False,
    allow_bots: bool=False,
    read_only: bool=False,
) -> UserProfile:
~~~

const getNavigatorLanguage = () => {

}

```console
$ cat test-intl.js
const puppeteer = require("puppeteer");

(async () => {

  const page = await browser.newPage();
  console.log(

})();

en-US-posix

en-US
```

 - python script uses the app token to send notifications

**Cyphase** · 2021-02-04 06:30 UTC

Basic auth is [HTTP Basic Authentication](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basic_access_authentication). If you're using `requests` or `httpx`, it's e.g.:

```python
session.post(url, auth=(username, password))
```

The flow would be as follows:

Automated code ..
1. .. uses the Gotify API to create other users while authed as `admin`, saving the usernames and passwords.
2. .. uses the Gotify API to create apps for each user while authed as that user, using the saved credential pairs, and saving the app tokens. Optionally also set an image for the app, e.g. the Zulip logo.
3. .. passes the saved app tokens and information about which users they belong to to the relay daemon.
3. .. sends an email and/or Zulip message and/or whatever else to each user, providing them with their Gotify username and password, as well as the server URL.
4. Users sign in to the Gotify mobile app by providing the server URL and their username and password. The mobile app will create a client token for itself.
5. Magic rainbows and unicorns.

**Vishnu KS** · 2021-02-04 17:02 UTC

```python
def get_hot_topics(
    all_topics: List[DigestTopic],
    stream_ids: Set[int],
) -> List[DigestTopic]:
    topics = [
        topic for topic in all_topics
        if topic.stream_id() in stream_ids
    ]
    topics_by_diversity = sorted(topics, key=lambda dt: dt.diversity())
    topics_by_length = sorted(topics, key=lambda dt: dt.length())

    # Start with the two most diverse topics.
    hot_topics = topics_by_diversity[:2]

    # Pad out our list up to 4 items, using the topics' length (aka message
    # count) as the secondary filter.
    for topic in topics_by_length:
        if topic not in hot_topics:
            hot_topics.append(topic)
        if len(hot_topics) >= 4:
            break

    return hot_topics
```

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-02-16 00:54 UTC

@Debayan Ganguly(LoopThrough-i-j) yep, that's exactly the right decision.  The reason for doing this is that way each commit is a complete self-contained atomic change, that can be reviewed and merged individually (at least after its parents are done).

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-02-16 00:55 UTC

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-02-16 00:55 UTC

(And if the tests are good and cover corner cases, it helps the reviewer confirm that the code is expected to handle those corner cases, which in turn makes reading the code itself easier).

## issue #T901: Inline type annotations

*2021-02-05 to 2021-02-06 · 10 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/issue.20.23T901.3A.20Inline.20type.20annotations/with/1113989)*

**Ahmed Abuamra (ahmedabuamra)** · 2021-02-05 23:00 UTC

I ran `com2ann` to move to Inline type annotations and made PR 910 (https://github.com/zulip/zulip-terminal/pull/910), but it fails the tests.
I think that's because python3.5 can't interpret the inline annotations.

@Neil Pilgrim , The solution is to upgrade python on Github CI?

**Neil Pilgrim (neiljp)** · 2021-02-05 23:08 UTC

We currently don't run python3.5 in ZT CI, so that shouldn't be an issue. Have you run the checks locally?

**Ahmed Abuamra (ahmedabuamra)** · 2021-02-05 23:17 UTC

Yes that's an error from `typing_extensions` package, sorry for that. I'm checking it now

**Ahmed Abuamra (ahmedabuamra)** · 2021-02-06 01:55 UTC

@Neil Pilgrim , 
According to this link https://stackoverflow.com/questions/41207128/how-do-i-specify-ordereddict-k-v-types-for-mypy-type-annotation,
Defining a variable of OrderedDict like that:

`KEY_BINDINGS: OrderedDict[str, KeyBinding] = OrderedDict([
    ('HELP', {
        'keys': ['?'],
        'help_text': 'Show/hide help menu',
        'excluded_from_random_tips': True,
        'key_category': 'general',
    })
])`


causes `TypeError: 'type' object is not subscriptable.` 
Would you suggest following the workarounds presented in the same link or there is a better way?

**Ahmed Abuamra (ahmedabuamra)** · 2021-02-06 01:56 UTC

The problem is in the definition of Key, Value pair [str, KeyBinding] of OrderedDict

**Ahmed Abuamra (ahmedabuamra)** · 2021-02-06 01:58 UTC

I tried it without the class as following

```
KEY_BINDINGS2: OrderedDict[str, str] = OrderedDict([
    ('HELP', 'TEST')
])
```

and got the same error `TypeError: 'type' object is not subscriptable.`

**Neil Pilgrim (neiljp)** · 2021-02-06 05:27 UTC

I believe the issue here is that there is OrderedDict the implementation, and the same name in `typing` which accepts the subscripts for type hinting. This is fixed in python3.7, I believe (https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.OrderedDict).

**Neil Pilgrim (neiljp)** · 2021-02-06 05:28 UTC

For now I suggest we stick with a type comment there, and anywhere where classes and typing names overlap if there are others.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2021-02-06 17:21 UTC

You can also use quotes for types that don’t evaluate at runtime:
```python
KEY_BINDINGS: "OrderedDict[str, KeyBinding]" = OrderedDict([
    …
])
```

**Neil Pilgrim (neiljp)** · 2021-02-06 18:31 UTC

I was going to ask how mypy knows the typing version of OrderedDict (assuming it doesn't have an internal typing variant before 3.7), but I'm not sure how these are checked in a type comment either.


## asking for help

*2021-02-06 to 2024-03-18 · 21 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/asking.20for.20help/with/1114084)*

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-02-06 01:22 UTC

I wanted to provide a few pieces of meta-feedback as I'm catching up on this thread:
* Mentioning specific people with your questions is discouraged.  Especially if that person is busy (E.g. I've been 80% AFK taking care of the newborn since mid-November), doing so tends to discourage other folks from answering.  Also, I read every thread in time (though I have 2K unreads right now from 5 streams that I haven't fully read since November), and so the extra mentions don't accomplish anything.
* It's best to pose your question in a way that provides the context that a friend of yours with more expertise in the relevant technology might be able to answer -- e.g. if you can turn it into "I don't know how to insert HTML <td> elements with JavaScript in this codebase correctly", that's a lot better than only pointing to a specific comment in a PR or the like, because you're requiring someone to click the link in order to understand your question.  This, too, decreases the chances that one of your peers will be able to give you a much time timely answer.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-02-06 01:22 UTC

I encourage other folks to post tips here as well!

You can rebase and re-push the branch, and it will re-run tests.

But if that's the only test that's failing, then you can comment that it's a test flake (linking to [the message which notes that](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/stream/43-automated-testing/topic/main.20failing/near/1759239)) and carry on regardless.

**Alex Vandiver** · 2024-03-18 21:40 UTC

(replying to Shashank Singh)
> Ahh yesss , looks like puppeteer tests have become more flaky lately.

In general, any flake is *quite bad*, and we should try to solve them quickly.  If every test failed 0.01% of the time, *we would never have a passing test run*.  Flaky tests reduce people's confidence in the real tests, making them more likely to dismiss any failing test as "probably a flake" rather than investigate it.  And they cause confusion for developers, when seemingly-unrelated tests fail -- as happened here.

So I encourage folks to try to take a stab at fixing them, rather than dismiss them.  It's a *very* valuable fix to contribute.

**Shashank Singh** · 2024-03-18 21:51 UTC

Totally agree. Initially I also had this low confidence on puppeteer tests due to its non-deterministic failures and took long to decide whether this is something related to my changes. 
But eventually I found ways to fix them because most of the non-deterministic flaky ones have been disabled or fixed currently and the issue was mostly due to my changes.

**Shanu** · 2021-04-03 21:46 UTC

On `resend` we change the `prereg_user`'s invited_at field to current time, but before sending the `invite` event we delete the confirmation object since we don't want two Confirmation object having foreign key to same prereg_user. Most importantly we'd have to pass an extra field `invite_expires_in_days` for setting up email reminder,  creating confirmation link and sending it via email, value for 'invite_expires_in_days` depends on if we want to keep expiry date same or extend it in accordance with invited_at.
```python3
 ## zerver/lib/actions.py

@@ -6365,31 +6381,37 @@ def do_revoke_multi_use_invite(multiuse_invite: MultiuseInvite) -> None:
 
 def do_resend_user_invite_email(prereg_user: PreregistrationUser) -> int:
     # These are two structurally for the caller's code path.
     assert prereg_user.referred_by is not None
     assert prereg_user.realm is not None
 
     check_invite_limit(prereg_user.referred_by.realm, 1)
 
     prereg_user.invited_at = timezone_now()
     prereg_user.save()
#     invite_expires_in_days = ??
+    prereg_user.confirmation.clear()
 
     do_increment_logging_stat(
         prereg_user.realm, COUNT_STATS["invites_sent::day"], None, prereg_user.invited_at
     )
 
     clear_scheduled_invitation_emails(prereg_user.email)
     # We don't store the custom email body, so just set it to None
     event = {
         "prereg_id": prereg_user.id,
         "referrer_id": prereg_user.referred_by.id,
         "email_body": None,
+        "invite_expires_in_days": invite_expires_in_days,
     }
     queue_json_publish("invites", event)
 
     return datetime_to_timestamp(prereg_user.invited_at)
```

There’s a local setting overriding your global one. It was probably created by `git clone`. This is why we tell you to configure `core.symlinks` before running `git clone`.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2021-02-17 19:16 UTC

Delete your clone, then proceed with the documented steps in order, running `git clone` at the appropriate time. (There may be a way to reconfigure the existing clone, but probably not worth it to figure out whether that would work correctly.)

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2021-02-17 19:18 UTC

Oh, from looking more closely at your screenshot, it appears that your home directory is itself a Git repository. Did you do that intentionally?

Can someone suggest some ways to handle this incompatibility in Linux, or perhaps an alternative to `pyperclip`?

Problem with `pyperclip`: It requires system installation of `xclip` in Linux

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-02-26 17:05 UTC

I didn't find something obviously better by googling.  I would look at what other terminal apps do; I would guess they just present the text in a way such that one can easily double-click to copy to clipboard.

**Neil Pilgrim (neiljp)** · 2021-02-26 17:42 UTC

This is what we currently do, but different terminal emulators support it to varying levels, requiring various modifiers to select text for example. That's not to say these are bad, just that they don't make it as easy to get data in and out. Also, some do not support areas of text, which is more applicable to TUIs where there are multiple columns.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-03-01 23:03 UTC

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-05-19 19:19 UTC

Oh, I suspect there's two things going on here:
* You had a bug in your code that prevented the CSRF token from being initialized, e.g. by throwing an exception before that module got loaded?  I've got a headache so not thinking clearly, but maybe the import order here is wrong?  I'm not sure `alert_popup` should be before `csrf` here, but also not sure that it is relevant:
```
import "core-js/features/promise";
import "core-js/features/symbol";
import "css.escape";
import "../webpack_public_path";
import "../../../tools/debug-require";
import "../alert_popup";
import "../csrf";
```

When an event request (`/json/event`) is sent during/before the password change request ( `password_change_in_progress = true` ) and event request  is finished after password change request is completed (`password_change_in_progress = false`), Hence [causing page to redirect to login page](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/f5b7e5d9346eb2d70941e907e48f1d6daba33ac9/static/js/setup.js#L45).

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2021-03-25 21:51 UTC

Waiting 1 second is never the right fix for a race condition.

What we need to check in the `ajaxError` handler is not whether `password_change_in_progress` is true when the request returns, but whether it was ever true while the request was in flight.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2021-03-26 21:29 UTC

`event.timeStamp` is not a `Date`. It’s measured in milliseconds from the beginning of the document’s lifetime, so it will always be less than a `Date`.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2021-03-26 21:30 UTC

What we need is the time when the failed request was initiated.

```javascript
$(document).ajaxSend((event, xhr) => {

});
```

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-03-29 18:41 UTC

Hmm, one question is how much resources running CI on Firefox is worth.  A few notes:
* Have we found any actual Firefox bugs with this?
* I think it'd add something like 5 minutes to total CI runtime to run it.
* We probably don't want to add it to the existing end-to-end job, since that'd increase the "total CI latency" before all jobs are done.
* Adding a new job has significant overhead in terms of total CPU minutes used.
* Maybe the right answer is to run Firefox just on the existing `backend` job?

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-03-29 18:42 UTC

One idea we could consider is randomly choosing between Firefox and Chrome for what to run in CI, to avoid increasing the expense but to get added exposure.  Has its own risks.

@Kenny Kariappa generally we don't want to pull in a dependency that requires a separate Docker image in order to run, as Docker isn't currently a requirement for running Zulip.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-03-02 19:42 UTC

I expect we would want an integration to work like GitLab's: https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/administration/integration/kroki.html

It's the same model we have for our Twitter integration -- we'd query the free third-party service to do the rendering if configured on a Zulip server (via specifying the URL to use), rather than requiring a self-hosted Zulip to run their Docker container as a dependency.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-03-02 19:42 UTC

Perhaps large installations like zulip.com would run their Docker container rather than using their API if there were a reason to do so, but I don't think it'd be worth adding a somewhat hard-to-install Docker dependency to a normal Zulip installation, so this should be optional.

The Twitter rendering integration is the most similar -- basically the code block for it starts with checking if the Twitter secrets are set, and if not, it does nothing:

```
def fetch_tweet_data(tweet_id: str) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:                                     
    if settings.TEST_SUITE:                                                                          
        from . import testing_mocks                                                                  
                                                                                                     
        res = testing_mocks.twitter(tweet_id)                                                        
    else:                                                                                            
        creds = {                                                                                    
            "consumer_key": settings.TWITTER_CONSUMER_KEY,                                           
            "consumer_secret": settings.TWITTER_CONSUMER_SECRET,                                     
            "access_token_key": settings.TWITTER_ACCESS_TOKEN_KEY,                                   
            "access_token_secret": settings.TWITTER_ACCESS_TOKEN_SECRET,                             
        }                                                                                            
        if not all(creds.values()):                                                                  
            return None                                                                              
```

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-03-05 22:00 UTC

So I'd add in `/etc/zulip/settings.py` (https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/subsystems/settings.html) a setting `KROKI_RENDERING_URL`, document that setting in way similar to the JITSI_SERVER_URL setting in `prod_settings_template.py` (maybe we'll have it default to the Cloud version, but folks can customize if they want to self-host Kroki).  And then basically the rendering logic will either call into Kroki or just render the raw input in a normal code block depending on that setting.

*2021-03-03 to 2021-03-03 · 5 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/enable.20notification.20for.20API.20created.20users/with/1126251)*

**Fabio M.** · 2021-03-03 12:10 UTC

Hi, I need to set up the notification settings for users programmatically created via API. I've found the [update-notification-settings](https://zulip.com/api/update-notification-settings) API, but there's no user ID parameter. Does it mean it's at global level, for all users?

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-03-03 17:59 UTC

@Fabio M. no, instead it just modifies your own user account.  There isn't a way to modify these settings for other users (though of course if you're self-hosting you can change the defaults).

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-03-03 17:59 UTC

Can you talk about what you're trying to do?

**Fabio M.** · 2021-03-03 20:10 UTC

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-03-03 22:51 UTC

@Fabio M. you can read zerver/models.py, the section around `enable_stream_push_notifications`, and adjust various values from False to True.  https://zulip.com/api/update-notification-settings has some documentation on what the fields do; it's not great but there's a pretty straightforward 1:1 mapping with the settings in the UI.

## updating installation count table

*2021-03-05 to 2021-03-12 · 11 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/updating.20installation.20count.20table/with/1127517)*

**Shanu** · 2021-03-05 03:18 UTC

This is related to the TODO(on line 263 -- Add support for updating installation data after changing an individual realm's values.) in `analytics/lib/counts.py` which needs to be addressed in order to fix [#13486](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/issues/13486) (Related PR [#13695](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/13695)).

One of the possible solution "seems" to be to use `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (key) DO UPDATE` (UPSERT), but the problem with this is that we use multiple constraint, where `ON CONFLICT` clause handles only one unique constraint.
```python
class InstallationCount(BaseCount):
    class Meta:
        # Handles invalid duplicate InstallationCount data
        constraints = [
            UniqueConstraint(
                fields=["property", "subgroup", "end_time"],
                condition=Q(subgroup__isnull=False),
                name="unique_installation_count",
            ),
            UniqueConstraint(
                fields=["property", "end_time"],
                condition=Q(subgroup__isnull=True),
                name="unique_installation_count_null_subgroup",
            ),
        ]
```
(which in raw SQL looks like this)
```postgresql
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX "unique_installation_count" 
ON "analytics_installationcount" ("property", "subgroup", "end_time") 
WHERE "subgroup" IS NOT NULL;

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX "unique_installation_count_null_subgroup" 
ON "analytics_installationcount" ("property", "end_time")
WHERE "subgroup" IS NULL;
```

**Shanu** · 2021-03-05 03:19 UTC

Another solution is to use  `COALESCE` function (returns the first argument that is not nulll)  which can replace NULL in the index:
```postgresql
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX "unique_installation_count" 
ON "analytics_installationcount" ("property", COALESCE("subgroup",  ''), "end_time");
```
This can handle duplicates in both the cases where subgroup is NULL and  NOT NULL.
Now we can UPSERT with this `ON CONFLICT` statement (installation_query):
```postgresql
...ON CONFLICT (property, COALESCE(subgroup, ''), end_time) DO UPDATE SET value = EXCLUDED.value;
```

**Shanu** · 2021-03-05 03:20 UTC

But I couldn't find any docs to handle this in Django, so maybe we'll have to do this manually in migration.

**Shanu** · 2021-03-05 03:20 UTC

Could there be a better approach? Is there something I'm missing here?

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-03-05 06:49 UTC

@Arpit Sharma has thought about this problem a good amount.

**Shanu** · 2021-03-08 14:48 UTC

Arpit Sharma suggested [to use ON CONFLICT...DO UPDATE(UPSERT) statement](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/13695#issuecomment-578953328) (which is not the outright solution as now we have two unique constraints) for updating data if the row  already exists in the table, but that was before he fixed [#12362](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/issues/12362) in [f299f313](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/commit/f299f31340ee36c8af700f9715c7e3001eebfb98) (adding different UniqueConstraint depending on the value of `subgroup`).  I couldn't find anything else from him on this.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-03-10 01:01 UTC

I think I'm imagining a more explicit solution, where if there is a conflict, we'd make a determination on whether to accept the new data, and if so, we'd just delete the old dataset for the relevant days before doing the insert.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-03-10 01:02 UTC

I think anything involving `UPSERT` is unlikely to make possible corruption in cases where different keys are present between the old and new versions.

**Shanu** · 2021-03-11 22:29 UTC

(replying to Tim Abbott)
> I think I'm imagining a more explicit solution, where if there is a conflict, we'd make a determination on whether to accept the new data, and if so, we'd just delete the old dataset for the relevant days before doing the insert.
Wouldn't deleting old data will produce wrong stats?

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-03-12 02:15 UTC

Well, the client Zulip server has the complete data set going back to the beginning of time.  So the core question here is how we handle these cases where there is inconsistency between the old and the new -- do we just want the "new" history.

For context, the root cause of this is likely to be end users who fork their Zulip server (E.g. spin up a backup for testing and that backup ends up submitting data to the server); it's kinda a hard problem in general.

**Shanu** · 2021-03-12 05:18 UTC

I was only thinking of the case when there is same values in rows for two different realm in RealmCount table, there would be an integrity error if we'd try to update InstallationCount table.
As for your point, I don't think if I understood it completely, but if some backup submits some data, yeah, that'd be a problem unless we differentiate between data submitted by main and backup.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-03-10 00:47 UTC

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-03-10 00:48 UTC

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-03-10 00:48 UTC

Yeah, so I think the bug is that `channel.js` (which we intend to be usable from portico pages) is importing `reload.js` (which we do not).

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-03-10 00:49 UTC

Ironically, looks like it's due to this block of code for handling CSRF errors:
```
        if (xhr.status === 403) {                                                                    
            try {                                                                                    
                if (JSON.parse(xhr.responseText).code === "CSRF_FAILED") {                           
                    reload.initiate({                                                                
                        immediate: true,                                                             
                        save_pointer: true,                                                          
                        save_narrow: true,                                                           
                        save_compose: true,                                                          
                    });                                                                              
                }                                                                                    
            } catch (error) {                                                                        
                blueslip.error(                                                                      
                    "Unexpected 403 response from server",                                           
                    {xhr: xhr.responseText, args},                                                   
                    error.stack,                                                                     
                );                                                                                   
            }                                                                                        
        }                                                                                            
        orig_error(xhr, error_type, xhn);                                                            
```

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-03-10 00:50 UTC

I think we probably want to figure out a way to change the interface to allow `channel.js` to trigger a reload without calling directly into the other module, e.g. it should probably be raising a special type of exception or triggering an event or something.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-03-10 00:52 UTC

As a secondary thing, we should probably figure out how to make blueslip report JS exceptions in portico pages as visibly as we do in app pages.

* For older mobile app clients, send a `realm_filters` key that gets constructed from the `realm_linkifiers` object.

## Backslash Escape Inline Pattern

*2021-03-17 to 2021-03-23 · 3 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/Backslash.20Escape.20Inline.20Pattern/with/1134301)*

**Akshat** · 2021-03-17 11:56 UTC

Please go through the conversation in #17511.
The problem I found that after re-enabling Backslash Escape Inline Pattern, characters like `<`, `>`, `&` remain unescaped and cause XSS issue.

**Akshat** · 2021-03-17 11:56 UTC

So, after debugging, I found that the `handleMatch` function in `InlineProcessor`, after every match:
> the region between the returned `start` and `end` are replaced with a placeholder token and the new element is added to the tree.

(Related [documentation](https://python-markdown.github.io/extensions/api/#example_3))
And that `placeholder token` is swapped back out for the actual elements by the parser.
In the case of [`ESCAPED_CHARS`](https://github.com/Python-Markdown/markdown/blob/master/markdown/core.py#L72), any single character is swapped by a placeholder over [here](https://github.com/Python-Markdown/markdown/blob/master/markdown/inlinepatterns.py#L325).
And that placeholder is swapped back by the actual text string over [here](https://github.com/Python-Markdown/markdown/blob/master/markdown/postprocessors.py#L129).

I can't understand why its class name is `UnescapePostprocessor` (and no escaping is done)? Though there is a possibility that chars like `<`, `>`, `&` can remain unescaped and can cause XSS issues.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-03-23 07:40 UTC

I don't think I understand the details of markdown processor internals to help with this without spending a bunch of time reading the code.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-03-25 19:12 UTC

So the issue there is largely that `nginx` output differs depending on the version of `nginx`.  We already have logic for that for the different Ubuntu versions in `tools/ci/success-http-headers.template.txt` -- there's a few variables that get substituted.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-03-25 19:13 UTC

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-03-25 19:13 UTC

But the other piece seems to be just different warning text for the fact that it's a self-signed certificate.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-03-25 19:14 UTC

Probably the least annoying workaround is to have a `tools/ci/success-http-headers.template.debian.txt`.

**Aryan Shridhar** · 2021-03-23 19:59 UTC

The GMT offset is because the locale is set to `en-us` within the pr and timezone abbreviations differ from locale to locale afaik. 
However, pytz supports the 'abbreviated' timezone using [tzinfo](https://pythonhosted.org/pytz/#tzinfo-api), something like: 
```
>>> tz = pytz.timezone("America/Los_Angeles")
>>> edt_value = tz.localize(datetime.datetime.now(), is_dst=False).tzname()
>>> edt_value
'PDT'

```

Proposed #17761 to modify the `timezones.json` to provide the 'abbreviated' value of each timezone as well(Modified [`build_timezone_values`](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/17761/files#diff-6f9436502eac6ac4253fa7ade5fb37f85306f4f5e32f47485f691a79453441be)). If it doesn't feel right, we can switch back to what Nikhil proposed.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-03-23 23:21 UTC

I'd be curious for @Anders Kaseorg's thoughts on formatting here.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2021-03-23 23:39 UTC

It’s always worth keeping in mind that the abbreviated timezones are ambiguous, e.g. US Central = Cuba = China = CST, India = Israel = Ireland = IST.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-03-23 23:39 UTC

Yes, though if it's showing the user's own personal timezone, that may not be an issue?

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-03-23 23:40 UTC

(Like, they will need to learn that's how this type of pill works if they're confused, but once they do, it'll be pretty clear).

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2021-03-23 23:40 UTC

Maybe. I guess the point of this is just to reassure the user that yes, this really has been converted to local time?

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-03-23 23:40 UTC

Yeah, exactly.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-03-23 23:40 UTC

(Which I think the timezone name does a lot better than -0700, since users might not have that value memorized)

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2021-03-23 23:43 UTC

The current PR is wrong though in that it might show `PDT` for a future or past time that’s `PST` or vice versa.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-03-23 23:44 UTC

Yeah, agreed we shouldn't do that.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-03-23 23:44 UTC

(Also we should check if we need to pass the timezone map data in via `pytz` or one of the `date-fns` libraries does this?)

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2021-03-23 23:49 UTC

Hmm maybe it’s not wrong in that way.

**Aryan Shridhar** · 2021-03-24 14:40 UTC

`date-fns-tz` also requires a `locale` to be passed within [utctozonedtime](https://github.com/marnusw/date-fns-tz#utctozonedtime) function. 
A raw example could be: 
```javascript
import enGB from 'date-fns/locale/en-GB'
const tz_format = "zzz";
const tz = "Europe/Paris";
const abbreviation = format(utcToZonedTime(new Date(), tz), tz_format, {
  timeZone: tz,
  locale: enGB
});
```
This does return `CET`, but when tz is set to `Asia/Kolkata` it returns `GMT+5:30`.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2021-03-24 18:56 UTC

I’m guessing you’ve created an import cycle. We have an unfortunate number of existing cycles, but certain cycles can cause code to load in the wrong order and lead to variables being used before they’re defined.

But yeah, bundles/app.js only needs to import certain specific modules for their side effects or to force import cycles to load in the right order. In general, modules should only be imported where they’re used.

function set_topic_edit_properties(group, message) {
    group.realm_allow_message_editing = page_params.realm_allow_message_editing;

**Smit Patel (smitpatel24)** · 2021-03-27 08:40 UTC

The following function worked normally before the changes: 
But now I it won't show the `bankruptcy_banner`. I used to set ` page_params.unread_msgs.count` and `page_params.furthest_read_time` to zero just so that I can check the changes I had made in the banner.
```export function should_display_bankruptcy_banner() {
    // Until we've handled possibly declaring bankruptcy, don't show
    // unread counts since they only consider messages that are loaded
    // client side and may be different from the numbers reported by
    // the server.

    if (!page_params.furthest_read_time) {
        // We've never read a message.
        return false;
    }

    const now = Date.now() / 1000;
    if (
        page_params.unread_msgs.count > 500 &&
        now - page_params.furthest_read_time > 60 * 60 * 24 * 2
    ) {
        // 2 days.
        return true;
    }

    return false;
}
```

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2021-03-27 08:44 UTC

That’s the `should_display_bankruptcy_banner` function in `unread_ui.js`? The function works fine. But it’s now looking at the `page_params` variable in the `page_params.js` module, not at your global variable.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2021-03-27 17:43 UTC

The braces `{}` are important there (this is [object destructuring](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Operators/Destructuring_assignment#object_destructuring)), but I guess browser consoles need extra syntactic context:

```js
const {page_params} = require("./static/js/page_params");

```

## audible notifications for ZT

*2021-03-28 to 2021-04-02 · 16 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/audible.20notifications.20for.20ZT/with/1145793)*

**Zeeshan Equbal** · 2021-03-28 12:54 UTC

I am working on adding support for audible notifications in ZT.
Currently, ZT only supports audible notifications for OSX, which it achieves using an AppleScript executed through `osascript`. I have figured out two ways to support audible notifications for other platforms(ie. Linux & WSL), but having a hard time deciding which would be better:
1. Using a python package (something like [`playsound`](https://pypi.org/project/playsound/))
2. Using a system-package (probably [`paplay`](https://manpages.debian.org/testing/pulseaudio-utils/paplay.1.en.html) from `pulseaudio-utils`)


The first option is a bit unreliable since there might be (system)dependency issues with it, as I recently experienced while testing it on Linux - This package uses `gi` which seemed to be inaccessible from inside a `venv`, without using something like `vext`(?), and probably other unexpected issues.

Using a system-package, in my opinion, is safe, since it's guaranteed to work?
I have tested `paplay` on both Linux and WSL and it seemed to work perfectly without any issues, however, I am skeptical whether pulseaudio is a pre-installed system package in all/most Linux distros or not?
Apart from the above options, is there any other way that I'm looking for?

One more thing to mention here is that we probably don't want to add audible notifications for WSL yet, because currently don't even [support desktop notifications there](https://github.com/zulip/zulip-terminal/issues/767).

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-03-29 00:10 UTC

I think `pulseaudio-utils` is reasonable to require for this feature on a Linux desktop system; I'm pretty sure it's included by default in an Ubuntu desktop environment.  One could consider falling back to the terminal bell if not available, which would be relevant if you're using it over SSH to a server?  Not sure if that's a good idea from a UX perspective.

**Zixuan James Li** · 2021-03-31 00:07 UTC

Does the `EmbeddedBotHandler` (or `zerver/lib/bot_lib`) have any documentation? How is it related to `zulip_bots` in zulip-api? It seems that bot_lib is only used in the queue processors. I'm wondering what are the expected fields for the dictionary `message` for methods like `react` and `update_message` as I can't find any specifications.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-03-31 00:54 UTC

@Zixuan James Li for context, this is an incomplete feature that is not usable in production yet.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-03-31 00:55 UTC

But basically the idea is that you should be able to take any bot from the `zulip_bots` project and run it in any of several runtimes:
* The default way of running a bot described here: https://zulip.com/api/running-bots
* zulip-botserver
* EmbeddedBotHandler, included in the Zulip server.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-03-31 00:56 UTC

The system is to some extent almost finished -- in that we figured out most of the structural problems and implemented things like BotStorage and BotConfig to do them -- but then we lost steam for doing UI and thinking through how to manage the security question of "What bots are allowed with `EmbeddedBotHandler` if we don't want to risk hacks to the Zulip server?".

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-03-31 00:57 UTC

So I'd read the `zulip_bots` implementation and print-debug to figure the structure out to some extent.

**Zixuan James Li** · 2021-03-31 11:07 UTC

OK. Thank you! This makes it a lot clearer.


## Error Handling for EmbeddedBotHandler

*2021-04-01 to 2021-04-11 · 26 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/Error.20Handling.20for.20EmbeddedBotHandler/with/1149986)*

**Zixuan James Li** · 2021-04-01 20:10 UTC

In the implementation for ExternalBotHandler, it's not responsible for dealing with any internal error that might occur when handling the bots' request. What it does is just returning the message from the server which might contain the error message. 
But for EmbeddedBotHandler, we can directly call functions like `do_add_reaction` and we need to deal with the error handling logic in the handler itself. What confuses me is that should we still return a dictionary formatted like `{"result":"error","msg":"asd"}`, or should we raise exceptions like `EmbeddedBotEmptyRecipientsList`?

**Zixuan James Li** · 2021-04-01 20:17 UTC

Well, intuitively the embedded implementation should just function just like the external one. The bots created should also work just the same. But if so, why don't we just reuse the APIs used by the external bot, because it ensures that everything will work in the same way?

**Steve Howell** · 2021-04-01 20:24 UTC

@Zixuan James Li Are you suggesting that the embedded bots would just run as a separate process?

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2021-04-01 20:25 UTC

This bugged me too. I think the Python API should always convert our `{"result": "error"}` dicts into Python exceptions to discourage unhandled errors.

**Zixuan James Li** · 2021-04-01 20:26 UTC

Then it might make no sense to call it `embedded bot` then. Perhaps we still need to figure out a way to let it work the same as the API does.

**Zixuan James Li** · 2021-04-01 20:30 UTC

Should the user of the bot api be aware of whether the bot will be running with either `EmbeddedBotHandler` or `ExternalBotHandler`? I'm not so sure about who should be dealing with the exceptions that occur in `EmbeddedBotHandler`.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2021-04-01 20:31 UTC

I’m suggesting that *both* `EmbeddedBotHandler` and `ExternalBotHandler` should throw exceptions.

**Zixuan James Li** · 2021-04-01 20:35 UTC

Oh, then perhaps we might also need to introduce some custom exceptions that work for both implementations of handlers.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2021-04-01 20:36 UTC

Right.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-04-01 22:54 UTC

Yeah, that sounds like the right plan to me as well.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-04-01 22:56 UTC

(The exception handling part of this might be at the `zulip` API bindings layer, not the `zulip_bots` layer).

I have created #17951 for issue #17863 (Extending support in production and development environments for Debian Bullseye). The pull request contains three commits currently:
1.  dev_environment: Add support for debian bullseye.
2. production: Add support for debian bullseye for production.
3. production_suite: Add Debian bullseye to production suite.

So the pull request is failing CI for the third commit where we test the production install on `Bullseye`. For the production install, the image is build from base image available on docker hub (`buildpack-deps: bullseye-scm`). Since Bullseye is not yet released, it is unstable and hence the `/etc/os-release` file does not contain useful meta-data such as `VERSION_CODENAME`,etc. which are used in the production-install script. Hence the script is exited with status code 1 and the check fails.

## Error message

*2021-04-02 to 2021-04-02 · 2 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/Error.20message/with/1151810)*

**Sahil Batra** · 2021-04-02 19:50 UTC

I wanted to discuss what is our preferred way to show error in case when a particular user is not allowed to do some task.

In some cases we show a very specific error messag like `Only organization administrators can subscribe others to stream`, while in some cases we just show `Must be an organisation administrator`, like in `who can invite others` setting.

Using a generic message though will reduce the error handling code, especially in some settings which use `COMMON_POLICY_TYPES` (and we are also planning to migrate other possible settings to use this) with the downside of not providing the correct error message with explicitly specifying what they are not allowed to do(though users must be aware of what they are doing actually).

So, we can try to maintain the conistent behaviour across the different settings if we prefer the one over other.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-04-02 21:52 UTC

Good question.  I think in an ideal world the properties we want are:
* Consistency, which both makes things more readable and saves time for translators.
* Making clear in which cases it's a configuration thing vs. an "impossible" thing -- e.g. "Must be an moderator" isn't ideal if you could potentially lobby your organization administrator to change it.
* In some security contexts, avoiding leaking information (E.g. if you try to access a stream_id from another organization, you should get the same error message as trying to access a stream_id that doesn't exist.

One thing we've been slowly doing is extracting reusable exception classes in `zerver/lib/exceptions.py` for common errors, and trying to just use those rather than having each error have its own string that might be written in a different style.

**Greg Price** · 2021-04-05 23:13 UTC

In zulip-mobile:tools/ I have the following solution for this class of problem, as a file `tools/lib/ensure-coreutils.sh`:
```bash
# Usage:
#   . ensure-coreutils.sh
#
# Ensures GNU coreutils are available in PATH.
# May add to PATH, or exit with a message to stderr.
#
# The GNU coreutils are a basic piece of infrastructure for having
# a reasonable 21st-century shell scripting environment, so we
# freely invoke this in any of our scripts that need `readlink -f`
# or other features not always found without them.
#
# On any GNU/Linux system this is of course a non-issue.  Likewise
# on Windows: we inevitably require Git, and Git for Windows comes
# with a GNU environment called "Git BASH", based on MSYS2.
#
# So this is really all about macOS.  Fortunately it's easy to get
# coreutils installed there too... plus, many people already have
# it installed but just not in their PATH.  We write our scripts
# for a GNU environment, so we bring it into the PATH.

check_coreutils() {
    # Check a couple of commands for GNU-style --help and --version,
    # which macOS's default BSD-based implementations don't understand.
    fmt --help >/dev/null 2>&1
    readlink --version 2>&1 | grep -q GNU
}

ensure_coreutils() {
    # If we already have it, then great.
    check_coreutils && return

    # Homebrew provides names like `greadlink` on the PATH,
    # but also provides the standard names in this directory.
    # Try that.
    homebrew_gnubin=/usr/local/opt/coreutils/libexec/gnubin
    if [ -d "$homebrew_gnubin" ]; then
        export PATH="$homebrew_gnubin":"$PATH"
        check_coreutils && return
    fi

    cat >&2 <<EOF
This script requires GNU coreutils.

Install from upstream:
  https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/
or from your favorite package manager; for example:
  brew install coreutils
EOF
    return 2
}

ensure_coreutils || exit

* Similarly the logic above that that looks for Homebrew versions and adds them to PATH can add /usr/local/gnu-getopt/something to PATH

## droplet 404 issue

*2021-04-06 to 2021-04-06 · 11 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/droplet.20404.20issue/with/1154902)*

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-04-06 17:31 UTC

@Ken Clary and I have been trying to debug an interesting set of issues he's seeing with a new remote development VM (Digital ocean droplet).

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-04-06 17:32 UTC

The first issue turned out to be https://github.com/zulip/zulip/issues/12565.  We should figure out how to set that configuration; I'm not sure if there's an easy way to do it in Vagrant because of container-based providers, but we can definitely do that sysctl setup in a droplet that we control the image for.

@Vishnu KS FYI for that question.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-04-06 17:47 UTC

The second issue appears to have been one or more Python process leaked from `run-dev.py` that ended up resulting in `webpack` OOM killing.  I'm not sure what we can do about that; we use `os.setpgrp()` to try to arrange that the processes all die together when one stops them.  

I think the only additional thing we could readily do is write PIDs to a file on startup, and read that file on `run-dev.py` startup and kill any leaked processes still running.  I've used this technique before (the `zephyr_mirror` script does it), so it is possible, but I'm not sure whether it's worth it.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-04-06 17:57 UTC

OK, and the third issue was that the room domain `http://example.zulipdev.org:9991`  was returning 404s.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-04-06 17:58 UTC

And that's actually just how our development droplets are configured.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-04-06 18:00 UTC

The reason for that is a bit subtle:

We want to support testing with multiple organizations on different subdomains, and for that we want e.g. `zulip.example.zulipdev.org`, `analytics.example.zulipdev.org`, `realm57.example.zulipdev.org`.  We have DNS setup properly, so that works.

But the question is what to do with the root domain, `example.zulipdev.org`?

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-04-06 18:09 UTC

We generally don't want to host a realm on a domain where other realms are on subdomains, because how cookies work can result in that causing weird behaviors where the subdomains see both cookies.  (Though possibly this is no longer a constraint with modern browser cookie features; worth investigating)

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-04-06 18:10 UTC

Oh, the other bug: Our droplets claim they are localhost:9991, because this bit of code in `run-dev.py` doesn't understand their configuration:
```
    external_host = os.getenv("EXTERNAL_HOST", f"localhost:{proxy_port}")
    print(f"\nStarting Zulip on:\n\n\t{CYAN}http://{external_host}/{ENDC}\n\nInternal ports:")
```

So we probably need a hacky bit of code for the droplet case there.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-04-06 18:18 UTC

OK, merged e51344ab2d8f3cc910a6cdf60955a938f3cb8105 for that last bug.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-04-06 18:20 UTC

(replying to Tim Abbott)
> The second issue appears to have been one or more Python process leaked from `run-dev.py` that ended up resulting in `webpack` OOM killing. I'm not sure what we can do about that; we use `os.setpgrp()` to try to arrange that the processes all die together when one stops them.

I can't reproduce this original issue with a leaked Python process, but I can reproduce on a droplet the webpack `node` process being leaked for like 15 seconds after one does `Ctrl+C`.  It does appear to die on its own, but it appears webpack has longish sections when it defers signal handling, or something?  Not sure

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-04-06 18:23 UTC

OK, for the domain issue, we kinda have a few things we can do:
* Adjust https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/request-remote.html to mention the subdomain
* Make example.zulipdev.org not 404, and instead show a page that lists the organizations on the server.  (I actually thought that was what it would do, so it's possible we just broke this at some point)
* Adjust cookie policy to allow hosting an organization on the root domain.

**Zixuan James Li** · 2021-04-11 18:23 UTC

When running tests with GitHub Actions for this #18082,
I got an error
```
ERROR: test_registration_of_active_mirror_dummy_user (zerver.tests.test_signup.UserSignUpTest)
```
Looking at the traceback, I know that it is `TimeoutError`
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
...
File "/srv/zulip-py3-venv/lib/python3.8/site-packages/DNS/Base.py", line 352, in sendUDPRequest
    r=self.processUDPReply()
  File "/srv/zulip-py3-venv/lib/python3.8/site-packages/DNS/Base.py", line 135, in processUDPReply
    raise TimeoutError('Timeout')
DNS.Base.TimeoutError: Timeout
```
I think this might be a problem of my PR, as neither running the same tests on my machine nor on Ubuntu 18.04 Bionic doesn't give me a failure. I wonder if this is a problem with the existing backend tests.

**Zixuan James Li** · 2021-04-11 18:24 UTC

The details of the errors can be found [here](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/runs/2318273076?check_suite_focus=true).

**Debayan Ganguly(LoopThrough-i-j)** · 2021-04-11 18:27 UTC

Did you try rebasing the current master?

**Zixuan James Li** · 2021-04-11 18:31 UTC

This branch is only two commits behind upstream, so I think it might not be the problem. Also, the PR passes same test on another job on Ubuntu 18.04 Bionic but fails it on Ubuntu 20.04 Focal, so I guess the error occurs randomly.

**Gaurav Pandey (ligmitz)** · 2021-04-11 18:32 UTC

Looks like a timeout error.

**Zixuan James Li** · 2021-04-11 19:04 UTC

Without any changes, the tests work just fine this time. I guess there should be a way to avoid such error?

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-04-13 17:49 UTC

This is a test setup bug -- our tests are intended to run without access to the Internet, precisely because that can result in nondeterministic test failures, and this particular test misses our logic for ensuring that (by disabling outgoing HTTP requests) because it only does a DNS query.

Fixed in 4e8a5f4da857705406dba123bb5818f2951b7953.  Thanks for the report @Zixuan James Li!

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-04-13 17:49 UTC

(I verified afterwards that `test-backend` passes with my network turned off, so this is the only bug of this form we had)

**Zixuan James Li** · 2021-04-13 18:24 UTC

This is great! Thank you.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2021-04-14 19:52 UTC

As for your original error, ``An `id` must be provided to format a message``: this is not a uniqueness issue. We generate an `id` that’s equal to `defaultMessage` (see `babel.config.js`), so there’s no risk of collision.

The issue is that you must literally write `$t({defaultMessage: "message"})` and not some refactoring like `descriptor = {defaultMessage: "message"}; $t(descriptor)`. Both the Babel plugin and the extraction system only recognize calls with a literal object argument.

If you need to define descriptors separately from calling `$t`, see [`defineMessage` and `defineMessages`](https://formatjs.io/docs/intl/#definemessages).

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-04-14 20:05 UTC

As a sidenote, the need to literally write `$t({defaultMessage: "message"})` and not pass some other variable into `$t` is true for every internationalization system I've seen.  Structurally, in order to find strings, the i18n system needs to parse the codebase to find every string, since you'll never find obscure conditions by trying to run it.  And so doing indirection through passing a variable to `$t` and the like makes it impossible for the i18n library to discover your string.

(The same thing applies to tagging backend strings for translation -- though we have a linter to complain about this mistake there).

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-04-14 20:06 UTC

I guess part of what's going on here is that the FormatJS syntax is annoyingly verbose, which is why you're tempted to do that refactor to avoid line-wrapping.  They really should have made the API just `$t(message, ...)` so that the common case would be cleaner.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2021-04-14 20:21 UTC

I think the reason for the verbosity is that in typical projects, `id` is different from `defaultMessage` and it’d be unclear which one you’re trying to abbreviate.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-04-14 20:24 UTC

Well, you could guess the one with the long name; `$t({id: "my_id"})` is fine, but yeah, I know. It's just a little sad to live in a world where having a string in your JavaScript code ends up being this big block because of internationalization, whereas it wouldn't have been that way were it in a template.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2021-04-14 20:25 UTC

There was a [proposal](https://github.com/formatjs/formatjs/issues/1532) to make `intl.formatMessage('xyz')` mean `intl.formatMessage({id: 'xyz'})`, which was rejected. I’m not finding a proposal to make it mean `intl.formatMessage({defaultMessage: 'xyz'})`, so maybe we should propose that and see what happens.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2021-04-14 20:27 UTC

The split between the `@formatjs/intl` core and `react-intl` is new last year, so it’s not too surprising that more polish has gone into the `react-intl` side of the API.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2021-04-14 20:31 UTC

Also, the TypeScript types would need careful finessing to make this pass type checking both before transformation (`babel-plugin-formatjs`) and after (`@formatjs/ts-transformer`).

**Greg Price** · 2021-04-14 20:34 UTC

(replying to Anders Kaseorg)
> There was a [proposal](https://github.com/formatjs/formatjs/issues/1532) to make `intl.formatMessage('xyz')` mean `intl.formatMessage({id: 'xyz'})`, which was rejected. I’m not finding a proposal to make it mean `intl.formatMessage({defaultMessage: 'xyz'})`, so maybe we should propose that and see w …

Yeah, in fact the reasoning in the rejection seems all about saying they want to encourage people to have the default message be right there in the source. (Which I agree with.) So that's encouraging for the chances of such a proposal.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-04-16 16:18 UTC

(replying to Ganesh Pawar (ganpa3))
> Shouldn't this be the default?
The problem with doing this is that `lint --modified` only looks at changes you haven't committed; what we'd actually want to check in many cases is that we probably actually want to check everything you've modified since you forked from master if the goal is to verify your PR isn't broken.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-04-16 16:19 UTC

One other useful thing to mention is `tools/setup-git-repo`, which will create a pre-commit hook that runs `lint` on just the files changed in your new commit.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-04-16 16:21 UTC

That all said, I've been thinking about starting a thread about `lint` time as well.  The core problem is `black` and `prettier` -- together, those two are a lot more expensive than our pre-existing linters (primarily because they each run like 10 processes in parallel and finish at about the same time as everything else).  I don't think I appreciated the extent to which introducing them would make `lint` multiplicatively slower.  (I also experience my computer locking up while it's running even though I have an extremely powerful laptop).

**Gaurav Pandey (ligmitz)** · 2021-04-16 16:25 UTC

I experience such locks quite regularly with my code editor (vscode) just crashing after some-time.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-04-16 16:25 UTC

I think it is probably worth rethinking a little bit the interface for how we run `prettier` and `black`. 
* One theory is that we should run them with `--fix` in the `pre-commit` hook before running our other linters there, since then you automatically always commit formatted code if you're using that tool.  
* Another theory is that we should configure them to in the default mode only run on files changed since `HEAD~100` or some such rule -- basically ensuring that it'll catch things if master is broken due to recent changes, and also anything in your branch -- and then we have some mode we run in CI to deal with black/prettier version upgrades.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-04-16 16:27 UTC

I do think this is one of the more important things for us to figure out a solution to, since anything like this that's annoying for doing regular development work is very costly to the project.

> My only issue with `tools/setup-git-repo` is that even if it fails it still goes to the commit which in my opinion it shouldn't.

(Last 40 commits is 263 files right now; I'm sure it's often less than that.  And we could also do `$(git merge-base upstream/master)` -- part of the reason to do a large number of commits is to handle large branches).

**Steve Howell** · 2021-04-16 16:39 UTC

I use the only-modified option pretty frequently, but my concern with any kind of `HEAD~N` strategy is that I think sometimes linters will only realized that B file is broken due to the change in A if you run the linter on both, even though B changed.  For example, maybe a change in A's mypy type causes B to be broken.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-04-16 16:40 UTC

We could constrain that special behavior to linters that have no cross-file behavior, which is essentially everything but the type-checkers.

The container is not currently running.

```
even though my commit is, well, good.

**Steve Howell** · 2021-04-16 16:42 UTC

My workflow is basically this:
* tweak code
* run linters in modified mode to catch stupid syntax errors and the like
* run tests (using options to make them efficient in incremental mode)
* if test fails, repeat above
* if tests succeed, continue below
* run code formatters on just the fixed files
* run fuller tests (checking for code coverage, etc.)

**Ganesh Pawar (ganpa3)** · 2021-04-16 16:43 UTC

(replying to Ganesh Pawar (ganpa3))
> Since we are discussing this, I would also mention that the `commit-msg` hook is kind of broken. In a vagrant setup, if the container is off, it fails to run raising a false alarm ```bash The container is not currently running. WARNING: Your commit message does not match Zulip's style guide. ``` eve …
It's because of `tools/commit-msg`

**Greg Price** · 2021-04-17 00:04 UTC

(replying to Tim Abbott)
> (replying to Ganesh Pawar (ganpa3)) ```quote Shouldn't this be the default? ``` The problem with doing this is that `lint --modified` only looks at changes you haven't committed; what we'd actually want to check in many cases is that we probably actually want to check everything you've modified sinc …

This is exactly what `tools/test` does in the mobile repo. I recommend it.

**Greg Price** · 2021-04-17 00:13 UTC

Having your tests run quickly when you're iterating really makes a big difference to the development experience, and the linters are part of the tests.

The fact that in order to have a good experience you basically have to discover a set of different variant commands you can do to get the tests to run reasonably quickly is not a developer-friendly way for things to work. The tools should proactively do the right thing in the first place.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-04-19 21:30 UTC

> The tools should proactively do the right thing in the first place.

Agreed.  It used to be the case with our linters that the right thing was to check everything because that was fast; but since moving `mypy`, `prettier`, and `black` into that framework, it definitely isn't and never will be again.  

@Aman Agrawal (amanagr) would you be up for looking at making `tools/lint` support a "lint  changes on this branch" feature?  We will likely want to make it the default with a `lint --all-files` or something mode for the current default behavior?

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2021-04-19 21:38 UTC

Okay, sure.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2021-04-20 01:27 UTC

Keep in mind that mypy and TypeScript fundamentally can’t check only modified files, because a change in one file may introduce a type error in another.

**Greg Price** · 2021-04-20 05:21 UTC

Yeah. Our `tools/test` in mobile doesn't try to do anything special about this when it comes to Flow, for exactly the same reason.

The bright side is that both Flow and mypy (and I'd expect TypeScript to be just as good on this front or even better) have their own caching that lets them not spend much time when things haven't changed. Plus Flow and perhaps also mypy will use inotify (or the equivalent on macOS or Windows) to notice when a file is modified and get started immediately on rechecking. So at least for mobile, the Flow check is often instantaneous because the daemon has already checked the current version of the files by the time you ask.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-04-20 17:49 UTC

Yeah, agreed; the main problem here is `black` and `prettier`, which are very expensive.  (They finish in a similar time to our other jobs on my computer, but each has like 6-10 processes using a full CPU while doing so).

Generally it's nice to group related functions together.

Ultimately, it's whether doing so improves the readability of the codebase.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-04-23 21:22 UTC

I think that's a hard question to summarize the considerations for quickly, but that's the right question in my mind.

## recursive call question

*2021-04-29 to 2021-04-29 · 5 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/recursive.20call.20question/with/1171371)*

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-04-29 19:15 UTC

Anyone have a good idea how to implement https://github.com/zulip/zulip/issues/18310 happily?  Basically, we have a function that takes like 12 parameters, and we'd like to have it do a recursive call to itself, in a way that is robust to changes.

Maybe we could have it accept a `dataclass` as its parameter rather than 12 individual arguments, and then it can just call itself with the dataclass?

@Purushottam Tiwari (m-e-l-u-h-a-n) FYI.

**Purushottam Tiwari** · 2021-04-29 20:36 UTC

One more problem, that is possible with current implementation is that if any parameter is updated in the function before the recursive call then in current implementation we call the function with updated value of that parameter.
(But currently no parameter is updated, within the function before the recursive call).

**Purushottam Tiwari** · 2021-04-29 20:55 UTC

I think we can save a copy of all the arguments at the beginning of the the function, using `locals()`.
I found it here: [https://stackoverflow.com/a/23982966](https://stackoverflow.com/a/23982966).
Then use it during recursive call, this will also solve possible problem of updating of parameters within the function.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2021-04-29 20:59 UTC

`locals()` doesn’t work well with mypy.

I think the real answer is that this should use a loop, not recursion: #18314.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-04-29 21:10 UTC

Hmm, yeah, that works.

## fetch-rebase-pull-request

*2021-04-30 to 2021-04-30 · 13 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/fetch-rebase-pull-request/with/1172112)*

**Alya Abbott** · 2021-04-30 21:17 UTC

Hey. I'm getting an error when trying to run `./tools/fetch-rebase-pull-request` on a Mac. Any thoughts on how to fix it? I did what I needed for today by copy-pasting lines from the script and manually filling in the variables, but it would be good to have a more general solution. :)
```
alya@wyndle zulip % ./tools/fetch-rebase-pull-request 18212
readlink: illegal option -- f
usage: readlink [-n] [file ...]
```

**Alya Abbott** · 2021-04-30 21:17 UTC

I tried upgrading bash from homebrew, but it didn't help.

**Alex Vandiver** · 2021-04-30 21:22 UTC

The problem is that it's getting the BSD `readlink`, not the GNU one that Linux machines will have. You can `brew install coreutils` to get a `greadlink`, but that's not a general solution.

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2021-04-30 21:30 UTC

You can still run it inside vagrant shell for now.

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2021-04-30 21:31 UTC

Will have to setup ssh keys though.

**Greg Price** · 2021-04-30 21:41 UTC

Ah. I think the simplest fix is to drop the `readlink` call. Does this patch fix it?
```diff
diff --git a/tools/fetch-rebase-pull-request b/tools/fetch-rebase-pull-request
index 115f61d9d..31ff4cdf7 100755
--- a/tools/fetch-rebase-pull-request
+++ b/tools/fetch-rebase-pull-request
@@ -1,9 +1,9 @@
 #!/usr/bin/env bash
 set -e
 
-this_file=$(readlink -f "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")
+this_dir=${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}
 # shellcheck source=lib/git-tools.bash
-. "${this_file%/*}"/lib/git-tools.bash
+. "${this_dir}"/lib/git-tools.bash
 
 require_clean_work_tree 'check out PR as branch'
 
```

**Greg Price** · 2021-04-30 21:43 UTC

The one thing that gives up behavior-wise is that if you make a symlink somewhere that points directly at that script (like in your `~/bin/` or something), and try to run it using that symlink, it won't work. (It'll still work just fine if there are symlinks somewhere higher up in the paths involved -- just not for the script itself.)

**Alya Abbott** · 2021-04-30 21:44 UTC

Cool, Greg's patch worked!

**Greg Price** · 2021-04-30 21:44 UTC

Cool, I'll push that, then

**Greg Price** · 2021-04-30 21:47 UTC

In the mobile repo's `tools/` directory, we have a bit of code that fixes this up nicely for you -- it makes sure you have the GNU coreutils on your PATH, and if you don't already it goes looking to see if you have them installed via Homebrew and seamlessly adds them that way. And if you don't have that either, it gives you a nice message saying to install them.

... But to *invoke* that common piece of code, we have to do basically exactly the same thing as those two lines of this script are doing -- we have to find a library file relative to the script's own location.

So just for that bootstrap step, we still give up on `readlink -f`.

**Greg Price** · 2021-04-30 21:47 UTC

(But at least then the rest of the script can count on coreutils.)

**Greg Price** · 2021-04-30 21:57 UTC

da8763d88975299a0887ddeaeb01e6a6a0cc7fea

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-04-30 21:59 UTC

We could do some sort of feature/feature check instead, I suppose, if we want that feature.
