*2021-05-10 to 2021-05-10 · 3 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/verify.20home.20page.20loaded.20in.20tests/with/1177800)*

**Dinesh Ch** · 2021-05-10 18:38 UTC

Working on #15449 which redirects a user to the password reset page on trying to load the home page after logging in with weak password. I have added a test for this and [verified the user is redirected to password reset page using url](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/15449/files#diff-940c870652d79870a457600e9cde59f74a5b9980268c9df6e62e0c0d846b7e66R745). In the same test I want to make sure the user isn't taken to this reset page after changing password. For this,  I wrote:
```
            result = self.login_with_return(user_profile.delivery_email, strong_password)
            result = self.client_get(result.url)
            self.assertEqual(result.status_code, 200)
```
But it fails with `status_code=400` with the result being a JSON error saying "Could not allocate event queue". For now, [the test just makes sure `result.status_code` is not 302](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/15449/files#diff-940c870652d79870a457600e9cde59f74a5b9980268c9df6e62e0c0d846b7e66R766-R768)(because the other case redirects to reset page), but it isn't probably the best way.

Any ideas on how to test this in a better way?

cc: @Mateusz Mandera

**Mateusz Mandera** · 2021-05-10 18:43 UTC

@Dinesh Ch `test_home,py` uses this helper for making requests to the home page:
```

    def _get_home_page(self, **kwargs: Any) -> HttpResponse:
        with patch("zerver.lib.events.request_event_queue", return_value=42), patch(
            "zerver.lib.events.get_user_events", return_value=[]
        ):
            result = self.client_get("/", dict(**kwargs))
        return result
```

Since it does some mocking of the event queue system, I presume that's to get around the problem you're facing - so you can probably utilize it in your tests as well

**Dinesh Ch** · 2021-05-10 18:57 UTC

That works. Thanks for the quick reply!

## vdom conditional updates

*2021-05-30 to 2021-06-07 · 23 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/vdom.20conditional.20updates/with/1191373)*

**Purushottam Tiwari** · 2021-05-30 06:39 UTC

I am working on #18505(Add topic filter in "more topics" view in left sidebar), design discussion thread(#**design>topic filter** ).
I've made changes for the search input to appear below stream name(in zoomed topic view, in left sidebar), and also added logic for filtering topics based on search terms.
I am facing a problem that, topic list is built using `vdom.js` so I had made changes to prepend `filter input li(list item)` to so it before all topics and below stream name. But on entering search terms in the input the topic list rebuilds, and as the items do not totally match the previous list items vdom rerenders the filter input li(list item) along with other topics. Because of this, the content of the search input get cleared on its own.

**Purushottam Tiwari** · 2021-05-30 06:39 UTC

This  GIF shows what the problem is:
[topic_filter.gif](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/d3/_mvpJO5-hmZPLSgriK4zQnRz/topic_filter.gif)

**Purushottam Tiwari** · 2021-05-30 08:06 UTC

I was curious if there could be a way re-rendering of the filter input could be prevented(though topic list could change based on search input)? 
(May be I'll try to keep filter input outside of the topic list so that its re-rendering could be prevented during search.)

**Steve Howell** · 2021-06-01 14:26 UTC

I don't understand why the filter widget needs to be part of the vdom-rendered stuff.

**Purushottam Tiwari** · 2021-06-01 14:44 UTC

Actually, most of the things in stream list in left-sidebar are rendered using vdom. So each stream name is a `li` element(rendered using vdom) and in zoomed topic view another unordered list(`ul`) is inserted in that stream li which lists the topics. So I had prepended the filter input widget before topics list to have smae styling as other topic items, that's why it was part of vdom rendered content.
But I think may be I should create a widget like stream filter input and style it using css to place it in a proper place. I'll try this currently I am in middle of [issues/#16233](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/issues/16233)(Show user groups and streams in user info popover).

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-06-01 17:16 UTC

@Purushottam Tiwari I'm not sure we want to be using `vdom` to adjust the set of visible elements when filtering; wouldn't it make sense to be just show/hiding individual topics based on the filtering state instead of adding/removing them from the DOM?

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-06-01 17:16 UTC

That's how filter widgets usually work, and seems appropriate for this context.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-06-01 17:17 UTC

That said, there's a related issue we're going to need to think hard about in the `topic_zoom` state, which is making sure that a new message coming in doesn't similarly rerender and replace the filter widget.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-06-01 17:19 UTC

But I do think we should consider restructuring things to have the `topic_zoom` view be more of its own thing (with its own HTML elements) that doesn't use `vdom` and is instead built with `list_widget` and a single stream-display element at the top, with the rest of the STREAMS section hidden anyway?

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-06-01 17:19 UTC

(I don't remember how this part of the codebase works, so maybe I'm missing something)

**Steve Howell** · 2021-06-01 18:38 UTC

It’s possible that we just need to pass a little more state into the vdom, like the current content of the textbox.  The vdom implementation isn’t really rocket science and can be upgraded as needed.  You just give it something to draw, and then on the second draw it tries to make basic shortcuts.

**Steve Howell** · 2021-06-01 18:51 UTC

I don't fully understand the problems here, but I know enough about `vdom.js` and`list_widget.js`that the solution here isn't to go to `list_widget.js`.  The two pieces of code are fairly similar in purpose.  I can elaborate on the differences, but I think in this particular case the differences are mostly moot.  I could be wrong.

**Steve Howell** · 2021-06-01 18:53 UTC

I think the main idea here is that all of our lazy-list-rendering widgets (we have three!) are good at lazy-rendering lists, and all have their sweet spots and flaws, but everything outside of the actual list (like search input boxes or clickable/sortable table headers) should be outside their scope.

**Steve Howell** · 2021-06-01 18:56 UTC

* list_widget: most legacy (~10 use cases), most maintened (and oldest), most bells and whistles, mostly used in settings panels, but RT is very notable exception
* buddy_list: good scrollbar behavior, just as performant as list_widget, no bells and whistles, not yet reusable (but close)
* vdom: most generic, zero bells and whistles, mostly performant for unread counts (you just feed it data and render functions, and it doesn't build new DOM for existing list items)

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-06-01 23:27 UTC

I wouldn't call `list_widget` legacy; I think of it as our standard way to do lists of objects across the codebase.  And yeah, I agree that they shouldn't be responsible for rendering filter/search widgets.

**Purushottam Tiwari** · 2021-06-03 18:28 UTC

So I solved it, by extending `TopicListWidget` class(which actually uses vdom) as it appeared most simple way  without disturbing vdom implementation. My approach is somewhat inspired by [steve's this message](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/stream/49-development-help/topic/vdom.20conditional.20updates/near/1198802). So I made following changes:
* Just before old dom was removed I stored the input value in class variable.
* Added a function to update input and its event handlers after rerender.
* When leaving zoomed view, again set the value of the class variable to `""`.

Changes are in [m-e-l-u-h-a-n/zulip/commit/504f6a1](https://github.com/m-e-l-u-h-a-n/zulip/commit/504f6a11479c03f74ec0739271128325a427183f).
@Steve Howell (showell) @Tim Abbott if anyone has time to look at this commit and suggest if my approach is correct. If this appears right I'll update the tests and move forward for handling live update on new message when search is going on.

**Purushottam Tiwari** · 2021-06-03 20:10 UTC

Oh btw, in above message by extending I meant adding functions to `TopicListWidget` class, not creating any child class to extend it.

@Purushottam Tiwari I think that strategy is reasonable if we feel the need to have it inside the `vdom` object.  

The main downside of that approach is that we need to be careful to avoid messing up keyboard focus in that text box when doing rerenders.

My guess is that'll be a fine strategy, and you should do a PR based on it; @Steve Howell (showell) may have thoughts on how to better organize the code, but it's certainly not so ugly we should block the feature or anything.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-06-01 17:21 UTC

@Sai Rohitth Chiluka at least part of your problem is that you need to set `EXTERNAL_HOST` to match the hostname you're actually typing into your browser, e.g. `localhost:3000`.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-06-01 17:22 UTC

(The simplest solution is usually to port-forward the same hostname).

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-06-01 17:23 UTC

You should read about `EXTERNAL_HOST` and `ALLOWED_HOSTS` and `REALM_HOSTS` if you want to do something more fancy, but basically, web security rules mean you need to tell the Zulip server what hostname(s) will be used to connect to it, not what hostname it's actually running on behind a proxy or port forwarder or whatever.

* The `openapi-generator` npm wrapper has the option to read OpenAPI data from and write the output to files only via CLI. Or should those files be generated at time of server start maybe and the bindings be read from those files on each query? There are also some python packages which might eliminate the temporary file issue, but I'm not sure how precise those would be.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-06-01 23:28 UTC

@Suyash Vardhan Mathur (MSurfer20) I think if we end up using its generated documentation, we'll want that to run in `update-prod-static` for production use and `provision` in development; it's probably 100x too slow to want to run in response to a request.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-06-01 23:29 UTC

I'm not sure what its generated documentation actually looks like; it's possible we can display it in tabs alongside Python/curl, and it's possible that doing so would be too messy and we'll want a basically independent site for it.

**Suyash Vardhan Mathur (MSurfer20)** · 2021-06-02 03:40 UTC

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-06-02 06:29 UTC

@Suyash Vardhan Mathur (MSurfer20) it sorta depends how we're thinking about these external bindings.  I think it's worth stepping back a bit from trying to integrate it into the tooling and actually just run the tool once and play with its output.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-06-02 06:29 UTC

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-06-02 06:30 UTC

So if you just have the output hosted somewhere (maybe a test GitHub repository?) that folks can browse the documentation and download/test it from, I think that's the next step for this project.

## RawPostDataException

*2021-06-10 to 2023-06-19 · 13 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/RawPostDataException/with/1205984)*

**Akshat** · 2021-06-10 15:59 UTC

I'm using the `responses` module to create mock responses in `test_push_notifications.py`. To create them, I've to use a callback function that will accept an argument (say `req`) of type `requests.models.PreparedRequest`.  I've to use `req.body` to further process the data, but this is rasing `RawPostDataException`. A part of the Traceback shows that:
```
  File "/srv/zulip/zerver/decorator.py", line 861, in wrapped_func
    return func(request, *args, **kwargs)
  File "/srv/zulip/zerver/lib/request.py", line 323, in _wrapped_view_func
    val = orjson.loads(request.body)
  File "/srv/zulip-py3-venv/lib/python3.6/site-packages/django/http/request.py", line 328, in body
    raise RawPostDataException("You cannot access body after reading from request's data stream")
django.http.request.RawPostDataException: You cannot access body after reading from request's data stream
```
`body` is again accessed inside  `zerver/lib/request.py`.

Any help? How can I access `body`/any workaround for this?

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-06-10 18:35 UTC

@Akshat (akshatdalton) I'm not sure what processing you need to do, and would wonder if that's actually the right design.

But if you really need to do this, what you should do is make a deepcopy of your `req` object, and process that.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-06-10 18:36 UTC

In order to support interactions with very large files that one might not want to load into memory all at once, the Django `request.body` field is a streaming object (think of it like an iterator), and so it can't be iterated through more than once on an individual object.  Obviously, in this specific case, you don't have a large file, so it's totally fine to copy.

**Akshat** · 2021-06-11 02:49 UTC

Oh, probably I confused you by using the term - "process the data"; by that, I mean "dynamic response". I added this design [here also](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/9f3d1fdbdba3b1f06e00c8cc37198a6e065e2ad7/zerver/tests/test_slack_importer.py#L55-L62). Earlier, I tried using `req.copy()`, but it was still giving me the same `RawPostDataException`.

Today, I've barely rewritten/done any changes in the code, and things are working smoothly :shrug:.
Don't know what was the actual issue.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-06-11 15:53 UTC

Yeah, I meant `copy.deepcopy()` or similar.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-06-11 15:54 UTC

`.copy()` generally just does a shallow copy of an object, and the problem you had was with an object referenced by the original.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2021-06-11 16:53 UTC

No, don’t use `copy.deepcopy()`. That will copy a huge amount of extra stuff with unpredictable side effects, such as all the `UploadHandler` objects in `req._upload_handlers` and everything they internally refer to and so on, and will probably just corrupt your requests instead of solving your actual problem, since `req.body` is a property that streams data in from the network.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-06-11 16:58 UTC

Well, I think this is just for a test, but yeah, it's probably still a bad idea.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-06-11 16:59 UTC

Since bad code in tests risky getting copied elsewhere.

**Akshat** · 2021-06-11 17:41 UTC

~~Django doc says~~ ~~https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/dev/ref/request-response/#django.http.QueryDict.copy:~~
> ~~Returns a copy of the object using `copy.deepcopy()`. This copy will be mutable even if the original was not.~~

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2021-06-11 17:42 UTC

That’s `QueryDict`, not `HttpRequest`.

**Akshat** · 2021-06-11 17:42 UTC

Ah, right, yes! I realised after sending the message.

You should use `stub_templates` if you're more interested in seeing what values get passed to the template than what the template returns.  There are arguments on both sides.

**Steve Howell** · 2021-06-11 04:36 UTC

This is a typical pattern for using `stub_templates`:

~~~ js
    let template_called;
    stub_templates((template_name, data) => {
        template_called = true;
        assert.equal(template_name, "message_reaction");
        assert.deepEqual(data, {
            count: 1,
            emoji_alt_code: false,
            emoji_name: "8ball",
            emoji_code: "1f3b1",
            local_id: "unicode_emoji,1f3b1",
            class: "message_reaction reacted",
            message_id: opts.message_id,
            label: "translated: You (click to remove) reacted with :8ball:",
        });
        return "<new reaction html>";
    });

    reactions.view.insert_new_reaction(opts);
    assert.ok(template_called);
~~~

**Steve Howell** · 2021-06-11 04:37 UTC

If @Anders Kaseorg truly believes the above code is an anti-pattern, I would like to see the alternative.  I don't doubt that there is a superior alternative; I would just like to see it.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2021-06-11 06:22 UTC

I’ll give you two answers and you can decide which one you like better:

1. Don’t mock templates. They’re pure functions with no side effects, and it’s typically not complicated to verify that they did something reasonable. Invoking the actual template gives us some level of checking that it was really invoked in the way it expects to be invoked, and increased coverage is good.
2. If you really want to mock templates anyway, templates are just modules now, so they can be mocked with `mock_cjs` like other modules. We shouldn’t need a special template-specific mechanism for this. With `mock_cjs` you can mock the specific template you’re interested in, instead of being forced to mock all templates with a single function.

**Steve Howell** · 2021-06-11 06:30 UTC

I prefer #2.

**Steve Howell** · 2021-06-11 06:35 UTC

My philosophy with respect to #1 is that we can verify that templates are reasonably well-formed with our `check-templates` tool, and while there are certainly possibilities for templates to get out of sync with JS code in terms of var names, those are superficial errors, not logic errors, and the main goal of node tests is to verify logic, not integration. Ideally our puppeteer tests will drive out integration errors. Or, maybe we can do something more laser-focused on making sure JS-template impedance mismatches don't occur.  It hasn't really been a pain point up until now.

**Steve Howell** · 2021-06-11 06:37 UTC

In order to accomplish #2, which I'm on board with, can you submit an example PR showing the technique?

**Steve Howell** · 2021-06-11 06:40 UTC

I think there are places where #1 applies.  For small enough templates, we should just do something like this:

~~~
assert.equal(html, `<div><span><h1>foo</h1></span><div>`)
~~~

But I think those can be annoying to maintain.

**Steve Howell** · 2021-06-11 12:50 UTC

I am working on the `stub_templates` -> `mock_template` migration.

**Steve Howell** · 2021-06-11 13:56 UTC

I am looking for a volunteer to continue the migration from `stub_templates` to `mock_template`.   If you look at the commits from #18802, the pattern should be fairly clear.  It's gonna be a pretty easy/mindless migration.  @Abhijeet Bodas this might be something you can knock out quickly, but there's no urgency.

## setting .append

*2021-06-11 to 2021-06-28 · 17 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/setting.20.2Eappend/with/1207492)*

**smalltext** · 2021-06-11 22:00 UTC

In the compose.js node test
```
(function () {
            let called;
            $("#compose_private_stream_alert").append = (html) => {
                called = true;
                assert.equal(html, "fake-compose_private_stream_alert-template");
            };
            return function () {
                assert.ok(called);
            };
        })(),
```
Why is the append function set equal to something, instead of using override?

**Steve Howell** · 2021-06-11 22:04 UTC

mostly because the zjquery objects get automatically cleaned at the end of run_test

**smalltext** · 2021-06-11 22:06 UTC

why does that matter when it's used in the body of a single call to run_test?

**Steve Howell** · 2021-06-12 13:05 UTC

@smalltext The short answer to your question is that we treat zjquery functions differently from Zulip functions in the tests for the same kinda reasons that jQuery has a different role in the system than the Zulip functions.

**Steve Howell** · 2021-06-12 13:09 UTC

Another short answer is that it's different, because that's just the way it is.  But let me work on a more satisfying answer...

**Steve Howell** · 2021-06-12 13:11 UTC

Basically, Zulip is the **app** here, and jQuery is the **library** here, and they have different properties in terms of testing.

**Steve Howell** · 2021-06-12 13:13 UTC

Whenever you stub a Zulip function, you generally want to do it only for the duration of one test, and then you want the original implementation of the real function to be restored for subsequent tests.

**Steve Howell** · 2021-06-12 13:18 UTC

Because there a few thousand functions within the **app**, it's impractical for the test runner to restore the entire state of the app after every test, so instead `run_test` has the optional `override` helper that you can use to express the fact that you're overriding the implementation of just one or a few functions during the test.  And `run_test` is wired up behind the scenes to both a) ensure you actually invoke the function and b) restore the old function afterward. And, of course, it ensures that the function you specify as the alternate implementation gets invoked during the test, which allows you to do assertions, simulate behavior of the mocked Zulip function, and so forth.

**Steve Howell** · 2021-06-12 13:21 UTC

jQuery, on the other hand, is a **library**.  Even though jQuery is an impressively powerful piece of code, it's actual surface area for the purposes of our node tests is quite small.  And when we mock jQuery with zjquery, we actually build an entire simulation of jQuery that's super easy and fast to tear down.

**Steve Howell** · 2021-06-12 13:24 UTC

With the exception of a few legacy test modules that I don't believe concern @smalltext at the moment, every time you invoke `run_test` you get a virgin, empty copy of zjquery.

**Steve Howell** · 2021-06-12 13:26 UTC

If you look at the actual implementation of `run_test`, you can see that we call `$.clear_all_elements` (unless you are unfortunate enough to be in one of the modules that still uses `sloppy_$`):

~~~ js
 19 exports.run_test = (label, f, opts) => {
 20     const {sloppy_$} = opts || {};
 21
 22     if (verbose) {
 23         console.info("        test: " + label);
 24     }
 25
 26     if (!sloppy_$ && $.clear_all_elements) {
 27         $.clear_all_elements();
 28     }
 29     zpage_params.reset();
 30
 31     try {
 32         namespace.with_overrides(f);
 33     } catch (error) {
 34         console.info("-".repeat(50));
 35         console.info(`test failed: ${current_file_name} > ${label}`);
 36         console.info();
 37         throw error;
 38     }
 39     // defensively reset blueslip after each test.
 40     zblueslip.reset();
 41 };

~~~

**Steve Howell** · 2021-06-12 13:29 UTC

So, kinda coming back full circle to your original question, it's perfectly fine to do this during your test:

~~~ js
$("#compose_private_stream_alert").append = (html) => {
   // do whatever
}
~~~

And you can do whatever you want in the scope of the test.  And you don't need to give `run_test` any hints about what tricks you do with the zjquery objects, because the whole thing is just gonna get rebuilt from scratch during the next `run_test` call.

**Steve Howell** · 2021-06-12 13:29 UTC

I hope this give a little more of the big picture, and I welcome follow up questions.

**Steve Howell** · 2021-06-12 13:33 UTC

I am going to assume you've read https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/master/frontend_tests/node_tests/zjquery.js, and even if you have done so, it might be worth another look. Unfortunately, those examples don't really  talk about situations where you just attach your own functions to the zjquery objects. I should probably improve that a bit.

**Steve Howell** · 2021-06-12 13:41 UTC

If this has piqued your curiosity at all, I would also recommend skimming the implementation of zjquery at some point:
https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/master/frontend_tests/node_tests/zjquery.js

**Neil Pilgrim (neiljp)** · 2021-06-12 16:39 UTC

This isn't python of course, but if it was it sounds like:
* zulip code would temporarily `patch` mocked parts to enable asserts on them while testing another part
* (z)jquery would be a single autospec'd mock

Is that a fair comparison Steve?

**Steve Howell** · 2021-06-28 13:26 UTC

(replying to Neil Pilgrim (neiljp))
> This isn't python of course, but if it was it sounds like: * zulip code would temporarily `patch` mocked parts to enable asserts on them while testing another part * (z)jquery would be a single autospec'd mock Is that a fair comparison Steve?

The analogy between `override` and `patch` is pretty accurate.  I haven't used autospeccing much in Python, but I believe that's a pretty distinct concept from zjquery.  I mean they're very vaguely similar in purpose, but I don't think they're enough alike for the analogy to be helpful.

## Message not as Any

*2021-06-16 to 2021-06-16 · 3 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/Message.20not.20as.20Any/with/1210346)*

**Zixuan James Li** · 2021-06-16 10:16 UTC

Currently, as Message objects are generated by Django, we consider them as `Any`. This allows us to conveniently monkey-patch extra fields without worrying about mypy errors.

However, while adding Django stubs to the server, `Message` objects are no longer `Any` and this causes a lot of errors when we want to access those attributes that are added in runtime. 

I tried to let functions like `render_markdown` that monkey-patched extra fields to `Message` to return `RenderedMessage` (which inherits `Message`). But it doesn't work since Django will recognize `RenderedMessage` as a model. And there are cases we expect messages to have attributes added by other functions that might not be compatible with `RenderedMessage`.

My current solution is to let such functions return an extra `TypedDict` that carries all the stuff that we used to monkey-patched to the `Message` object, but this requires a lot of refactoring and I'm not sure if it is the best practice.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2021-06-16 18:48 UTC

`RenderedMessage` could be a dataclass with a `Message` as one of its fields rather than its superclass?

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2021-06-16 18:54 UTC

No, that’s probably not the right answer, since it’s really an output of Markdown conversion rather than an input. Now I see that Tim has better suggestions on #18777.

I would encourage you to look at less invasive alternative libraries. ## handlebars translations

*2021-06-25 to 2021-06-25 · 12 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/handlebars.20translations/with/1219210)*

**Aryan Shridhar** · 2021-06-25 14:56 UTC

Hey, While recently working with frontend translations, I am stuck between these two methods to interpolate custom HTML string in handlebars.
Basically, here are the 2 different methods that yield the same UI strings. 
* First - 

```handlebars
{{#tr}}
That query would search for messages sent <z-email>user@example.com</z-email> to stream.
{{#*inline "z-email"}}<span class="operator_value">{{> @partial-block}}</span>{{/inline}}
{{/tr}}
```
* Second -

```handlebars
{{#tr}}
That query would search for messages sent <z-email></z-email> to stream.
{{#*inline "z-email"}}<span class="operator_value">user@example.com</span>{{/inline}}
{{/tr}}
```


I read about partials in handlebar docs: https://handlebarsjs.com/guide/partials.html#partial-blocks, and got to know that they are used to inject contents into the partial. But would it make any difference in case of just passing a string (here, "user@example.com")
Would be great if you someone can shed some light on it :)

**Steve Howell** · 2021-06-25 16:01 UTC

Why does the tr tag even need to surround the partial here?

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2021-06-25 16:31 UTC

The difference is that the first method allows the translator to translate the “user@example.com” part, while the second method doesn’t.

(Either way, I think you’re missing several words in that message.)

> Why does the tr tag even need to surround the partial here?

That scopes the partial to the `{{#tr}}` block—this is how we do [frontend HTML translation](https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/translating/internationalization.html#handlebars-templates) now.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2021-06-25 16:35 UTC

It looks like you’re working on the message in `templates/zerver/app/search_operators.html`, which is documenting the meaning of a specific untranslated query, so the second method is appropriate.

**Aryan Shridhar** · 2021-06-25 18:22 UTC

> which is documenting the meaning of a specific untranslated query, so the second method is appropriate.

Yea, but the original issue (#18504) is to mark the red text as variable so that later it can be translated. Shouldn't the first methodology be adopted for all such words ?

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2021-06-25 18:31 UTC

The reason to mark the red text as a variable is not so the red text can be translated; it’s so the red text can be properly word-ordered into the surrounding translated string.

**Steve Howell** · 2021-06-25 18:52 UTC

It might be helpful to explain that syntax a bit more in the docs.  Do I understand correctly that `z-link` is an arbitrary tag name that we sort of invent on the fly here, and that `{{> @partial-block}}` refers to whatever was in the `z-link` tag above?

When I read it casually, I was thinking the partial mean some other handlebars file, although looking at it more carefully, that's not the case.

(It's been a while since I've done anything non-trivial with Handlebars.)

**Steve Howell** · 2021-06-25 18:52 UTC

It might be helpful to give an example of what the translator would see, and then how it would be rendered.

**Aryan Shridhar** · 2021-06-25 19:17 UTC

(replying to Anders Kaseorg)
> The reason to mark the red text as a variable is not so the red text can be translated; it’s so the red text can be properly word-ordered into the surrounding translated string.
Ah! Awesome, Thanks!

**Aryan Shridhar** · 2021-06-25 19:22 UTC

> It might be helpful to explain that syntax a bit more in the docs. Do I understand correctly that z-link is an arbitrary tag name that we sort of invent on the fly here, and that {{> @partial-block}} refers to whatever was in the z-link tag above?

Yup, We also have the `z-link` documented [here](https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/translating/internationalization.html#handlebars-templates) and adding a couple of examples would really help like you mentioned!

**Aryan Shridhar** · 2021-06-25 19:34 UTC

Also, Just as a side question - Why don't we directly pass the `email` variable in [`confirm_resend_invite.hbs`](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/master/static/templates/confirm_dialog/confirm_resend_invite.hbs)? 
Currently, our `confirm_resend_invite.hbs` modal looks like: 
```handlebars
{{#tr}}
    Are you sure you want to resend the invitation to <z-email></z-email>?
    {{#*inline "z-email"}}<strong>{{email}}</strong>{{/inline}}
{{/tr}}
```

What's the issue if it's changed to: 
```handlebars
{{#tr}}
    Are you sure you want to resend the invitation to <strong>{{ email }}</strong>?
{{/tr}}
```
As `strong` is supported within the [`default_html_elements`](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/166bfa4cf83bcb012d2cc613e05ef64e27ba00df/static/js/i18n.ts#L31) as well.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2021-06-25 19:38 UTC

Because before your commit 994a965aa5424e25115d731e8efba8266ba8761b, there was also a `<span class="email">`.

It can also useful to have that abstraction in case we want to change the HTML details in the future without waiting for translators to re-translate the string.

## Inconsistent timezone abbreviation

*2021-06-26 to 2021-06-28 · 6 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/Inconsistent.20timezone.20abbreviation/with/1219742)*

**Dinesh Ch** · 2021-06-26 19:57 UTC

```js
> new Date().toLocaleTimeString('en-US', {timeStyle: 'long', timeZone: 'America/New_York'})
'3:27:15 PM EDT'
> new Date().toLocaleTimeString('en-IN', {timeStyle: 'long', timeZone: 'America/New_York'})
'3:32:45 pm GMT-4'
> new Date().toLocaleTimeString('en-US', {timeStyle: 'long', timeZone: 'Asia/Kolkata'})
'1:01:30 AM GMT+5:30'
> new Date().toLocaleTimeString('en-IN', {timeStyle: 'long', timeZone: 'Asia/Kolkata'})
'1:01:47 am IST'
```

Is there anyway to get only the short form of timezone instead of GMT+x.y across different locales and timezones? Tried `date-fns`'s `format` too but that too isn't working.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2021-06-26 20:10 UTC

The abbreviation is inherently ambiguous and locale-sensitive. IST might be India Standard Time (+05:30), Israel Standard Time (+02:00), or Ireland Standard Time (+01:00), depending on who you ask.

**Dinesh Ch** · 2021-06-26 20:23 UTC

Yes, that is true. For the use case I'm working on(tooltip for message timestamp), that ambiguity is fine as we'll be appending `(UTC+/-x.y)`.

The format that we desire for that is, as discussed in [#18856Comment](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/18856#discussion_r659098020), `{date} at {time} PST (UTC+N)`. I'm sure we'll almost never get `GMT+/-x:y` as the time will be in user's timezone and their browser's locale, the one that gives right short form i.e., IST, PST etc.

But I wanted to make sure that we don't show `{date} at {time} GMT+x:y (UTC+N)` in those rare cases too, if possible.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2021-06-26 20:41 UTC

Maybe check if something like `/^GMT[-+]/.test(new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", {timeStyle: "long", timeZone: "Asia/Kolkata"}).formatToParts(new Date()).find(({type}) => type === 'timeZoneName').value)`.

**Dinesh Ch** · 2021-06-27 17:58 UTC

yeah, we can avoid showing both `GMT+N`, `UTC+N` and just show one of them. We'll be missing the timezone abbreviations like `PST`, `IST` etc., but it's fine as that'll only happen very rarely. Did something like that [here.](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/19026/commits/189e225fdfd6ce8031e2f877be38693aa2b1ac3a#diff-b86fa95d7a54649b56d5037c3c3dd95997063cc639fe062d33553d9868cc6afcR323-R326)

Thanks @Anders Kaseorg

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-06-28 00:00 UTC

It's also worth noting that in this particular context, the timezone will always be the user's current timezone, so ambiguity isn't really an issue.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-07-05 21:13 UTC

@Palash Singh Raghuwanshi I think we probably want to implement this by having `rendered_markdown.js` process the mention object to style it in the frontend, rather than changing the syntax.

Changing the markdown processor only affects future messages, not ones sent before the change, and that's not what we want for this sort of styling change.

**Suyash Vardhan Mathur (MSurfer20)** · 2021-07-20 21:25 UTC

@Karun The existing tests are just above the function you mention -- 
```
def test_api_doc_endpoints(self) -> None:
        # We extract the set of /api/ endpoints to check by parsing
        # the /api/ page sidebar for links starting with /api/.
        api_page_raw = str((self.client_get("/api/").content))
        ENDPOINT_REGEXP = re.compile(r"href=\"/api/\s*(.*?)\"")
        endpoint_list_set = set(re.findall(ENDPOINT_REGEXP, api_page_raw))
        endpoint_list = [f"/api/{endpoint}" for endpoint in endpoint_list_set]
        # Validate that the parsing logic isn't broken, since if it
        # broke, the below would become a noop.
        self.assertGreater(len(endpoint_list), 70)

        for endpoint in endpoint_list:
            self._test(endpoint, "", doc_html_str=True)

        result = self.client_get(
            "/api/nonexistent-page",
            follow=True,
            HTTP_X_REQUESTED_WITH="XMLHttpRequest",
        )
        self.assertEqual(result.status_code, 404)
```

## ✔ git clone not pulling updated changes

*2021-07-23 to 2021-07-27 · 8 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/.E2.9C.94.20git.20clone.20not.20pulling.20updated.20changes/with/1237235)*

**Abhishek Sivakumar** · 2021-07-23 15:56 UTC

Hi, I just encountered a pretty weird problem, I initially force pushed a commit 4 days ago, Now I wanted to work on this PR again but my dual boot ubuntu isn't working for some reason, I freshly cloned my forked repository and then checked out the issue branch I was working on, But I saw that the changes that are present in github are present locally on the commit, but the dates are completely different, I have attached the screenshots so please do take a look.

This makes me unable to rebase changes from the upstream master as well.

[image.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/13/PjAg5aaIJzVMfWUUs6EleoPa/image.png) (One currently in github)
[image.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/be/E_8LNsKxrSP3UMzJmSrch6yL/image.png)  (Same branch on local fresh clone)

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-07-23 17:48 UTC

@Abhishek Sivakumar there's nothing wrong there, other than GitHub being confusing.  What you're seeing is that Git has two dates that it keeps track of for a commit: When the author first created an initial commit (the "Author date") and when the commit (with the indicated hash) was actually created through amending/rebasing/etc. that original commit.  You can see both dates with the following command:

```
$ git show --pretty=fuller
commit 78ff74d3fd1243043b6fda538fbac32456ad523b (HEAD -> master, upstream/master)
Author:     Eeshan Garg <eeshan@zulip.com>
AuthorDate: Thu Jul 22 14:59:55 2021 -0230
Commit:     Tim Abbott <tabbott@zulip.com>
CommitDate: Fri Jul 23 10:29:41 2021 -0700
```

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-07-23 17:48 UTC

So what's happening is just that the GitHub UI is showing the commit date while your local repository is showing the author date.

**Greg Price** · 2021-07-23 19:41 UTC

The way to uniquely identify that you're definitely looking at the exact same commits in two places is the commit ID. That is generated as a hash of the commit's entire contents and all its history.

In your GitHub screenshot, the commit ID is that string on the right: `56ee8ea`. (Well, that's the start of the commit ID. In general you can always give Git a prefix of a commit ID, and it'll accept it if it's unique within the repo.)

In your terminal screenshot, it's cut off, but it'd be the next line above what you're showing.

**Greg Price** · 2021-07-23 19:42 UTC

(A hash of the commit's entire contents and history, including all the metadata like the author date and commit date, that is. So if the dates are different, the commit IDs will be different.)

**Greg Price** · 2021-07-23 19:53 UTC

So once you look at the commit ID and confirm it's the same, there's no need to look at the dates or anything else -- it's definitely the same commit.

And if the commit IDs are the same and the dates or something else don't seem to match, then you know that it's just some UI being buggy or weird, like GitHub's often can be.

**Abhishek Sivakumar** · 2021-07-24 14:47 UTC

Thank you @Tim Abbott @Greg Price  for the answers, My doubt is cleared :sweat_smile:, Yep the commit ids are the same after expanding them locally.

**Notification Bot** · 2021-07-27 18:25 UTC

@Abhishek Sivakumar has marked this topic as resolved.

def allocate_ids(model_class: Any, count: int) -> List[int]:
    """
    Increases the sequence number for a given table by the amount of objects being
    imported into that table. Hence, this gives a reserved range of IDs to import the
    converted Slack objects into the tables.
    """

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-08-02 00:16 UTC

@Abhijeet Bodas I believe that's the correct solution.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-08-02 00:17 UTC

Basically, that code needs to know the `sequence` object that postgres has associated with the database table in question to implement the auto-incrementing ID field.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-08-02 00:17 UTC

And renaming a table does not rename those sequence objects; so that bit of code, which is the one place that we interact with those sequence elements, need to be told explicitly how to find the right name.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-08-02 00:20 UTC

There's probably some internal Django system function we could call to get the sequence for these ID field without hardcoding the list, but we rename tables rarely enough that it's probably not necessary.

## Emoji Variable Selectors

*2021-08-08 to 2021-08-30 · 9 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/Emoji.20Variable.20Selectors/with/1245311)*

**Sai Rohitth Chiluka** · 2021-08-08 06:15 UTC

I have some doubts regarding emojis ad how they are handled.
The additional 15 & 16 variable selector modifier for emojis break the rendering in ZT. I wanted to know how the server differentiates between these in the HTML that we get. They look the same irrespective of the modifier.
```html
<span aria-label="check mark" class="emoji emoji-2714" role="img" title="check mark">:check_mark:</span>
```
Even in the case of combined emojis only the first emoji is seen and the others are rendered directly.

**Greg Price** · 2021-08-17 20:44 UTC

Yeah. The breakage where the start of the emoji sequence gets rendered as an independent emoji, and then the other bits of the sequence show up separately, is a known bug: #11767.

**Greg Price** · 2021-08-17 20:44 UTC

(@Sai Rohitth Chiluka ^ since this question was a while ago)

**Greg Price** · 2021-08-17 20:47 UTC

For the effects of U+FE0E VARIATION SELECTOR-15 and U+FE0F VARIATION SELECTOR-16, it'd be helpful for you to say more specifically what you're seeing.

**Greg Price** · 2021-08-17 20:50 UTC

One thing to know about those is that they are supposed to change how the character looks. See this section of the spec:
http://www.unicode.org/reports/tr51/#Presentation_Style

**Neil Pilgrim (neiljp)** · 2021-08-17 21:49 UTC

@Sai Rohitth Chiluka has been the one really diving into this recently, but we've had issues with various unicode characters breaking the display (offsetting columns) for some time. We currently use a very limited set of symbols for the UI for precisely this reason. The challenge is then message content and metadata, which we don't have the same control over.
In many cases - at least in my experience - I'm unable to see full unicode emoji (and other unicode) on the terminal in any case, and some basic (and combination, ie. with selectors) unicode cause the display breakage/corruption too.
One of Rohitth's recent approaches has been to split out the selectors and similar characters, since this could resolve the rendering issues. However, we need to know how to map between the server and ZT text, since eg. I was concerned that adding `U+FEOF` adjacent to another appropriate codepoint in a topic might make it a different topic, such as during a reply, even if it may look the same!
Other ideas about this are welcome :)
Rohitth has a WIP PR which goes beyond this at #T114; ideally we'd just fix the display breakage first, but that may be mixed up in the interactions with the server?

**Sai Rohitth Chiluka** · 2021-08-18 07:10 UTC

I have actually resolved the original issue raised here wherein all the other emoji components go into the NavigableString next to span. Using this I was able to strip off all zero width modifiers as they break ZT rendering. 

The only other issue with this is that forced emojis (i.e. emojis which are pasted directly) which are not in the servers list of emojis don't get sent in the emoji format (i.e they end up in the NavString). 
The issue this creates for ZT is only styling related (not breakage of rendering) which would hopefully get solved once the server updates to the latest Unicode.

**Sai Rohitth Chiluka** · 2021-08-18 07:19 UTC

Re topics having different modifiers, this is mainly a user facing issue. Internally even if 2 topics use the same emoji but different modifiers they would be unique and would not result in messages going from one to the other. Visually they may look the same though (in ZT atleast).

The question is should we allow that?
If we do should we indicate that somehow?
Or is it so rare that it can be ignored?

**Greg Price** · 2021-08-30 23:28 UTC

(replying to Sai Rohitth Chiluka)
> Re topics having different modifiers, this is mainly a user facing issue. Internally even if 2 topics use the same emoji but different modifiers they would be unique and would not result in messages going from one to the other.

Right -- and as I understand what @Neil Pilgrim (neiljp) was suggesting above, that's exactly the issue: the concern is that when you reply to a message, it could end up going to a distinct topic if the client were to insert U+FE0F (or almost anything else, really) and end up using its modified version of the topic for replying.

@Felix (strifel) The server API and server code don't have a specific item for resolving a topic. The way a client resolves a topic is by making an ordinary request to edit the messages' topic, that just happens to add a prefix of "✔ ".

Is it possible to have an additional requirement that is only installed on Windows systems? :thinking:

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-09-29 16:59 UTC

@Robert (ro-i) I'm pretty sure it's possible to define additional platform-specific requirements.  I don't know how to do it without doing research; one option is to just find another package using pypi search that depends on `python-magic` and supports windows, and see how that declares things in its `setup.py`.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-09-29 17:00 UTC

(This sort of thing can work through conditionals in `setup.py`, but I would expect there to be a `requirements.txt` syntax for it these days as well)

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-09-29 17:00 UTC

As for why to offer Windows CI, if someone has a Windows system, it's nice for them to be able to use our Python API without extra setup work, and without CI to test, it's very likely someone will introduce a bug with how paths are managed.

## exit ./tools/run-dev.py if error

*2021-10-08 to 2021-10-08 · 6 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/exit.20.2E.2Ftools.2Frun-dev.2Epy.20if.20error/with/1264046)*

**Yash RE** · 2021-10-08 13:26 UTC

Is it possible to run `./tools/run-dev.py` such that if there's an error from django or webpack then the process ends.

I'm asking because of how my dev env is setup, I use code-server from a droplet, and run `./tools/run-dev.py` from the shell VS code. If django has an error, it usually causes code-server to disconnect, and I have to wait for it to reconnect, then give a keyboard interrupt to exit `./tools/run-dev.py`... This is further made worse by the fact that VS-code will auto save at random points, causing the zulip dev server to hot reload with incomplete code, give a django error and disconnect me. It doesn't happen very often, so it's possible to work with things as they are, but it is annoying.

**Steve Howell** · 2021-10-08 14:22 UTC

I'm not sure, but in principle it should be fairly easy to modify the tool so that it stops when any child process fails.  I suppose the nuance here is that once you survive the initial startup sequence your desires may change.

**Steve Howell** · 2021-10-08 14:23 UTC

I don't recall the run-dev code being super complicated (except for a few deep things that it delegates to).

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-10-08 18:20 UTC

Interesting question!  I'd certainly be happy to have an option to do that.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-10-08 18:21 UTC

The ideal solution would be to just fix our Tornado autoreload behavior to not end up in a broken state after a save.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-10-08 18:21 UTC

One possible option would be to try to add an `on_reload` hook for the Django process to kill its associated Tornado process, rather than having Tornado autoreload itself, because it's only the Tornado autoreloader that has this problem.

I feel like our documentation could be improved:
(1) It could be made more explicit that signing up will require a credit/debit card and can take up to 24 hours (even to just use the free version).
(2) Using the recommended 1 GiB ram instance and running `./tools/provision` will result in the following error:
```
You have insufficient RAM (0.96 GB) to run the Zulip development environment.
We recommend at least 2 GB of RAM, and require at least 1.5 GB.
```
which can be resolved by changing lines 43 - 56 of `/tools/lib/provision.py`:
```diff
diff --git a/tools/lib/provision.py b/tools/lib/provision.py
index 43336e3659..615161adcf 100755
--- a/tools/lib/provision.py
+++ b/tools/lib/provision.py
@@ -40,21 +40,6 @@ if not os.path.exists(os.path.join(ZULIP_PATH, ".git")):
     print("from GitHub, rather than using a Zulip production release tarball.")
     sys.exit(1)
 
-# Check the RAM on the user's system, and throw an effort if <1.5GB.
-# This avoids users getting segfaults running `pip install` that are
-# generally more annoying to debug.
-with open("/proc/meminfo") as meminfo:
-    ram_size = meminfo.readlines()[0].strip().split(" ")[-2]
-ram_gb = float(ram_size) / 1024.0 / 1024.0
-if ram_gb < 1.5:
-    print(
-        "You have insufficient RAM ({} GB) to run the Zulip development environment.".format(
-            round(ram_gb, 2)
-        )
-    )
-    print("We recommend at least 2 GB of RAM, and require at least 1.5 GB.")
-    sys.exit(1)
-
 try:
     UUID_VAR_PATH = get_dev_uuid_var_path(create_if_missing=True)
     os.makedirs(UUID_VAR_PATH, exist_ok=True)
```
Running `./tools/provision` after this will lead to a `ENOSPC: no space left on device, write` error.

Which will require stopping the instance and resizing the volume. (I used 20 GB. Be sure not to exceed the limits of aws free tier, which I do not know.)

Running `./tools/provision` after this will take some time and give an aws warning of low memory, while running migrations, which can be ignored.

After provision succeeds, running `./tools/run-dev.py` will cause cloud 9 to freeze.

## Building after fetching upstream

*2021-10-17 to 2021-10-18 · 5 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/Building.20after.20fetching.20upstream/with/1267864)*

**Aryaman M** · 2021-10-17 17:50 UTC

Do I need to run ./tools/provision every time I pull from the main repo?

**Palash Raghuwanshi** · 2021-10-18 02:30 UTC

Yes, I think it's a good practice, it keeps your environment up to date, read https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/setup-vagrant.html#maintaining-the-development-environment

**Palash Raghuwanshi** · 2021-10-18 02:35 UTC

Also, FYI, you shouldn't `pull` from the main repo(if you were doing it at all), you are supposed to `git fetch upstream` and then rebase your desired branch on the top of  the upstream/main by using `git rebase upstream/main`. Read https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/git/using.html#keep-your-fork-up-to-date

**Aryaman M** · 2021-10-18 04:14 UTC

(replying to Palash Raghuwanshi)

Read https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/git/using.html#keep-your-fork …
I use the fetch and merge button on my fork and then pull from my fork. Is this better practice?

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-10-18 04:23 UTC

@Aryaman M I think that workflow will work, as long as you never push extra commits to the `main` branch on your fork.

## Translate welcome bot commands.

*2021-10-26 to 2021-10-27 · 8 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/Translate.20welcome.20bot.20commands.2E/with/1271872)*

**Palash Raghuwanshi** · 2021-10-26 06:16 UTC

I'm working on PR #19985 for issue "**Make Welcome Bot more interactive**"(#19900). I am stuck on marking string containing bot commands for translation, as the commands will need to be in English, but the surrounding punctuations, and `and` need to be translated to the specific language(as pointed out by @Tim Abbott in [this](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/19985#discussion_r734091917) review). I was not able to find anything of much use in the documentation apart from this:
> Don’t translate variables or code (usually preceded by a %, inside HTML tags <...>, or enclosed in braces like {variable}); just keep them verbatim.

So by this I understood that translators don't translate variables.

I found this from the [Django documentation](https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/3.0/topics/i18n/translation/#standard-translation):
>The strings you pass to _() or gettext() can take placeholders, specified with Python’s standard named-string interpolation syntax. For example:
```python
def my_view(request, m, d):
    output = _('Today is %(month)s %(day)s.') % {'month': m, 'day': d}
    return HttpResponse(output)
```
I also found out:
>The caveat with using variables or computed values, as in the previous two examples, is that Django’s translation-string-detecting utility, django-admin makemessages, won’t be able to find these strings.

So by my understanding of all this I made a function to return bot commands:
```python
def bot_commands() -> str:
    commands = ["apps", "edit profile", "dark mode", "light mode", "streams", 
    "topics", "message formatting", "keyboard shortcuts"]
    return _(
        '"%(command1)s", "%(command2)s", "%(command3)s", "%(command4)s", "%(command5)s", '
        '"%(command6)s", "%(command7)s",and "%(command8)s".'
    ) % {f"command{i+1}":f"**{command}**" for i, command in enumerate(commands)}}
```

So my concern is that hardcoding the commands seems odd, and what if some usage of the function needs an extra command(as there is a case),  only way I can think of, so that makemessages can find the string, is to make an `if-else` block and copy paste the above command string with one more command, which seems not a really good thing to do. Is there a better way of doing this I missed?

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-10-26 22:54 UTC

@Palash Raghuwanshi good question.  I don't think I know what the best way to do this sort of list is in the Django i18n system.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-10-26 22:55 UTC

One possible answer would be to send a bulleted list (or other structure) that doesn't require the ,/and construction; I'm not sure that would look visually good, but it's an option.

**Greg Price** · 2021-10-26 23:04 UTC

For a long list like this, I think just commas without "and" also works pretty smoothly (and is a common solution in UIs.)

**Greg Price** · 2021-10-26 23:07 UTC

The commas won't be the same kind of comma expected in some languages, but I think that will be a much smaller awkwardness than the fact that the commands themselves are in English. :wink:

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-10-26 23:11 UTC

Yeah, that'd be a fine option if we don't like the visuals of having it be tall, which I suspect is the case.

**Palash Raghuwanshi** · 2021-10-27 05:07 UTC

Yeah, commas without "and" seems like a good substitute here, I think we will also need to skip the quotation marks around the commands here, as by googling it I saw that some languages do have different symbols for them, will that be okay @Alya Abbott?

**Alya Abbott** · 2021-10-27 06:06 UTC

Ah, that's right -- thanks for pointing that out, @Palash Raghuwanshi ! Yes, removing the "and" and the quotation marks seems reasonable to me.

export const max_size_before_shrinking = 600;

**Yash RE** · 2021-10-29 16:13 UTC

```js

function user_is_recently_active(user_id) {
    // return true if the user has a green/orange circle
    return level(user_id) <= 2;
}

function maybe_shrink_list(user_ids, user_filter_text) {
    if (user_ids.length <= max_size_before_shrinking) {
        return user_ids;
    }

    if (user_filter_text) {
        // If the user types something, we want to show all
        // users matching the text, even if they have not been
        // online recently.
        // For super common letters like "s", we may
        // eventually want to filter down to only users that
        // are in presence.get_user_ids().
        return user_ids;
    }

    user_ids = user_ids.filter((user_id) => user_is_recently_active(user_id));

    return user_ids;
}
```

**Julia Bichler** · 2021-10-28 12:58 UTC

**Greg Price** · 2021-10-28 21:07 UTC

(replying to Yash RE)
> Just to be clear, you need to have “Fixes: #xyz.” in your last *commit* on the pull request.

It's best to have both: a reference in the commit that fixes the issue, and also a reference in the PR description.

The reason for a reference in the PR description (even when there's already one in a commit) is that it causes GitHub to make a nice link from the issue back to the PR, plus it helps make it easy to get to the issue from the PR.

**Greg Price** · 2021-10-28 21:07 UTC

I recently opened PR #20183.  I had to squash three of my previous commits into one. However after, using `git rebase -i HEAD~3`, I mistakenly clicked enter with all commits preceded by `pick` instead of squash. And I pushed the changes. Is there any way to revert back and squash the commits?

**Manan Rathi** · 2021-11-06 10:21 UTC

**Yash RE** · 2021-11-06 10:31 UTC

You seem to have made a merge commit, probably because of running git pull, you're probably not seeing the commits because of the order they are being displayed in, https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/git/troubleshooting.html will help you undo the merge commit, and then you can just rebase -i again and squash your commits together.

Pay attention to the `important` box which says you should use `git reset --merge <commit>` instead of `git reset --hard <commit>`

            message_id__in=message_ids_to_use, user_profile=user_profile                                 
        ).values_list("message_id", flat=True)                                                           
    )                                                                                                    
                                                                                                         
    # Mark the newest ONBOARDING_UNREAD_MESSAGES as unread.                                              
    marked_unread = 0                                                                                    
    ums_to_create = []                                                                                   
    for message_id in reversed(message_ids_to_use):                                                      
        if message_id in already_ids:                                                                    
            continue                                                                                     
                                                                                                         
        um = UserMessage(user_profile=user_profile, message_id=message_id)                               
        if marked_unread < ONBOARDING_UNREAD_MESSAGES:                                                   
            marked_unread += 1                                                                           
        else:                                                                                            
            um.flags = UserMessage.flags.read                                                            
        ums_to_create.append(um)                                                                         
                                                                                                         
    UserMessage.objects.bulk_create(reversed(ums_to_create))                                             
```

## Best way to resolve merge conflicts?

*2021-11-20 to 2021-11-22 · 4 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/Best.20way.20to.20resolve.20merge.20conflicts.3F/with/1284606)*

**Aryaman M** · 2021-11-20 10:29 UTC

I created PR #20096 a while ago. A few commits were merged and now there is a merge conflict in my commit. What is the best way to resolve the conflict? Should I rebase and then commit again or can I just resolve it on Github as it is just one conflict? Thanks

**Yash RE** · 2021-11-20 10:34 UTC

I see that you've made the changes on a separate branch, `issue-20080`, so I recommend checking out to `main`, fetch;rebase-ing with upstream main, and then checkout `issue-20080` and using `git rebase main` on that branch.

The rebase will stop when it reaches the merge conflict, and you can resolve each conflicting change individually,  `add` your changes, and `---continue` the rebase.

**Greg Price** · 2021-11-22 19:54 UTC

Those instructions work fine, but I'd typically use a slightly simpler sequence: `git fetch` (or `git fetch upstream` to make it explicit), then rebase the branch directly on upstream/main, without involving the local `main` branch. So e.g.
```
$ git fetch upstream
$ git rebase upstream/main issue-20080
```

**Greg Price** · 2021-11-22 19:55 UTC

(That last command
```
$ git rebase upstream/main issue-20080
```
is a handy shorthand for
```
$ git checkout issue-20080
$ git rebase upstream/main
```
.)

 [general-testorg69-Zulip.gif](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/7b/BXPc6wWlFW8PGU1BXml174XT/general-testorg69-Zulip.gif)

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2021-11-22 14:00 UTC

You can put `console.trace` somewhere in `reload.js` as it tries to preserve state to find out what is triggering the reload.

**shlok (madrix01)** · 2021-11-24 10:40 UTC

I tried using `console.trace()` at various places in `static/js/reload.js` and tested with both `Rename Topic` and `Move Topic`. Both of them shows the same trace.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-11-24 19:35 UTC

The problem is this line:
`<form class="new-style" id="rename_topic_form">`

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-11-24 19:36 UTC

At least, I suspect so.  @shlok patel(madrix01) if you have a form element in HTML, it comes with default behavior that hitting `enter` submits the form in the browser, which often comes with a page reload.

We generally avoid using `form` elements in the Zulip web application, and when we do use them, we have JavaScript that captures the `Enter` key.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-11-24 19:37 UTC

Hmm, though I don't see an action on that form, so maybe it isn't that.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-11-24 19:38 UTC

When you say "both show the same trace", what is that trace?

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-11-24 19:38 UTC

In any case, I'd debug considering the possibility that the reload is triggered by the browser, not by code we wrote.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-11-24 19:39 UTC

One technique you can try is deleting section of your implementation until the failure mode no longer occurs, to isolate what aspect of what you did introduces the bug.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2021-11-24 19:40 UTC

The right thing is `<form>` with JavaScript that captures the `submit` event (which can be generated either  by clicking a submit button or pressing Enter in any field).

It doesn’t matter whether there’s an `action`. The default is `action=""`, and the empty string is a relative URL for the current page.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-11-24 19:41 UTC

I'm a bit surprised that the `dialog_widget` component / Micromodal doesn't handle this for you; CC @Ganesh Pawar (ganpa3) in case you have thoughts on this.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2021-11-24 19:49 UTC

Micromodal doesn’t care whether your modal has a form or a submit button. `dialog_widget` looks incapable of putting the submit button inside a form.

**shlok (madrix01)** · 2021-11-24 19:49 UTC

(replying to Tim Abbott)
> When you say "both show the same trace", what is that trace?

**Ganesh Pawar (ganpa3)** · 2021-11-25 10:22 UTC

@shlok patel(madrix01) You can use the `form_id` attribute of the `dialog_widget`:
https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/b9629d72a92a9fce6a0393c0f31850a9d2f0e857/static/js/dialog_widget.js#L83

It will bind the submit button to the form so that pressing Enter triggers a click on the submit button, which can be handled by the `on_click` function.
https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/b9629d72a92a9fce6a0393c0f31850a9d2f0e857/static/js/dialog_widget.js#L119-L124

MDN docs:
https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/button#attr-form

We don't want an Enter key handler. We want to let the browser translate the Enter press to a submit event, and handle that.

## mark_as_read

*2021-12-03 to 2021-12-04 · 13 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/mark_as_read/with/1290735)*

**Collin Whitlow** · 2021-12-03 14:34 UTC

apologies if this is a dumb question, but i am still new to the zulip community. i am looking at the mark_as_read parameter of do_send_messages() at line 1954 of actions.py.  i am having a hard time figuring out what its purpose is and why it is set to be an empty list. any help would be appreciated.

**Steve Howell** · 2021-12-03 14:58 UTC

Not a dumb question at all.  It's a default parameter that most callers don't pass, in which case the list of users who automatically mark the message as read defaults to an empty list.  But see `zerver/views/streams.py` , line 681.  If we're sending out a message to new subscribers to say that a stream has been created, we automatically mark the notification message as read for the stream creator.  (At least I think that's what the code is doing--I may be a little off on details, but that's the gist.)

**Steve Howell** · 2021-12-03 14:58 UTC

I found the caller via `git grep` (and it helps that I'm familiar with the code to be able to fairly quickly find the example).

**Steve Howell** · 2021-12-03 15:00 UTC

@Collin Whitlow Feel free to ask follow ups here--this is a pretty tricky part of the codebase.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-12-03 23:29 UTC

Generally when I see this type of question, my first thought is that we should add a comment/docstring.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-12-03 23:29 UTC

@Collin Whitlow are you working on the "Resolve topic" logic?  I think for that we probably want to add a new parameter to `internal_send_message` and the functions it calls, perhaps named "unread_only_for_participants" rather than trying to reuse that parameter.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-12-03 23:30 UTC

Trying to reuse `mark_as_read` would require doing redundant calls to fetch the full set of recipients of the message.

**Collin Whitlow** · 2021-12-04 17:38 UTC

Thank you for the help, guys. @Tim Abbott  I am working on the resolve topic logic. As a follow up, how would one access a list of subscribers to a given topic? I looked in a couple files that I thought seemed relevant but I'm having a hard time tracking that down.

**Steve Howell** · 2021-12-04 18:13 UTC

Users subscribe to streams, not topics.  Look at the `Subscription` and `Recipient` models in `models.py` for starters.  I am sure you will have some questions after that, but that should at least help you to grep around.

**Steve Howell** · 2021-12-04 18:14 UTC

`zerver/lib/stream_subscription.py` is also a good thing to read (and may pretty much directly answer your question, but not sure)

Good luck!

**Collin Whitlow** · 2021-12-04 20:27 UTC

Ah looking back, using the word "subscribers" was super misleading. I apologize for the confusion. I was trying to ask for was whether or not there was a way to access a list of people who had *participated* in a given topic.

**Steve Howell** · 2021-12-04 20:28 UTC

ah, `Message.sender` on the DB side

**Steve Howell** · 2021-12-04 20:29 UTC

and `Message.subject` (subject being the old word for topic)

**Yash RE** · 2021-12-06 10:46 UTC

in this case, you just force push with `git push -f`

**Yash RE** · 2021-12-06 10:47 UTC

that will set the origin fixed-issue#19865 branch to what you have locally

**Anusha Roy** · 2021-12-06 10:56 UTC

(replying to Yash RE)
> that will set the origin fixed-issue#19865 branch to what you have locally
thank you! this worked!
It is now showing me a merge conflict on the GitHub website:
https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/20019/conflicts

Should I worry or do I just keep the part of the code that I want and delete the rest?

**Yash RE** · 2021-12-06 11:02 UTC

you need to resolve the merge conflicts locally and the force push

**Yash RE** · 2021-12-06 11:03 UTC

okay lets do it like this:

**Yash RE** · 2021-12-06 11:03 UTC

lets first squash your commits together

**Yash RE** · 2021-12-06 11:03 UTC

and then rebase with main

**Yash RE** · 2021-12-06 11:04 UTC

so, to squash you can run `git rebase -i HEAD~7`

**Yash RE** · 2021-12-06 11:04 UTC

which will show you the last 7 commits, of which the last five are yours

**Yash RE** · 2021-12-06 11:05 UTC

we want to squash four of those into the first one, to do that change the word `pick` to `squash` on each of the last 4 commits

**Yash RE** · 2021-12-06 11:05 UTC

then save

**Yash RE** · 2021-12-06 11:06 UTC

and that will squash the commits and open the commit message for editing, remove the extra lines and save, you'll then only have 1 commit on your branch by you

**Yash RE** · 2021-12-06 11:07 UTC

then you can run:
`git fetch upstream`
and `git rebase upstream/main fixed-issue#19865`

**Yash RE** · 2021-12-06 11:08 UTC

which will stop mid way and show you all the conflicts in the files, once you fix those conflicts, save those files, `add` them and `git rebase --continue`

**Yash RE** · 2021-12-06 11:09 UTC

**Yash RE** · 2021-12-06 14:44 UTC

right, so, `https://github.com/AnushaNathRoy/zulip.git` is supposed to be `origin` and `upstream` is supposed to be `https://github.com/zulip/zulip.git`

**Greg Price** · 2021-12-06 17:47 UTC

(replying to Anusha Roy)
> EDIT: After running the git rebase command I am getting the following output on my terminal: ``` ❯ git rebase upstream/main fixed-issue#19865 Current branch fixed-issue#19865 is up to date. ``` It did not stop midway to show any errors/merge conflicts.

This is telling you that the branch `fixed-issue#19865` is already rebased on top of upstream/main.

But your remote called `upstream` isn't really very upstream, because you created it to point to your own fork instead of to the real upstream repo. You can fix that with `git remote remove` and then a new `git remote add`.

You can just use the `html` returned from mock_template and call `set_find_results` there itself. Something like -
```javascript
mock_template("dialog_widget.hbs", true, (data, html) => {
        $(html).set_find_results(".dialog_submit_button", child);
        return html
});
```

**Cyphase** · 2021-12-07 17:12 UTC

**Cyphase** · 2021-12-07 17:13 UTC

[History of the user-agent string](https://humanwhocodes.com/blog/2010/01/12/history-of-the-user-agent-string/)

**Yash RE** · 2021-12-07 17:17 UTC

>  its codename was Mozilla (short for “Mosaic Killer”)

Ohhh! So that's where Mozilla comes from!

**Cyphase** · 2021-12-07 17:18 UTC

I was just looking at that. :big_smile: I checked Wikipedia and it says it was from "Mosaic" and "Godzilla", which matches the mascot. I haven't dug into sources for either claim though.

**Steve Howell** · 2021-12-07 17:27 UTC

This may be a bug. I am pretty sure we have code that tries to detect the browser properly, and it was definitely common knowledge in ~2014 that browsers lied about the user-agent.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-12-07 17:38 UTC

The plan was to add a Python library that parses user agents further, but the ones we've tried were too slow to be used in high throughout code paths.

**Greg Price** · 2021-12-07 18:26 UTC

(replying to Tim Abbott)
> but the ones we've tried were too slow to be used in high throughout code paths.

Sounds like a symptom of trying to write all the logic in Python. Which is an understandable thing for someone to try to do when writing a Python library to parse user agents -- you'll try to cover things in full generality, and then you'll want to write a bunch of Python code.

If we want to answer a question like "is it Firefox or Chrome or Safari or Edge or something-else", I think the most effective way to do so would be a handful of regexps. That should then perform just fine.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-12-07 18:27 UTC

I think these libraries use regexs; they just probably don't have a thoughtful structure.  But it's also possible this has improved since @Dinesh Ch worked on this a couple years ago.

**Tim Abbott** · 2021-12-09 05:38 UTC

```
    _get_msg_timestring(message_container) {                                                             
        let last_edit_timestamp;                                                                         
        if (message_container.msg.local_edit_timestamp !== undefined) {                                  
            last_edit_timestamp = message_container.msg.local_edit_timestamp;                            
        } else {                                                                                         
            last_edit_timestamp = message_container.msg.last_edit_timestamp;                             
        }                                                                                                
        if (last_edit_timestamp !== undefined) {                                                         
            const last_edit_time = new Date(last_edit_timestamp * 1000);                                 
            const today = new Date();                                                                    
            return (                                                                                     
                timerender.render_date(last_edit_time, undefined, today)[0].textContent +                
                " at " +                                                                                 
                timerender.stringify_time(last_edit_time)                                                
            );                                                                                           
        }                                                                                                
        return undefined;                                                                                
    }                                                                                                    
```

But I need input. When I mark topic resolved the logic correctly avoids adding `MOVED` label. But how should it behave when we mark the topic unresolved? With existing logic it shows everything `MOVED`. Because, the `RESOLVE_TOPIC_PREFIX` is no longer there. **Tim Abbott** · 2022-02-01 01:50 UTC

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-02-01 01:51 UTC

**baali** · 2022-02-02 04:35 UTC

Thank you for the input. This is the logic I have so far on following the topic through resolved/unresolved states:
1. If the topic itself has `RESOLVE_TOPIC_PREFIX`, consider that as resolved and don't mark messages as `MOVED`. Here is a screenshot:
[Resolved topic, not being marked as `MOVED`](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/67/h42kC9a8Zn4XEDlrEYgDB4tF/Screenshot-from-2022-02-02-09-56-44.png) 

2. To find out if the topic was marked unresolved, look at most recent `edit_history` entry and find `prev_topic` of that entry. Either that entry should have `RESOLVE_TOPIC_PREFIX` or that entry will have same topic as the current topic. In both cases, the topic has been unresolved and don't mark the label `MOVED`. Here is a screenshot of how it looks when topic is marked unresolved:
[Topic marked unresolved](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/45/abt3G3fVTdOapt4X8QVb2cqy/Screenshot-from-2022-02-02-10-00-20.png) 

In both the above case, `EDITED` label is maintained through the transition and edit history button is available:
[EDITED label](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/fe/_5uELHlWidbHwkM2MILSVwo6/Screenshot-from-2022-02-02-10-01-15.png) 

The logic of marking message as `MOVED` is now not clear to me. With above logic in place, some messages correctly get marked `MOVED` but some don't:
[Topic is moved altogether](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/41/jABP87PKcJXYVxg8xrJ0PHyo/Screenshot-from-2022-02-02-10-05-01.png)

**baali** · 2022-02-03 06:10 UTC

**baali** · 2022-02-03 06:11 UTC

Similarly in `edit_history` of any message there is `prev_subject` and `prev_topic`.

**baali** · 2022-02-03 06:13 UTC

API documentation for `get-messages` mentions about `subject` attribute, and it says:
> The topic of the message. 

So are they same?

**baali** · 2022-02-03 06:13 UTC

Later it also talks about legacy code:
> The field name is a legacy holdover from when topics were called "subjects" and will eventually change.

So, what drives the logic of how a message is displayed? Topic or Subject?

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-02-04 01:11 UTC

@baali the background is that the API has always called it `subject`, but it's been `topic` in the UI for many years, and we've been slowly trying to encapsulate all use of `subject` to a few corners of the code in preparation for doing a cutover.

**Tim Abbott** · 2022-02-04 01:12 UTC

There's a set of helper functions that are used to access these, but I would expect legacy objects like `edit_history` rows to potentially use the old labels.  I don't expect there to be many objects that contain keys with both names.
