*2023-01-12 to 2023-01-12 · 6 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/.E2.9C.94.20changing.20model.20field.20type/with/1490160)*

**Prakhar Pratyush** · 2023-01-12 18:16 UTC

I am working on the issue [19905](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/issues/19905)

In the UserBaseSetting Model, I am  updating [`realm_name_in_notifications`](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/1a3b0edf4bfbc953975eb66eb9af474f1be118f3/zerver/models.py#L1599) field type from `bool` to `enum`

More accurately,
```python
realm_name_in_notifications = models.BooleanField(default=False)
```
is updated to

```python
    REALM_NAME_IN_NOTIFICATION_AUTOMATIC = 1
    REALM_NAME_IN_NOTIFICATION_YES = 2
    REALM_NAME_IN_NOTIFICATION_NO = 3
    REALM_NAME_IN_NOTIFICATION_CHOICES = [
      REALM_NAME_IN_NOTIFICATION_AUTOMATIC,
      REALM_NAME_IN_NOTIFICATION_YES,
      REALM_NAME_IN_NOTIFICATION_NO,
    ]
    realm_name_in_notifications = models.PositiveSmallIntegerField(default=REALM_NAME_IN_NOTIFICATION_AUTOMATIC)
```

This will create a migration file resulting in the field value for everyone being updated to `automatic`.

But we want to preserve the setting for those who have changed the setting manually (the current default is False).
In simple terms, after the migration, the value of those users who have currently the value stored as `true` should be updated as `Yes` not `automatic`.

Possible ways to do this:
1. We create a script that finds the user_ids of such users and after migration, we can update the value for those users.
2. I [googled](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/22600056/django-south-changing-field-type-in-data-migration) and found a third-party package for this (I don't think we use this approach in zulip)

My question is:
1. If we are using the first approach mentioned above, how do we convey this information to self-hosters to run a such script after migration on their server to update the values.
2. If there's some doc on this, please let me know. I googled and searched zulip docs and CZO but didn't find any.

  File "/srv/zulip/zerver/lib/db.py", line 19, in wrapper_execute
    action(sql, params)
django.db.utils.ProgrammingError: cannot cast type boolean to smallint
LINE 1: ... TYPE smallint USING "realm_name_in_notifications"::smallint
```

So, we can't directly update this.

**I should remove the field and then create a new field in separate migrations?**

**Alex Vandiver** · 2023-01-12 18:49 UTC

Yes.  The usual way we do these sorts of migrations is:
1. Add the new field with a different name; this includes a migration to translate the value in the old field to the new field.
2. Delete the old field
3. Rename the new field to the old name

If we decide that there is a better name for the field, then we can use that name in step 1, and omit step 3.

**Alex Vandiver** · 2023-01-12 18:54 UTC

You may want to read https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/subsystems/schema-migrations.html is you've not already.

I believe that you're asking about the assertion in `do_delete_messages` in `zerver/actions/message_delete.py`.

```python
def do_delete_messages(realm: Realm, messages: Iterable[Message]) -> None:
    # messages in delete_message event belong to the same topic
    # or is a single private message, as any other behaviour is not possible with
    # the current callers to this method.
```

If the first message is not a stream message, then it is a private message. And as the comment says, currently the callers of this function only support deleting a single private message.

## shift+tab producing weird artifacts in recipient boxes

*2023-01-23 to 2023-03-03 · 11 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/shift.2Btab.20producing.20weird.20artifacts.20in.20recipient.20boxes/with/1495273)*

**Joseph Ho** · 2023-01-23 21:53 UTC

Hello @Tim Abbott, this is regarding the bug that was reported in [#23627](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/23627).

I'm pretty sure the bug comes from the bootstrap-typeahead file. 
```js
keyup: function (e) {
      const pseudo_keycode = get_pseudo_keycode(e);

      switch(pseudo_keycode) {
        case 9: // tab
        case 13: // enter
          if (!this.shown) return
          this.select(e)
          break
      default:
          var hideOnEmpty = false
          if (e.keyCode === 8 && this.options.helpOnEmptyStrings) { // backspace
            hideOnEmpty = true
          }
          this.lookup(hideOnEmpty)
      }
```

When we press down the shift key and tab key, the cursor will move to the previous box and highlight. 

The weird artifacts begin when we start to let go of the keys. When we let go of the shift key first, ```this.lookup(hideOnEmpty)``` will run and display the typeahead. Then when we let go of the tab key, ```this.select(e)``` will run.

I'm not sure how to implement a fix for this.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-01-24 01:03 UTC

@Nehal Sharma is probably a good person to help with this.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-01-24 01:10 UTC

That does seem a bit subtle -- might be there's a `stopPropagation` we can add somewhere for it, or we should have the Bootstrap code (which we should feel comfortable patching) check if `shift` had been pressed during the `keyUp` handler? 

In Zulip's own code, we basically only use `keydown` handlers, precisely because `keydown` handlers have issues like this with the release order of modifier keys. So it's possible a larger change to migrate away from `keyup` might be required to fix this :/

**Nehal Sharma** · 2023-01-25 13:29 UTC

For the typeahead showing up momentarily when letting go of `shift`, I think a simple break for the `shift` case will do. However, it will also mean that one can't make the typeahead appear by pressing (and letting go of, of course) the `shift` key when the cursor is at an apt position, which is possible currently. We need to decide if this a trade-off we are willing to make to stop the distracting glitching of the typeahead on `shift + tab` (imo it is, since it seems rare that you'll need to make the typeahead menu like that)

**Nehal Sharma** · 2023-01-25 13:49 UTC

The highlighting is not due to releasing the `tab` key though :thinking: It happens before that

**Nehal Sharma** · 2023-01-25 15:15 UTC

Okay, I have a fix locally that involves overriding rate limiting rules for this endpoint, but I need to step away for a bit. When I'm back to The Vim Lands I need to do some history reconstruction: I've wound up adding two changes to `test_external:rate_limit_rule()` that need factored into their own commits (plus the relocation of and new use of that function as a third deal). Hope to have that up for review either late tonight, or early in the morning PST.

The rate limiting engine understands it needs to not interfere with localhost or internal requests, but does *not* understand Vagrant networking, and so my host IP of `172.17.0.1` (image is `172.17.0.2`) is not a "local address" for rate limiting purposes and `/emails/generate` gets caught by two sets of rate limiting domains. This is the correct behavior most of the time, but for this particular endpoint, we don't actually care where the request comes from, it's a dev-only endpoint to begin with and is designed to generate a bunch of emails.

You are probably running one of the Node tests that mocks the `clipboard` library. These mocks support the bare minimum functionality needed to run the existing tests with the existing code. The code might very well be fine; you’ll just need to fix the tests.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2023-02-04 06:40 UTC

(This is one of the pitfalls of tests that make such heavy use of implicit magically-injected mocks. It’s not at all obvious how to start debugging a problem that’s caused because a module that’s being imported is not the module that the code says it’s importing.)

          description: |
            [Policy][permission-level] for which users can post messages to the stream.

            - 1 => Any user can post.
            - 2 => Only administrators can post.
            - 3 => Only [full members][calc-full-member] can post.
            - 4 => Only moderators can post.

            **Changes**: New in Zulip 3.0 (feature level 1), replacing the previous
            `is_announcement_only` boolean.

            [permission-level]: /api/roles-and-permissions#permission-levels
            [calc-full-member]: /api/roles-and-permissions#determining-if-a-user-is-a-full-member

        is_announcement_only:
          type: boolean
          deprecated: true
          description: |
            Whether the given stream is an announcement only or not.

            **Changes**: Deprecated in Zulip 3.0 (feature level 1). Clients
            should use `stream_post_policy` instead.
```

So, Which is the preferred approach?

**Prakhar Pratyush** · 2023-02-26 09:57 UTC

@Sahil Batra -- maybe you could help me out with this?

As [4c8339f](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/commit/4c8339fa8c148e04cb4f0aac0a5db9790d187e2c#diff-7d09c06f7ab16ed46eeff8eb6e1a342f75fc9f3c780c6f10643303145316581eR3020) was authored by you.

**Sahil Batra** · 2023-02-26 11:51 UTC

It depends whether we want backwards compatibility to support older versions of mobile and terminal apps.

**Sahil Batra** · 2023-02-26 11:54 UTC

I don't think we would want backwards compatibility so we can remove the old field and mention in the "changes" entry of the new field that it replaces the older one.

**Prakhar Pratyush** · 2023-02-26 14:53 UTC

OK

Unrelated to the original issue -- But, how in general we decide, whether we want backward compatibility for some feature or not?

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-02-27 01:48 UTC

@Prakhar Pratyush generally the question is whether the existing mobile app implementations use the setting. In this case, we know they don't -- it's a setting that only controls the behavior of outgoing emails, and the mobile app doesn't have a settings UI for that class of field.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-02-27 01:49 UTC

However, it's probably still worth your posting a message in #**api design** explaining the API change (draft documentation is great for this) to get feedback from folks who think about this sort of thing (I know I've suggested a different name for the new setting twice in review; probably my last proposal is the right one, but extra eyes on this sort of thing are valuable).

The gross hackaround here is to remove the `unminimize` call and add an `apt-get update` call so future `install` calls work (since we depend on the implicit update in `unminimize`), but I have a feeling there has to be some better way.

For what it's worth, the host is a Void Linux x86_64 musl (not glibc) system on a ZFS root. The only differences between this setup and my prior one are new physical hardware, and the change in libc, which both seem like things that shouldn't matter for something running in namespaced/containerized environments (the libc used will be the glibc inside the container, for example). ZFS root seems like a potential quirk, but I have been using ZFS roots for years without issue, including on the old dev rig.

**Lalit** · 2023-03-14 15:29 UTC

I have opened #24237 for adding a new user display setting that allows them to choose the streams for which the user wants to see the unread count in the left sidebar. I have almost implemented the new setting. However @Alya Abbott  suggested in review to always show unread messages count when a stream is active i.e if it is expanded or if it is in "more topics" view irrespective of the new display setting.

Now I want some advice on how to approach this before proceeding further in my PR!
One way I thought was to use `topic_list.active_stream_id` function for finding out if a stream is expanded and build the stream row accordingly but then I would have to call my `update_counts_visibility_in_dom` to update the new setting at all the places which collapse the active stream for example when "Recent Conversations" is clicked, the expanded stream gets collapsed!

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-03-16 01:11 UTC

@Lalit the `narrow_state` module is what exports the information of what stream is active, but if you're doing something in CSS there's an `active-filter` class and related `active-sub-filter` class worth looking at.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-03-16 01:12 UTC

Though maybe we stopped setting `active-filter` for the stream when viewing a topic inside.

**Lalit** · 2023-03-17 16:20 UTC

Oh! thanks for the info about CSS classes I think I will try to come up with a CSS based solution for it!

**Lalit** · 2023-03-17 16:47 UTC

(replying to Tim Abbott)
> Though maybe we stopped setting `active-filter` for the stream when viewing a topic inside.
Is there any other way such that I can found out which stream is expanded using a CSS class because as you said I don't think that this is possible for now when viewing a topic inside?

**Lalit** · 2023-04-01 16:37 UTC

So, one possible solution I think is adding a new class for example `stream-expanded`which will be set if we have expanded a stream regardless of the current view we are in.  I did this using this code:
```ts
function deselect_stream_items(active_stream_id) {
    $("ul#stream_filters li").removeClass("active-filter stream-expanded");
    if (active_stream_id) {
        const active_stream_li = get_stream_li(active_stream_id);
        if (active_stream_li) {
            active_stream_li.addClass("stream-expanded");
        }
    }
}
```
And then use this `stream-expanded` in css to always show unread count. I have updated the PR #24237 with latest changes.

I have been working on this issue #23089 and created the PR  #24221 for the same, but @Alya Abbott  suggested that 
> I think, similarly to the current UI, we want to displace the "N minutes" notice on narrow screens but leave the buttons all on one line.

The summary of what I am trying to do for the message edit UI is:

 -  Keep the markdown tools on the extreme left.
 -  Keep the save/cancel buttons on the right.
 -  Keep the editing time period in the center.
 -  Keep all three sections on one line.

On narrow screens:

 - The markdown tools and save/cancel buttons should stay inline, but the "N" minutes notice should wrap to the next line.

To wrap the minutes notice to the next line while keeping the other two sections in one line, I have to change the order of the minutes notice. However, there are multiple intervals of screen widths where there is enough room for all three sections to stay in one line. If you reduce the screen width a little bit, the minutes notice should wrap.

To implement this, I defined multiple media queries for the intervals. The problem arises when you switch to a different language. Since the media query widths are defined according to the English language, this implementation does not work as expected in Russian language, and the buttons wrap to the next line rather than the minutes notice because of the defined screen widths.

I am not sure of any other alternative implementation, but I would really appreciate it if someone could suggest a different approach

*2023-03-24 to 2023-03-28 · 4 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/.E2.9C.94.20TS.20Type.20Guard.20Failing/with/1532548)*

**Satyam Bansal** · 2023-03-24 11:12 UTC

I was migrating some code to TS when I realized that in some places the inference is just not working as expected. I was able to cut down the problem to the bare minimum and was able to reproduce the situation into a smaller code. The code is available [here](https://www.typescriptlang.org/play?#code/MYewdgzgLgBAhjAvDA2gKBpmAiKBTAWwAdsAaNAXXghlEigG400oBPIvGAIyRgG8MWMHAJ4AXDGgAnAJZgA5kyw58xbAH4JYAK4EueKWgC+zOtFoSuKKshQDlw0ROxwyxiswBmIKTAAUZrBSeEQgAPqOnCCe8ACU-IKYiTAyMX5sHNG0KAAMFCjBoREieDaIyNg6egbY8fbKWIEwAG5wADa8wLn5heGRHg2DMAD0wwB66skmyakB3QUhfSUUsfWDTa0dyF15C0X9SkPKoxNTzMpNIFAAFgad873FogNHWCeTM57p7HhZV7e+coVKr6KS1NYNDbtXj-AyHV4jcaTZTTZSzWFSVbJC7gcybGE3OHYobvM7GZhAA).

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2023-03-24 19:17 UTC

You might just be expecting too much. For TypeScript to remember the narrowed type of `c[0][repo_name]`, it would need to track the identity and mutations of `repo_name`, which is a lot of extra complexity. Perfect type inference is undecidable, so TypeScript has to draw the line between what inferences it will and won’t make *somewhere*.

**Satyam Bansal** · 2023-03-24 19:23 UTC

Thanks for the clarification. The complexity is there for sure, but I expected the type inference to work just because type guards are there. But since it's not working because it can be computationally complex I guess I will use another way to check the types, which would be to assign the value to another variable and then put type guards on that.

@Satyam Bansal has marked this topic as resolved.

**Notification Bot** · 2023-03-27 10:50 UTC

This topic was moved here from #**issues>Set an optional max connection lifetime** by @Lauryn Menard.

**Alex Vandiver** · 2023-03-27 18:37 UTC

@qiqi tang: It should be a new setting in `settings.py` -- see https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/subsystems/settings.html

This means you'll need to add a default in `zproject/default_settings.py` (setting it to 0), and a commented-out line in `zproject/prod_settings_template.py` showing that default, along with a comment block above it saying when one might want to change the setting, and what its value should be (e.g. "...a timeout in minutes, or 0 to not keep long-lived SMTP connections.")

That means you'll be able to access the setting via `settings.SMTP_MAX_CONNECTION_MINUTES`

For testing, you can use [the `time-machine` library](https://github.com/adamchainz/time-machine), and mock out the connection object so you can verify that `close`/`open` are called.

Your code is generally in the right direction, though Python is indentation-sensitive, so that very much will not work as written.  You'll also want to figure out:
1. Where to store the time the connection was opened
2. How to initialize that value if this is the first time the connection is opening
3. How to handle the case where the setting is 0, which means we should not hold the connection open after we're done

So apparently my test database was corrupted and I had to run `tools/rebuild-test-database` to fix it.

**Sahil Batra** · 2023-03-30 06:45 UTC

I think it is because `./tools/test-backend` runs unapplied migrations, and thus `Nobody` group was created at the last when all all other groups are present and the tests assume different order of user groups being created.

Running `tools/rebuild-test-database`, creates the realm again and thus the groups are created in order which is expected in tests.

Hmm, I wonder if we can tweak that test to be less ordering-sensitive, if it's just that one that failed for folks?

I needed some help writing node tests for this [PR](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/24966). Specifically, in `hotkey.js` where I need to check if a message container is hidden.

I've used this code in my PR - 

```
const message_container = message_lists.current.view.message_containers.get(msg.id);
```

This is how `message_container` is used - 

```
if (!message_container.is_hidden) {
    condense.toggle_collapse(msg);
}
```

**Sameep Aher** · 2023-04-03 13:57 UTC

`message_container.is_hidden` is used to avoid `toggle_collapse` when the selected message is hidden.

The shortcut for toggling collapse is `-` and it operates on a message. The function for toggling message collapse (in `hotkey.js`) is - 

```
case "toggle_message_collapse": {
     if (!message_container.is_hidden) {
         condense.toggle_collapse(msg);
     } else {
         if (msg.collapsed) {
             condense.toggle_collapse(msg);
         }
     }
     return true;
 }
```

**Sameep Aher** · 2023-04-04 12:39 UTC

Below is the screenshot of the error I'm getting - 

[collapse-message-node-test-error.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/c0/exVXEJWAZAhw0o9QDoaMtkQm/collapse-message-node-test-error.png)

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-04-05 00:12 UTC

@Sameep Aher I think my main advice is to add your new logic inside `toggle_collapse` - the `hotkey.js` file is intended to not have any business logic in it, and it's tests just verify that the right function is called, so you won't have this problem if you avoid violating that design model.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-05-18 19:23 UTC

@Akshat you can get it via `./scripts/get-django-setting LOCAL_DATABASE_PASSWORD`

**Akshat** · 2023-05-18 19:58 UTC

If I'm not wrong then we are using postgres database right? I passed the following creds:
```
user: zulip
password: value from LOCAL_DATABASE_PASSWORD

port: 5432

```
But the connection was not established. Anything I missed?

**Akshat** · 2023-05-26 07:59 UTC

I think I need to connect with TablePlus using `Over SSH` option. Can someone help me what values should I enter for `server`, `port`, `User`, and `Password` field to connect over ssh?

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-05-26 17:44 UTC

@Akshat oops, I guess I forgot to send a reply I'd meant to last week.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-05-26 17:45 UTC

So the situation here is that the database is running on your Vagrant guest, which is a different server from your host.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-05-26 17:46 UTC

So if you want to use a GUI app, you need to do something in order to either have Vagrant expose port 5432 from the guest system to your host computer. There's probably a way to do that by fiddling with `Vagrantfile`, or using `ssh -L`; I imagine that "Over SSH" option basically is a way to do that for you.

Personally I like inspecting tables with Postgres' own `\d` and `\dt` in `manage.py dbshell`.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-05-26 17:47 UTC

`vagrant ssh` is the command Vagrant offers to SSH into the system; I'm sure there's a way to get the credentials it uses, though the right source for that is gonna be the upstream Vagrant documentation.

**Akshat** · 2023-05-29 11:17 UTC

I finally got it working!
In my case I didn't have to expose any port; I had to specify the `Server`, `Port` and `User` fields in `Over SSH` and most importantly I had to specify the path to the private key - to keep the settings to the default I just did: `vagrant ssh-config >> ~/.ssh/config` this added the vagrant ssh config.

## ✔ Upgrade to 7.0 without S3 (nginx)

*2023-06-05 to 2023-06-05 · 3 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/.E2.9C.94.20Upgrade.20to.207.2E0.20without.20S3.20.28nginx.29/with/1585220)*

**Christoph** · 2023-06-05 12:38 UTC

The upgrade to 7.0 broke our deployment today, because of the changes made in the nginx include files for S3 integration.

In detail: the file **/etc/nginx/zulip-include/app.d/uploads-internal.conf** contains options for S3 AND local storage uploads, but even when S3 is not activated [1], nginx still fails and cannot find variables like **s3_disposition_cache_key**, because they're referenced in this file, but are of course not initialised and thus produce only errors.

Solution: comment out the whole S3 block in this file, check nginx again and restart it, worked like a charm. IMO the options for S3 and local storage should not be in the same config file in this manner, since they only break the upgrade process.

**details about setup**
Debian 11.7
nginx 1.18.0


[1] https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/7.x/docs/production/upload-backends.md#migrating-from-local-uploads-to-amazon-s3-backend

**Christoph** · 2023-06-05 13:03 UTC

Marked as solved, because re-opened it in #**production help**

**Notification Bot** · 2023-06-05 13:03 UTC

@Wurzelmann has marked this topic as resolved.

@Joseph Ho Those users specifically just don't exist in the default fake ldap data. See this comment around those settings:

# Fake LDAP data has e.g. ("ldapuser1", "ldapuser1@zulip.com") for username/email.

**Hemant Umre** · 2023-06-23 15:13 UTC

(replying to Sahil Batra)

**Hemant Umre** · 2023-06-23 15:17 UTC

Doc: Provisioning and third-party dependencies [said](https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/subsystems/dependencies.html#other-third-party-and-generated-files):
> **Translations data** New translations data is downloaded from `Transifex` and then compiled to generate both the production locale files and also language data in `locale/language*.json` using `manage.py compilemessages`, which extends the default Django implementation of that tool.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-06-23 18:58 UTC

@Hemant Umre I think it's possible `TypedChoiceField` isn't a great choice for this application, in that the set of choices is a thing that changes dynamically when we sync languages from Transifex, and we very likely don't want to add an import-time dependency on `get_language_list`. My guess is the easiest answer will be to just write your own code that results in `get_language_list` only being called at runtime.

## overloaded REQ

*2023-07-24 to 2023-07-25 · 15 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/overloaded.20REQ/with/1615218)*

**Zixuan James Li** · 2023-07-24 22:42 UTC

I'm developing a new API for `has_request_variables` to replace validators with `cattrs` that structure the parsed JSON data using the type annotation of the function parameter for the `REQ`. This feature adds a `auto` (tentatively) parameter in a fashion similar to `json_validator`. For some reason, mypy reports that 
```
error: Overloaded function signatures 4 and 6 overlap with incompatible return types  [misc]
```
Here are the conflicting overloads:
```python
# Overload 4: no converter/validator, default=None, argument_type=None
@overload
def REQ(
    whence: Optional[str] = ...,
    *,
    default: None,
    str_validator: Optional[Validator[str]] = ...,
    intentionally_undocumented: bool = ...,
    documentation_pending: bool = ...,
    aliases: Sequence[str] = ...,
    path_only: bool = ...,
) -> Optional[str]:
    ...

```

```python
# Overload 6: auto=True
@overload
def REQ(
    whence: Optional[str] = ...,
    *,
    default: ResultT = ...,
    auto: Literal[True] = ...,
    argument_type: Optional[Literal["body"]] = ...,
    intentionally_undocumented: bool = ...,
    documentation_pending: bool = ...,
    aliases: Sequence[str] = ...,
    path_only: bool = ...,
) -> ResultT:
    ...

**Zixuan James Li** · 2023-07-24 22:44 UTC

Also, I'm not sure if the new overload will work because `ResultT` might not be specified if we allow `default` to be omitted.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2023-07-24 22:45 UTC

Your overload 4 declares that `auto` is not provided; your overload 6 declares that `auto` may *or may not* be provided (since a default is present), so they overlap.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2023-07-24 22:45 UTC

Delete the `= ...`.

**Zixuan James Li** · 2023-07-24 22:47 UTC

Thanks, that fixed the problem.

**Zixuan James Li** · 2023-07-24 22:48 UTC

(replying to Zixuan James Li)
> Also, I'm not sure if the new overload will work because `ResultT` might not be specified if we allow `default` to be omitted.
I'm assuming that mypy infers `ResultT` from the type annotation of the parameter, so that should be fine.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2023-07-24 22:55 UTC

A test case that may inform what this API should look like is how we’d handle parameter that’s supposed to be validated as a non-negative integer.

**Zixuan James Li** · 2023-07-25 00:56 UTC

I'm thinking if a type annotation like `Annotated[int, post_validator]` for `REQ` is reasonable, where the `post_validator` can be a function that satisfies `Callable[[str, ResultT], ResultT]`.

 Or we can add `post_validator: Optional[Callable[[str, ResultT], ResultT]] = ...` to the `auto` overload variant.

**Zixuan James Li** · 2023-07-25 00:59 UTC

I guess the latter is better because it is easier to implement, and we can restrict the type of `post_validator` during static analysis.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2023-07-25 01:05 UTC

Ideally we wouldn’t need a new mechanism for this; it would be naturally related to the way [`attrs` validators](https://www.attrs.org/en/stable/examples.html#validators) already work for struct fields.

**Zixuan James Li** · 2023-07-25 01:07 UTC

Yeah. I would prefer to use existing infrastructure for this kind of task. `post_validator` will only be needed for parameters typed with a primitive type.

**Zixuan James Li** · 2023-07-25 01:09 UTC

The validators I looked at require a separate class to be defined.
I guess most of the cases I mentioned above can be solved with `attrs` validators by rewriting the view function so that we define a dedicated class for all request parameters.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2023-07-25 01:09 UTC

Perhaps one should be able to pass an instance of `field(…)` to `REQ`, or instead of `REQ`.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2023-07-25 01:12 UTC

Quite possibly if we go far enough down this design path we will reinvent FastAPI, so it’s worth taking a look at how FastAPI does this.

**Zixuan James Li** · 2023-07-25 01:14 UTC

## babel error in node tests.

*2023-07-30 to 2023-08-01 · 13 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/babel.20error.20in.20node.20tests.2E/with/1617868)*

**Lalit** · 2023-07-30 13:17 UTC

Hi, so I raised this PR for stream_data typescript conversion -- #26381 and I haven't modified any of the test files but for some reason running node tests gives me this weird error: 
```
"TypeError: /__w/zulip/zulip/web/src/stream_data.ts: Property property of OptionalMemberExpression expected node to be of a type ["Identifier"] but instead got "CallExpression"
```
Any help on this? I don't really understand this error 😕

**Zixuan James Li** · 2023-07-30 22:54 UTC

I looked into this and it appears that having `function is_web_public` in `stream_data` breaks property access of `is_web_public: boolean`.

**Zixuan James Li** · 2023-07-30 22:56 UTC

Renaming either the function or the property makes the error go away:
```ts
export function is_web_public(stream_id: number): boolean | undefined {
    const sub = sub_store.get(stream_id);
    return sub?.is_web_public;
}
```

**Zixuan James Li** · 2023-07-30 22:58 UTC

Yet I'm not sure what causes that.

**Lalit** · 2023-07-31 16:14 UTC

Also, weirdly if we remove the optional chaining and just use a ternary instead the error goes away.
```ts
export function is_web_public(stream_id: number): boolean {
    const sub = sub_store.get(stream_id);
    return sub ? sub.is_web_public : false;
}
```

**Karl Stolley** · 2023-07-31 16:20 UTC

Aren't those checking two different things? `sub?.is_web_public` is looking for an `is_web_public` member on `sub`, returning `undefined` if it's missing, whereas `sub ? sub.is_web_public` is checking `sub` for a non-falsey value, and assuming the existence of the `is_web_public` value

**Lalit** · 2023-07-31 16:22 UTC

Oh yeah it should ideally be `sub ? sub.is_web_public : undefined`

**Lalit** · 2023-07-31 16:23 UTC

If we do not have a sub then we were returning undefined as we are doing in this new ternary condition.

**Lalit** · 2023-07-31 16:24 UTC

Actually we are guaranteed to have a member called `is_web_public` on `sub` objects.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2023-08-01 00:28 UTC

> `sub?.is_web_public` is looking for an `is_web_public` member on `sub`, returning `undefined` if it's missing,

No, you have described the normal behavior of `sub.is_web_public` there.

`?.` is the [optional chaining](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Operators/Optional_chaining) operator; its special property is that `sub?.is_web_public` checks whether *`sub` itself* is `undefined` or `null`, and evaluates to `undefined` if it is.

```js
{}.is_web_public  // undefined
null.is_web_public  // TypeError
undefined.is_web_public  // TypeError

{}?.is_web_public  // undefined
null?.is_web_public  // undefined
undefined?.is_web_public  // undefined
```

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2023-08-01 00:50 UTC

I haven’t confirmed this yet but your Babel error is almost certainly a bug in the unmaintained babel-plugin-rewire-ts plugin, which we really need to get rid of.

**Lalit** · 2023-08-01 04:01 UTC

(replying to Anders Kaseorg)
> I haven’t confirmed this yet but your Babel error is almost certainly a bug in the unmaintained babel-plugin-rewire-ts plugin, which we really need to get rid of.

Yeah it looks like this is not our error to handle so I guess I will just use a ternary here instead of optional chaining and leave a refactor comment for now.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2023-08-01 07:36 UTC

One workaround is to force Babel to compile out optional chaining.

```diff
--- a/web/babel.config.js
+++ b/web/babel.config.js
@@ -15,6 +15,7 @@ module.exports = {

Ah, yeah, OK.  `zerver/management/commands/send_custom_email.py` says:
```python3
    def handle(self, *args: Any, **options: str) -> None:
        users: QuerySet[UserProfile] = UserProfile.objects.none()
        # ...
        if options["entire_server"]:
            users = UserProfile.objects.filter(
                is_active=True, is_bot=False, is_mirror_dummy=False, realm__deactivated=False
            )
        elif options["marketing"]:
            users = ...
        elif options["remote_servers"]:
            # ...
        elif options["all_sponsored_org_admins"]:
            users = ...
        elif options["json_file"]:
            users = UserProfile.objects.filter(id__in=[int(user_id) for user_id in user_data])
        else:
            realm = self.get_realm(options)
            users = self.get_users(options, realm, is_bot=False)
        # ...
        send_custom_email(
            users, target_emails=target_emails, options=options, add_context=add_context
        )
        if options["dry_run"]:
            print("Would send the above email to:")
            for user in users:
                print(f"  {user.delivery_email} ({user.realm.string_id})")
```

So having the ordering in `get_users` is necessary to affect the order that the lines are printed in `dry_run` (#26054), but only affects one potential way that we could generate `users`, so the ordering in `send_custom_email` (#26539) is also useful to have a consistent ordering for actually sending in all of those cases.

**Alex Vandiver** · 2023-08-24 01:08 UTC

OK, and attempting to upgrade to `main` from that point hits:
```
Migrations which are currently applied, but missing in the new version:
  twofactor - 0001_squashed_0008_delete_phonedevice
2023-08-24 01:06:24.104 ERR  [] This is not an upgrade -- the current deployment (version 8.0-dev-563-g29bdaaf5b5) contains 1 database migrations which /home/zulip/deployments/2023-08-24-01-03-52 (version 8.0-dev-1009-g29bb346480) does not.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2023-08-24 01:08 UTC

The bug is in either django-two-factor-auth or Django itself, see the minimal reproduction in my [upstream comment](https://github.com/jazzband/django-two-factor-auth/pull/642#issuecomment-1690497043).

**Alex Vandiver** · 2023-08-24 01:09 UTC

Can we pull the `django-two-factor-auth` version bump out of `7.x` safely, at this point?

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2023-08-24 01:10 UTC

I don’t think that will help. I think you’ll see the same symptom on a no-op upgrade from 29bdaaf5b582e112cc44bc3901e6f180faa34d5d to 29bdaaf5b582e112cc44bc3901e6f180faa34d5d.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2023-08-24 01:13 UTC

The `twofactor` typo is in 1.15.3 and was *removed* in 1.15.4.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2023-08-24 01:15 UTC

So at this point we need to

```diff
--- a/scripts/lib/check-database-compatibility
+++ b/scripts/lib/check-database-compatibility
@@ -120,6 +120,10 @@ missing.difference_update(
 # https://github.com/python-social-auth/social-app-django/pull/25
 missing.discard(("default", "0005_auto_20160727_2333"))
 
+# This was a typo (twofactor for two_factor) corrected in
+# https://github.com/jazzband/django-two-factor-auth/pull/642
+missing.discard(("twofactor", "0001_squashed_0008_delete_phonedevice"))
+
 for key, migration in loader.disk_migrations.items():
     missing.discard(key)
     missing.difference_update(migration.replaces)
```

which doesn’t solve all our problems, but does solve that one.

**Alex Vandiver** · 2023-08-24 01:17 UTC

Hm.  I guess that will silence the don't-go-backwards logic, sure.  And kicks down the line the actual migration confusion?

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2023-08-24 01:18 UTC

Yeah, the actual confusion remaining in 1.15.4 is about the real `two_factor`, not the typo `twofactor`.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2023-08-24 01:21 UTC

Like maybe Django is somehow confused by how `phonenumber.0001_squashed_0001_initial` replaces `two_factor.0001_squashed_0008_delete_phonedevice` which itself replaces `two_factor.0001_initial` through `two_factor.0008_delete_phonedevice`, but the transitive replacements are not explicitly included.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2023-08-24 01:34 UTC

Including them explicitly does seem to fix it: https://github.com/jazzband/django-two-factor-auth/pull/649.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2023-08-24 01:38 UTC

Either way I cannot reproduce the `test-js-with-puppeteer` failure that started this thread. So that’s something unrelated.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2023-08-24 01:50 UTC

#26561 for the `check-database-compatibility` change.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2023-08-24 02:17 UTC

#26562 to pull in the transitive replaces fix from Git.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-08-24 05:22 UTC

Those two seem reasonable, merged. Hopefully upstream merges the fix soon and we can upgrade to that.

## Custom gravatar url

*2023-08-22 to 2023-08-23 · 16 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/Custom.20gravatar.20url/with/1629300)*

**Lukas Assmann** · 2023-08-22 11:11 UTC

Hello everyone,

We are using Zulip for a couple of weeks now in my company and really enjoy it. However we would like to get our avatars from our self hosted gravatar-alternative server. 

So i thought i’d implement such a functionality since it’s not to big of a task and would be a nice first contribution. This would also fix issue 15123. 

To get to the point:

My initial thought was to provide a new setting parameter `CUSTOM_GRAVATAR_URL` which would then replace the `https://secure.gravatar.com` part of the url in `zerver/lib/avatar.py`, if provided.

Only issue with this is that the user would still see the "Hosted by Gravatar" link underneath their avatar in the frontend, which would be incorrect. 

Question now is if i should introduce a new avatar source like “C” (e.g. “Hosted on custom domain”) in `zerver/models.py` . This would then mean that with creation/update of a user, the avatar source would need to be set to this new value, if a (newly introduced) setting is set to use custom avatars. However this would also mean, that all existing users would need to be migrated from source “G” to “C”, whenever this new setting is changed, which i find a bit messy. 

Should i open this can of worms? Any help/pointers would be much appreciated :)

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-08-22 18:20 UTC

@Lukas Assmann howdy! I think we definitely want to offer an alternative to Gravatar here; I think the main question is why the right semantics are.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-08-22 18:21 UTC

What I've sorta had in mind is changing the default avatars to be our own procedurally generated avatar system, and compute them based on a hash of `(realm_url, user_id)`, with the resulting system not being dependant on any third-party, with Gravatar remaining as an option for those who want to use that.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-08-22 18:22 UTC

I guess I'm curious to hear more about your self-hosted gravatars system, both in terms of its goals and technical setup -- does it use the same hash algorithm for constructing URLs as gravatar.com proper does?

**Lukas Assmann** · 2023-08-22 18:40 UTC

Hi @Tim Abbott ! 
I agree that having a default alternative to gravatar would be good. 
Nevertheless, the reason we have our “own gravatar” is that it is tedious to set/change an avatar for every application in our company and since we are exclusively using self-hosted open source software we want to implement a solution that allows us to change it once and use everywhere. Many OSS already use gravatar and that makes it easy to substitute it with another server. 
There is only one self-hosted alternative to gravatar i could find: https://www.libravatar.org
Since we want to expand on that idea internally we started developing an alternative inhouse. 
Both libravatar and our solution conform to the gravatar api, using the `/avatat/{hash}` route with the hash being the trimmed and lowercased email as an md5 hash. 
The only thing that differs is the base url, of course.

**Lukas Assmann** · 2023-08-22 18:42 UTC

If i replace the `https://secure.gravatar.com` part of the gravatar domain in zerver with our own base url, all our images are correctly displayed, so that tracks.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-08-22 18:43 UTC

So the `CUSTOM_GRAVATAR_URL` concept would work if having that setting disabled also disabled the `client_gravatar` feature (which tells clients they can compute the gravatar locally if they like). I think it makes sense for it to be a server-level setting set in `/etc/zulip/settings.py`; it seems like the sort of thing that is likely to only be relevant for self-hosters given the fairly limited set of implementations, so I don't see a reason to add it as a setting with UI in the web app.

**Lukas Assmann** · 2023-08-22 18:44 UTC

Yes correct, exactly this was my intention :)

**Lukas Assmann** · 2023-08-22 18:47 UTC

But since i would then simply replace the the url, the user would still have “hosted by gravatar” in the frontend, since the avatar_source value in the user would still be “G”, meaning Gravatar (if i understood everything in the code correctly)

**Lukas Assmann** · 2023-08-22 18:50 UTC

And the user would therefore be forwarded to the gravatar website when clicking on that link which would be incorrect. 
I know this is a very small nitpick and if it was just for myself i would just leave it at that. I wouldn’t care if it said gravatar in the frontend/app

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-08-22 22:51 UTC

(replying to Lukas Assmann)
> And the user would therefore be forwarded to the gravatar website when clicking on that link which would be incorrect. I know this is a very small nitpick and if it was just for myself i would just leave it at that. I wouldn’t care if it said gravatar in the frontend/app

I think it wouldn't be a hard follow-up to plumb the setting through to the web app to adjust that behavior; that's also roughly what we'd need to do in order to make the `client_gravatar` not need to be disabled with your setting.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-08-22 22:53 UTC

@Lukas Assmann basically you'd put a `server_gravatar_base_url` parameter in `page_params`; see `zerver/lib/events.py` and more generally https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/tutorials/new-feature-tutorial.html for how to plumb that sort of thing.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-08-22 22:54 UTC

See also https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/subsystems/settings.html. I think you can prototype something using the information in that documentation that works for your installation, and then we can look at what the easiest path is to integration.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-08-22 22:55 UTC

I think basically these are the places that would need to refer to the new variable.
```
$ git grep gravatar.com web/src/ zerver/lib/
web/src/people.ts:    const avatar_url = "https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/" + hash + "?d=identicon";
web/src/people.ts:    const avatar_url = "https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/" + hash + "?d=identicon";
zerver/lib/avatar.py:        return f"https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/{hash_key}?d=identicon{gravitar_query_suffix}"
zerver/lib/events.py:            if client_gravatar and person["avatar_url"].startswith("https://secure.gravatar.com/"):
zerver/lib/events.py:                        "https://secure.gravatar.com/"
zerver/lib/realm_icon.py:        return f"https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/{hash_key}?d=identicon"
```

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-08-22 22:55 UTC

(There's more work to be done end-to-end because of mobile apps to fully add such a setting, but I think the above should be pretty simple and not make the code base worse)

**Lukas Assmann** · 2023-08-23 07:41 UTC

Thank you so much @Tim Abbott ! I will have a look and give an implementation a try :)

export function set_message_booleans(message) {
    const flags = message.flags || [];

    function convert_flag(flag_name) {
        return flags.includes(flag_name);
    }

    message.unread = !convert_flag("read");
    message.historical = convert_flag("historical");
    message.starred = convert_flag("starred");
    message.mentioned = convert_flag("mentioned") || convert_flag("wildcard_mentioned");
    message.mentioned_me_directly = convert_flag("mentioned");
    message.wildcard_mentioned = convert_flag("wildcard_mentioned");
    message.collapsed = convert_flag("collapsed");
    message.alerted = convert_flag("has_alert_word");

    // Once we have set boolean flags here, the `flags` attribute is
    // just a distraction, so we delete it.  (All the downstream code
    // uses booleans.)
    delete message.flags;

    console.log("Log 1:", {...message});
    console.log("Log 2:", message);
}

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2023-09-26 16:04 UTC

In Chrome and Firefox, when you log an object, the browser console loads its properties lazily when you expand the triangle. Any mutations until that time are visible, even if they happened after the log statement. Chrome gives you an ℹ️ tooltip “This value was evaluated upon first expanding. It may have changed since then.”

**Lalit** · 2023-09-27 12:48 UTC

So if I return `{...message}` or just `message` from this function and use that in the downstream code, they both should be equivalent right?

**Zixuan James Li** · 2023-09-27 15:37 UTC

In case of returning, mutations of `message` should still be visible to the callee, while with `{...message}` you create a new object with the same properties.

Hi fellas, I'm working on this issue [#15029](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/issues/15029). In short, the problem is that I've got to detect the user environment during `./tools/provision`. The constraints are that if the environment is a dedicated container to run the Zulip dev server, I need to write the source activation command to the respective user's bash profile. I've written this logic; I need to know whether it covers the checks for all the dedicated containers. Please let me know.

```python
import os
import pwd

user_id = os.getuid()
wsl_path = "/proc/sys/fs/binfmt_misc/WSLInterop"

# A dedicated container is those VM's that are specificaclly
# available to run zulip development server.
# i.e. WSL/Vagrant/Droplet setups

if os.path.exists(wsl_path) or pwd.getpwuid(user_id) in ("vagrant", "zulipdev"):
    print("Environment is a dedicated container")
```

Previously, I used env-variables/file-paths for a given container to identify its type, but sometimes that can give a false positive flag, and we want to avoid that. So I'm using `getpwuid()` as used [here](zulip/zulip/tools/lib/sanity_check.py) and [here](zulip/zulip/tools/run-dev).

## Setup with Vagrant

*2023-10-12 to 2023-10-14 · 3 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/Setup.20with.20Vagrant/with/1661006)*

**victoria Abioye** · 2023-10-12 11:10 UTC

(replying to victoria Abioye)
> Thank you @Karl Stolley for the prompt response. So as outlined in the contribution guide, i was able to successfully run vagrant ssh in my command line, kindly find the attached screen shot [Screenshot-2023-10-11-at-4.15.19-PM.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/db/OQWwj056MTi9fGRL42fsOY-d/Screenshot-2023-10- …

So,  updating my environment and Re-provisioning my Vagrant machine using  "vagrant provision"  as outlined in the contribution guide did not work for me as i was still encountering   "incomplete /var/log/provision.log file " error and also Vagrant guest doesn’t show (zulip-py3-venv) at start of prompt. But this did the trick for me and i thought i should share.

- Delete the node_modules directory and the pnpm-lock.yaml file.
- Reinstall packages using npm install.
- Start the Vagrant machine with the Docker provider: vagrant up --provider=docker.
-   If you get  this error "ERR_PNPM_LOCKFILE_CONFIG_MISMATCH" 
-  run: pnpm install --no-frozen-lockfile.
-  If Terminal Prompt  still Displays "vagrant@" Instead of "zulip-py3-venv"
- Navigate to the Zulip repository folder and run the provisioning script: ./tools/provision.
-  And finally change the prompt to "zulip-py3-venv" with: source /srv/zulip-py3-venv/bin/activate

After completing these steps, you should be able to start the Zulip server for development with ./tools/run-dev.

Make sure to adapt the file paths to your specific environment.
I hope this helps others who might encounter similar issues.

*2023-10-24 to 2023-11-27 · 6 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/.27is.27.20queries.20filter.20verification.20in.20narrow.2Epy.20.2327309/with/1668040)*

**Nimish Medatwal** · 2023-10-24 15:06 UTC

Hey everyone, I am working on [issue#27309](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/issues/27309) in which I am adding is:followed to the search filter.
I came across this function in marrow.py which validates `is` queries in filter
```python
def by_is(self, query: Select, operand: str, maybe_negate: ConditionTransform) -> Select:
        # This operator class does not support is_web_public_query.
        assert not self.is_web_public_query
        assert self.user_profile is not None

        if operand in ["dm", "private"]:
            # "is:private" is a legacy alias for "is:dm"
            cond = column("flags", Integer).op("&")(UserMessage.flags.is_private.mask) != 0
            return query.where(maybe_negate(cond))
        elif operand == "starred":
            cond = column("flags", Integer).op("&")(UserMessage.flags.starred.mask) != 0
            return query.where(maybe_negate(cond))
        elif operand == "unread":
            cond = column("flags", Integer).op("&")(UserMessage.flags.read.mask) == 0
            return query.where(maybe_negate(cond))
        elif operand == "mentioned":
            cond1 = column("flags", Integer).op("&")(UserMessage.flags.mentioned.mask) != 0
            cond2 = column("flags", Integer).op("&")(UserMessage.flags.wildcard_mentioned.mask) != 0
            cond = or_(cond1, cond2)
            return query.where(maybe_negate(cond))
        elif operand == "alerted":
            cond = column("flags", Integer).op("&")(UserMessage.flags.has_alert_word.mask) != 0
            return query.where(maybe_negate(cond))
        elif operand == "resolved":
            cond = get_resolved_topic_condition_sa()
            return query.where(maybe_negate(cond))
       elif operand == "followed":
            cond=get_followed_topic_condition_sa()
           return query.where(maybe_negate(cond))
        raise BadNarrowOperatorError("unknown 'is' operand " + operand)
```
I tried writing  `get_followed_topic_condition_sa()` function in topics.py but it's just not working.
```python
def get_followed_topic_condition_sa() -> ColumnElement[Boolean]:
       followed_topic_cond = select(UserTopic.VisibilityPolicy, Text).where(visibility_policy == UserTopic.VisibilityPolicy.FOLLOWED)
       return followed_topic_cond 
```

**Kedar Shidhaye** · 2024-01-05 16:47 UTC

(replying to Kedar Shidhaye)
> I am trying to setup zulips codebase on by debian machine and I have completed till step 2 get zulip code from [recommended setup guide](https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/setup-recommended.html#step-2-get-zulip-code). In step 3 I executed the command ``` vagrant up --provider=docker …
I found the solution
So the problem was that Vagrantfile could only be accessed by root on my debian machine so now I have modified its permission and t works fine.
It was a noobie mistake since I am a frequent windows user and new to debian

It depends on the issue and the part of the codebase you're working in. These streams are common areas of the code base to be working on: #**frontend**, #**backend** and #**design**. This stream, #**development help**, can also be a fine place to post. You can start a new topic with the issue number at the end so that it links to the issue on GitHub. An example of this would be #**development help>'is' queries filter verification in narrow.py #27309**.

```
class WebhookIntegration(Integration):
    DEFAULT_FUNCTION_PATH = "zerver.webhooks.{name}.view.api_{name}_webhook"
    DEFAULT_URL = "api/v1/external/{name}"
    DEFAULT_CLIENT_NAME = "Zulip{name}Webhook"
    DEFAULT_DOC_PATH = "{name}/doc.{ext}"

    def __init__(
        self,
        name: str,
        categories: List[str],
        client_name: Optional[str] = None,
        logo: Optional[str] = None,
        secondary_line_text: Optional[str] = None,
        function: Optional[str] = None,
        url: Optional[str] = None,
        display_name: Optional[str] = None,
        doc: Optional[str] = None,
        stream_name: Optional[str] = None,
        legacy: bool = False,
        config_options: Sequence[Tuple[str, str, OptionValidator]] = [],
    ) -> None:
        if client_name is None:
            client_name = self.DEFAULT_CLIENT_NAME.format(name=name.title())
        super().__init__(
            name,
            client_name,
            categories,
            logo=logo,
            secondary_line_text=secondary_line_text,
            display_name=display_name,
            stream_name=stream_name,
            legacy=legacy,
            config_options=config_options,
        )

        if function is None:
            function = self.DEFAULT_FUNCTION_PATH.format(name=name)

        if isinstance(function, str):
            # We rename the imported function as view_function here to appease
            # mypy, since it does not allow redefinition of variables with
            # different types.
            view_function = import_string(function)

        self.function = view_function

        if url is None:
            url = self.DEFAULT_URL.format(name=name)
        self.url = url

        if doc is None:
            doc = self.DEFAULT_DOC_PATH.format(name=name, ext="md")

        self.doc = doc

    @property
    def url_object(self) -> URLResolver:
        assert self.function is not None
        return path(self.url, self.function)
```

## codebase

*2023-12-19 to 2025-12-23 · 9 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/codebase/with/1706902)*

**Krish Suthar** · 2023-12-19 14:31 UTC

Hello everyone,

I'm Krish Suthar, and today I successfully set up my local environment. Now, I'm eager to start contributing, but I need guidance on understanding the codebase. It would be greatly appreciated if anyone could assist me in navigating and comprehending the codebase.

Thank you!

**Karl Stolley** · 2023-12-19 14:37 UTC

Definitely work through our developer tutorials at https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/tutorials/index.html, especially https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/tutorials/new-feature-tutorial.html You’ll also want to get comfortable with your `git grep` skills.

**Ananay Sharma** · 2025-12-21 02:19 UTC

Is there a go to way to find the files related to an issue except just asking LLMs(output is often unreliable)? Since Zulip has such a complex codebase covering alot of aspects, it is gets especially challenging when you try to understand and solve problems that cover multiple parts of the codebase.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-12-21 02:27 UTC

Yeah there's a lot of ways to do it. One thing that works pretty well for frontend is to use your developer tools "inspect elements" feature to inspect an element, and that'll tell you what file that is defined in, as well as names for identified you can `git grep` for.

Another is to `git grep` for a string you see in the UI, to see where that's defined.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-12-21 02:27 UTC

The Zulip codebase is actually quite small for a project of its complexity; we try a lot harder to avoid having 10 duplicate ways to do something than most software projects.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-12-21 02:28 UTC

But I think the investment in learning how to find things via `git grep` or your codebase's search tools will serve you well through your career.

**Ananay Sharma** · 2025-12-21 02:40 UTC

(replying to Tim Abbott)
> But I think the investment in learning how to find things via `git grep` or your codebase's search tools will serve you well through your career.

Thanks, I will definite look into it.

**Ananay Sharma** · 2025-12-21 02:51 UTC

(replying to Tim Abbott)
> The Zulip codebase is actually quite small for a project of its complexity; we try a lot harder to avoid having 10 duplicate ways to do something than most software projects.


I wanted to better understand the design tradeoffs behind Zulip’s frontend architecture.
In particular, given your comment about avoiding multiple overlapping ways to do the same thing, how did the team evaluate (or repeatedly reevaluate) React-style component frameworks versus the current Jinja2 + Handlebars + explicit event-driven model?
I’m asking mainly to make sure I’m reasoning about the frontend in the way maintainers expect, rather than assuming this is primarily   legacy code inertia or performance-driven choice.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-12-23 19:35 UTC

We've been reluctant to move to a framework like React that is (1) hard to migrate onto or off of incrementally, because it takes over your entire codebase and (2) greatly limits control over performance.

But I also ran it on Zulip Cloud, which has a lot more reactions -- and it still did a sequential scan, despite there being an index on `message_id`.  So the specific formulation of a sub-select with `SELECT DISTINCT message_id FROM zerver_reaction` may not be a good one.

**Alex Vandiver** · 2024-03-05 14:20 UTC

Here's a much more performant query:
```sql
EXPLAIN ANALYZE
SELECT message_id,
       flags
  FROM zerver_usermessage
  JOIN zerver_message
    ON zerver_message.id = zerver_usermessage.message_id

 WHERE sender_id = 428054
   AND zerver_usermessage.user_profile_id = 428054
   AND EXISTS
        (SELECT 1
          FROM zerver_reaction
         WHERE zerver_reaction.message_id = zerver_message.id
       )
 ORDER BY message_id DESC
 LIMIT 50
```

**Alex Vandiver** · 2024-03-05 14:22 UTC

        Sort Key: zerver_usermessage.message_id DESC

        ->  Nested Loop  (cost=1.72..1717.24 rows=1 width=12) (actual time=0.370..1.360 rows=11 loops=1)
              ->  Nested Loop Semi Join  (cost=1.01..1685.18 rows=14 width=8) (actual time=0.302..1.143 rows=11 loops=1)
                    ->  Index Only Scan using zerver_message_sender_recipient_id on zerver_message  (cost=0.57..463.87 rows=1822 width=4) (actual time=0.063..0.639 rows=66 loops=1)
                          Index Cond: (sender_id = 428054)

                    Index Cond: ((user_profile_id = 428054) AND (message_id = zerver_message.id))
```

## running-tests

*2023-12-26 to 2023-12-26 · 3 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/running-tests/with/1709709)*

**Joydeep Bhattacharjee** · 2023-12-26 11:39 UTC

How can I run a specific test. for example if I want to run alert-meesage-ui.test.js file only,  to test the alert words, how can I do that.

**Mehtab Singh** · 2023-12-26 13:37 UTC

Hi there!
If you want to run a specific test located in a certain repository you shall run the command:
`tools/test-js-with-node` command and specify the file path name
for example: let's say that the test file alert-message-ui.test.js is located in web/tests/
Then you shall write the command as follows:
`./tools/test-js-with-node web/tests/alert-message-ui.test.js`
For more information you can refer the documentation:
1. https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/testing/testing.html#major-test-suites
2. https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/testing/testing-with-node.html

*2024-01-06 to 2024-02-02 · 12 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/.E2.9C.94.20creating.20singleton.20tooltip/with/1714841)*

**Shashank Singh** · 2024-01-06 15:04 UTC

Today , I was trying to create a singleton tooltip for compose-box buttons.

Now there are 2 ways to do that - 
1) Create a ```delegate ("parent",__)``` function in ```compose_tooltips.js``` function. 
2) Create a Javascript/jquery function in ```click_handlers.js.```

Problem with - 
1)  To use singleton function you need to create an array of tippy instances. Even if I pass this array as ```target: array```, it re-triggers and singleton does not work as expected.
2) Writing a new function actually solves the problem but it does not render the HTML of data-tooltip-template-id and we need to write a new renderTemplate function for each type of template.

Is there a better approach or there are possible ways to improve the above approaches?
Reference PR #28387. (Using approach-2)

**Shashank Singh** · 2024-01-28 13:57 UTC

Hello @Sayam Samal tried to address the feedback from my PR #28387 but couldn't figure out - 

> We already have a get_tooltip_content method, which does the same, let's use that in

The above method is defined in typescript file , how can I use this in javascript to render data-tooltip-template-id HTML template?

Implementation I have added to remove those extra instances - 

```
    const buttons = document.querySelectorAll('.compose_control_button[data-tooltip-template-id], .compose_control_button[data-tippy-content], .compose_control_button_container');

    const tippyInstances = tippy(buttons);
    const singletonInstance = createSingleton(tippyInstances, {
        delay: 5000,
        onTrigger(instance, event) {

                instance.setProps({ delay: 0 });
            } else {
                instance.setProps({ delay: 500 });
            }
        },
    });
```
But this does not render the tooltips with data-tooltip-template-id.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-01-29 19:35 UTC

@Shashank Singh if you `git grep data-tooltip-template-id`, you'll find it's implemented via JS code in the `get_tooltip_content` helper function, which you should probably be using either directly or indirectly via it being a default prop.

**Sayam Samal** · 2024-01-30 23:57 UTC

(replying to Shashank Singh)
> But this does not render the tooltips with data-tooltip-template-id.

@Shashank Singh Okay, so this took quite some while to figure out. So, the reason we are unable to get any tooltip content when using is `data-tooltip-template-id` is because the function `get_tooltip_content()` expects the reference element of the tooltip, i.e, the element invoking the tooltip. In the case of singletons, the reference passed by default to the function being called for the content prop is an empty div (I believe this is how a singleton replaces all the existing tippy instances and handles a common trigger detection). We therefore [need to extract the actual current reference](https://github.com/atomiks/tippyjs/issues/964#issuecomment-932054272) in this case.

**Shashank Singh** · 2024-02-01 16:29 UTC

For general instance -

For singleton instance - 
[Screenshot-2024-02-01-at-9.47.49PM.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/73/tpUbSUnt2w72WDdXASV-DO1-/Screenshot-2024-02-01-at-9.47.49PM.png)

Due to which the HTML couldn't be rendered using get_tooltip_content.

**Shashank Singh** · 2024-02-01 16:32 UTC

> We therefore [need to extract the actual current reference](https://github.com/atomiks/tippyjs/issues/964#issuecomment-932054272) in this case.

I wonder how can we do this because first we first of all we create a combined tippy instance using all the buttons. How can we filter the ones which uses data-tooltip-template-id ? 
Even if we do so do how should I extract the actual current reference ?
Just a general idea would help.

**Sayam Samal** · 2024-02-01 21:41 UTC

To filter ones that do use `data-tooltip-template-id`, a simple condition checking if that attribute exists would suffice, maybe the same condition we use in the `get_tooltip_content` method: `if (reference.dataset.tooltipTemplateId !== undefined)`

**Sayam Samal** · 2024-02-01 21:45 UTC

(replying to Shashank Singh)
> Even if we do so do how should I extract the actual current reference ?
Did you visit the link I have mentioned above? Cause that pretty much answers this already. (quoting the same below)
> `onTrigger(instance, event)` => `event.currentTarget` will point to the "current" reference

**Shashank Singh** · 2024-02-02 07:24 UTC

## Rename #recent_topics to #recent

*2024-01-14 to 2024-01-16 · 4 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/Rename.20.23recent_topics.20to.20.23recent/with/1719218)*

**Shubham Padia** · 2024-01-14 14:43 UTC

Hi, I am working on #25781 which intends to rename #recent_topics to #recent. 

Right now, the frontend passes "recent_topics" as a value for web_home_view. Before running the migration renaming #recent_topics to #recent, I need to make sure that the respective endpoints to update settings accept #recent as an valid option and that frontend doesn't pass "recent_topics" as a value. 

For self hosted or zulip cloud,  **will the migration run before or after the code is live**? If it runs before, I need to somehow make sure that any web_home_view set to recent_topics in the time the migration was run and new code was deployed are changed to recent again. If it runs after, there's no issue

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-01-15 20:23 UTC

Generally you should expect the server to update before the web app -- since we send a signal to web apps instances to reload the browser into the new code in the background, distributed over time.

So the migration will generally run before the web app code is updated.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-01-15 20:26 UTC

We can of course do multiple deployments for Zulip Cloud if appropriate. 

This sort of migration isn't usually a problem for self-hosted instances, because they generally do major version upgrades with the app shut down for long enough that all web browser clients will reload.

**Shubham Padia** · 2024-01-16 05:45 UTC

Got it, thanks Tim!

## typescript migration help

*2024-01-20 to 2024-01-20 · 5 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/typescript.20migration.20help/with/1723033)*

**Joydeep Bhattacharjee** · 2024-01-20 08:16 UTC

I've created stubs for **web/third/marked/lib/marked** inside the file **web/src/marked.d.ts** . Now when I'm trying to import it in the `web/third/marked/lib/marked` in **markdown.js**  getting this error **Could not find a declaration file for module '../third/marked/lib/marked'.**  How to make the typescript compiler understand that marked.d.ts is the type definitions of marked.js ?? Please check the PR #28627 for some more context.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2024-01-20 08:28 UTC

`declare module` is not the thing to use here. That’s for declaring modules outside the source tree, and even then is not generally the preferred way to do so.

A `.d.ts` file for in-tree code belongs right next to the corresponding `.js` file, and contains declarations at top level.

(If you aren’t familiar with TypeScript’s rules here, this might not be the project for you, as TypeScript will not check that the `.d.ts` file actually matches the `.js` file and you are solely responsible for paying careful attention to avoid writing unsound declarations.)

**Joydeep Bhattacharjee** · 2024-01-20 09:18 UTC

Thanks for the clarification ! Yah actually I'm little unfamiliar with typescript in general but I'm working on it. Can you please tell me what should be the right approach one should follow here to create stubs for the file `web/third/marked/lib/marked.js` file?

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2024-01-20 09:21 UTC

I just told you.

**Joydeep Bhattacharjee** · 2024-01-20 09:59 UTC

ok I got it, I just missed the second part you wrote sorry for that....so I should be at the same folder with marked.js file. It solves the problem of importing it in the markdown.ts file...thanks...

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2024-02-11 02:06 UTC

I don’t want to discourage you from experimenting and learning about Zulip, but I’m skeptical that Web Components are the right direction for us. The main selling point of Web Components is that it provides an abstraction that enables runtime interoperability between components written in multiple frameworks. But for Zulip, I’m much more interested in using a single framework like [SolidJS](https://www.solidjs.com/) or [Svelte](https://svelte.dev/) that’s able to do much more optimization at build time, and provide both components and fine-grained reactivity with very low overhead.

I’m willing to be convinced by good arguments for other approaches, of course. And in later stages, an important piece of those arguments will consist of prototyping increasingly large representative pieces of the app with various approaches. However, given the amount of work involved, I want to make sure you aren’t misled: we’re unlikely to accept contributions that make major architectural decisions that haven’t been thoroughly discussed.

Our [contributing guide](https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/contributing/contributing.html) explains how to find good projects for new contributors, as well as how to get started with the development environment. Our development environment is significantly different from production deployments, to a much greater degree than what you might be used to from other projects, and you probably won’t be able to contribute effectively without using it.

**kla** · 2024-02-11 19:20 UTC

Hi, Here's what my research today showed:

It's a spectrum rather than binary fine/coarse granularity I'd say
- IIRC solid for instance only ever calls a component's function once for initial render, after that updates are handled by its reactivity primitives. That would be the far end of the fine grained spectrum

- Compared to react at the other end of the spectrum which (in worst case) has the approach of re-render the entire world whenever anything changes

-You possibly need some observable/signal primitive or a compiler (a la svelte) to get the absolute finest granularity

- DOM changes are fine-grained, but the element update cycle runs by default based on any reactive property changing.

When a reactive property changes, the element's reactive update cycle runs. This calls render to update the rendered DOM via Lit's template processing  and then calls any implemented updated method on the element. To update the DOM, Lit dirty checks values in the result returned from render and updates those are that different. It does this with great care to minimize actual DOM changes.

You can use @lit-labs/preact-signals and its special html method to get true fine-grained reactivity in response to changes in Signal values.

**kla** · 2024-02-11 19:24 UTC

which means you don't need to monitor properties at component level state.

**kla** · 2024-02-11 19:25 UTC

and overall I would say this worked really well in an array of use cases done in some other apps

**kla** · 2024-02-11 19:47 UTC

I think of  it split into two steps. The first is knowing that something has changed (and what) and the second how to react to that change. Lit's way of keeping track of when something has changed is coarse in the sense that it has a reactivity lifecycle per component that will run the same way regardless of one or ten properties change. These changes are batched and handled together. The reactivity life cycle includes a step called `render`. This step will always run. However the result of running this will not re-render. It keeps track of what to change by a concept called Parts. You can think of these as precise pointers to parts of the DOM. After the initial render it will calculate a value and compare it to the previously committed value and only update the DOM corresponding to each Part.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2024-02-11 20:27 UTC

Right. So in exchange for that performance loss, relative to a fine-grained reactive framework, my question is: what do you gain?

- The runtime interoperability of Web Components is cool but I don’t think we have a use case for it (and if we ever do, we can build and consume Web Components in any framework).
- The ability to run without a bundler is great for toy projects, but it’s of no interest to a project of our size, which realistically needs a bundler in any case.
- Shadow DOM encapsulation has some real advantages for CSS maintainability. It’s not the only solution to that problem though.

There’s no framework named “Quick”. You brought it up, not me—perhaps you mean [Qwik](https://qwik.dev/)? ```python
def get_extra_data_from_widget_type(content: str, widget_type: Optional[str]) -> Any:
    if widget_type == "poll":
        # This is used to extract the question from the poll command.
        # The command '/poll question' will pre-set the question in the poll
        lines = content.splitlines()
        question = ""
        options = []
        if lines and lines[0]:
            question = lines.pop(0).strip()
        for line in lines:
            # If someone is using the list syntax, we remove it
            # before adding an option.
            option = re.sub(r"(\s*[-*]?\s*)", "", line.strip(), count=1)
            if len(option) > 0:
                options.append(option)
        extra_data = {
            "question": question,
            "options": options,
        }
        return extra_data
    return None
```
So from this piece of code I can see that the `options` in `extra_data` is `string array` in widget.py. So I thought this extra data is somehow flowing to poll_widget.ts.

(replying to Tim Abbott)
> You likely need to use use `stopPropagation` to avoid the click handler for the area behind the icon also being processed.

I think problem was here,  clicking `zulip-follow-icon` was having same effect as of clicking on topic list item as `topic-markers-and-controls` was also in the classes that triggers the topic_click.
```
export function initialize({
    on_topic_click,
}: {
    on_topic_click: (stream_id: number, topic?: string) => void;
}): void {
    $("#stream_filters").on("click", ".sidebar-topic-check, .topic-name, **.topic-markers-and-controls**", (e) => {
        if (e.metaKey || e.ctrlKey) {
            return;
        }
        if ($(e.target).closest(".show-more-topics").length > 0) {
            return;
        }

        const $stream_row = $(e.target).parents(".narrow-filter");
        const stream_id_string = $stream_row.attr("data-stream-id");
        assert(stream_id_string !== undefined);
        const stream_id = Number.parseInt(stream_id_string, 10);
        const topic = $(e.target).parents("li").attr("data-topic-name");
        on_topic_click(stream_id, topic);

        e.preventDefault();
    });

    $("body").on("input", "#filter-topic-input", (): void => {
        const stream_id = active_stream_id();
        assert(stream_id !== undefined);
        active_widgets.get(stream_id)?.build();
    });
}
```

Downgrade first, optionally passing `--fake` to skip the reverse migration if necessary:

**Notification Bot** · 2024-02-28 23:14 UTC

This topic was moved here from #**issues>valid file doubt on github** by @Greg Price.

**Alex Vandiver** · 2024-02-29 00:54 UTC

If you look to the right of the word "Blame", you see the words "Symbolic Link".  Which means this file, if checked out on a filesystem, is a file which points to the main `CONTRIBUTING.md` file:
```
$ ls -l docs/contributing/contributing.md
lrwxrwxrwx 21 zulipdev 31 Jan 02:29 docs/contributing/contributing.md -> ../../CONTRIBUTING.md
```

And if you edit it, means you actually edit the main `CONTRIBUTING.md` file:
```
$ head docs/contributing/contributing.md
# Contributing guide

Welcome to the Zulip community!

## Zulip development community

The primary communication forum for the Zulip community is the Zulip
server hosted at [chat.zulip.org](https://chat.zulip.org/):

- **Users** and **administrators** of Zulip organizations stop by to
```
```
head CONTRIBUTING.md
# Contributing guide

Welcome to the Zulip community!

## Zulip development community

The primary communication forum for the Zulip community is the Zulip
server hosted at [chat.zulip.org](https://chat.zulip.org/):

- **Users** and **administrators** of Zulip organizations stop by to
```

**Alex Vandiver** · 2024-02-29 00:55 UTC

It's mostly that GitHub's UI doesn't show this well.

**Bedo Khaled** · 2024-02-29 01:36 UTC

Thanks for the clarification! my only left doubt is why we need a file to point to another file ?

**Greg Price** · 2024-02-29 01:42 UTC

It's because there are two places we want that file to be:
* CONTRIBUTING.md in the root of the repo is a GitHub convention that causes GitHub to show it to people sending PRs and so on
* the `docs/` subdirectory is what builds our developer documentation as a whole, as published at zulip.readthedocs.io, and `docs/contributing/contributing.md` places it there and within the `docs/contributing/` subdirectory we want it to live in as part of the organization of those docs.

**Greg Price** · 2024-02-29 01:44 UTC

Fortunately we can have it physically be in just one of those places and have the other place point to it with a symbolic link, and readthedocs is smart enough that it can follow the link.

**Bedo Khaled** · 2024-02-29 01:51 UTC

(replying to Greg Price)
> Fortunately we can have it physically be in just one of those places and have the other place point to it with a symbolic link, and readthedocs is smart enough that it can follow the link
