**Jayant Pranjal** · 2024-03-01 20:52 UTC

```
import _ from "lodash";

import type {Message} from "./message_store";
import * as people from "./people";

// For simplicity, we use a list for our internal
// data, since that matches what the server sends us.
type AlertWords = {
    word: string,
    follow_topic: boolean,
};
let my_alert_words: AlertWords[] = [];

export function set_words(words: AlertWords[]): void {
    my_alert_words = words;
}

export function get_word_list(): {word: AlertWords}[] {
    // Returns a array of objects
    // (with each alert_word as value and 'word' as key to the object.)
    const words = [];
    for (const word of my_alert_words) {
        words.push({word});
    }
    return words;
}

export function has_alert_word(word: string): boolean {

    for (const alert_word of my_alert_words) {
        if (alert_word.word === word) {
            return true;
        }
    }
    return false;

    // return my_alert_words.includes(word);
}

const alert_regex_replacements = new Map<string, string>([
    ["&", "&amp;"],
    ["<", "&lt;"],
    [">", "&gt;"],
    // Accept quotes with or without HTML escaping
    ['"', '(?:"|&quot;)'],
    ["'", "(?:'|&#39;)"],
]);

export function process_message(message: Message): void {
    // Parsing for alert words is expensive, so we rely on the host
    // to tell us there any alert words to even look for.
    if (!message.alerted) {
        return;
    }

    for (const word of my_alert_words) {
        const clean = _.escapeRegExp(word.word).replaceAll(
            /["&'<>]/g,
            (c) => alert_regex_replacements.get(c)!,
        );
        const before_punctuation = "\\s|^|>|[\\(\\\".,';\\[]";
        const after_punctuation = "(?=\\s)|$|<|[\\)\\\"\\?!:.,';\\]!]";

        const regex = new RegExp(`(${before_punctuation})(${clean})(${after_punctuation})`, "ig");
        message.content = message.content.replace(
            regex,
            (
                match: string,
                before: string,
                word: string,
                after: string,
                offset: number,
                content: string,
            ) => {
                // Logic for ensuring that we don't muck up rendered HTML.
                const pre_match = content.slice(0, offset);
                // We want to find the position of the `<` and `>` only in the
                // match and the string before it. So, don't include the last
                // character of match in `check_string`. This covers the corner
                // case when there is an alert word just before `<` or `>`.
                const check_string = pre_match + match.slice(0, -1);
                const in_tag = check_string.lastIndexOf("<") > check_string.lastIndexOf(">");
                // Matched word is inside an HTML tag so don't perform any highlighting.
                if (in_tag) {
                    return before + word + after;
                }
                return before + "<span class='alert-word'>" + word + "</span>" + after;
            },
        );
    }
}

export function get_alert_words_array(): string[] {
    return my_alert_words.map((word) => word.word);
}

export function notifies(message: Message): boolean {
    // We exclude ourselves from notifications when we type one of our own
    // alert words into a message, just because that can be annoying for
    // certain types of workflows where everybody on your team, including
    // yourself, sets up an alert word to effectively mention the team.
    return !people.is_current_user(message.sender_email) && message.alerted;
}

export const initialize = (params: {alert_words: AlertWords[]}): void => {
    my_alert_words = params.alert_words;
};

    }

    words.sort();
    const $word_list = $("#alert-words-table");

function update_alert_word_status(status_text: string, is_error: boolean): void {
    const $alert_word_status = $("#alert_word_status");
    if (is_error) {
        $alert_word_status.removeClass("alert-success").addClass("alert-danger");
    } else {
        $alert_word_status.removeClass("alert-danger").addClass("alert-success");
    }
    $alert_word_status.find(".alert_word_status_text").text(status_text);
    $alert_word_status.show();
}

function add_alert_word(): void {
    const alert_word = $<HTMLInputElement>("input#add-alert-word-name").val()!.trim();

    if (alert_words.has_alert_word(alert_word)) {
        ui_report.client_error(
            $t({defaultMessage: "Alert word already exists!"}),
            $("#dialog_error"),
        );
        dialog_widget.hide_dialog_spinner();
        return;
    }

    const words_to_be_added = [alert_word];

    const data = {alert_words: JSON.stringify(words_to_be_added)};
    dialog_widget.submit_api_request(channel.post, "/json/users/me/alert_words", data);
}

function remove_alert_word(alert_word: string): void {
    const words_to_be_removed = [alert_word];
    void channel.del({
        url: "/json/users/me/alert_words",
        data: {alert_words: JSON.stringify(words_to_be_removed)},
        success() {
            update_alert_word_status(
                $t(
                    {defaultMessage: `Alert word "{alert_word}" removed successfully!`},
                    {alert_word},
                ),
                false,
            );
        },
        error() {
            update_alert_word_status($t({defaultMessage: "Error removing alert word!"}), true);
        },
    });
}

function toggle_follow_alert_word_topic(alert_word: string): void {
    // If the word is not already being followed, add it to the list.
    // If the word is already being followed, remove it from the list.

    void channel.patch({
        url: "/json/users/me/alert_words",
        data: {alert_word},
        success() {
            update_alert_word_status(
                $t(
                    {defaultMessage: `Alert word "{alert_word}" toggled successfully!`},
                    {alert_word},
                ),
                false,
            );
        },
        error() {
            update_alert_word_status($t({defaultMessage: "Error toggling alert word!"}), true);
        },
    });
}

export function show_add_alert_word_modal(): void {
    const html_body = render_add_alert_word();

    function add_alert_word_post_render(): void {
        const $add_user_group_input_element = $<HTMLInputElement>("input#add-alert-word-name");
        const $add_user_group_submit_button = $("#add-alert-word .dialog_submit_button");
        $add_user_group_submit_button.prop("disabled", true);

        $add_user_group_input_element.on("input", () => {
            $add_user_group_submit_button.prop(

            );
        });
    }

    dialog_widget.launch({
        html_heading: $t_html({defaultMessage: "Add a new alert word"}),
        html_body,
        html_submit_button: $t_html({defaultMessage: "Add"}),
        help_link: "/help/dm-mention-alert-notifications#alert-words",
        form_id: "add-alert-word-form",
        id: "add-alert-word",
        loading_spinner: true,
        on_click: add_alert_word,
        on_shown: () => $("#add-alert-word-name").trigger("focus"),
        post_render: add_alert_word_post_render,
    });
}

export function  (): void {

## Download attachments using buttons in upload files section

*2024-03-11 to 2024-03-12 · 12 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/Download.20attachments.20using.20buttons.20in.20upload.20files.20section/with/1755968)*

**Shashank Singh** · 2024-03-11 18:11 UTC

Presently, we use links or href attribute of "anchor" tag to download attachments in uploaded files section. 
But it would be better to convert the links to buttons to maintain consistency in "settings section".
It is a great idea and came into existence while working on #28653 .
I gave it a try but got a little confused at a point. Clicking on the "anchor" tag link downloads the attachment but when changed to "button" attribute ( and writing a new javascript for handling click event ), clicking on the link opens a new page. 

@Sayam Samal would love to hear your feedback on this.

**Karl Stolley** · 2024-03-11 18:13 UTC

Looks like the switch to a button isn't actually yet part of that PR? It would be helpful to see the logic you've tried to write.

**Shashank Singh** · 2024-03-11 18:20 UTC

Ohh currently I am just redirecting the user to the url where the href attribute of "anchor" tag did. Should I implement some new logic to copy the same behaviour  of "anchor" tag?

**Karl Stolley** · 2024-03-11 18:35 UTC

Most likely. The `download` attribute that the `<a>` tag can take causes different behavior than a normal `href`attribute ordinarily does: [MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/a#download).

**Karl Stolley** · 2024-03-11 18:35 UTC

It would be worth thinking about what type of "consistency" moving to a `<button>` element would achieve. I would much prefer making use of a native `download` attribute on an `<a>` tag than writing our own custom logic on a `<button>` element that we then have to debug and maintain.

**Shashank Singh** · 2024-03-11 19:11 UTC

Agreed , I think it would be preferable to let the existing behaviour of "anchor" tag be in action without writing additional javascript which could have potential consequences.

One thing which we can do for sure and which is presently inhibited in #28653 is to give the "anchor" tag a look of button but the functionality remains that of an `<a>` tag. But there is a slight issue which was pointed out by @Sayam Samal , that being the additional little line below the icon when using `<a>` with button UI.
[Screenshot-2024-03-12-at-12.38.45AM.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/d5/IngsA-EWT1wDaakfUabD-BLn/Screenshot-2024-03-12-at-12.38.45AM.png)

**Karl Stolley** · 2024-03-11 19:23 UTC

That line should be trivial to remove with CSS. Let me know if you attempt that and would like a look or a hand with it.

**Shashank Singh** · 2024-03-11 19:50 UTC

Ohh right , I guess setting the `text-decoration` property to `none` should suffice.

**Karl Stolley** · 2024-03-11 19:50 UTC

## Potential solutions to issue #29152

*2024-03-21 to 2024-03-22 · 6 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/Potential.20solutions.20to.20issue.20.2329152/with/1762860)*

**Aditya Bajaj** · 2024-03-21 03:50 UTC

I'm working on issue #29152 (related CZO thread [here](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/stream/137-feedback/topic/Disabled.20content.20in.20push.20notifications.20has.20bad.20error.20message/near/1747141)) and wanted to ask for feedback on a couple of nuances about the solution:
1. My current fix (Draft PR #29385): Replacing the long string in favour of "* New Message*"
- Pros: A low complexity solution that's easy to read
- Cons: Not a very clean solution from the user's client
2. Italicising the string to say "*New Message*"
- Pros: A cleaner solution
- Cons: More complex since it would likely require some sort of parser logic on the frontend and adoption of a convention to style notifications (in [`zulip/zulip-mobile/src/notification/`](https://github.com/zulip/zulip-mobile/tree/main/src/notification) ?)

While I prefer the second solution's end result, I wanted to run this by the community/maintainers for thoughts on whether we'd like to prioritise the added complexity for a cleaner user facing solution. Any advice would be greatly appreciated!

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-03-21 20:30 UTC

I'm pretty sure the mobile apps have some limited support for a limited subset HTML in the notification libraries? I don't remember the story there; maybe @Greg Price can remind us?

We're definitely not going to add new mobile app changes for this in the legacy `zulip-mobile` project.

**Greg Price** · 2024-03-21 20:33 UTC

No, the clients don't support any kind of markup in the notification content.

We do have some code on the server, within `zerver.lib.push_notifications`, that interprets some HTML to produce a reasonable approximation of "the plain text of the message". That's probably the logic you're thinking of.

**Greg Price** · 2024-03-21 20:34 UTC

So I think that means we'll be doing a version of the first solution, either with asterisks or whatever else (in plain text) we think makes things clearest.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-03-21 20:37 UTC

OK, so I think the answer is "no asterisks" is the best we can do here.

**Aditya Bajaj** · 2024-03-22 01:54 UTC

Thanks for looking into this @Tim Abbott @Greg Price !

Of all the things that are frustrating about the design of zjquery, this is one of them. But yes, if the code uses `$foo[0]` then you need to stub `$foo[0]`.

**Prakhar Pratyush** · 2024-04-22 03:56 UTC

See `UserProfile` model. It is documented there as:
```py
    # For historical reasons, Zulip has two email fields.  The
    # `delivery_email` field is the user's email address, where all
    # email notifications will be sent, and is used for all
    # authentication use cases.
    #
    # The `email` field is the same as delivery_email in organizations
    # with EMAIL_ADDRESS_VISIBILITY_EVERYONE.  For other
    # organizations, it will be a unique value of the form
    # user1234@example.com.  This field exists for backwards
    # compatibility in Zulip APIs where users are referred to by their
    # email address, not their ID; it should be used in all API use cases.
    #
    # Both fields are unique within a realm (in a case-insensitive
    # fashion). Since Django's unique_together is case sensitive, this
    # is enforced via SQL indexes created by
    # zerver/migrations/0295_case_insensitive_email_indexes.py.
    delivery_email = models.EmailField(blank=False, db_index=True)
    email = models.EmailField(blank=False, db_index=True)
```

## Update the "more topics" topic list component

*2024-04-15 to 2024-04-18 · 4 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/Update.20the.20.22more.20topics.22.20topic.20list.20component/with/1780518)*

**Nada** · 2024-04-15 10:55 UTC

I've been working on enhancing our topic list component in the `topic_list.js` file to integrate Solid.js for reactive rendering, aiming to improve performance and user experience [link to the  issue](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/issues/29666)

Here are the changes I've made so far:

1. Integrated Solid.js signals (`createSignal`, `onCleanup`) for state management and resource cleanup.
2. Refactored the `TopicListWidget` class in `topic_list.js` to utilize Solid.js signals (`this.signal`) for dynamic rendering based on state changes.
3. Implemented conditional rendering using Solid.js syntax to render elements based on the current state (`{this.signal[0]().listInfo && ...}`).
4. Updated the `build` method in `TopicListWidget` to return a Solid.js component for dynamic UI updates.
5. Incorporated a cleanup function (`onCleanup`) in `TopicListWidget` for resource management when the component unmounts or updates.

However, I'm unsure if any additional files need modifications or if there are other considerations to fully resolve the rendering issue and implement Solid.js effectively.

**Nada** · 2024-04-15 10:59 UTC

this is the updated code in 'topic_list.js':
```javascript
import $ from "jquery";
import _ from "lodash";
import { createSignal, onCleanup } from "solid-js";

import render_more_topics from "../templates/more_topics.hbs";
import render_more_topics_spinner from "../templates/more_topics_spinner.hbs";
import render_topic_list_item from "../templates/topic_list_item.hbs";

import * as blueslip from "./blueslip";
import * as popover_menus from "./popover_menus";
import * as scroll_util from "./scroll_util";
import * as stream_topic_history from "./stream_topic_history";
import * as stream_topic_history_util from "./stream_topic_history_util";
import * as topic_list_data from "./topic_list_data";


const active_widgets = new Map();


let zoomed = false;

export function update() {
  for (const widget of active_widgets.values()) {
    widget.build();
  }
}

export function clear() {
  popover_menus.get_topic_menu_popover()?.hide();

  for (const widget of active_widgets.values()) {
    widget.remove();
  }

  active_widgets.clear();
}

export function close() {
  zoomed = false;
  clear();
}

export function zoom_out() {
  zoomed = false;

  const stream_ids = [...active_widgets.keys()];

  if (stream_ids.length !== 1) {
    blueslip.error("Unexpected number of topic lists to zoom out.");
    return;
  }

  const stream_id = stream_ids[0];
  const widget = active_widgets.get(stream_id);
  const parent_widget = widget.get_parent();

  rebuild(parent_widget, stream_id);
}

export function keyed_topic_li(conversation) {
  const render = () => render_topic_list_item(conversation);

  const eq = (other) => _.isEqual(conversation, other.conversation);

  const key = "t:" + conversation.topic_name;

  return {
    key,
    render,
    conversation,
    eq,
  };
}

export function more_li(
  more_topics_unreads,
  more_topics_have_unread_mention_messages,
  more_topics_unread_count_muted
) {
  const render = () =>
    render_more_topics({
      more_topics_unreads,
      more_topics_have_unread_mention_messages,
      more_topics_unread_count_muted,
    });

  const eq = (other) =>
    other.more_items && more_topics_unreads === other.more_topics_unreads;

  const key = "more";

  return {
    key,
    more_items: true,
    more_topics_unreads,
    render,
    eq,
  };
}

export function spinner_li() {
  const render = () => render_more_topics_spinner();

  const eq = (other) => other.spinner;

  const key = "more";

  return {
    key,
    spinner: true,
    render,
    eq,
  };
}

export class TopicListWidget {
  prior_dom = undefined;

  constructor($parent_elem, my_stream_id) {
    this.$parent_elem = $parent_elem;
    this.my_stream_id = my_stream_id;
    this.signal = createSignal({ listInfo: null, spinner: false });
  }

  async build_list(spinner) {
    const listInfo = await topic_list_data.get_list_info(
      this.my_stream_id,
      zoomed,
      get_topic_search_term()
    );

    const numPossibleTopics = listInfo.num_possible_topics;
    const moreTopicsUnreads = listInfo.more_topics_unreads;
    const moreTopicsHaveUnreadMentionMessages =
      listInfo.more_topics_have_unread_mention_messages;

    const isShowingAllPossibleTopics =
      listInfo.items.length === numPossibleTopics &&
      stream_topic_history.is_complete_for_stream_id(this.my_stream_id);

    const nodes = listInfo.items.map((conversation) =>
      keyed_topic_li(conversation)
    );

    if (spinner) {
      nodes.push(spinner_li());
    } else if (!isShowingAllPossibleTopics) {
      nodes.push(
        more_li(
          moreTopicsUnreads,
          moreTopicsHaveUnreadMentionMessages,
          listInfo.more_topics_unread_count_muted
        )
      );
    }

    this.signal[0]({ listInfo, spinner });
  }

  get_parent() {
    return this.$parent_elem;
  }

  remove() {
    this.$parent_elem.find(".topic-list").remove();
    this.prior_dom = undefined;
  }

  build(spinner) {
    this.signal[0]({ spinner });

    const replaceContent = (html) => {
      this.remove();
      this.$parent_elem.append(html);
    };

    const find = () => this.$parent_elem.find(".topic-list");

    onCleanup(() => {
      
    });

    return () => (
      <div>
        {this.signal[0]().listInfo &&
          vdom.ul({
            attrs: [["class", "topic-list"]],
            keyed_nodes: nodes,
          })}
        {this.signal[0]().spinner && spinner_li().render()}
      </div>
    );
  }
}

export function clear_topic_search(e) {
  e.stopPropagation();
  const $input = $("#filter-topic-input");
  if ($input.length) {
    $input.val("");
    $input.trigger("blur");

    
    const streamIds = [...active_widgets.keys()];

    const streamId = streamIds[0];
    const widget = active_widgets.get(streamId);
    const parentWidget = widget.get_parent();

    rebuild(parentWidget, streamId);
  }
}

export function active_stream_id() {
  const streamIds = [...active_widgets.keys()];

  if (streamIds.length !== 1) {
    return undefined;
  }

  return streamIds[0];
}

export function get_stream_li() {
  const widgets = [...active_widgets.values()];

  if (widgets.length !== 1) {
    return undefined;
  }

  const $stream_li = widgets[0].get_parent();
  return $stream_li;
}

export function rebuild($stream_li, streamId) {
  const activeWidget = active_widgets.get(streamId);

  if (activeWidget) {
    activeWidget.build();
    return;
  }

  clear();
  const widget = new TopicListWidget($stream_li, streamId);
  widget.build();

  active_widgets.set(streamId, widget);
}

export function zoom_in() {
  zoomed = true;

  const streamId = active_stream_id();
  if (!streamId) {
    blueslip.error("Cannot find widget for topic history zooming.");
    return;
  }

  const activeWidget = active_widgets.get(streamId);

  function onSuccess() {
    if (!active_widgets.has(streamId)) {
      blueslip.warn("User re-narrowed before topic history was returned.");
      return;
    }

    if (!zoomed) {
      blueslip.warn("User zoomed out before topic history was returned.");
      return;
    }

    activeWidget.build();
  }

  scroll_util.get_scroll_element($("#left_sidebar_scroll_container")).scrollTop(
    0
  );

  const spinner = true;
  activeWidget.build(spinner);

  stream_topic_history_util.get_server_history(streamId, onSuccess);
}

export function get_topic_search_term() {
  const $filter = $("#filter-topic-input");
  if ($filter.val() === undefined) {
    return "";
  }
  return $filter.val().trim();
}

export function initialize({ on_topic_click }) {
  $("#stream_filters").on(
    "click",
    ".sidebar-topic-check, .topic-name, .topic-markers-and-controls",
    (e) => {
      if (e.metaKey || e.ctrlKey) {
        return;
      }
      if ($(e.target).closest(".show-more-topics").length > 0) {
        return;
      }

      const $stream_row = $(e.target).parents(".narrow-filter");
      const streamId = Number.parseInt($stream_row.attr("data-stream-id"), 10);
      const topic = $(e.target).parents("li").attr("data-topic-name");
      on_topic_click(streamId, topic);

      e.preventDefault();
    }
  );

  $("body").on("input", "#filter-topic-input", () => {
    active_widgets.get(active_stream_id()).build();
  });
```

## Approach for name change permissions

*2024-05-15 to 2024-05-16 · 6 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/Approach.20for.20name.20change.20permissions/with/1800226)*

**Aditya Kasaudhan** · 2024-05-15 08:55 UTC

To address issue [#30077](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/issues/30077), I've thoroughly reviewed the codebase and proposed a solution. I'll write a migration to convert the 'Prevent users from changing their name' boolean field into a 'who can change' short integer. We'll provide 5 options for this field, such as admins, admins and moderators, etc., and store the chosen option accordingly. Subsequently, I'll develop a dedicated function to determine the user's name modification privileges based on these choices. Finally, I'll proceed with implementing the necessary frontend adjustments. This encapsulates my approach to resolving the issue. May I proceed with this plan?

## DM vs PM for newer features

*2024-06-04 to 2024-06-06 · 4 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/DM.20vs.20PM.20for.20newer.20features/with/1815202)*

**Shubham Padia** · 2024-06-04 09:43 UTC

I'm working on Make DMs searchable in the left sidebar #22113. For the code that I am adding, should I use `pm` or `dm`? 

I think `pm` would be better since that's used everywhere in the code and we can have a different name for DMs in the code and the user facing side. While using `dm` right now may help us in incrementally renaming `pm` to `dm`, I think without a proper renaming effort planned, using `dm` would cause more confusion than benefit.

**Lauryn Menard** · 2024-06-04 09:58 UTC

There is a goal to rename "private/pm" to "direct/dm" in the frontend codebase. See #**frontend>private => direct renaming** for the most recent conversation I have flagged for that, which was not followed-up on.

So I think the preference would be to use `dm` or `direct_message` depending on the context/case.

**Shubham Padia** · 2024-06-04 10:03 UTC

hmm, but the question then is would using `dm` make things harder to search if it is used at a few places before a big renaming happens?

Or would it make the future renaming much harder?

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-06-06 19:51 UTC

We should use new names involving `direct`, any other choice is just adding more work to the future sweep.

We generally try to avoid abbreviations/acronyms as a whole in the project's implementation, since it's a habit that as a whole leads to things being harder to read. So use `direct_message` unless you think there's a good reason to do something otherwise. (An example would be something in user-facing UI, like the `dm:` search operator)

## ✔ zjquery wont allow `one` and `on` handlers for same event

*2024-06-14 to 2024-06-15 · 4 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/.E2.9C.94.20zjquery.20wont.20allow.20.60one.60.20and.20.60on.60.20handlers.20for.20same.20event/with/1826236)*

**Nehal Sharma** · 2024-06-14 21:39 UTC

In #30396 I added an event handler using `on` for the same event as of a pre-existing `one` handler:
```javascript
        $("textarea#compose-textarea")
            .off("autosize:resized")
            .one("autosize:resized", () => {
                maybe_scroll_up_selected_message(autosize_callback_opts);
            })
            .on("autosize:resized", (e) => {
                const height = e.currentTarget.style.height;
                const max_height = e.currentTarget.style.maxHeight;
                if (height >= max_height) {
                    $("#compose").addClass("automatically-expanded");
                } else {
                    $("#compose").removeClass("automatically-expanded");
                }
            });
```
 This should be just fine, but zjquery throws an error saying:
```
Error: dup autosize:resized handler for textarea#compose-textarea
```

It also acknowledges:
```
Either the app or the test can be at fault here..
(sometimes you just want to call $.clear_all_elements();)
```

This error seems to be due to zjquery's inability to treat `on` and `one` events separately. I'd really appreciate some help on how to fix it!

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-06-15 05:06 UTC

`zjquery` is hacky and one direction is to extend it to either allow multiple handlers, unconditionally or under some option. Alternatively, you could probably use a state variable and not need to do `.one` at all.

## name_changes_disabled use in registration

*2024-06-24 to 2024-06-26 · 8 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/name_changes_disabled.20use.20in.20registration/with/1836408)*

**Kunal Sharma** · 2024-06-24 14:09 UTC

I am working on #30077. So I need to update the `name_changes_disabled` function accordingly. I have a question related to that - what does the `if` block do in the following code in `zerver/views/registration.py`:
```py
postdata = request.POST.copy()
if name_changes_disabled(realm):
    # If we populate profile information via LDAP and we have a
    # verified name from you on file, use that. Otherwise, fall
    # back to the full name in the request.
    try:
        postdata.update(full_name=request.session["authenticated_full_name"])
        name_validated = True
    except KeyError:
        pass
form = RegistrationForm(postdata, realm_creation=realm_creation, realm=realm)
```

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-06-25 18:26 UTC

Let me answer with the technique I'd use to find this out:

```
$ git grep authenticated_full_name
zerver/tests/test_signup.py:            # Click confirmation link. This will 'authenticated_full_name'
zerver/views/registration.py:            del request.session["authenticated_full_name"]
zerver/views/registration.py:            request.session["authenticated_full_name"] = ldap_full_name
zerver/views/registration.py:                request.session["authenticated_full_name"] = prereg_user.full_name
zerver/views/registration.py:                postdata.update(full_name=request.session["authenticated_full_name"])
zerver/views/registration.py:        "full_name": request.session.get("authenticated_full_name", None),
```

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-06-25 18:27 UTC

From that, one can find how `authenticated_full_name` is set:
```
        if ldap_full_name:                                                                              
            # We don't add "full_name" to initial here, because if the realm                            
            # already exists and form is complete (that is, no additional fields                        
            # need to be filled out by the user) we want the form to validate,                          
            # so they can be directly registered without having to go through                           
            # this interstitial.                                                                        
            form = RegistrationForm(                                                                    
                {"full_name": ldap_full_name},                                                          
                initial=initial_data,                                                                   
                realm_creation=realm_creation,                                                          
                realm=realm,                                                                            
            )                                                                                           
            request.session["authenticated_full_name"] = ldap_full_name                                 
            name_validated = True                                                                       
```

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-06-25 18:28 UTC

And `ldap_full_name` is set in a block that starts with this comment:
```
        ldap_full_name = None                                                                           
        if settings.POPULATE_PROFILE_VIA_LDAP:                                                          
            # If the user can be found in LDAP, we'll take the full name from the directory,            
            # and further down create a form pre-filled with it.                                        
```

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-06-25 18:32 UTC

So the answer is that for organizations using LDAP as the source of truth for users' names, that block of code is designed to prefer the LDAP name if available, and I think present it as already decided (not an editable input).

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-06-25 18:33 UTC

A few other techniques that may help understand something like this:
- You can try deleting the code and seeing what tests fail if you do so -- that will often be revealing.
- https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/stable/development/authentication.html#testing-ldap-in-development explains how to test LDAP in the development environment, so you could see how the UI looks end-to-end with and without that code.

**Kunal Sharma** · 2024-06-26 02:59 UTC

Thanks @Tim Abbott for such a detailed explanation.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-06-26 20:20 UTC

Yeah I like to live-blog this sort of investigating from time-to-time, since I feel like it can help others get a feel for what techniques I use to answer questions like this -- I don't have it all memorized.

```
    # These last several parameters are only used by functions
    # wrapping get_chart_data; the callers are responsible for

    realm: Optional[Realm] = None,

These parameters should not be parsed from the request.

**Zixuan James Li** · 2024-07-01 23:44 UTC

`argument_type_is_body` is usually used for [webhooks](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/df68d3cff64c9b72807f6f11904609870ffe0c5b/zerver/webhooks/intercom/view.py#L328-L334) via [`JsonBodyPayload`](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/df68d3cff64c9b72807f6f11904609870ffe0c5b/zerver/lib/typed_endpoint.py#L100-L102), where there is a special parameter called "body" that comes from the request body. It does not seem to be the best alternative for this.

**Zixuan James Li** · 2024-07-01 23:48 UTC

We want the default value as a placeholder (like we did for `has_request_variables` endpoints, where `REQ` objects are the defaults that are processed by the decorator), so that when calling `get_chart_data` that default value is not actually used.

**Zixuan James Li** · 2024-07-01 23:51 UTC

(replying to Bedo Khaled)
> Also [here](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/5ac6d671fcf4ee90ebeeeef0708950fab5483703/analytics/views/stats.py#L233) and [here](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/5ac6d671fcf4ee90ebeeeef0708950fab5483703/analytics/views/stats.py#L218) `chart_name` is not passed to `get_chart_data` although it's …

I think those are intentional. The value of `chart_name` comes from `request`. `has_request_variables` make sure that the decorated function would extract the value for the caller.

**Bedo Khaled** · 2024-07-02 00:09 UTC

So long story short, we should set a default value for `chart_name` to silence the linter but at the same time this default value shouldn't be used because `chart_name` is required to have only specific values.

Am i understanding correctly ?

(replying to Zixuan James Li)
> make sure that the decorated function would extract the value for the caller

How to ?

**Zixuan James Li** · 2024-07-03 17:58 UTC

Maybe we can also use the `chart_name` from the wrapper function and pass that to `get_chart_data`.

```py
@require_server_admin_api
@has_request_variables
def get_chart_data_for_installation(
    request: HttpRequest, /, user_profile: UserProfile, chart_name: str = REQ(), **kwargs: Any
) -> HttpResponse:
    return get_chart_data(request, user_profile, char_name=chart_name, for_installation=True, **kwargs)
```

**Zixuan James Li** · 2024-07-03 17:58 UTC

In case the wrappers are migrated to use `typed_endpoint`, this same approach should still work.

Is there a reason for using [check_int_in](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/main/zerver/lib/typed_endpoint_validators.py#L24) over something like `Literal[VALID_INT_VALUES]` ?

``` python
VALID_INT_VALUES = [1,2,3]

export function initialize_topic_edit_typeahead(
    form_field: JQuery<HTMLInputElement>,
    stream_name: string,
    dropup: boolean,
): Typeahead<string> {
    const bootstrap_typeahead_input: TypeaheadInputElement = {
        $element: form_field,
        type: "input",
    };
    return new Typeahead(bootstrap_typeahead_input, {
        dropup,
        highlighter_html(item: string): string {
            return typeahead_helper.render_typeahead_item({primary: item});
        },
        sorter(items: string[], query: string): string[] {
            const sorted = typeahead_helper.sorter(query, items, (x) => x);
            if (sorted.length > 0 && !sorted.includes(query)) {
                sorted.unshift(query);
            }
            return sorted;
        },
        source(): string[] {
            const stream_id = stream_data.get_stream_id(stream_name);
            return topics_seen_for(stream_id);
        },
        items: 5,
    });
}
```

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-07-11 17:18 UTC

That looks like the right code to be looking at.  I believe the algorithm is pretty simple:
- Fetch the set of topics we know about in the stream. 
- Always offer what they typed (this is the `sorted.unshift` code in `sorter`), for the "creating a new topic" case.
- The `matcher` parameter isn't passed, so we're using this very simple default code to determine which match:
```
    defaultMatcher(item: ItemType, query: string): boolean {                                            
        assert(typeof item === "string");                                                               
        return item.toLowerCase().includes(query.toLowerCase());                                        
    }                                                                                                   
```
- See `stream_topic_history_util.ts` and `stream_topic_history` for where we get the set of topics. The short story is that we will initially display what we have locally from having fetched a bunch of recent message history, and in parallel ask the server via `get_server_history` (a function also used for "show all topics" in the left sidebar) for the complete set of topics in the channel, which will be used for future keystrokes.

**Neil Pilgrim (neiljp)** · 2024-07-30 18:32 UTC

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-07-30 19:35 UTC

You can see the Pydantic parser definitions for these. It's indeed not allowed to be a mix.
```
@typed_endpoint                                                                                         
def remove_subscriptions_backend(                                                                       
    request: HttpRequest,                                                                               
    user_profile: UserProfile,                                                                          
    *,                                                                                                  
    streams_raw: Annotated[Json[list[str]], ApiParamConfig("subscriptions")],                           
    principals: Json[list[str] | list[int]] | None = None,                                              
) -> HttpResponse:                                                                                      
```

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-07-30 19:36 UTC

(replying to Bedo Khaled)
> like that's the whole idea of data validation, right?

Yes, exactly, Pydantic validates these as a core part of how `typed_endpoint` works.

## access request which saves current session

*2024-08-03 to 2024-08-16 · 8 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/access.20request.20which.20saves.20current.20session/with/1912035)*

**Bedo Khaled** · 2024-08-03 08:41 UTC

Within the `SessionStore`, what is the right way of accessing the request which saved that session?

My approach was to override django's `SessionMiddleware.process_response()` 

Here is the function for reference : 

```python3
def process_response(self, request, response):
    """
    If request.session was modified, or if the configuration is to save the
    session every time, save the changes and set a session cookie or delete
    the session cookie if the session has been emptied.
    """
    try:
        accessed = request.session.accessed
        modified = request.session.modified
        empty = request.session.is_empty()
    except AttributeError:
        return response
    # First check if we need to delete this cookie.
    # The session should be deleted only if the session is entirely empty.
    if settings.SESSION_COOKIE_NAME in request.COOKIES and empty:
        response.delete_cookie(
            settings.SESSION_COOKIE_NAME,
            path=settings.SESSION_COOKIE_PATH,
            domain=settings.SESSION_COOKIE_DOMAIN,
            samesite=settings.SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE,
        )
        patch_vary_headers(response, ("Cookie",))
    else:
        if accessed:
            patch_vary_headers(response, ("Cookie",))
        if (modified or settings.SESSION_SAVE_EVERY_REQUEST) and not empty:
            if request.session.get_expire_at_browser_close():
                max_age = None
                expires = None
            else:
                max_age = request.session.get_expiry_age()
                expires_time = time.time() + max_age
                expires = http_date(expires_time)
            # Save the session data and refresh the client cookie.
            # Skip session save for 5xx responses.
            if response.status_code < 500:
                try:
                    request.session.save()
                except UpdateError:
                    raise SessionInterrupted(
                        "The request's session was deleted before the "
                        "request completed. The user may have logged "
                        "out in a concurrent request, for example."
                    )
                response.set_cookie(
                    settings.SESSION_COOKIE_NAME,
                    request.session.session_key,
                    max_age=max_age,
                    expires=expires,
                    domain=settings.SESSION_COOKIE_DOMAIN,
                    path=settings.SESSION_COOKIE_PATH,
                    secure=settings.SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE or None,
                    httponly=settings.SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY or None,
                    samesite=settings.SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE,
                )
    return response
``` 

Then I would modify the following line :
from 
```python3
request.session.save()
``` 
to 
```python3
request.session.save(request=request)
``` 
so now the sessions' `save()` method has access to the request, but I don't like this approach, It would require overrwriting a function of `60` lines just to modify a single line,  also I don't think`super()` would seem to be useful here

**Bedo Khaled** · 2024-08-03 08:41 UTC

Is there a cleaner way to do this ?

**Bedo Khaled** · 2024-08-15 12:53 UTC

any suggestion ?🤔

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-08-15 23:40 UTC

I'm not sure I understand the problem statement.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-08-15 23:40 UTC

The original `HttpRequest` that created a session is a Python object that may have been in another process or been garbage-collected.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-08-15 23:41 UTC

If you want the current request, generally that should be passed in to code that needs it from the caller.

**Bedo Khaled** · 2024-08-16 08:14 UTC

(replying to Tim Abbott)

From within the [save method](https://github.com/abdelrahman725/zulip/blob/session-indexing/zerver/models/sessions.py#L65) I just want to access the request which saves it

**Arturo** · 2024-08-23 19:20 UTC

Ok, after debugging patiently, I've found that yes, the bot is making again and again the call to the endpoint, making the files be sent several times until the bot fails. I have changed my endpoint to use a cache in order to manage the messages, and if the message is already in process, returns that information to the bot in order to make it stop

I share the code with the solution that worked for me. I cut the parts that are from my system and I only let the cache and message management

```php
header('Content-Type: application/json');

$cacheDir = __DIR__ . '/cache';
if (!is_dir($cacheDir)) {
    mkdir($cacheDir, 0755, true);
}

function processZulipMessage($data) {
    global $cacheDir;

    // Generar un identificador único para este mensaje
    $messageId = $data['message']['id'] ?? uniqid();
    $cacheFile = $cacheDir . '/zulip_message_' . md5($messageId);

    // Verificar si el mensaje ya ha sido procesado
    if (file_exists($cacheFile) && (time() - filemtime($cacheFile) < 300)) {
        return ['success' => true, 'message' => 'Mensaje ya procesado anteriormente'];
    }

    // Marcar el mensaje como procesado
    touch($cacheFile);

    // Enviar el mensaje de Zulip a Telegram
    $contenidoZulip = $data['message']['content'];
    return enviarMensajeZulipATelegram($telegram, $contenidoZulip, $data['message']['stream_id']);
}

// Función para limpiar archivos de caché antiguos
function limpiarCacheAntiguo($cacheDir) {
    $files = glob($cacheDir . '/*');
    foreach ($files as $file) {
        if (is_file($file) && (time() - filemtime($file) > 300)) {
            unlink($file);
        }
    }
}

// Procesar la solicitud
$json = file_get_contents('php://input');
$data = json_decode($json, true);

$response = processZulipMessage($data);
echo json_encode($response);

// Limpiar caché antiguo
limpiarCacheAntiguo($cacheDir);
```

In #31361, it makes the opposite of the following change:

```
$ git diff
diff --git a/zerver/decorator.py b/zerver/decorator.py
index f020243337..1ec012a9bd 100644

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-08-20 17:15 UTC

It'd be good to isolate and report upstream as suggested in the output. @Kenneth R FYI.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2024-08-20 23:00 UTC

While a mypy crash is always a bug whether the code is right or wrong, the code here is wrong. The signature

```python
def internal_api_view(
    is_tornado_view: bool,
) -> Callable[
    [Callable[Concatenate[HttpRequest, ParamT], HttpResponse]],
    Callable[Concatenate[HttpRequest, ParamT], HttpResponse],
]:
```

requires that the `internal_api_view()` decorator outputs a function of the same type as its input. But the output function `_wrapped_func_arguments` is typed to require a `secret: str` argument that the input function `view_func` does not.

**Alex Vandiver** · 2024-09-03 21:16 UTC

I wrote there:

> I am beginning to suspect that we may want to *only use this subclass* if persistent connections are used (`EMAIL_MAX_CONNECTION_LIFETIME_IN_MINUTES != 0`) because it's not necessary in the case where it's `== 0`, and it complicates both the logic, and how easy the code is to reason about.

We *do* need to subclass `open` in the case where we want to have a persistent connection.  We need to put the reconnection logic *somewhere*, and either it ends up in `initialize_connection` or in `zerver.worker.email_senders` -- or in `open`.  The latter is rthe best option because it lets us potentially split the simple case out, by only using the subclass in cases where it's necessary.  Otherwise we end up having the same confusing logic we're working through, just in `initialize_connection` or `zerver.worker.email_senders`.

function process_layout($rendered_html: JQuery): void {

**Alex Vandiver** · 2024-09-18 14:05 UTC

If you're seeing all of the pages flicker through on hover, then that means that we successfully generated the thumbnails.  The fact that the pages are being treated as *frames* in an animation is a separate bug -- we need to exclude TIFFs from being possibly treated as animated, since their "pages" in libvips terminology are *actually* pages, not frames.

But thumbnailing isn't failing here, so that file can't be used as a basis for examining #31007.  The fact that a broken image is what renders in the lightbox is because your browser doesn't know how to show TIFF images inline -- that is, we are sending `<img src="thing.tiff">` which is a valid TIFF file, and the browser is declining to render it ([see also](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Media/Formats/Image_types#tiff_tagged_image_file_format)).  That's also unrelated to #31007 -- the fix would be to produce a high-resolution webp version of the image(s) and show them in the lightbox, so browser support for TIFF wouldn't be relevant.

**Alex Vandiver** · 2024-10-04 14:40 UTC

Nope, I can replicate exactly the bug that #31007 describes.

Steps to replicate:
1. Start django without the thumbnailing worker
2. Upload `multipage_tif_example.tif`, but *edit the message content* before sending, to be `[](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/34/whatever/multipage_tif_example.tif)`
3. Send that message.  It will render as just an empty image block with a spinner in it.
4. Start the thumbnailing worker
5. The spinner image will update to an empty message, which gives users no way to access the uploaded file.

**Alex Vandiver** · 2024-10-04 14:44 UTC

And a quick log message I inserted into the block I linked to shows it as being called, as I explained above

**Alex Vandiver** · 2024-10-04 14:47 UTC

The part of #31007 which was not sufficiently explicit was the key word "later" in:

> ...and points to an image which has a valid image header but later fails to thumbnail

Specifically, this bug only shows up if  the image has not gotten processed by the thumbnailing worker by the time it is sent.  Which is what causes it to be rendered initially as a spinner, and then *later* removed.

**Alex Vandiver** · 2024-10-04 14:48 UTC

And the "which is the *only* part" requires that the image be linked as `[](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/...)` and not the default of `[multipage_tif_example.tif](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/...)`; that is what causes the Markdown renderer to only insert the image tag.

## ✔ dependency cycle error - eslint

*2024-09-26 to 2024-09-26 · 5 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/.E2.9C.94.20dependency.20cycle.20error.20-.20eslint/with/1949306)*

**Kumar Aniket** · 2024-09-26 13:48 UTC

I was working on this issue ([#30890](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/issues/30890)) and the issue was solved locally but before adding a PR when I ran `./tools/lint --fix` the following error occurred:

[image.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/ea/Hm1jzu5VAgfiInQN0ApfNVnZ/image.png)

I have imported `people.ts` in `user_groups.ts` and maybe because of that import cycle error was introduced.
So how do I remove the above error? Should I remove all the code I added in `user_groups.ts`and add it to `people.ts` or is there any other way to solve it? 
Added function in `user_groups.ts` is:
```
export function are_all_members_deactivated(user_group_id: number): boolean {
    const user_group = user_group_by_id_dict.get(user_group_id);
    if (user_group === undefined) {
        blueslip.error("Could not find user group", {user_group_id});
        return true;
    }

    const member_ids = new Set(user_group.members);
    const subgroup_ids = new Set(user_group.direct_subgroup_ids);
    for (const subgroup_id of subgroup_ids) {
        const subgroup = user_group_by_id_dict.get(subgroup_id);
        if (subgroup === undefined) {
            blueslip.error("Could not find subgroup", {subgroup_id});
            return false;
        }
        for (const subgroup_member_id of subgroup.members) {
            member_ids.add(subgroup_member_id);
        }
        for (const direct_subgroup_id of subgroup.direct_subgroup_ids) {
            subgroup_ids.add(direct_subgroup_id);
        }
    }
    for (const member_id of member_ids) {
        if (people.is_person_active(member_id)) {
            return false;
        }
    }
    return true;
}
```
Once this error is removed I will open my PR.

Try running `./tools/test-backend --rerun` when the test fails.

No need to run `test-all` locally. [See docs](https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/testing/testing.html#running-tests):
```md
./tools/test-all

However, you will rarely want to do this while actively developing, because it takes a long time.
Instead, your edit/refresh cycle will typically involve running subsets of the tests with commands like these:

./tools/lint zerver/models/__init__.py # Lint the file you just changed
./tools/test-backend zerver.tests.test_markdown.MarkdownTest.test_inline_youtube
./tools/test-backend MarkdownTest # Run `test-backend --help` for more options
./tools/test-js-with-node util
# etc.
```

**Maneesh Shukla** · 2024-10-24 18:55 UTC

Greetings everyone,

I’m currently working on an issue related to user sign-up and password inputs. I’ve noticed an inconsistency between the development and production environments regarding the password strength alert. Specifically, the **weak password alert** that appears in the production environment is not showing in the dev environment.

I’m  attaching the links to videos demonstrating the behavior in both environments.

[Production env](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/42/nqL02NtMZbRq8PVhqwwlJA_G/Screen-Recording-2024-10-25-at-12.07.25AM.mov)

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-10-25 00:14 UTC

Good question, this is controlled by configuration.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-10-25 00:15 UTC

These settings in `zproject/dev_settings.py` disable enforcement:
```
# Don't require anything about password strength in development                                         
PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH = 0                                                                                 
PASSWORD_MIN_GUESSES = 0                                                                                
```

So usually you'll want to change those temporarily while working on that feature.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-10-25 00:15 UTC

(It's really annoying to have to type a secure password when testing account creation repeatedly in the development environment, so that's why we have those defaults set that way)

2. completing:string variable sets what we are trying to complete in the typeahead menu such as "stream", "topic_jump", etc.
3. select function in web/src/bootstrap_typeahead.ts handles the text replacement  on selecting a particular menu option and triggers the changes

**The problem I am facing**
1. I was able to successfully replace stream selection replacement text from #**streamname**` to `#**streamname> ,  and also remove hinting as mentioned in the issue, however after going through the code in  composebox_typeahead.ts and bootstrap_typeahead.ts, I haven't been able to figure out how to trigger a consecutive typeahead menu after selecting a particular stream.
2. Right now, selecting a stream just places the #**streamname>  in the textarea without triggering any menu for the channels

[32184.webm](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/77/UpnkBztQTzLONKmGhGEzU6BK/32184.webm)

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-10-31 18:12 UTC

You'll probably need to do some print-debugging. But I guess the `topic_jump` logic is what I'd grep for and read to see how we do that for hitting `>` to select a partially typed channel and still have typeahead open afterwards.

**Apoorva Pendse** · 2024-11-02 04:59 UTC

Thanks a lot for this suggestion, was able to make it work after a lot of debugging.

I changed a part of tokenize_compose_str, since it returned "topic_jump" as the current_token in get_candidates() whenever some stream was selected from the typeahead menu. I made it return the token instead, basically slicing it to return #stream_name>sometext

Also had to alter the condition which triggered stream typeahead on finding # at the start, to also check whether the current token ended with ">sometext", if it did, we don't trigger the stream typeahead, but instead trigger the topic list by returning  the topicname items and setting completing="topic_list"

returning "topic_jump" as before caused the topic list to not get triggered since return value of topic_jump meant that the topic was already selected.
This effectively returned an empty array from the get_candidates i.e. the source function in lookup() in the bootstrap_typeahead.ts file,
```javascript
if (!items.length && this.shown) {
            this.hide();
        }
        return items.length ? this.process(items) : this;
```
This part of the code inside lookup() caused the next typeahead to not trigger, since items was an empty arr 
Hope this explanation helps others


Here is the demo:

**Lauryn Menard** · 2024-11-05 16:49 UTC

I'm not sure the best channel for this discussion, but starting it here since it relates to the development environment.

I often work on issues/changes where I'm creating realms from the devlogin page. And I find it distracting/confusing that the realm name and subdomain for these new realms are based on the UserProfile count.

I think my preference would be for:
- New realms to be incremented by the Realm count in the database. So the first time you create a realm it would be `realm-3` vs `realm-24`.
- New users to be incremented by the non-bot UserProfile count. So the first new user would be `user-12` and not `user-24`.

But maybe other folks find the current behavior useful or helpful in a way that I'm not aware of?

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-11-05 18:07 UTC

I suspect that this was just cargo-culting/copy-paste done when new realm feature was built after the new user one, you should feel free to change it to use realm-count.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2024-11-18 19:07 UTC

In #32261 we upgraded Node. The `install-node` script is automatically run by `tools/provision`. You need to let it use the version of Node it wants rather than trying to install it yourself. Sorry, I'm not an insider but someone already asked what the private channel is. Zulip is dedicated for business and other serious usage like communication for teams behind programming languages. As you can imagine they need to stay focused and any kind of distraction is not good here. Because of that you have public and private channels plus streams.

The warning warns you that:
your local file `typing.py` shadows (overrides) the built-in `typing` module.

I don't think that's an issue since since Python resolves the standard library modules first as per [the documentation](https://docs.python.org/3/tutorial/modules.html#the-module-search-path).
Others can correct me on this.

You can suppress that warning in vscode by adding
```json
"python.analysis.diagnosticSeverityOverrides": {
    "reportShadowedImports": "none"
}
```
in your workspace or remote settings(since you seem to be on WSL) by searching for that in your command palette.

@Tim Abbott I guess there is a old method through which i do can that , even for github 
i am sharing a example for that 
```javascript
// Function to handle the 'copy' event
    function handleCopyEvent(event) {
      const plainText = "This is plain text.";
      const htmlText = "<p>This is <strong>HTML</strong> text.</p>";
      const markdownText = "**This is markdown text 23.**";

      // Prevent the default clipboard action
      event.preventDefault();

      // Set multiple MIME types using clipboardData.setData
      event.clipboardData.setData("text/plain", plainText);
      event.clipboardData.setData("text/html", htmlText);
      event.clipboardData.setData("text/x-gfm", markdownText);

      console.log("Data copied to clipboard with multiple MIME types!");
    }

    // Add event listener to the button that triggers the copy event
    document.getElementById("copy-btn").addEventListener("click", function() {
      document.addEventListener("copy", handleCopyEvent); // Add the event listener
      // Trigger a 'copy' event manually
      document.execCommand('copy'); // This will trigger the copy event
      document.removeEventListener("copy", handleCopyEvent); // Remove the event listener
    }); 
```
would it be nice to use this approach ? As:
> The modern Clipboard API offers a more streamlined and powerful way to handle clipboard operations, while the older method using `document.execCommand` is more verbose and less secure but offers broader compatibility with older browsers.

## Avatar Options

*2024-12-31 to 2025-01-01 · 7 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/Avatar.20Options/with/2022569)*

**Aman (whilstsomebody)** · 2024-12-31 19:17 UTC

I want to know how all the options for avatars are linked to their literals. For example, the literal 'G' represents an avatar hosted by Gravatar, and 'U' represents one provided by the user.
How are these linked?

**Pieter K** · 2025-01-01 06:08 UTC

They are declared in the `models/users.py` and are choices for the `Users` tables `avatar_sources` field, if that's what you're asking:

```python
class UserProfile(AbstractBaseUser, PermissionsMixin, UserBaseSettings):
...
    AVATAR_FROM_GRAVATAR = "G"
    AVATAR_FROM_USER = "U"
    AVATAR_SOURCES = (
        (AVATAR_FROM_GRAVATAR, "Hosted by Gravatar"),
        (AVATAR_FROM_USER, "Uploaded by user"),
    )
    avatar_source = models.CharField(
        default=AVATAR_FROM_GRAVATAR, choices=AVATAR_SOURCES, max_length=1
    )
...
```

**Aman (whilstsomebody)** · 2025-01-01 08:49 UTC

Umm no. I already found this.
I mean how are all these avatars linked to their paths.

**Pieter K** · 2025-01-01 09:24 UTC

So when we upload a users avatar, the image files name is actually an encoded string containing user id + avatar version + the servers avatar salt, this avatar file have no direct link or connection to the `Users` table.

So when the client asks for a user's avatar file, how do the server know which image file to get from the media server? well, we look at the users `avatar_source`, if its user uploaded then do the same procedure we would when we upload the image avatar, that is to encode the user id, etc, etc to get the same filename.

`avatar_url` in `zerver/lib/avatar.py` handles this.

**Pieter K** · 2025-01-01 09:25 UTC

might miss a couple of details but I think that's roughly how you get avatar URLs, CMIIW :smile:

**Aman (whilstsomebody)** · 2025-01-01 09:35 UTC

So, if I want to save a different avatar image, then first I have to hash it and then I can save it.
And another option is to give that image to the client then the server itself will do the whole process.

**Aman (whilstsomebody)** · 2025-01-01 10:23 UTC

I could do that with the help of this.
Thanks @Pieter K !

## conflicts due to API updates.

*2025-01-09 to 2025-01-10 · 4 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/conflicts.20due.20to.20API.20updates.2E/with/2034625)*

**Apoorva Pendse** · 2025-01-09 02:54 UTC

I get conflicts on #32864 on a daily basis due to merged API updates for the files: `api_docs/changelog.md` and `version.py`.
Would it be wise to let the conflicts remain and only handle them when the PR is about to get merged?

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-01-10 21:02 UTC

If those are the only conflicts, yes it's fine, I often will renumber as part of merging. But if you have other feedback, please do renumber when you address that, since it is nice to be able to merge without editing PRs once they've addressed all feedback.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-01-10 21:03 UTC

I will note that PRs without merge conflicts do generally get faster review, because of how I use GitHub's filtering features for recently updated work.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-01-10 21:03 UTC

What I'd like us to have is some better system for naming/numbering these that doesn't involve merge conflicts, but I've yet to come up with anything suitable.

const clipboardItem = new ClipboardItem({

If you apply this diff and run the `left_sidebar_navigation_area` test again , then you'll find that .removeClass doesn't work as expected i.e. remove all instances of "top-left-active-filter" from everywhere.
The reason can be found in `zjquery_element.cjs`.
Every element has it's own `classes` map, and removeClass just removes the said classes from that elements map, and not from everywhere, as JQuery would from the DOM.

So the potential solution to pass this test (IMO) would be to override `select_top_left_corner_item` in your test, and remove the class `top-left-active-filter` from all the five targets, then add it to whatever `narrow_to_activate` was just like you did in the actual implementation.

This solution makes sense to me, since that is the behavior we achieve in the browser. But I'd be happy to to hear better solutions from other folks.

Here is my hasty implementation of that overridden function
```javascript
let targets = [
        $(".top_left_all_messages"),
        $(".top_left_mentions"),
        $(".top_left_starred_messages"),
        $(".top_left_recent_view"),
        $(".top_left_inbox") ] 
select_top_left_corner_item: (narrow_to_activate) => {
            targets.forEach((t)=>{
                t.removeClass("top-left-active-filter")
            })
            if(narrow_to_activate!==''){
                $(narrow_to_activate).addClass("top-left-active-filter");
            }
        },
```

I definitely have a love/hate relationship with zjquery. It solves some problems, but it gets overused in our codebase. **Steve Howell** · 2025-01-13 12:46 UTC

Just to get on my soapbox (and I am kind of repeating myself from another thread), I truly believe that software developers should learn to treat test code as a first-class concept in their process.  Tests should never be an afterthought.  It's true that the main purpose of tests is to prevent regressions in later changes, but the more elegant purpose of good tests is that they force you to write better code in the quote-unquote "real codebase".

If your real code is hard to test, then the tests are telling you something.  It's almost always possible to improve the quality of the real code to make testing easier, so if your tests are presenting difficulty to you, then your instinct should be to look at the real code and see if the real code is actually problem.  There are exceptions to this rule of thumb, to be sure, but I would wager that 90% of the time overly complicated tests are just exposing overly complicated code.

**Steve Howell** · 2025-01-13 12:48 UTC

In particular, I think the Zulip codebase does a pretty terrible job of abstracting UI concepts (relative to the high bar of Zulip code in general).  The jQuery library is an extremely low-level library with a very high surface area.  Whenever possible, if I were the code czar, I would encapsulate uses of jQuery into higher-level APIs with a much more narrow interface.  But that's just me.

**Steve Howell** · 2025-01-13 13:01 UTC

Hey, sorry for the slow reply, it's been a busy day. I would recommend in a situation like this where another contributor helped write the code that @Maneesh Shukla include a `Co-authored-by` or textual note in the commit message, like:

**Greg Price** · 2025-01-15 00:59 UTC

(replying to Steve Howell)
> Hickson, who is the project leader of Flutter, apparently says "the purpose of a test is so we don't accidentally break your change". I think that's only partially true. […] I would amend Hickson's recommendation to something like "Tests should reflect the original developer's intentions as concisel …

Yeah, to clarify a bit the context of that line: the occasions where he'd be saying that all the time were as part of explaining a rule in the Flutter project (a rule which I'm guessing he laid down) that all PRs must include tests, unless they're docs-only changes or pure refactors.

This rule is enforced by a robot that checks if you include a test and if the PR is docs-only, and if the robot can't verify the PR complies with the rule then, historically, you had to get an exemption from Hixie personally by pinging him in a Discord channel (their analogue of our #**general**, or perhaps our #**backend** plus #**frontend**). (Today there's a small rotation of maybe three "test exemption reviewers", and you ping that group in the same channel.) The point of all that is to push people to test their changes, with very few exceptions other than docs-only changes and pure refactors.

**Greg Price** · 2025-01-15 00:59 UTC

So that means a steady stream of people who would like to skip out on writing a test because that seems like work, or because at first glance they don't see how you even could write a test for their change.

And "the purpose of a test is so we don't accidentally break your change" is a line for (a) helping motivate people to do it, and (b) helping guide them to think through how a test could be written after all. The next line is often: "Is there something your change does that you would prefer not get reverted in the future?"

**Greg Price** · 2025-01-15 01:01 UTC

I don't know that Hixie would necessarily agree with your rewriting, but I imagine he wouldn't disagree that writing tests can be useful for other purposes too, including helping write the change.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-01-15 06:19 UTC

Personally I think people are getting far too stressed and argumentative about what is in the scheme of contributions  small bit of work. A few thoughts:
- I think this is the first dispute of this sort about credit that I can recall in 50K commits that I've integrated into Zulip.
- I do not want my job to include extensively adjudicating the authorship story for the node testing changes attached to a relatively minor refactor.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-01-15 06:20 UTC

- I think it's reasonable to credit someone for putting time into helping with something even if they were not successful in finding the solution you went with on something. 
- Generally the Co-Authored-By tag specifically is to record the joint copyright for the code contributed to the project. Realistically, this small refactoring change may not even be substantive enough to have any copyright notice, and it has immaterial impact on things like GitHub statistics, so what is important here is figuring out how to have both of you satisfied with the interaction.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-01-15 06:22 UTC

In my experience, the most productive next step in this sort of situation is for the parties to the disagreement to have a friendly live conversation with each (a video call is best), express appreciation for each others' work, and jointly figure out a resolution that feels good to both of you.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-01-15 06:23 UTC

From my standpoint, I appreciate both of your effort on this PR, including @Apoorva Pendse participating actively in trying to debug someone else's work. It's really important to the community that people feel excited to help others out, and feel that sort of work is appreciated regardless of whether it results in a commit merged into the project authored by the person who was helping.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-01-15 06:24 UTC

Ultimately, open source is about jointly creating a work together, and I think the less attention spent on thinking about who contributed what idea, and the more spent on trying to add ideas to make the project better, the more successful the project will be and the happier its members will be.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-01-15 06:26 UTC

There was a time a very long time ago that I motivated myself by trying to optimize for metrics like those GitHub will give you (commits merged, etc.), and I noticed that kind of metrics-based motivation caused me to be tempted to do counterproductive or antisocial things. Stuff like thinking about breaking a PR into extra commits not because I thought it was most readable that way, but because it would make my score go up.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-01-15 06:30 UTC

So I'd encourage you to not let yourself get distracted by trying to make numbers go up or focusing on credit/attribution especially for micro tasks, like fixing a broken test. What one should care about is creating a great body of work as a whole.

Certainly when evaluating who to accept for GSoC, our evaluation process does not include looking at numbers of commits or PRs merged at all, but instead at how someone engages in the community, whether they've shown clear learning/progress through the coaching we provide in reviewing PRs, and the quality of their best work. I have a very good memory, and Zulip/GitHub have an even better one ;), and that makes it easy for us to our evaluations based on those factors, not some game-able metrics.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-01-15 06:32 UTC

I hope this helps. I expect we'll be doing some AMA type discussion sessions as GSoC starts up, and I think the issue of credit/attribution both in open source/community activities and the corporate world, and how those differ and how they are similar, could be an interesting topic to delve into.

**Steve Howell** · 2025-01-15 12:44 UTC

I hate to prolong this conversation, but anybody who is exhausted by it can just mute it, so I feel ok throwing in my two cents here.

It's just a fact that you have to accept when working on Zulip, and probably free software projects in general, that you are not always going to get proper attributions in commit messages for contributions that you made to solving the problem.  Commit messages aren't designed to give credit to everybody who participated.  They're designed, at least partly, to give accountability to the person who makes the commit.

I've helped countless folks on commits without getting any Co-Author shout-out on the commit itself.  And it's not because the other folks lack gratitude; in contrast, I have found folks to be extremely grateful in this community for relatively small things I have done.  Often folks ask for my help, and I just give the slightest of encouragements or hints, and then they take it to the finish line.  And they still thank me.

**Steve Howell** · 2025-01-15 12:45 UTC

I've also been on the other side, where I made a commit that was heavily influenced by PR suggestions or heavily cribbed off of another contributor's work.  I try to shout out those situations in the commit message, but I have surely neglected it at times.

**Steve Howell** · 2025-01-15 12:56 UTC

The only way to build reputation on a free software project is to keep making steady contributions, whether it's your own PRs, or helping others, and eventually credit gets served where credit is due.  It's an imperfect human process.

I've had a relationship with Tim for over a decade.  He knows all my strengths and weaknesses.  The reason Tim puts up with me is that he knows there are certain things in my wheelhouse that only about five people in the world can solve, and the other four people are too busy.

And you can also build a lot of social credit just by being tactical and strategic.  I like to work on controversial things, because I am sort of contrarian by nature.  But I try to balance that with an occasional completely non-controversial commit.  Fix a simple bug.  Add a simple animation effect.  Fix a typo in the docs.  That kind of stuff really helps the project too.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-01-14 18:39 UTC

It's possible the `REALM_HOSTS` setting is what you want, to map the default realm (normally on `localhost:9991`) to the IP address you have?

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-01-14 18:39 UTC

```
external_host_env = os.getenv("EXTERNAL_HOST")                                                          
if external_host_env is None:                                                                           
    if IS_DEV_DROPLET:                                                                                  
        # For our droplets, we use the hostname (eg github_username.zulipdev.org) by default.           
        # Note that this code is duplicated in run-dev.                                                 
        EXTERNAL_HOST = os.uname()[1].lower() + ":9991"                                                 
    else:                                                                                               
        # For local development environments, we use localhost by                                       
        # default, via the "zulipdev.com" hostname.                                                     
        EXTERNAL_HOST = "zulipdev.com:9991"                                                             
        # Serve the main dev realm at the literal name "localhost",                                     
        # so it works out of the box even when not on the Internet.                                     
        REALM_HOSTS = {                                                                                 
            "zulip": "localhost:9991",                                                                  
        }                                                                                               
else:                                                                                                   
    EXTERNAL_HOST = external_host_env                                                                   
    REALM_HOSTS = {                                                                                     
        "zulip": EXTERNAL_HOST,                                                                         
    }                                                                                                   
```

>The high-level steps are as follow:
>
>1. `bash` into our Linux distro
>2. `git clone` our project there, outside of the Windows file system
>3. `explorer.exe .` back into windows (or `\\wsl$` there, from Windows explorer directly)
>4. `vscode .` from Windows into ou Linux project folder

To work with Windows-only IDEs or tools (4th step will differ) :up:

# Generated by Django 5.0.10 on 2025-01-16 14:46

from django.db import migrations, transaction
from django.db.backends.base.schema import BaseDatabaseSchemaEditor
from django.db.migrations.state import StateApps
from django.db.models import Max, Min


def render_all_user_group_descriptions(
    apps: StateApps, schema_editor: BaseDatabaseSchemaEditor
) -> None:
    # FIXME: Application code should not be imported from migrations.
    from zerver.actions.user_groups import render_group_description

    NamedUserGroup = apps.get_model("zerver", "NamedUserGroup")
    BATCH_SIZE = 1000
    max_id = NamedUserGroup.objects.exclude(description="").aggregate(Max("id"))["id__max"]
    if max_id is None:
        # Do nothing if there are no user groups on the server.
        return

    lower_bound = NamedUserGroup.objects.exclude(description="").aggregate(Min("id"))["id__min"]

    while lower_bound <= max_id:
        upper_bound = lower_bound + BATCH_SIZE - 1
        print(f"Processing batch {lower_bound} to {upper_bound} for NamedUserGroup")

        with transaction.atomic():
            all_named_user_groups = NamedUserGroup.objects.exclude(
                id__gte=lower_bound, id__lt=upper_bound, description=""
            )
            for user_group in all_named_user_groups:
                user_group.rendered_description = render_group_description(
                    user_group.description, user_group.realm
                )
            NamedUserGroup.objects.bulk_update(
                all_named_user_groups, fields=["rendered_description"], batch_size=BATCH_SIZE
            )

        lower_bound += BATCH_SIZE


class Migration(migrations.Migration):
    atomic = False

    dependencies = [
        ("zerver", "0649_namedusergroup_rendered_description"),
    ]

    operations = [
        migrations.RunPython(
            render_all_user_group_descriptions,
            reverse_code=migrations.RunPython.noop,
            elidable=True,
        ),
    ]

from django.db import migrations, models
from django.db.backends.base.schema import BaseDatabaseSchemaEditor
from django.db.migrations.state import StateApps


def render_all_stream_descriptions(
    apps: StateApps, schema_editor: BaseDatabaseSchemaEditor
) -> None:
    # FIXME: Application code should not be imported from migrations.
    from zerver.lib.streams import render_stream_description

    Stream = apps.get_model("zerver", "Stream")
    all_streams = Stream.objects.exclude(description="")
    for stream in all_streams:
        stream.rendered_description = render_stream_description(stream.description, stream.realm)
        stream.save(update_fields=["rendered_description"])


class Migration(migrations.Migration):
    dependencies = [
        ("zerver", "0205_remove_realmauditlog_requires_billing_update"),
    ]

    operations = [
        migrations.AddField(
            model_name="stream",
            name="rendered_description",
            field=models.TextField(default=""),
        ),
        migrations.RunPython(
            render_all_stream_descriptions, reverse_code=migrations.RunPython.noop, elidable=True
        ),
    ]
