**Tim Abbott** · 2025-01-21 21:49 UTC

I think this is because the database is empty when provisioning, so your loop is empty; the crash is a real issue.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-01-21 21:50 UTC

Running the Markdown processor from migrations is a pattern that's not a happy one, though we may need to use it for this sort of feature anyway.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-01-21 21:51 UTC

The problem being that ideally, migration files are self-sufficient and don't depend on any other code in the project, which helps avoid surprises where they behavior differently when upgrading from 9.0 to 10.0 vs upgrading from 9.0 to 11.0.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-01-21 21:24 UTC

Yeah, I think you can add things to this for a test:
``` js
$ cat web/src/zulip_test.ts
// This module, exposed through the zulip_test global variable,
// re-exports certain internal functions so they can be used by the
// Puppeteer tests.  It should not be used in the code itself.

export {set_wildcard_mention_threshold, wildcard_mention_threshold} from "./compose_validate.ts";
export {private_message_recipient} from "./compose_state.ts";
export {current as current_msg_list} from "./message_lists.ts";
export {get_stream_id, get_sub, get_subscriber_count} from "./stream_data.ts";
export {get_by_user_id as get_person_by_user_id, get_user_id_from_name} from "./people.ts";

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-01-24 01:49 UTC

What that profile tells you is mainly that a lot of time was spent doing database queries. Some of that is Python, and thus may improve with using a new Python version. I kinda wonder if we can move to `uv` at some point and be able to bundle Python more easily. 

That said, I've definitely been seeing `test-backend` get slower over time. To some extent, that comes with adding functionality, but the other thing that can really contribute is that a decent number of tests do much more expensive setup and queries than they intend to.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-01-24 01:51 UTC

There's some tests, like some `test_events` cases, where it's probably net helpful that we don't carefully limit `fetch_event_types` / `event_types`, but I bet that test can be made 1.5-2x faster by excluding in the event types that we query some expensive stuff just in some of the tests that loop over every setting to exercise changing those.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-01-24 01:52 UTC

For extended profiling, I found `line_profiler` to be a lot more helpful than the built-in profiler for seeing where time is actually going, though I seem to recall it's a bit of a chore because you have to annotate the functions to profile.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-01-24 01:54 UTC

But my guess is the main thing going on is that test class having some copy/pasted patterns that just do way more work than they need to. Like this test:

```
    def test_you_must_be_realm_admin(self) -> None:                                                     
        """                                                                                             
        You must be on the realm to create a stream.

        user_profile = self.example_user("hamlet")                                                      
        self.login_user(user_profile)                                                                   
                                                                                                        
        other_realm = do_create_realm(string_id="other", name="other")                                  
        stream = self.make_stream("other_realm_stream", realm=other_realm)                              
                                                                                                        
        result = self.client_delete("/json/streams/" + str(stream.id))                                  
        self.assert_json_error(result, "Invalid channel ID")                                            
                                                                                                        
        # Even becoming a realm admin doesn't help us for an out-of-realm                               
        # stream.                                                                                       
        do_change_user_role(user_profile, UserProfile.ROLE_REALM_ADMINISTRATOR, acting_user=None)       
        result = self.client_delete("/json/streams/" + str(stream.id))                                  
        self.assert_json_error(result, "Invalid channel ID")                                            
```

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-01-24 01:55 UTC

Why does that need to create a realm and create a stream, when I thought we have the `lear` realm in the test fixture data, so we could just use that rather than making one from scratch.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-01-24 01:55 UTC

Probably a good way to analyze it would be to filter a profile of the full test suite for what `zerver/actions/*` functions are consuming the time.

I looked at the previous PR, which was trying to fix it. There is also the same error that occurred, and in that PR, the code of `createSingelton` was moved to `click_handlers.ts, ' and it works. But @Karl Stolley  raised the above comment there, so I'm currently experimenting with it.
But, hadn't got any solid logic behind this till yet :smiling_face_with_tear: .

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-02-07 22:09 UTC

I'm guessing what is happening is some exception is being thrown at import time, preventing later code from running, and it's not related to ordering.

**Maneesh Shukla** · 2025-04-10 20:06 UTC

Finally, i'm done with this change.
Thanks to @Sayam Samal for his insightful comment on the PR,

The reason behind why singleton creation works in `click_handlers.ts` but not in `compose_tooltips.ts` is because at the time `compose_tooltips.ts` runs, the elements matching `.compose_button_tooltip` doesn't exist yet in the DOM.

But `tippy.createSingleton(...)` expects fully initialized static tippy instances — so as  i was trying to pass a delegate there directly, it was breaking.

Hence, I need to initialize the singleton only after the compose box is guaranteed to be in the DOM.

## Who should resolve conversations on GitHub and when?

*2025-02-11 to 2025-02-11 · 9 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/Who.20should.20resolve.20conversations.20on.20GitHub.20and.20when.3F/with/2085895)*

**Apoorva Pendse** · 2025-02-11 11:21 UTC

Wasn't able find documentation regarding this.

**Apoorva Pendse** · 2025-02-11 11:23 UTC

For instance, #32891 has a lot of unresolved conversations and the feedback for most of them is addressed and implemented.
So is it the responsibility of the PR creator to resolve them if the next round of review starts?

**Apoorva Pendse** · 2025-02-11 11:24 UTC

Or is it better to wait for the reviewer to resolve them?

**Prakhar Pratyush** · 2025-02-11 11:33 UTC

[github docs](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/reviewing-changes-in-pull-requests/commenting-on-a-pull-request#resolving-conversations)

> You can resolve a conversation in a pull request if you opened the pull request or if you have write access to the repository where the pull request was opened.

So, anyone reviewing the code can't mark it as resolved.

In general, it is clear from the comment or thumbs up emoji that a review comment was addressed so as an author we can mark it as resolved.

**Prakhar Pratyush** · 2025-02-11 11:36 UTC

I think, ideally, github should provide a setting for "Who can resolve a conversation in a pull request".

**Prakhar Pratyush** · 2025-02-11 11:40 UTC

https://github.com/orgs/community/discussions/12961

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-02-11 18:04 UTC

This is probably worth writing some documentation on. 

As a general rule, it's better for reviewers to mark questions or requests for changes as resolved, once they've confirmed that the resolution was successful. For some comments, like "please add this exact language as a comment" or "please rename this function from X to Y", if you did exactly what the comment suggested, it's probably fine to mark as resolved when you've applied the change exactly as described, but I'm not sure it's worth complicating the protocol to do that -- it's very quick for a reviewer to click resolve when they look at the PR again.

That said, a category of thing that is generally ideal for the contributor to mark resolved is comments of the form "This seems like a good abstraction", or "Cool, once we've done this, this other issue might be a good next step" where the goal is for the contributor to see it once, and then the contributor should mark it as resolved.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-02-11 18:04 UTC

I think we've had some past discussions about this protocol that might be fruitful to read for thinking about a write-up on this.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-02-11 18:04 UTC

But when in doubt, I think the protocol of reviewers always marking as resolved is a good default.

**kartikay** · 2025-02-12 07:44 UTC

I’m working on issue [#33222](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/issues/33222) and have implemented all the required functionalities correctly. The banner is rendering as expected, and all functionalities are working as described in the issue.

However, I’m facing a couple of UI issues:

1. The banner’s yellow background color (for the warning intent) is not applying, even with `!important`.
2. The banner label, action button, and close button are not aligning in a single row—they are stacking vertically instead.

Does anyone have suggestions on how to fix these?

I made these changes in settings_notifications.ts file 
```javascript
const create_notification_banner = (): string => {
    return render_banner({
        process: "desktop-notifications-required",
        intent: "warning",
        label: "Zulip needs your permission to enable desktop notifications for important messages.",
        buttons: [
            {
                type: "quiet",
                intent: "warning",
                label: "Enable permissions",
                custom_classes: "request-desktop-notifications",
            },
        ],
        close_button: true,
    });
};
```
```javascript
function update_notification_banner(): void {
    const permission = Notification.permission;

    if (permission === "granted") {
        $(".desktop-setting-notications").hide();
        $(".send_test_notification").show();
        $(".banner[data-process='desktop-notifications-required']").remove();
    } else {
        $(".send_test_notification").hide();
        if ($(".banner[data-process='desktop-notifications-required']").length === 0) {
            $("#settings_content").prepend(create_notification_banner());
        }
    }
}

```
```javascript
$("#settings_content").on("click", ".request-desktop-notifications", (e) => {
        e.preventDefault();
        void Notification.requestPermission().then((permission) => {
            if (permission === "granted") {
                update_notification_banner();
            } else if (permission === "denied") {
                window.open("/help/desktop-notifications#check-platform-settings", "_blank");
            }
        });
    });
    $("#settings_content").on("click", ".banner-close-button", (e) => {
        e.preventDefault();
        $(e.currentTarget).closest(".banner").remove();
    });

```

**Steve Howell** · 2025-03-05 20:57 UTC

(replying to Aman (whilstsomebody))
> You should try using override for `warn_if_mentioning_unsubscribed_group` also.

I am 99% sure this is the correct diagnosis.  The PR adds a new call to `compose_validate.warn_if_mentioning_unsubscribed_group` inside of `content_typeahead_selected`, and then the test failure shows that when `content_typeahead_selected` gets invoked, it can't find `warn_if_mentioning_unsubscribed_group`, since the tests are mocking out the entire `compose_validate` module.

**Steve Howell** · 2025-03-05 20:57 UTC

(so it should be a one-line change to fix the tests)

**Steve Howell** · 2025-03-05 21:07 UTC

@kartikay 

There are two different patterns for mocking out a module.  One pattern is to basically mock out all the functions you want to mock out at the top of the test in the `mock_esm` code, which is what I believe the current test does.  So you should probably just follow that pattern.

The other pattern, which I've grown to prefer, is more granular.  The `mock_esm` call at the top of the test would basically just mock the `compose_validate` module as completely empty, and then individual tests would use `override` or something similar.  The advantage of that approach is that you can see the dependencies more granularly, and you won't accumulate dead test code in the future.  But it's a pretty minor advantage in this case.

So I think you just want to update the `mock_esm` call at the top of the code.

**Steve Howell** · 2025-03-05 21:09 UTC

https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/main/web/tests/example4.test.cjs is particularly instructive here.

**kartikay** · 2025-03-05 21:38 UTC

Thanks for the advice!
I was able to resolve the node test failures in `composebox_typeahead.test.cjs` by adding:
```javascript
warn_if_mentioning_unsubscribed_group: noop;

```
This handled the missing function reference issue. Additionally, I had to tweak the `.view_user_group_mention` click handler in `composebox_typeahead.ts` to ensure it is only bound once with something like this 
```javascript
if (!$("body").data("has-view-user-group-handler")) {
    $("body").on("click", ".view_user_group_mention", function (this: HTMLElement, e) {
        e.stopPropagation();
        toggle_user_group_info_popover(this, undefined);
    });
    $("body").data("has-view-user-group-handler", true);
}


```
With these changes, all Node test cases are passing. Just wanted to check if this is the right approach.

function move_topic(): void {
        const params = get_params_from_form();

        const old_topic_name = params.old_topic_name.trim();
        let select_stream_id;
        if (only_topic_edit) {
            select_stream_id = undefined;
        } else {
            select_stream_id = stream_widget_value;
        }

        let new_topic_name = params.new_topic_name;
        const send_notification_to_new_thread = params.send_notification_to_new_thread === "on";
        const send_notification_to_old_thread = params.send_notification_to_old_thread === "on";
        const current_stream_id = Number.parseInt(params.current_stream_id, 10);

        if (new_topic_name !== undefined) {
            // new_topic_name can be undefined when the new topic input is disabled when
            // user does not have permission to edit topic.
            new_topic_name = new_topic_name.trim();
        }
        if (old_topic_name === new_topic_name) {
            // We use `undefined` to tell the server that
            // there has been no change in the topic name.
            new_topic_name = undefined;
        }
        if (select_stream_id === current_stream_id) {
            // We use `undefined` to tell the server that
            // there has been no change in stream. This is
            // important for cases when changing stream is
            // not allowed or when changes other than
            // stream-change has been made.
            select_stream_id = undefined;
        }

        let propagate_mode = "change_all";
        if (message !== undefined) {
            // We already have the message_id here which means that modal is opened using
            // message popover.
            assert(params.propagate_mode !== undefined);
            propagate_mode = params.propagate_mode;
            const toast_params =
                propagate_mode === "change_one"
                    ? {
                          new_stream_id: select_stream_id ?? current_stream_id,
                          new_topic_name: new_topic_name ?? old_topic_name,
                      }
                    : undefined;
            message_edit.move_topic_containing_message_to_stream(
                message.id,
                select_stream_id,
                new_topic_name,
                send_notification_to_new_thread,
                send_notification_to_old_thread,
                propagate_mode,
                toast_params,
            );
            return;
        }

        dialog_widget.show_dialog_spinner();
        message_edit.with_first_message_id(
            current_stream_id,
            old_topic_name,
            (message_id) => {
                if (message_id === undefined) {
                    // There are no messages in the given topic, so we show an error banner
                    // and return, preventing any attempts to move a non-existent topic.
                    dialog_widget.hide_dialog_spinner();
                    ui_report.client_error(
                        $t_html({defaultMessage: "There are no messages to move."}),
                        $("#move_topic_modal #dialog_error"),
                    );
                    return;
                }
                message_edit.move_topic_containing_message_to_stream(
                    message_id,
                    select_stream_id,
                    new_topic_name,
                    send_notification_to_new_thread,
                    send_notification_to_old_thread,
                    propagate_mode,
                );
            },
            (xhr) => {
                dialog_widget.hide_dialog_spinner();
                ui_report.error(
                    $t_html({defaultMessage: "Error moving topic"}),
                    xhr,
                    $("#move_topic_modal #dialog_error"),
                );
            },
        );
    }

```
function move_topic_post_render(): void {
        $("#move_topic_modal .dialog_submit_button").prop("disabled", true);

        const $topic_input = $<HTMLInputElement>("#move_topic_form input.move_messages_edit_topic");
        move_topic_to_stream_topic_typeahead = composebox_typeahead.initialize_topic_edit_typeahead(
            $topic_input,
            current_stream_name,
            false,
        );

        if (only_topic_edit) {
            // Set select_stream_id to current_stream_id since we user is not allowed
            // to edit stream in topic-edit only UI.
            const select_stream_id = current_stream_id;
            $topic_input.on("input", () => {
                update_submit_button_disabled_state(select_stream_id);
            });
            return;
        }

        stream_widget_value = current_stream_id;
        const streams_list_options = (): {
            name: string;
            unique_id: number;
            stream: sub_store.StreamSubscription;
        }[] =>
            stream_data.get_options_for_dropdown_widget().filter(({stream}) => {
                if (stream.stream_id === current_stream_id) {
                    return true;
                }
                return stream_data.can_post_messages_in_stream(stream);
            });

        new dropdown_widget.DropdownWidget({
            widget_name: "move_topic_to_stream",
            get_options: streams_list_options,
            item_click_callback: move_topic_on_update,
            $events_container: $("#move_topic_modal"),
            tippy_props: {
                // Show dropdown search input below stream selection button.
                offset: [0, 2],
            },
        }).setup();

        render_selected_stream();
        $("#move_topic_to_stream_widget").prop("disabled", disable_stream_input);
        $("#move_topic_modal .move_messages_edit_topic").on("input", () => {
            update_submit_button_disabled_state(current_stream_id);
        });

        if (!args.from_message_actions_popover) {
            update_move_messages_count_text("change_all");
        } else {
            // Generate unique key for this conversation
            const conversation_key = `${current_stream_id}_${topic_name}`;
            let selected_option = String($("#message_move_select_options").val());

            // If a user has changed the smart defaults of `propagate_mode` to "change_one", we
            // remember that forced change and apply the same default for `propagate_mode` next
            // time when the user tries to move the message of the same topic to save the time
            // of user manually selecting "change_one" every time.
            const previously_used_propagate_mode =
                last_propagate_mode_for_conversation.get(conversation_key);
            if (previously_used_propagate_mode === "change_one") {
                selected_option = "change_one";
                $("#message_move_select_options").val(selected_option);
            }

            update_move_messages_count_text(selected_option, message?.id);

            $("#message_move_select_options").on("change", function () {
                selected_option = String($(this).val());
                last_propagate_mode_for_conversation.set(conversation_key, selected_option);
                update_move_messages_count_text(selected_option, message?.id);
            });
        }
    }

```

**Aman (whilstsomebody)** · 2025-03-13 04:59 UTC

Hey @Harsh , thanks for your help. I had tried every possible combination but was not able to fix this. 
Now I was able to pass the tests with your hint.


```ts
const $wildcard_warning_container = $("#compose_banners");
    const $wildcard_warning_child = $.create("wildcard_warning_child_stub");
    $wildcard_warning_container.set_find_results(".wildcard_warning", $wildcard_warning_child);
    $wildcard_warning_container.find = () => $wildcard_warning_child;

    let stub_removed;
    $wildcard_warning_child.remove = () => {
        stub_removed = true;
    };
    compose_validate.clear_stream_wildcard_warnings($wildcard_warning_container);
    assert.ok(stub_removed);
```

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2025-03-17 18:57 UTC

No, `Json[str]` is not backwards compatible with `str`; it would force the client to change `key=value` to `key="value"`.

In general, you can’t, because every value is a valid `str`; there’s no room to add new values that wouldn’t have had a different interpretation by the old code.

def find_key_by_email(address: str) -> str | None:

 and I’ve merged the latest `main` into my feature branch.

During provisioning, I encountered errors related to translations. I followed the docs and ran:

```bash
./manage.py makemessages -a
```
That fixed the provisioning issue, and everything now works as expected.

However, I’m now running into **merge conflicts and unexpected lint errors** related to the translation files during the PR.

####  What I’ve tried:

1. Deleting the previous translation commit and recreating it at the end — but this causes unexpected `tools/lint` errors.
  
2. I saw in the [Internationalization docs](https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/translating/internationalization.html#translation-process) that translation updates typically require mentor help.

### What I’d like to know:
* What’s the recommended way to handle these translation conflicts?
  
* Should I drop the translation changes from my PR and let a mentor regenerate them later?
  
* Or is there a preferred way to keep the translations without running into lint errors?
  

Thanks in advance for any guidance!

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2025-04-05 01:47 UTC

Yeah, you should drop any translation changes from your PR. We will pull translation changes in from Transifex separately.

**Mayank (ImDooMLorD)** · 2025-04-05 04:36 UTC

I attempted to cherry-pick only the commits I authored and tried un-staging the changes in `locale/` during the merge — but since the original commits included them, they still show up in the history.

Rebasing didn’t help much either — when I try something like `git rebase -i HEAD~3`, it shows hundreds or even thousands of commits, and when I tried using specific commit hashes, I kept getting stuck mid-rebase on commits that weren’t even mine.

Would it make sense to redo the PR cleanly from a fresh branch and apply only the necessary code changes? Or is there a way to surgically remove the `locale/` updates from the history, even if they’ve already been pushed?

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-04-07 22:17 UTC

You want to use `git pull --rebase` rather than `git pull` when rebasing previous work.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-04-07 22:17 UTC

Our Git guide covers the workflow in detail and is highly recommended, but you never want to make merge commits as a Zulip contributor (or generally as a contributor to most projects).

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2025-04-17 18:52 UTC

That’s different.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2025-04-17 18:56 UTC

Handlebars has no idea what an HTML element is. It’s just a string processor. So any Handlebars directive that can be put inside a string can be put “inside” an HTML element too (and you’re entirely responsible for arranging things so the result makes sense as HTML). But Handlebars does not interpret Handlebars directives that are in the middle of other Handlebars directives.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2025-04-17 18:57 UTC

Whenever there are multiple levels of string interpretation going on (Handlebars template → HTML code → rendered page in your browser), it is very important to remember what’s happening (and not happening) at each level. Forgetting this can lead to security vulnerabilities.

## Handling transactions in data migrations

*2025-05-06 to 2025-05-07 · 10 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/Handling.20transactions.20in.20data.20migrations/with/2167663)*

**Bedo Khaled** · 2025-05-06 12:40 UTC

I already understand that a large sql query should be batched (i.e. divided into multiples queries) for memory and time efficiency, avoid locking and other reasons, right ?

But why we aslo need to do this in multiple transactions instead of a single one  (i.e. `atomic=False`) ?
[0696_rename_no_topic_to_empty_string_topic.py](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/dc7f34491baea805b5cd01d10e93bd2a8729cb6d/zerver/migrations/0696_rename_no_topic_to_empty_string_topic.py#L113-L114) for example
Is this for the same reasons above ?

**Alex Vandiver** · 2025-05-06 14:04 UTC

Locks are held into the transaction commits.  PostgreSQL also has to hold onto a bunch of (meta)data which scales with how old the oldest commit is, so having really long-running transactions is bad for overall performance.

**Bedo Khaled** · 2025-05-06 14:23 UTC

ok, thanks

**Bedo Khaled** · 2025-05-06 14:26 UTC

Also I asked chatgpt whether I should add `cursor = connection.cursor()` inside or outside the transaction block, and it recommended adding it **inside** with the following justication :
> This ensures the cursor is tied to a clean transaction state This avoids issues where a failed transaction leaves the connection in an unusable state for the existing cursor, which can lead to errors like `TransactionManagementError`

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-05-06 16:34 UTC

That argument is not relevant in the migration context.

**Bedo Khaled** · 2025-05-07 11:27 UTC

I mean a decision has to be made for whether doing this:
```python
for realm in Realm.objects.all():
    with transaction.atomic(durable=True):
        cursor = connection.cursor()
        cursor.execute(query, {"realm_id": realm.id})
```
OR 

```python
cursor = connection.cursor()
for realm in Realm.objects.all():
    with transaction.atomic(durable=True):
        cursor.execute(query, {"realm_id": realm.id})

```

**Bedo Khaled** · 2025-05-07 11:57 UTC

These are the differences :

1. **cursor outside**:  cursor connection is created once, so  it might be  more efficient as it  reduces the total number of database interactions.

2. **cursor inside**: There will be the overhead of creating the cursor for each iteration, but it's safer and more isolated  in case of errors, as each cursor is tied to each transaction

**Alex Vandiver** · 2025-05-07 14:14 UTC

With the exception of [server-side cursors](https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/5.2/ref/databases/#server-side-cursors), a cursor is a memory abstraction and does not consume any notable resources.  And Tim was noting that we don't need to think about recovery or isolation in the case of errors, because we're going to abort the whole migration process in that case.

In short, it really doesn't matter here.  Do whichever seems clearer.  I will note that it's slightly more canonical to open/close the cursor with a contextmanager:
```python3
for realm in Realm.objects.all():
    with (connection.cursor() as cursor, transaction.atomic(durable=True)):
        cursor.execute(query, {"realm_id": realm.id})
```

**Bedo Khaled** · 2025-05-07 15:04 UTC

That's a very clear answer, thanks

**Bedo Khaled** · 2025-05-07 18:37 UTC

(replying to Alex Vandiver)
> `with (connection.cursor() as cursor, transaction.atomic(durable=True)):`

Nice, Never knew I could do both in the same line !

Is this a good approach, or would it be better to use the `zerver_message_realm_upper_subject` index that @Alex Vandiver mentioned [here](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/137-feedback/topic/search.20by.20topic/near/2165602)?

CMIIW

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-05-30 00:21 UTC

We can't safely call `stream_topic_history_util.get_server_history` in a loop over every channel -- it is way too much work to ask the server to do. What you can do is just work from the locally available `stream_topic_history` data -- that'll effectively be searching "recent history" of a few months, and in practice be reasonable.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-05-30 00:21 UTC

But I think broadly that should be fine if you drop the attempts to fetch history for channels other than the current one.

**Steve Howell** · 2025-05-28 12:27 UTC

@EricGT It sounds like you are using the official Zulip synchronous Python bindings, but you might want to consider just using something like `aiohttp`if you want to optimize how you fetch a bunch of data.  It's quite straightforward to do, and you can still use all the good documentation for the Python API to know what kind of parameters to pass and what kind of responses to expect.  In my case, for example, I immediately slurp all my data into pydantic (not shown, and a bit off topic).  Anyway, here is some example code that I use:

~~~ py
    @asynccontextmanager
    async def post(self, url_ending, data):
        async with aiohttp.ClientSession() as session:
            url = self.url_prefix + url_ending
            async with session.post(url, auth=self.auth, data=data) as response:
                yield response
~~~

**Alex Vandiver** · 2025-05-28 15:08 UTC

Rate-limiting is by user, except when it's unauthenticated, in which case it's by IP.  Because `alex@example.com` on `foo.zulipchat.com` is a different "user" than `alex@example.com` on `bar.zulipchat.com`, the rate limit is server-specific for logged-in pages.

You can see all of the default rate limit rules [here](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/main/zproject/default_settings.py#L263-L339).  We don't have any long-duration rate-limits currently, so I would not advise making an extra account for that purpose.  Parallel requests will not help at all.  We have logs which could track folks hitting rate-limits, but that's not a thing that you should worry about.

**Steve Howell** · 2025-05-28 15:15 UTC

Just to clarify what happens with parallel requests, here is my understanding.  The rate-limiting code has no notion of how many parallel requests are being processed; it only knows how many requests have arrived in the last relevant interval.  The good news is that you can parallelize requests to decrease the overall amount of time that it takes you to get your data.  The bad news is that you can't fire them all of at once--you need to rate-limit sending the requests.  And you have to be a bit conservative in your staggering, since I may have fancy code on the client that knows to send exactly N requests per second, but they may still arrive at the server with a burst.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-06-25 17:44 UTC

I think the feeling might be that giving crack times in the password strength meter is not obviously helpful UI. Nobody else seems to be doing that, and ultimately I don't think it is the right number for explaining risk to an end user.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-06-25 17:45 UTC

Both because actual crackers use highly parallel code, or even specialized hardware, to try to crack a password, so for example, "100 years" might actually be weak. And of course the password is only actually at risk if someone captures the hash; our rate limits will make anything but a truly terrible password that we outright reject hard to brute force remotely.

## quick renumber migrations

*2025-06-27 to 2025-06-30 · 8 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/quick.20renumber.20migrations/with/2206250)*

**Kunal Sharma** · 2025-06-27 10:17 UTC

I've often found it frustrating to renumber migrations after rebasing a PR. I mostly work on the settings side, where each commit typically adds 3 or more migrations, and recently I have worked on PRs with multiple settings in a single PR with more than 6 migrations divided over multiple commits, which makes renumbering even more cumbersome after rebasing.

I’m aware of `tools/renumber-migrations`, but it still requires manually specifying the order of migrations. When a PR has several migrations and is behind by more than a couple, the tool prompts for the order multiple times, making it even more inefficient than doing it manually.

Has anyone else faced the same issue? Or is there a better way to do this?

I was thinking it could be useful to add a flag to `tools/renumber-migrations` to automatically renumber all new migrations in the uncommitted changes and push them to the end of the migration tree.

**Alex Vandiver** · 2025-06-27 13:46 UTC

We [previously discussed](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/18-tools/topic/renumber-migrations.20gets.20stuck.20at.200501/near/1777705) using https://github.com/adamchainz/django-linear-migrations which is a little nicer -- but it needed a [PR](https://github.com/adamchainz/django-linear-migrations/pull/343) to be useful, which the maintainer never merged.  Might be worth poking at that more.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-06-27 20:15 UTC

@Rohan Gudimetla do you think you'd be up for picking that up again? I think usually busy maintainers are more excited about a proposal where one does the work as a proposal.

**Rohan Gudimetla** · 2025-06-27 20:27 UTC

Ya, sure I can work on a PR for it. The last PR's work involved user to use a flag `./manage.py makemigrations --new` when he makes migration for first time in a commit (to track users migrations in that branch). The maintainer felt it might be a burden for user to add the `--new` for every new branch.

I just needed feedback if maybe adding the flag automatically to user's local branch using:

```git
git config branch.$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD).migrationCreated true
```
might be a good idea. What do you think?

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-06-30 19:05 UTC

I suspect that sort of branch-level configuration, being invisible to users, would feel a bit annoying.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-06-30 19:06 UTC

Can you explain the reasoning for why you wanted this `--new` option? I feel like maybe we just need a better UX proposal here.

**Rohan Gudimetla** · 2025-06-30 19:16 UTC

the way the tool's current version works is it maintains and updates the `max_migration` number in a text file. So, when user makes a new migration using `makemigrations` it would update number, and when he rebases the migration is renumbered to the CURRENT CHANGE of max_migration.txt + 1. This would make sense only if a single migration exists in branch.

So what I proposed was we maintain a different txt file, which would note all the migrations a user adds in a branch to a text file. So when the branch is rebased and user rebases migrations, we can iterate and renumber each migration of INCOMING CHANGE as per the max number of CURRENT CHANGE of txt file. The problem is this would work properly only if we are able to wipe out the record of old migrations in the txt file when he makes a new migration.

This would require either some explicit command like `makemigrations --new` or some implicit state that says this is the first migration of the branch.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-06-30 19:31 UTC

Hmm. I feel like ideally we'd be able to identify the new migrations in the branch using `git` metadata.

``` typescript
export function is_emojis_only_message($content: JQuery): boolean {
    const $paragraphs = $content.find("p");

    if ($paragraphs.length === 0) {
        return false;
    }

    let i = 0;
    while (i < $paragraphs.length) {
        // Get each paragraph
        const $p = $paragraphs.eq(i);

        const $emojis = $p.find(".emoji");
        // Checks if there are any emojis in the message
        if ($emojis.length === 0) {
            return false;
        }

        // If there are emojis, we remove them from the content
        // And check if there is any text in the message
        const $pClone = $p.clone();
        $pClone.find(".emoji").remove();

        const text = $pClone.text().trim();

        if (text.length > 0) {
            return false;
        }

        i += 1;
    }

    return true;
}
```

## 📂Backticks get inserted on Ctrl-V in many situations #30954

*2025-07-28 to 2025-07-30 · 6 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/.F0.9F.93.82Backticks.20get.20inserted.20on.20Ctrl-V.20in.20many.20situations.20.2330954/with/2231821)*

**Newton Chung** · 2025-07-28 23:57 UTC

I think I have a better picture of this issue now, and made some steps towards building a solution. 

### 1. **Limitations of Marked.js for Code Block Detection**
* Marked.js (markdown render) only detects completed code blocks (with both opening and closing backticks). When an in-line code block is started, but not closed with another backtick, it is not treated as a code block. I will refer to these as **unclosed in-line blocks**.
* The desired behavior for this issue should also prevent inserting backticks when pasting in unclosed in-line code blocks.

### 2. **Existing Behavior**
* This works correctly for multi-line code blocks: no new backticks are added when pasting inside them.
* There is an additional check that prevents backticks, but *only* when pasting directly after a backtick.
[correct_behavior.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/23/XZ4YxRbX-xlrqkUYFq_j9dbG/Screenshot-2025-07-28-142402.png)
[correct_behavior.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/d9/5lBEyf1wJy3UmvPGf_mbLt-X/Screenshot-2025-07-28-142430.png)
* Backticks are inserted when pasting inside in-line code blocks, whether closed or unclosed.
[incorrect_behavior.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/4b/CDRXNhAQPM0EkAKxXynYnDX3/image.png)
[incorrect_behavior.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/96/97s4EkQC87Pm_QOWsawrvVHD/image.png)
* Rather than requiring the same number of backticks, Zulip's markdown parser allows in-line code spans to be closed with at least 1 backtick, regardless of how many opening backticks there are. The left-most opening backticks will be closed by the closing backticks, and everything else will be placed inside the code block. 
Ex: ``` This is an in-line code block with 3 opening backticks and 1 closing backtick. `

### 3. Changed(But still incomplete) Behavior
* When pasting inside a closed in-line code block, no backticks are added.
[image.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/40/_Rb-Q9NrZqIijBoaik3Nj-SD/image.png)
[image.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/41/3kuSSPQiMxzUyB7xJAicoApd/image.png)
[image.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/14/quIM-84sFAWIbJOZxetEeK3j/image.png)
* When pasting inside an unclosed in-line code block, new backticks are still added.

To implement the rest of the desired behavior, I was considering a heuristic approach like the counting backticks algorithm suggested earlier, as the markdown parser alone doesn't seem sufficient. Is my understanding correct?

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-07-29 00:06 UTC

@Newton Chung that message is super long, and time-consuming to read as a result; did you have AI generate it? If so, it's important to manage AI's habit of producing more text than anyone wants to read before sharing it..

I think you're also on the wrong track; isn't `turndown` what we the paste handler uses?

**Notification Bot** · 2025-07-29 00:07 UTC

2 messages were moved here from #**issues>📂Backticks get inserted on Ctrl-V in many situations #30954** by @Tim Abbott.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-07-29 00:07 UTC

Let's move this here, since it's not really about the user-facing problem or issue.

**Newton Chung** · 2025-07-29 19:31 UTC

Got it, thank you for the feedback. I'll keep it more concise next time. 

And looking into compose_paste.ts further, you're right. I found the logic for preventing backticks using turndown, and I think I have a better idea of where my solution needs to go. I'll follow up when I have an update!

## #2746: Add join/leave notifications for private channels

*2025-08-01 to 2025-08-05 · 5 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/.232746.3A.20Add.20join.2Fleave.20notifications.20for.20private.20channels/with/2235197)*

**Zied Boughdir** · 2025-08-01 20:19 UTC

## Issue #2746: Add join/leave notifications for private channels

### **What is this issue?**

This issue requests adding IRC-style join/leave notifications specifically for **private channels only**. The feature should:

1. **Send notifications when users join private channels** - showing who added whom
2. **Send notifications when users leave private channels** - showing who left
3. **Use the Notification Bot** to send these messages
4. **Send messages to the "channel events" topic** in the affected channel
5. **Only apply to private channels** (not public channels to avoid spam)

### **Specific Requirements (from the issue update):**

The notification messages should say:
* `@user1 added @user2 to this channel.` (for joins)
* `@user left this channel.` (for leaves)

### **Current State Analysis**

From my code analysis, I found:

1. **Topic name**: `"channel events"` is defined as `Realm.STREAM_EVENTS_NOTIFICATION_TOPIC_NAME`
2. **Notification pattern**: Existing channel events (like name changes, description changes) already use this pattern
3. **Key functions**:
  * `internal_send_stream_message()` - sends messages to channels
  * `channel_events_topic_name()` - gets the correct topic name
  * `get_system_bot(settings.NOTIFICATION_BOT, realm.id)` - gets the notification bot
  * `silent_mention_syntax_for_user()` - creates user mentions
4. **Where to implement**:
  * **Join notifications**: In `bulk_add_subscriptions()` in `zerver/actions/streams.py`
  * **Leave notifications**: In `bulk_remove_subscriptions()` in `zerver/actions/streams.py`

## Failing Puppeteer tests in PR #35723

*2025-08-28 to 2025-09-04 · 2 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/Failing.20Puppeteer.20tests.20in.20PR.20.2335723/with/2250730)*

**Arielle** · 2025-08-28 00:01 UTC

@Qilan  and I have been working on [PR #35723](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/35723) which adds a “frequently used” section to the emoji picker. As part of this feature, we updated the rebuild_catalog function in emoji_picker.ts to fetch data from the database instead of using hardcoded values. This function was also refactored to use async/await.

We are currently having some difficulty getting the Puppeteer tests to pass reliably and have been getting nondeterministic failures.

To address this, we added additional waitForSelector calls as suggested in the documentation. This seems to improve test reliability locally, but we're still seeing failures in GitHub CI.

Our current hypotheses are:
- The introduction of async/await introduced a race condition, and our implantation is in need of refactor.
- The new database calls need optimization.

We're continuing to investigate, but any suggestions would be greatly appreciated.

**Karl Stolley** · 2025-10-02 13:47 UTC

If you look at some of the styles in your browser’s inspector, that should help you locate the correct files—which will be `.css`, not `.scss`.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-10-02 16:53 UTC

It's quite likely the CSS you're looking for is in `node_modules`, i.e. something provided by Altcha upstream. **Rakshit** · 2025-10-03 16:49 UTC

I was working on issue #36076 and also filed a PR #36100 as mentioned in the issue i need to make the word "channel"/"archived channel" link go to the "general" setting panel for that channel , **if user is allow to view the channel**

**Rakshit** · 2025-10-03 16:58 UTC

I figured out the logic to check if the user has permission to view the channel is located in the `stream_data.ts` file
```javascript
export let has_content_access = (sub: StreamSubscription): boolean => {
    if (sub.is_web_public) {
        return true;
    }

    if (page_params.is_spectator) {
        return false;
    }

    if (sub.subscribed) {
        return true;
    }

    if (!has_metadata_access(sub)) {
        return false;
    }

    if (current_user.is_guest) {
        /* istanbul ignore next */
        return false;
    }

    if (has_content_access_via_group_permissions(sub)) {
        return true;
    }

    if (sub.invite_only) {
        return false;
    }

    // We do not do an admin check here since having admin permissions
    // to a private channel does not give user access to that channel's
    // content.

    return true;
};

```

**Rakshit** · 2025-10-03 16:59 UTC

The [documentation](https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/production/video-calls.html#zoom) that I could find also doesn't talk about this endpoint.

Did I miss something?

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-11-04 18:56 UTC

Yeah the Zoom marketplace has a feature where users can inside Zoom deauthorize the app. This endpoint is a required endpoint for Zoom to notify us that the user did so, in case we need to update any state on our side for that. I don't remember what information Zoom gives us in that request, but I suspect it does not suffice to easily look up which user to delete the `zoom_token` property from, so we just return a success.

We should probably add a comment explaining this.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-11-04 18:57 UTC

https://developers.zoom.us/docs/platform/auth/deauthorization/ is Zoom's documentation for it.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-11-04 18:58 UTC

I think we could probably make it work if we:
- Switched to ` jsonb` field.
- Started storing the `zoom_user_id` as well.
- Had our deauthorize endpoint find the record to delete using that `zoom_user_id`.

**Apoorva Pendse** · 2025-11-10 16:46 UTC

One thing I noticed is that this change will require adding new scopes to our existing General OAuth app integrations. The [Get a User](https://developers.zoom.us/docs/api/users/#tag/users/get/users/{userId}) endpoint requires additional scopes for the access token to retrieve the zoom user’s `id`, which we will need later if the user decides to deauthorize our app.

Maybe we can try to handle this gracefully by silently failing and skipping `id` storage when the access token lacks the required scope.

But does it seem worthwhile to implement and maintain this?
The stale tokens will anyways be deleted on [logout](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/b571e33c54f44a36bf11f684cceb8a843322eb09/zerver/signals.py#L115).

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-11-10 16:50 UTC

Hmm. It's probably not worth a transition in what scopes we ask for over this, but maybe worth leaving a comment next to the scopes list about this potential change; if we need to increase scopes later for some reason, we might want to bundle this in.

**Apoorva Pendse** · 2025-11-10 17:30 UTC

Noted in #36502, commit 5.

## Styling conflict with pill-container on user profile modal

*2025-11-12 to 2025-11-13 · 3 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/Styling.20conflict.20with.20pill-container.20on.20user.20profile.20modal/with/2297963)*

**Raj Vishwakarma** · 2025-11-12 09:43 UTC

Hi team, I'm running into a styling issue while working on [#36301](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/issues/36301)

**The Problem:-**

The  `input_pill.ts` that builds the pill widget need  `.pill-container` class .This class is also used in the compose box, where it has global CSS (a background, border, and padding) to make it look like an input box.

This works great for the compose box, but in the user profile modal, it messes the pill styling and adds unwanted styling.(refer the screenshot)
[image.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/ff/4YTddsjRr2d7zJmF37g0I0VB/image.png)


**The Options:-**

I see two ways to fix this, and I'm not sure which approach is preferred:
**Option 1: CSS Override**
* We can add a small, targeted CSS override in the `input_pill.css` file.
  
* The rule would be something like `.custom_user_field .pill-container { background: none; border: none; padding: 0; box-shadow:none}`.
  
* **Pro:** It's a simple, fast, and low-risk fix. It only affects the pill container *inside* the user profile and won't break it anywhere else.
  
* **Con:** It's a CSS override, which isn't always the cleanest solution.
  
**Option 2: Create a New Container Class & Modify TypeScript**
* We could use a new class in the HTML template (e.g., `profile-pill-container`).
  
* Then, we'd have to modify the `custom_profile_fields_ui.ts` to look for this new class.
  
* **Pro:** This is a "cleaner" solution that decouples the profile styling from the compose box styling.
  
* **Con:** This seems much more complex, as it requires changing the core pill widget's **TypeScript** behavior.
  
but since @Sahil Batra left a review on the PR suggesting to use the existing CSS classes, I am not really sure which approach I should go for.
[image.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/b2/TjRvIPAtWZ4QhhiqSiFbFab0/image.png)
PR link:- [#36439](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/36439)


Need help from maintainers 
Thanks!

**Karl Stolley** · 2025-11-12 21:23 UTC

I think the `.pill-container` class is confusing. The use of a `.user-pill-container` class in the search bar is probably a good example, but it would be useful to distinguish between inputs and input-like things that truly *contain* pills, versus some kind of presentational chrome that's just put around pills that are non-interactive and simply displayed.

### **Current Search Behavior - Test Results:**
#### **What Currently Works:**

1. **Prefix Matching** - The system correctly matches starting characters
  
-   Example: "p" finds all users starting with p (Peter, Paul, Priya)
-   Example: "pet'' finds "Peter" (exact prefix match)

    
#### **Identified Limitations:**

1. **Typo Handling Not Supported**
  
-    Test: "petr" (typo for "peter") - Result: No matches found   
-    Test: "jhon" (typo for "john") - Result: No matches found

    
2. **Partial/Substring Matching Not Available**
  
-   Test: "eter" (for "peter") - Result: No matches - only prefix works
-   Test: "ohn" (for "john") - Result: No matches

    
3. **Similar Name Matching Not Supported**
  
-    Test: "jon" (for "john") - Result: No matches
-    Test: "michal" (for "michael") - Result: No matches

  
### **Proposed Solution:**

Implement fuzzy search algorithm to:
- Maintain existing prefix matching capabilities
- Add tolerance for spelling errors and typos
- Enable matching anywhere in the name not just prefix only

1. Does this analysis align with your understanding of the current search system?

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-12-03 18:48 UTC

@Yash Atkari if you can figure out how you ended up doing that, it would be helpful. We very explicitly document that you need a clean environment for WSL, and I'd be curious if there's something we could tweak in the documentation that would have helped you not encounter this failure.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2025-12-03 20:08 UTC

#36888 will catch this mistake earlier during `provision`.

**Yash Atkari** · 2025-12-04 00:48 UTC

SOLVED!
I had NVM installed in my WSL environment, which was forcing `run-dev` to use my local Node v20 instead of Zulip's internal version.

1. I disabled NVM (commented out lines in `~/.bashrc`).
 
2. I removed the manually installed node binaries (`/usr/local/bin/node`).
 
3. I ran `rm -rf node_modules` and re-ran `./tools/provision`.
  
The provision script successfully downloaded the correct Node version, and the server is now running perfectly. 
Thanks for the help!

## Optimize database queries in message sending code path when

*2025-12-18 to 2025-12-19 · 9 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/Optimize.20database.20queries.20in.20message.20sending.20code.20path.20when/with/2330723)*

**Yash Rana** · 2025-12-18 11:23 UTC

# Assign this issue to me username - yash-rana0101

## The Problem

When someone sends a 1-to-1 direct message in Zulip, the system is making **3 unnecessary database queries** that slow things down. At large scale (hundreds of thousands of users), these extra queries create performance bottlenecks.

## Why Extra Queries Happen

Think of it like this:

1. **First check**: "Does a conversation between Alice and Bob already exist?" (Query #1)
2. **Second check**: "Who are the participants in this conversation?" (Query #2)
3. **Third check**: "Who should I show as recipients when displaying this message?" (Query #3)

The problem? **We already know it's Alice and Bob from the very beginning!** But the system keeps asking the database "who's in this conversation?" multiple times.

## The Smart Solution

### Core Insight
**Stop asking questions we already know the answers to.**

When Alice sends a message to Bob:
* We know Alice is sending it
* We know Bob is receiving it
* We don't need to ask the database "who's involved?" - it's Alice and Bob!

### How It Works (Step by Step)
**Step 1: Remember What We Know**
When we first determine the message is between Alice and Bob, we write this down (cache it) right on the message object itself - like putting a sticky note that says "this message is between User #123 (Alice) and User #456 (Bob)".
**Step 2: Read the Sticky Note Instead of Asking Again**
Later, when the code needs to know "who's in this conversation?", instead of querying the database, it just reads the sticky note we attached earlier.
**Step 3: Reuse Information**
When displaying the message, use that same sticky note instead of making another database trip.

## Scalability Advantages

### At Small Scale (1,000 users)
* Saves 2-3 database queries per message
* Faster message delivery (2-5 milliseconds improvement)

### At Large Scale (100,000+ users)
* **30,000 fewer database queries per second** (assuming 10,000 messages/sec)
* **15% reduction in database load**
* Less database connection pool exhaustion
* Better response times during peak usage
* Lower infrastructure costs

### Why It Scales Well

1. **No extra memory**: The sticky note (cache) is tiny - just two numbers (16 bytes)
2. **No new bottlenecks**: We're not adding complexity, we're removing unnecessary work
3. **Works with existing code**: Minimal changes to the codebase
4. **Backwards compatible**: Old and new code can coexist during migration

## The Three Eliminated Queries
**Query #1 Eliminated**: "Get the list of users in this DM group"
* **Why unnecessary**: We passed Alice and Bob's IDs to the function - we already know!
* **Saved**: 1 database round trip
**Query #2 Eliminated**: "Get user profile IDs for notification settings"
* **Why unnecessary**: Same answer as Query #1 - it's still Alice and Bob!
* **Saved**: 1 database round trip
**Query #3 Eliminated**: "Get user info for displaying recipients"
* **Why unnecessary**: Still the same Alice and Bob we've known all along!
* **Saved**: 1 database round trip

## Real-World Impact

### Before Optimization
User sends message → 
  Ask DB: "Does DM group exist?" → 
  Ask DB: "Who's in it?" → 
  Process message → 
  Ask DB: "Who's in it again?" → 
  Display message
  
Total: 19 database queries

### After Optimization
User sends message → 
  Ask DB: "Does DM group exist?" → 
  Remember: "It's Alice & Bob" → 
  Process message (read sticky note) → 
  Display message (read sticky note again)
  
Total: 16-17 database queries

## Why This Matters for Lakhs of Users

At massive scale, every saved database query multiplies:
* **1 saved query** × 10,000 messages/second = **10,000 saved queries/second**
* **3 saved queries** × 10,000 messages/second = **30,000 saved queries/second**

index c90c246429..b807eff3a3 100755

         elif test_template_db_status == "current":

index be51651f54..970d969b22 100755
--- a/tools/setup/postgresql-init-dev-db

**Adarsh Pandey** · 2026-01-08 21:20 UTC

**Tim Abbott** · 2026-01-08 21:55 UTC

What editor technology are you using? From a technical standpoint, there's two things that need to work for it to hot reload for you.
- The filesystem inside the Docker container needs to see that file is updated and trigger the code watching for changes to run and hot reload.
- The save in your editor needs to trigger the filesystem inside your Docker container to see the file has changed.

I expect the problem is that second step isn't happening. You can probably test by running `touch <path>` inside the container, or editing the file inside the container using a terminal editor, and seeing if it hot reloads then.

def fix_spoilers_in_html(
    fragment: lxml.html.HtmlElement,
    language: str,
    message_url: str | None = None,
) -> None:
    with override_language(language):
        spoiler_title: str = _("Open Zulip to see the spoiler content")
    spoilers = fragment.find_class("spoiler-block")
    for spoiler in spoilers:
        header = spoiler.find_class("spoiler-header")[0]
        spoiler_content = spoiler.find_class("spoiler-content")[0]
        header_content = header.find("p")
        if header_content is None:
            # Create a new element to append the spoiler to)
            header_content = e.P()
            header.append(header_content)
        else:
            # Add a space.
            rear = header_content[-1] if len(header_content) else header_content
            rear.tail = (rear.tail or "") + " "
        if message_url is not None:
            # Make only the "Open Zulip" part of the text a link to the message.
            span_elem = e.SPAN(**e.CLASS("spoiler-title"), title=spoiler_title)
            span_elem.text = " "
            link_text_prefix = "Open Zulip"
            if spoiler_title.startswith(link_text_prefix):
                link_text = link_text_prefix
                suffix = spoiler_title[len(link_text_prefix) :]
                link_elem = e.A(link_text, href=message_url)
                span_elem.append(link_elem)
                link_elem.tail = suffix
            else:
                # Fallback for non-English translations: link the full text.
                link_elem = e.A(spoiler_title, href=message_url)
                span_elem.append(link_elem)
        else:
            span_elem = e.SPAN(
                f" {spoiler_title}",
                **e.CLASS("spoiler-title"),
                title=spoiler_title,
            )
        header_content.append(span_elem)
        header.drop_tag()
        spoiler_content.drop_tree()

 ) -> dict[str, str | Markup]:

- Reproduced on: chat.zulip.org (production) ✅
- Also in: dev environment ✅

**Steve Howell** · 2026-01-10 13:25 UTC

@Tanaya Pawar Hello!  I'm actually the original author of the poll widget, but I'm no longer in charge of new features for it, so take my comments with a grain of salt.

I consider the current "bug" to actually be a somewhat intentional feature.  For example, if you are truly using the widget for brainstorming (and I can say with authority that was at least one of the original intentions), then it's reasonable to just open up a poll and let the other folks suggest ideas.

Having said that, I concede it can also lead to a confusing experience, so I am not dogmatic about resisting change here.

Before you start any development, you will want to monitor #**frontend>widgets refactor** to make sure some of my recent changes hit the main branch.

**Steve Howell** · 2026-01-10 13:27 UTC

There's a possible compromise where we still allow the poll author to provide zero options and just clean up some of the messaging for the other folks who see the poll.  And maybe make the poll author get a slightly more stern warning that they may have accidentally created a zero-option poll.

```
(zulip-server) vagrant@40d5d4143783:/srv/zulip$ tools/lint --skip-provision-check

```

These all seem to be correct errors to me (the commit messages do not match the defined rules).  Is this expected?  If you run `./tools/test-all`, it will fail because the lint command failed, blocking the run of the other test suites.

**Tim Abbott** · 2026-02-03 00:20 UTC

The way we use `gitlint`, it should only run tests on your commits not already in `main`.

**Tim Abbott** · 2026-02-03 00:21 UTC

There's no way to fix commits that are already merged -- rewriting Git history is a big nono.

**Robert Dyer 🎓** · 2026-02-03 01:21 UTC

If you just run `./tools/lint` it will trigger gitlint on all commits, not just commits off of `main`.  This particular clone of the repo only has a `main` branch and I have no local edits/changes on it.

Granted, you really only need to lint changed files, and that is what the Git hooks do.  But the lint command is also run from `./tools/test-all`, so if you want to run the full test suite, you get failures here.  This prevents further test suites from running (and since linting goes first, it really means the test-all command will not run any other tests).  So moving forward, the `./tools/test-all` command is essentially broken/useless.

These are the offending commits:

https://github.com/zulip/zulip/commit/06df5bf7e71f09ae4e307f19e3079c04b921057b
https://github.com/zulip/zulip/commit/67d30fe43f5749062c85e3cf742a3cd131489241
https://github.com/zulip/zulip/commit/c0554b6add29e189e46ef27f9825044afddfa070
https://github.com/zulip/zulip/commit/ddbaf7c6ac8774af243f5ff91c8a27a45842c12b
https://github.com/zulip/zulip/commit/c4adc7e741105dac3cdff5a238630b8ea5958896

They are all within the last 4 days.  The messages do appear to violate the gitlint rules.  So at the very least, it seems like bad commit messages are getting through the review process.  Or perhaps the commit message linter rules were relaxed, but if so, then the linter config was not updated to reflect that.

A possible solution, assuming these were just bad commits that snuck through, is to update the test-all command so that it excludes `gitlint` when calling the linter.

**Tim Abbott** · 2026-02-04 20:06 UTC

We don't consider `gitlint` to be a high signal linter. We integrated it because it's better than nothing for helping contributors avoid mistakes when drafting their commits. But, for example, it doesn't have a way to approve long URLs appearing in commit messages, which is how 2/5 of those fail.

(Another put the `.` inside the `"` rather than outside, which is not important for human usage of commit messages)

**Tim Abbott** · 2026-02-04 20:07 UTC

It might be reasonable to pull it out of the linter options used with `tools/test-all`, and run it directly on just changes since the upstream main branch? Not sure.

**Robert Dyer 🎓** · 2026-02-04 20:43 UTC

It is understandably a low-priority linter.  But it does effectively make the `test-all` script completely useless moving forward.

I would encourage adding an exclude for gitlint into `./tools/test-all` so that the other linters still run, gitlint won't cause the first command to fail, and then the other test suites will be able to also run.  If not, you might as well remove that script, as moving forward, it will never work due to those five (and possibly more in the future) bad commits.

I personally only use that script to verify I have a working dev environment.  Then from that point forward, I run specific linters/test suites and never run that script again.  This is also how I encourage other developers on the project (e.g., my students) to verify they have working environments.

This is the current version I use of the script:

```diff
diff --git a/tools/test-all b/tools/test-all
index c9c5a03a90..15d2cc140a 100755
--- a/tools/test-all
+++ b/tools/test-all
@@ -49,7 +49,7 @@ echo
 run ./tools/check-provision "${forcearg[@]}"

 # ci/backend
-run ./tools/lint --groups=backend "${forcearg[@]}"
+run ./tools/lint --groups=backend --skip=gitlint "${forcearg[@]}"
 run ./tools/test-tools
 run ./tools/test-backend --include-webhooks --ban-console-output "${forcearg[@]}"
 run ./tools/test-migrations
@@ -68,7 +68,7 @@ run uv lock --check
 # run ./tools/test-queue-worker-reload

 # ci/frontend
-run ./tools/lint --groups=frontend "${forcearg[@]}"
+run ./tools/lint --groups=frontend --skip=gitlint "${forcearg[@]}"
 run ./tools/test-js-with-node
 run ./tools/check-schemas
 run ./manage.py makemessages --locale en
```
```

origin	git@github.com:[MY-ORG-NAME]/zulip.git (push)

```

**Robert Dyer 🎓** · 2026-02-04 22:21 UTC

My origin merges `upstream` daily. I fetched before running the lint command.

Is the implication here that you guys are not seeing similar behavior?

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2026-02-04 22:24 UTC

Er sorry, I meant `git fetch upstream`.

No, it works for me. Note that it’s not enough to merge things from upstream to your fork *separately*; you need to `git fetch upstream` *in this Git working tree*.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2026-02-04 22:26 UTC

The other kind of problem that developers sometimes run into is that they accidentally rebased upstream commits onto their local commits rather than the other way around; in that case gitlint will treat them as new commits.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2026-02-04 22:30 UTC

If you see any upstream commits in `git log upstream/main..HEAD`, then one of those is likely the reason.

**Robert Dyer 🎓** · 2026-02-04 22:52 UTC

Ah, I didn't realize your script was comparing the local branch against the `upstream` (and not my `origin`).  So that is why it was detecting "changed" commits (including those 5) and running `gitlint` on them!  Thanks @Anders Kaseorg !

So then it is not necessary to skip `gitlint` in the `test-all` script (though perhaps that is still a good idea, if the commit messages are not being strictly enforced).

## sender-side link preview removal

*2026-02-19 to 2026-02-27 · 10 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/sender-side.20link.20preview.20removal/with/2385931)*

**Aadyot Nandan S** · 2026-02-19 20:15 UTC

I’ve been digging into #19466 - Allow link previews to be removed from a message, and the earlier PR (#21509). 

Some previous discussions for this issue happened in [this thread](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/137-feedback/topic/Remove.20individual.20preview.20of.20linked.20website.28s.29.3F/with/2322603). I’m starting a fresh topic here to focus specifically on the data model and implementation approach before moving forward.

From the issue and CZO discussions, the intended behavior is sender-side, per-message, per-URL, and global - if the sender removes a preview, it should be hidden for everyone.

The earlier PR stored this as a per-user `UserMessage` boolean flag. That would make the behavior user-scoped and hide all previews in the message at once. Here, the sender is deciding how the message renders for all readers, and the requirement is per-link control within a message. That’s message-owned state rather than per-recipient flags.

I also looked at `SubMessage`, but that subsystem is tightly coupled to interactive widgets (polls, etc.). This is static rendering metadata, so it seems cleaner to keep it directly on the message.

The approach I’m leaning toward is adding a nullable `hidden_preview_urls` TextField (JSON list) to `AbstractMessage`, similar to `edit_history`. Most messages would have this as NULL.

When the sender removes a preview:
* Append the URL to `hidden_preview_urls`
  
* Re-render using the same `content`
  
* Pass hidden URLs as `None` in `url_embed_data` so the renderer skips generating the preview block
  
* Use the existing embedded-data update path so `rendered_content` updates and an `update_message` event is emitted with `rendering_only: True`
  

This would extend the existing `PATCH /messages/{id}` endpoint with a parameter for the URL to hide, reusing the same message edit permission checks.

That should suppress the preview without triggering another embed fetch and without showing an “edited” indicator. Since this goes through the normal `update_message` flow, the UI should update without additional frontend logic.


Before I start coding this -  @Tim Abbott , @Alya Abbott  does this data model and re-render approach look reasonable?

**Aadyot Nandan S** · 2026-02-23 13:25 UTC

@Tim Abbott   - just following up on this when you have a moment. I’d like to start implementing soon and want to make sure the direction looks right before I proceed.

**Notification Bot** · 2026-02-23 19:19 UTC

This topic was moved here from #**design>sender-side link preview removal** by @Alya Abbott.

**Alya Abbott** · 2026-02-23 19:46 UTC

@Aadyot Nandan S Can you describe the core question more concisely, being sure to follow the AI use policy? 

For implementation details, you should go ahead and try them and then put up a PR with the actual code. That's a far more efficient format to review them in.

**Aadyot Nandan S** · 2026-02-25 06:18 UTC

Understood - thanks. I’ll open up a PR and we can look at the implementation details there.

**Aadyot Nandan S** · 2026-02-25 06:20 UTC

Concisely, I see three possible approaches for #19466 (hide link previews):

1) The previous PR #21509 used a per-message boolean. That works, but it makes the behavior all-or-nothing. Either all previews in the message are hidden or none are. It doesn’t support per-link control when there are multiple previews in the same message.

2) SubMessage - I explored this in the code. SubMessages seem to be used mainly for widget-related things (polls, etc.) and interactive state. Link previews are just part of the rendered message content, so using SubMessage here felt a bit off.

3) Add a new nullable field on the Message model (e.g., hidden_preview_urls). It would stay NULL in the common case, and only be populated when the sender hides a specific preview. On hide, we store the URL and re-render the message without that preview. To me, this feels clearer since the state just lives with the message itself.

**Aadyot Nandan S** · 2026-02-25 06:21 UTC

There might be some concern about adding a new column, but since it’s NULL for almost all messages, it wouldn’t really take up much storage in practice.

On the UI side, I’m currently using an "x" button on each preview (shown on hover), and the permissions follow the same rules as message content editing.

**Aadyot Nandan S** · 2026-02-25 06:39 UTC

I’m currently testing this across different preview types (standard links, YouTube, inline images) to make sure the behavior is consistent.

**Aadyot Nandan S** · 2026-02-27 11:37 UTC

I've opened PR #38175 with the implementation.

It uses the third approach - `hidden_preview_urls` on the Message model to allow per-preview control. Ready for review.

**Aadyot Nandan S** · 2026-02-27 13:54 UTC

One clarification @Alya Abbott - Since #11773 tracks several related preview-behavior issues, is there a preferred order in which these should land? 

I'm also interested in working on #21766 - recipient-side hide/unhide. Would it make sense to start on that while #38175 is under review?

I looked into it  and I think this issue has been solved in [commit  5583ddd](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/commit/5583ddd3bf274d8ad830a8cc1cb028631ca0f355). 
```javascript
export let message_send_error = (message_id: number, error_response: string): void => {
    // Error sending message, show inline
    const message = message_store.get(message_id)!;
    message.failed_request = true;
    message.show_slow_send_spinner = false;

    show_message_failed(message_id, error_response);
};
```
```javascript
function show_message_failed(message_id: number, _failed_msg: string): void {
    // Failed to send message, so display inline retry/cancel
    message_live_update.update_message_in_all_views(message_id, ($row) => {
        $row.find(".slow-send-spinner").addClass("hidden");
        const $message_controls = $row.find(".message_controls");
        $message_controls.html(render_message_controls_failed_msg());
    });
```

In this commit dynamic rendering was added for failed messages, so when there is an error in sending message then only the `cancel/retry ` ui template is rendered

## rootless podman

*2026-03-14 to 2026-04-05 · 5 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/rootless.20podman/with/2409721)*

**kousu 🦦** · 2026-03-14 20:40 UTC

I am trying to set up a development environment using podman and the docker-podman shim since I already have it installed and it's lighter than docker.

I have vagrant 2.4.9 and podman 5.8.0 and I'm on ArchLinux. My subuid(5) is set up properly (and I use `docker run` without sudo fairly often):

```
[kousu@laptop zulip]$ grep -E . /etc/sub{u,g}id
/etc/subuid:kousu:100000:65536
/etc/subgid:kousu:100000:65536
```

Naively, I followed [the guide](https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/stable/development/setup-recommended.html) hoping the shim would just work.

It got pretty far but failed at

```
==> default: Running provisioner: shell...
    default: Running: /tmp/vagrant-shell20260314-3643-zj2q3n
    default: + set -e
    default: + set -o pipefail
    default: + '[' '!' '' ']'
    default: + sudo ln -nsf /srv/zulip/tools/setup/dev-motd /etc/update-motd.d/99-zulip-dev
    default: + sudo rm -f /etc/update-motd.d/10-help-text /etc/update-motd.d/99-bento
    default: + sudo dpkg --purge landscape-common
    default: dpkg: warning: ignoring request to remove landscape-common which isn't installed
    default: + sudo dpkg-divert --add --rename /etc/default/motd-news
    default: Adding 'local diversion of /etc/default/motd-news to /etc/default/motd-news.distrib'
    default: + sudo sh -c 'echo ENABLED=0 > /etc/default/motd-news'
    default: + grep -q LC_ALL=C.UTF-8 /etc/default/locale
    default: + echo LC_ALL=C.UTF-8
    default: + sudo tee -a /etc/default/locale
    default: LC_ALL=C.UTF-8
    default: + export SKIP_VENV_SHELL_WARNING=1
    default: + SKIP_VENV_SHELL_WARNING=1
    default: + set +x
    default: The vagrant user is unable to write to the zulip directory.
    default: To fix this, run the following commands on the host machine:
    default:     vagrant halt -f
    default:     rm -rf /PATH/TO/ZULIP/CLONE/.vagrant
    default:     sudo chown -R 1000:$(id -g) /PATH/TO/ZULIP/CLONE
    default: Replace /PATH/TO/ZULIP/CLONE with the path to where zulip code is cloned.
    default: You can resume setting up your vagrant environment by running:
    default:     vagrant up
```

[(full log here)](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/e0/-VoeLAbjsnJnatWbgejRFs3o/vagrant-up-rootless-1.txt)

Eventually I realized that the problem is the way rootless containers map UIDs: given my subuid file, container UID n = system UID (100000-1)+n in all cases EXCEPT for my personal UID; that one gets mapped to root (0).

```
[kousu@laptop zulip]$ vagrant ssh
Welcome to Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS (GNU/Linux 6.19.6-arch1-1 x86_64)

This is the Zulip development environment.  Popular commands:
* tools/provision - Update the development environment
* tools/run-dev - Run the development server
* tools/lint - Run the linter (quick and catches many problems)
* tools/test-* - Run tests (use --help to learn about options)

Read https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/testing/testing.html to learn
how to run individual test suites so that you can get a fast debug cycle.

vagrant@4bdf7ba1b209:~$ whoami
vagrant
vagrant@4bdf7ba1b209:~$ ls -ldh /srv/zulip/
drwxr-xr-x 25 root root 4.0K Mar 14 19:39 /srv/zulip/
``` 

---

I found this solution, use podman to chown the source folder to the expected container UID:

```
mkdir -p .vagrant
podman unshare chown -R 1000:1000 .  # everything owned by containerized vagrant user
podman unshare chown -R 0:0 .vagrant  # but not this one
vagrant up --provider=docker  # succeeds!
```


Finally fix up my permissions externally so I can use my out-of-container editors.
```
sudo groupadd -g 100999 -U $USER vagrant-podman  # grant me access; I have to log in again after doing this
sudo chmod -R g+w .
```

This works but it's a little inelegant.  Any file written by Zulip is going to be owned by host UID 100999. I'm going to constantly be having to re-run chown and chmod -R to keep things sensible. I wonder if there's a better way.

---

I tried [setting VAGRANT_UID=0](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/bbc7d4b7378eb17ff1ba48f2f5de2125b0f6748f/Vagrantfile#L69)

```diff
[kousu@allium zulip]$ git diff
diff --git a/Vagrantfile b/Vagrantfile
index 6824b09..b2e5908 100644
--- a/Vagrantfile
+++ b/Vagrantfile
@@ -66,7 +66,7 @@ Vagrant.configure("2") do |config|
   config.vm.provider "docker" do |d, override|
     override.vm.box = nil
     d.build_dir = File.join(__dir__, "tools", "setup", "dev-vagrant-docker")
-    d.build_args = ["--build-arg", "VAGRANT_UID=#{Process.uid}"]
+    d.build_args = ["--build-arg", "VAGRANT_UID=0"]
     if !ubuntu_mirror.empty?
       d.build_args += ["--build-arg", "UBUNTU_MIRROR=#{ubuntu_mirror}"]
     end
```

but this failed almost immediately with

```
    default: useradd: UID 0 is not unique
    default: Error: building at STEP "RUN dpkg-divert --add --rename /bin/systemctl     && curl -fLsS --retry 3 -o /bin/systemctl 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gdraheim/docker-systemctl-replacement/v1.5.9063/files/docker/systemctl3.py'     && echo '1744aa7281159668d51fc97e57d834b6f116da10796f7f3352de48ad0cbba5b2  /bin/systemctl' | sha256sum -c     && chmod +x /bin/systemctl     && ln -nsf /bin/true /usr/sbin/policy-rc.d     && mkdir -p /run/sshd     && ln -ns /lib/systemd/system/postgresql@.service /etc/systemd/system/multi-user.target.wants/postgresql@14-main.service     && useradd -ms /bin/bash -u "$VAGRANT_UID" vagrant     && mkdir -m 700 ~vagrant/.ssh     && curl -fLsS --retry 3 -o ~vagrant/.ssh/authorized_keys 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hashicorp/vagrant/be7876d83644aa6bdf7f951592fdc681506bcbe6/keys/vagrant.pub'     && chown -R vagrant: ~vagrant/.ssh     && echo 'vagrant ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL' > /etc/sudoers.d/vagrant": while running runtime: exit status 4
```

I tried setting it to 1001

```diff
diff --git a/Vagrantfile b/Vagrantfile
index 6824b09..5e85cd5 100644
--- a/Vagrantfile
+++ b/Vagrantfile
@@ -66,7 +66,7 @@ Vagrant.configure("2") do |config|
   config.vm.provider "docker" do |d, override|

-    d.build_args = ["--build-arg", "VAGRANT_UID=#{Process.uid}"]

but then I was just in the same situation as before and had to

```

Could I maybe add some flag to [this line](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/bbc7d4b7378eb17ff1ba48f2f5de2125b0f6748f/Vagrantfile#L21) in `Vagrantfile`

```
  config.vm.synced_folder ".", "/srv/zulip", docker_consistency: "z"
```

?
