**kousu 🦦** · 2026-03-15 00:43 UTC

I have a solution:

```diff
diff --git a/Vagrantfile b/Vagrantfile
index 6824b09..5525a5f 100644
--- a/Vagrantfile
+++ b/Vagrantfile
@@ -71,7 +71,27 @@ Vagrant.configure("2") do |config|
       d.build_args += ["--build-arg", "UBUNTU_MIRROR=#{ubuntu_mirror}"]
     end
     d.has_ssh = true
-    d.create_args = ["--ulimit", "nofile=1024:65536"]
+    d.create_args = ["--ulimit", "nofile=1024:65536",
+     # adjust the container => host user ID mapping so that
+     # instead of the default:
+     # - container root is host #{Process.uid}
+     # - container #{Process.uid} is 100000
+     # we have:
+     # - container root is host 100000
+     # - container #{Process.uid} is host #{Process.uid}
+     #
+     # This is double confusing because these parameters are
+     # relative to the mapping already imposed by /etc/subuid:
+     # 1000:0 means mapping container 1000 to subuid mapping 0 which is mapped to host 1000.
+     # TODO: compute these from Process.uid and reading /etc/subuid instead of assuming default values
+     "--uidmap", "0:100000:1000",
+     "--uidmap", "1000:0:1",
+     "--uidmap", "1001:101001:64535",
+     # ditto for groups
+     "--gidmap","0:100000:1000",
+     "--gidmap","1000:0:1",
+     "--gidmap", "1001:101001:64535"
+      ]
   end
 
   config.vm.provider "virtualbox" do |vb, override|
```

With this patch `vagrant up --provider=docker` runs successfully on rootless podman.

It a pretty tricky fix, assumes you're on Linux and you're UID 1000, and I haven't tested it with docker (I suspect it does not work with docker). But if anyone reading this also likes podman, take this and run with it. and maybe together we can get a patch worth submitting.

**Lauryn Menard** · 2026-03-24 14:02 UTC

**Abdallah Rabie** · 2026-03-24 14:24 UTC

Thank you Lauryn Menard for pointing that out. I took a deep dive into the server's `zerver/views/message_flags.py` and I think I found the source of the discrepancy:

1. The `mark_all_as_read` view (line 135) explicitly returns a `complete` boolean field.
  
2. However, the `update_message_flags_for_narrow` view (line 79) does NOT include a `complete` field in its response data.
  source Code:
```def mark_all_as_read(request: HttpRequest, user_profile: UserProfile) -> HttpResponse:
    request_notes = RequestNotes.get_notes(request)
    count = do_mark_all_as_read(user_profile, timeout=50)
    if count is None:
        return json_success(request, data={"complete": False})

    log_data_str = f"[{count} updated]"
    assert request_notes.log_data is not None
    request_notes.log_data["extra"] = log_data_str

    return json_success(request, data={"complete": True}) 
```

Since my PR #P909 refactors `mark_all_as_read` to use the batching logic of the narrow-based helper, the OpenAPI validator is catching the fact that the narrow-based response lacks the `complete` field required by the original `mark_all_as_read` schema.

This explains why the CI is throwing the `SchemaError`. I’ll adjust the helper to ensure it returns the fields expected by the legacy endpoint's schema."


## Implementation:Placeholders for deleted files in edit histry

*2026-03-27 to 2026-04-06 · 5 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/Implementation.3APlaceholders.20for.20deleted.20files.20in.20edit.20histry/with/2419930)*

**Ashu Rajput** · 2026-03-27 05:42 UTC

> Hi everyone! I’m working on [PR #37443](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/37443) which addresses [#36486](https://www.google.com/search?q=https://github.com/zulip/zulip/issues/36486&authuser=1). The goal is to show specific placeholders (image/video/file) when a file is deleted but still referenced in the message edit history.
> 
> **The Challenge:** Currently, the edit history DOM doesn't have MIME type metadata. My current PR uses a list of file extensions in the frontend to guess the type, but @amanagr rightly pointed out we should avoid tracking so many extensions manually.
> 
> We are looking for the best path forward:
> 
> * **Option A (Frontend):** Create a centralized mapping utility in the frontend (extension → MIME) to keep the logic clean but still "guess" based on the URL.
>   
> * **Option B (Backend/API):** Update the message edit history API to include MIME types for all referenced uploads so the client doesn't have to guess at all.
>   
> 
> Option B seems more robust long-term but is a larger change. I’d love some guidance on which direction the community prefers before I sink more time into the implementation!
> 
> Tagging @Aman (amanagr)  and @Alya Abbott  for context.

**Tim Abbott** · 2026-04-05 21:29 UTC

Option B seems very expensive, so I'd recommend A.

**Alex Vandiver** · 2026-04-06 14:59 UTC

We should never have app behaviour depend on the file extension, only the recorded mime-type.  File extensions are buggy and unreliable.

(please just use our linkifiers, so typing #36486, instead of accidentally constructing Google search links to Github URLs)

**Alex Vandiver** · 2026-04-06 15:03 UTC

I don't think you've adequately explained why we need to know the mime-type?  `<img>` tags should show "This image has been deleted" and `<video>` tags should show "This video has been deleted" -- why do we need to know the mime-type?

**Alex Vandiver** · 2026-04-06 15:04 UTC

IMHO the most correct solution is that we should, when a file is deleted on the server, rewrite the messages which reference it, and push updates for those message bodies out to the clients.  Those updated message bodies can contain the mime-time of the content that is now missing, if we actually need that.

But that's an API change, and I'm not sure worth the complexity.

Me and @Satyam Bansal were having a discussion on usage of `partial`.  I was using `partial` in PR #37490 grouping 4 events under the same handler as shown in the block below, the reason for this is  that, the four events grouped under `get_admin_action_message` (`admin.added_to_workspace`, `admin.removed_from_workspace`, `admin.logged_in`, `admin.logged_out`) share identical payload structures and only the `topic` field differs. The message-framing logic is also identical that is extract `data.item.name`, fill a string template, and return `("Admin: {name}", body)`.

```
def get_admin_action_message(phrase: str, template: str, payload: WildValue) -> tuple[str, str]:
    admin_name = get_admin_name(payload)
    body = template.format(name=admin_name, phrase=phrase)
    topic_name = get_entity_topic_name("Admin", admin_name)
    return (topic_name, body)

EVENT_TO_FUNCTION_MAPPER: dict[str, Callable[[WildValue], tuple[str, str]]] = {
    "ping": get_ping_message
    "ping": get_ping_message,
    "admin.activity_log_event.created": get_admin_event_log_event_created_message,
    "admin.added_to_workspace": partial(get_admin_action_message, "now", ADMIN_ROLE_UPDATED),
    "admin.removed_from_workspace": partial(
        get_admin_action_message, "no longer", ADMIN_ROLE_UPDATED
    ),
    "admin.away_mode_updated": get_admin_away_mode_updated_message,
    "admin.logged_in": partial(get_admin_action_message, "logged in", ADMIN_LOGIN_LOGOUT),
    "admin.logged_out": partial(get_admin_action_message, "logged out", ADMIN_LOGIN_LOGOUT),
}

```

## nested lists, #38436

*2026-07-07 to 2026-07-08 · 8 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/nested.20lists.2C.20.2338436/with/2491173)*

**Taha Valiji** · 2026-07-07 15:34 UTC

Hi @Alya Abbott   @Tim Abbott 
For the issue(#38436) :
I have managed to implement an extra function which added a pre-processing step in `web/src/compose_paste.ts`. When a user pastes plain text, the paste handler checks if the text contains a tab-indented list. If it does, it intercepts the text and safely converts all leading tabs into 2-space indents before inserting it into the compose box.

```ts
export function normalize_tabs_to_spaces(text: string): string {
    return text
        .split("\n")
        .map((line) => {
            // Check if the line starts with tabs followed by a list marker and a space
            if (/^\t+([*+-]|\d+\.)\s/.test(line)) {
                // Replace leading tabs with '2' spaces per tab level
                return line.replace(/^(\t+)/, (match) => "  ".repeat(match.length));
            }
            return line;
        })
        .join("\n");
}

## peer_data: subscriber count can go negative

*2026-09-23 to 2026-09-23 · 1 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/peer_data.3A.20subscriber.20count.20can.20go.20negative/with/2528192)*

**Aaditya Rawat** · 2026-09-23 15:45 UTC

In peer_data.ts, increment_subscriber_count skips the update when the user is already in the loaded subscriber set, but decrement_subscriber_count only skips when we have full subscriber data for the channel. So on a channel whose subscribers we haven't fetched, repeated or unmatched peer_remove events keep subtracting and the count can go below zero — and it stays there, since set_subscriber_count is only called when the channel is hydrated.

 Minimal repro in peer_data.test.cjs:

 peer_data.set_subscribers(sub.stream_id, [me.user_id], false);
 peer_data.set_subscriber_count(sub.stream_id, 1);
 peer_data.bulk_remove_subscribers({stream_ids: [sub.stream_id], user_ids: [me.user_id]});
 peer_data.bulk_remove_subscribers({stream_ids: [sub.stream_id], user_ids: [me.user_id]});
 assert.equal(peer_data.get_subscriber_count(sub.stream_id), 0);  // actual: -1

 I see the note that subscriber_count can be wrong due to backend races. Is a negative value worth clamping with Math.max(count - 1, 0), or is that already covered by that caveat? I haven't worked out whether the server actually emits a peer_remove the client can't match.


## Rename topic UI / time limit

*2026-09-25 to 2026-09-30 · 2 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/Rename.20topic.20UI.20.2F.20time.20limit/with/2529084)*

**Prakhar Pathak** · 2026-09-25 01:41 UTC

Hi! I was investigating the topic rename behavior and wanted to check whether I’m understanding the intended behavior correctly.

I noticed that there are two UI paths for renaming a topic:

1. The pencil icon, which is gated by `is_topic_editable()`. This considers the message/topic edit time limit, so the pencil disappears after the limit expires.
  
2. The three-dot topic menu, which exposes `Rename topic` based on `can_rename_topic`, which ultimately checks `user_can_move_messages_within_channel()`. This appears to check channel/user permissions but not the topic's time limit.
  

Following the second path led me to `build_move_topic_to_stream_popover()` → `move_topic_containing_message_to_stream()` → `PATCH /json/messages/{message_id}` → `check_update_message()`.

There I found that when `propagate_mode == "change_all"`, the backend calls `check_time_limit_for_change_all_propagate_mode()`. That function checks the `date_sent` of the messages in the topic and can either reject the operation completely or allow only the messages still within the time limit.

So my current understanding is that renaming a topic is implemented as moving/changing the topic of its messages, and the backend is ultimately responsible for enforcing the time limit.

What I'm unsure about is whether the `Rename topic` menu item is intentionally shown even when the topic has already exceeded the time limit (perhaps because partial moves are supported), or whether the UI is expected to hide it in that situation.

Is this behavior intentional?

**Prakhar Pathak** · 2026-09-30 01:10 UTC

Just following up on this when someone has a chance. I’d mainly like to confirm whether the difference between the two rename UI paths is intentional, before I investigate further.

## Prioritize non-deactivated users in search results #35976

*2026-10-08 to 2026-10-12 · 2 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/Prioritize.20non-deactivated.20users.20in.20search.20results.20.2335976/with/2535718)*

**Ameya Khyati** · 2026-10-08 20:13 UTC

Hello everyone, 
I am currently working on this [issue](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/issues/35976) and I looked around a bit for any ongoing discussion related to this, however apart from 3 closed and 1 open (but abandoned?) PR, I found nothing else, so I am adding this topic to not only ask any query related to the issue but also post my findings alongside to get any form of feedback while working on it. 

The issue had `help-wanted`  tag, however I noticed that though it's been more than a year since the issue has been opened, the issue still looks relevant when I looked around the codebase a bit (especially the file `search_suggestion.ts`).

*`If, by any chance, I have missed any fix that has been done in relation to this issue, please lemme know. In the mean while, I'll be working on the fix`*

**Ameya Khyati** · 2026-10-12 06:50 UTC

I traced back to check where the issue really comes from:

In `search_suggestion.ts`, `build_filterer_list` calls `get_people` for 4 categories to build the people’s suggestion list: dm, sender, dm-including and mentions. The filterer runs once for every category, and it never really takes into consideration the status of the account (active/deactivated). It sorts users on the basis of recency => alphabetical order.

> For example, if User A is searching in the suggestion list, where User B and User C are included, and User A and User B shared a recent DM before User B was deactivated, then User B will be listed above the active user account, User C.

Also, in `get_suggestions`, the suggestion list is built such that when the people suggestions for each category are returned, they are simply added back to a master list. So even if we sort users by account status in the shared list, the result might look like this:

```
dm: C
dm: B (deactivated)
sender: C
sender: B (deactivated)
...
```

This is not the intended output, as the requirement is to put all suggestions pertaining to deactivated user accounts at the end.

The proposed fix:
Instead of modifying the sorting order, we take the type of user account (active/deactivated) into consideration when initially fetching the people suggestion list for each category. The fetch and sort in `make_people_getter` still happen only once; the result is just split by account status. This means there are 8 `get_people` filterers instead of 4: 4 for active accounts (one for each category), followed by 4 for deactivated accounts (one for each category). Listing all the active ones before the deactivated ones is what gives the intended ranking.
